*A source of truth for what Natural Hypertrophy teaches about muscle, strength and the gym look: 2331 principles with stable IDs, distilled from his videos and posts (2020-2026). Built 2026-10-24.*

Each principle: **Statement · Numbers · Scope · Confidence · Status · Check · Sources**. Search it with `python _work/ask.py "<words>"`; test a program against `book/CHECKLIST.md`.

# 1. His journey & stats

This chapter records who Natural Hypertrophy is as a lifter: where he started, how his bodyweight, physique, programming and mindset changed over ~15 years, and the stats he has given for himself. The facts describe his own history, not advice; he repeatedly calls himself a "special case" whose volume most people do not need. His overall story is a weak, bullied teen who built a 6 ft, ~220 lb natural physique slowly, lost years to strength chasing, dirty bulking and injuries, and moved to self-written, hypertrophy-only training with more balance in life.

## Starting point and early years

He started from very low and spent years at home with almost no equipment before ever entering a gym.

<a id="JRN-01"></a>
### JRN-01 · Started small, weak and untrained at 14-15
- **Statement:** He began training at 14-15 as the smallest kid in his class after losing arm wrestling to a girl; he could not do a single push-up and could only train about 10 minutes (knee push-ups, sit-ups, light curls).
- **Numbers:** start age 14 or 15; 100, 110 or 120 lb; under 5 ft / 5'5" / ~5'2" at 14-15; 0 push-ups; ~10 min sessions
- **Scope:** his own starting point
- **Confidence:** high — ~9 videos, 2020→2024
- **Status:** contradicted — start age (14 vs 15), weight (100 vs 110 vs 120 lb) and teen height vary between videos
- **Sources:** ([STORY TIME： My entire training history, 2021-08](https://youtu.be/aIjUTEtXOcM?t=63); [10 Year Natural Transformation 15-25 (from 110 to 210 lbs), 2020-04](https://youtu.be/yenqGI_FVQ4?t=63); [Natural Hypertrophy： my lifting history, 2020-01](https://youtu.be/S1h9qEhIo-I); [You weren't chosen by God. Now what?, 2024-06](https://youtu.be/AZSZmhOJZJI?t=316))

- **Numbers:** 10 min → 20 → 40 min → 1 h → 2 h
- **Scope:** his own start as a complete beginner
- **Confidence:** medium — ~3 videos, 2020→2021

## Bodyweight history and bulking lessons

His weight story runs from slow teenage gains, through a dirty bulk to 240 lb and a crash cut, to a long recomp and a slow bulk to 220 lb. See the stats timeline at the end of the chapter.

<a id="JRN-11"></a>
### JRN-11 · Bodyweight path from 110 to 220 lb
- **Statement:** He went from about 110 lb at 15 to a fat peak of 235-240 lb around age 23, crash-cut to ~205-210, recomped at 210 for about three years, then slowly bulked to 220 lb, which he now maintains.
- **Numbers:** 110 (15) → 140 (17-18) → 150-160 (19) → 170 (20) → 185-190 (21) → 200-205 (22) → 235-240 peak (~23, 21-22% BF) → ~205-210 → mini-bulk 225 → ~215 → 210 recomp (2019-2022) → 215 (2023) → 220 (2024)
- **Scope:** his own bodyweight
- **Confidence:** high — ~25 videos, 2020→2024
- **Status:** contradicted — weight at 22 given as 200-205 or 220 lb; the 240-lb peak dated ~2017 in one video and 2018-2019 in others; in 2025 he recalled 110 kg in Dec 2019
- **Sources:** ([10 Year Natural Transformation 15-25 (from 110 to 210 lbs), 2020-04](https://youtu.be/yenqGI_FVQ4?t=577); [Recomp guide (part. 2)： Who can do it & diet manipulation, 2020-05](https://youtu.be/IeYLu4_hkZY?t=317); [Escape Intermediate Hell (Path to Exceptional Physique), 2023-10](https://youtu.be/16fjHEtZTCA?t=763); [20 inch arms CMON (Hypertrophy Log #9), 2024-12](https://youtu.be/qvWxIzhT1QU?t=317))

<a id="JRN-12"></a>
### JRN-12 · His gains rate halved about every five years
- **Statement:** Each five-year block brought roughly half the bodyweight gain of the one before.
- **Numbers:** +60 lb (ages 15-20), +30 lb (20-25), +15 lb in 3 years (25-28)
- **Scope:** his own natural progress
- **Confidence:** medium — 1 video, 2023
- **Status:** current
- **Sources:** ([Escape Intermediate Hell (Path to Exceptional Physique), 2023-10](https://youtu.be/16fjHEtZTCA?t=763))

<a id="JRN-13"></a>
### JRN-13 · Best gains came from a tiny surplus held for years
- **Statement:** As a skinny teen eating what his parents served, plus a little extra each day, he gained steadily for years without tracking, supplements or ever getting chubby; he calls the clean bulk that poverty forced on him "a blessing".
- **Numbers:** +1 bowl of rice or some roast beef/day; ~10-15 lb quality mass/year; 110 → 170 lb in 5 years
- **Scope:** his teen years, beginner
- **Confidence:** high — ~7 videos, 2020→2023

## Training phases and programming lessons

His programming went from no plan, through a productive simple plan, to a strength-focused era that stalled him, and finally to self-written hypertrophy programs.

<a id="JRN-21"></a>
### JRN-21 · No program at first meant stalling
- **Statement:** For his first one to two years he trained randomly (machines, bench) with no program; he still gained but never adapted neurologically and stalled, and a plan would have been far more productive.
- **Numbers:** ~1-2 years without a program
- **Scope:** his early training
- **Confidence:** high — ~5 videos, 2020→2022
- **Status:** current
- **Check:** Does the lifter follow a written plan rather than picking exercises at random?
- **Sources:** ([Natural Hypertrophy： my lifting history, 2020-01](https://youtu.be/S1h9qEhIo-I?t=187); [The issue with Novice Programs, 2021-03](https://youtu.be/S0qBQppUtTQ?t=50); [𝐓𝐡𝐢𝐬 𝐈𝐬 𝐖𝐡𝐲 𝐖𝐞 𝐋𝐢𝐟𝐭, 2022-10](https://youtu.be/E1er3oQ3IeM?t=2138); [5 Things I Wish I Knew Before I Started Lifting, 2022-09](https://youtu.be/6HGBdDOAReA?t=191))

<a id="JRN-22"></a>
### JRN-22 · A simple linear dumbbell plan gave his best gains
- **Statement:** About three years on a simple linear dumbbell program in his bedroom took him from skinny to visibly trained; he trained full body for three years as a beginner.
- **Numbers:** ~3 years linear DB program; 3 years full body
- **Scope:** his beginner years
- **Confidence:** medium — ~3 videos, 2021→2022
- **Status:** current
- **Sources:** ([5 Things I Wish I Knew Before I Started Lifting, 2022-09](https://youtu.be/6HGBdDOAReA?t=191); [Fullbody template review, 2021-01](https://youtu.be/G7rVTseabFU?t=63); [Hypertrophy Q&A #5, 2021-01](https://youtu.be/-anA4CV2SVU?t=691))

# 2. Mindset, natural vs enhanced & genetics

This chapter covers the mental side of training (discipline, adherence, goals, comparison, ego, dysmorphia), his position on performance-enhancing drugs (PEDs) and testosterone replacement (TRT), and what he thinks genetics do and don't decide. His overall stance: discipline and years of consistency, not motivation or talent, carry a natural lifter. Never take PEDs, because the gains leave with the drug and enhanced advice doesn't transfer to naturals. Genetics are real but mostly set speed and shape, not whether you can get big, so "bad genetics" and "the natural limit" are usually excuses. General life philosophy (stoicism, media habits, social life) is in ch. 14.

## Discipline and habits

He ranks discipline above motivation and treats it as a learned, daily habit. In 2024 he softens the rigidity but keeps the core.

<a id="MND-01"></a>
### MND-01 · Discipline over motivation
- **Statement:** Motivation spikes and fades; discipline gets you to the gym. The top level is training without deliberation because it's simply on the schedule and you love it.
- **Numbers:** three levels: motivation → discipline → "just doing it"; after 10-15 years he is rarely motivated
- **Scope:** all lifters
- **Confidence:** high — ~14 videos, 2020→2024
- **Status:** contradicted — he also once called motivation "the most important half" alongside method, against his usual view that it is too unreliable to carry you
- **Check:** Is training run as a fixed habit rather than left to how motivated the lifter feels?
- **Sources:** ([The Educated Barbarian： Hagakure analysis (part. 3), 2020-07](https://youtu.be/RPUhg61IV-g); [Natural Q&A #6, 2021-03](https://youtu.be/kkbfHkyQ_q0?t=825); [Judging and Grading every Fitness Channel (ⅠⅠ： Jeff Nippard, Eric Bugenhagen, 2022-04](https://youtu.be/GowuEmDClqY?t=4152); [Winter Arc 2025 is CANCELLED, 2024-11](https://youtu.be/z9MttM0Bq-I?t=380))

## Why stay natural: gains, health, lifespan

His core message is "never take PEDs": not one cycle, not a low dose, not TRT. The NAT principles below give his reasons and what follows for training.

<a id="NAT-01"></a>
### NAT-01 · PED gains don't stay
- **Statement:** Stop the drugs and most of the muscle goes, because the hormonal environment it grew in is gone, even with PCT and hard training; remove the drug and the physique collapses, remove the training and it largely stays.
- **Numbers:** users shrink to normal or mediocre within ~3-4 months off
- **Scope:** anyone considering PEDs
- **Confidence:** high — ~14 videos, 2020→2025
- **Status:** contradicted — he has also said PEDs "have been shown to increase myonuclei" and regaining is slightly easier after use, while later rejecting lasting myonuclei gains "in practice"
- **Sources:** ([How to spot a fake natty： rollercoaster progress, 2020-01](https://youtu.be/tqf2di_v9KY?t=131); [Reasons you should stay natural： you will become physically dependent on PEDs, 2020-03](https://youtu.be/q1dr6WlETJU?t=124); [Nucleus overload guide (part. 1)： What it is & how to implement it, 2020-05](https://youtu.be/T74sR7AIOZc?t=1198); [💉 Taking steroids is cheating ｜ Natural Bodybuilder Reacts 💪, 2025-01](https://youtu.be/thqDZPgE2kY?t=1323))

## Genetics vs work

He accepts that genetics are real but holds that for almost everyone they set speed and shape, not whether you can get big.

<a id="GEN-01"></a>
### GEN-01 · Genetics exist but are never an excuse
- **Statement:** How you play your cards matters more than the cards; whatever your starting point, doing the work decides the outcome, and blaming genetics avoids responsibility. Genetics only make it easier; mindset decides whether a natural gets big.
- **Numbers:** —
- **Scope:** all lifters
- **Confidence:** high — ~20 videos, 2020→2024
- **Status:** current — see GEN-28 for how much more openly he credits genetics in 2024-2025
- **Check:** Is stalled progress traced to method, effort or time before genetics are blamed?
- **Sources:** ([Why your Genetics don't matter, 2020-12](https://youtu.be/xCzoFKSPkIc?t=62); [What having bad genetics means (to me), 2020-04](https://youtu.be/CrPz7efvTGU?t=248); [Tales of Genetics： Aquatic Twat, 2021-12](https://youtu.be/n-n3txKjGmE?t=943); [You weren't chosen by God. ## Natural potential and limits

<a id="GEN-11"></a>
### GEN-11 · There is no locatable natural limit
- **Statement:** Progress continues, slower, as long as you keep raising weight, volume and intensity; about 99% of people who say they hit the limit only reached the point where the work stopped seeming worth it, or never had a progressive overload scheme. He calls it "a cultural limit, not a biological one".
- **Numbers:** ~99%
- **Scope:** naturals
- **Confidence:** high — ~25 videos, 2020→2024
- **Status:** changed — 2020-2023: no limit, you "progress until you die"; 2024: limits exist but you can't locate them, and self-assessments almost always underestimate
- **Check:** Is a plateau treated as a programming problem to solve rather than a natural limit?
- **Sources:** ([Natty or not (.com)： Jeff Nippard, 2020-05](https://youtu.be/f0vdsC2yyhY?t=1634); [Why do so many lifters quit once they become intermediates?, 2020-03](https://youtu.be/K9hKDPaDFsI?t=125); [The Monster Natty that trains EVERY DAY (Geoffrey Verity Schofield), 2023-04](https://youtu.be/aJ1e41y8Na4?t=2139); [Your standards are too low., 2024-12](https://youtu.be/uKOuj3Mzc9c?t=566))

# 3. Volume, intensity, frequency & rest

This chapter covers the four dials of a training program: how hard each set is (intensity, failure, reps in reserve), how many hard sets you do (volume), how you spread them over the week (frequency and splits), and how long you rest between sets. His later stance is that hard sets close to failure are what make naturals grow. He wants the least volume that keeps you progressing, spread over 2-3 sessions per muscle, with heavy work rested fully and everything else supersetted. He started (2020) as a high-volume maximalist and moved toward intensity and minimal-effective volume by 2024.

## The frame: tonnage and the trinity

He reasons about training through tonnage (reps x weight) from hard sets, produced by three linked variables.

<a id="VOL-01"></a>
### VOL-01 · Volume, intensity and frequency form one system
- **Statement:** Volume, intensity and frequency are one trinity; none works alone, and pushing one while ignoring the others breaks the system.
- **Numbers:** —
- **Scope:** All trainees; the basis for every programming decision in this chapter.
- **Confidence:** high — ~10 videos, 2020→2023
- **Status:** current
- **Sources:** ([The hypertrophy series： the issue of volume without intensity, 2020-05](https://youtu.be/lJyrBDvtQFU?t=62); [The hypertrophy series： the primordial metric for muscle growth, 2021-01](https://youtu.be/V4aBuYpdY34?t=55); [Mike Mentzer： Mustachioed fraud or Bodybuilding genius? (🆃🅷🅴 🅷🅸, 2022-08](https://youtu.be/lmhW2W2UQto?t=1514); [What everyone gets WRONG about Range of Motion, 2023-03](https://youtu.be/1apseBbt0-o?t=62))

<a id="VOL-02"></a>
### VOL-02 · Growth comes from tonnage in a relevant window
- **Statement:** Hypertrophy is driven by tonnage (reps x weight) accumulated over time, but volume counts only when the load sits in a relevant intensity window.
- **Numbers:** 10 reps at 315 lb beats 2 at 350; 300x5 beats 350x1; 135 lb bench for 1000 reps won't make you big.
- **Scope:** All trainees; tonnage means hard-set tonnage, never raw reps.
- **Confidence:** high — ~25 videos, 2020→2024
- **Status:** current
- **Sources:** ([Wisconsin method aka Bulgarian light review (from a muscular hypertrophy standpo, 2020-02](https://youtu.be/RaGX9rPQr4k?t=435); [The hypertrophy series： volume vs intensity, 2020-04](https://youtu.be/UQguwgxTC9E?t=255); [No one understands training intensity, 2021-11](https://youtu.be/UrFS3Gs5zh0?t=960); [1st Natural Hypertrophy stream! ASK YOUR QUESTIONS AND I SHALL ANSWER, 2024-09](https://youtu.be/bRKQIOYo2u4?t=10631))

<a id="VOL-03"></a>
### VOL-03 · Count working sets only
- **Statement:** Only relevant tonnage from hard sets counts; warm-ups and very light work add tonnage but of low quality.
- **Numbers:** 4000 lb of nucleus-overload work is worth about 400 lb of quality work.
- **Scope:** All trainees; he still sees warm-ups as mildly useful.
- **Confidence:** high — ~8 videos, 2020→2022
- **Status:** current
- **Sources:** ([The issue with 10x10 / German Volume Training, 2020-11](https://youtu.be/s8mGWwTGLOo?t=360); [The hypertrophy series： volume vs tonnage, 2020-03](https://youtu.be/dpwvdQqKxQI?t=308); [☣️ Biohacking Muscle Growth with Nucleus Overload 💪, 2022-03](https://youtu.be/LNggSj0WBd8?t=1071); [Hypertrophy Q&A #9, 2022-01](https://youtu.be/9y2s6kyFkPc?t=2253))

<a id="VOL-04"></a>
### VOL-04 · Stop a muscle when loads become irrelevant
- **Statement:** End a muscle's work when it can no longer return to a load relevant to the opening strength work; judge this against absolute (fresh) intensity, not the rising relative intensity of a tired muscle.
- **Numbers:** A 300 lb squatter who ends up doing a variation with 150 lb has "dug too deep"; 225x10 squats is easy as an opener but brutal after three other leg lifts.
- **Scope:** All trainees; he prefers this in-session cue to MRV guesses.
- **Confidence:** high — ~12 videos, 2020→2022
- **Status:** current
- **Sources:** ([The hypertrophy series： absolute vs relative intensity, 2020-10](https://youtu.be/4uTKFMZVgSs?t=230); [The hypertrophy series： absolute vs relative intensity, 2020-10](https://youtu.be/4uTKFMZVgSs?t=470); [Hypertrophy Q&A #8, 2021-09](https://youtu.be/P89o8FBSWDI?t=1060); [Hypertrophy Q&A #10, 2022-06](https://youtu.be/QfHfxLYRu88?t=1321))

<a id="VOL-05"></a>
### VOL-05 · Muscular endurance caps the number of sets
- **Statement:** The real limit on sets is muscular endurance: being able to return to baseline and repeat. It sets your maximum recoverable volume and differs by body part.
- **Numbers:** —
- **Scope:** All trainees; bigger muscles have more endurance, so set counts should differ per body part.
- **Confidence:** medium — ~7 videos, 2020→2021
- **Status:** current
- **Sources:** ([The hypertrophy series： the optimal number of sets per muscle group, 2020-10](https://youtu.be/82CguFy4piw?t=125); [The hypertrophy series： the optimal number of sets per muscle group, 2020-10](https://youtu.be/82CguFy4piw?t=314); [ANIME WORKOUTS - Would Jack Hanma's Transformation in Grappler Baki be possible , 2020-12](https://youtu.be/WyxeMHovPJ8?t=330); [Rep Goal System (by Steve Shaw of Massive Iron) review, 2020-07](https://youtu.be/LYBdXCcmOO0?t=1130))

<a id="VOL-06"></a>
### VOL-06 · Tonnage creeps up slowly, driven by set and rep progress
- **Statement:** Tonnage should stay stable and rise slowly without big dips or spikes; let progress in sets and reps drive tonnage, and use tonnage math mainly to diagnose stalls.
- **Numbers:** Adding a 10-rep set at 200 lb adds 2000 lb vs 50 lb from adding 5 lb to the bar.
- **Scope:** All trainees; don't add sets just to hit a tonnage number.
- **Confidence:** medium — ~7 videos, 2020→2022
- **Status:** current

- **Scope:** All trainees.
- **Confidence:** high — ~11 videos, 2020→2024
- **Status:** current

### INT-09 · Absolute vs relative intensity
- **Statement:** Absolute intensity is what you can move fresh and warmed up; relative intensity climbs rep by rep, set by set and through the session as fatigue builds.

- **Statement:** Because relative intensity keeps climbing, programming only by absolute percentages misprograms; optimal intensity exists only at the session's start, which is where strength work belongs.

- **Statement:** Low reps can be low intensity and high reps high intensity; "low reps for strength, high reps for size" is false, and any range means nothing without effort.

### INT-13 · "Heavy" is relative to the lifter and context
- **Statement:** Whether a load is heavy depends on the lifter and where it falls in the session; don't let other people's standards push you into ever-lower reps.
- **Numbers:** A 120 lb deadlift can be 30% for one lifter and 90% for another; for him 205x12 and 265x2 bench are both heavy; 185x10 close-grip late in a session would be 205-215 as an opener.
- **Scope:** All trainees.
- **Confidence:** medium — ~4 videos, 2020→2021
- **Status:** current
- **Sources:** ([Do you need to lift heavy to get big?, 2020-02](https://youtu.be/aiVrEt5ziHQ?t=314); [Do you need to lift heavy to get big?, 2020-02](https://youtu.be/aiVrEt5ziHQ?t=442); [No one understands training intensity, 2021-11](https://youtu.be/UrFS3Gs5zh0?t=603); [Keep Ronnie Coleman's name out of your unworthy hardgainer's mouth, 2021-07](https://youtu.be/5Nhv3cgzrAg?t=63))

<a id="INT-14"></a>
### INT-14 · Raising intensity without adding load
- **Statement:** Pre-fatigue, supersets, variations and density raise intensity without more weight, but fatigue-inflated intensity should stay marginal, never the foundation of the program.
- **Numbers:** Push-ups before bench make a 50% bench act like 65%; the same tonnage in 2 h instead of 4 h is more intense; with supersets, 4x10-15 instead of 3x12-20.
- **Scope:** All trainees; planned pre-fatigue helps, unplanned pre-fatigue hinders progression.
- **Confidence:** medium — ~6 videos, 2020→2022
- **Status:** current
- **Sources:** ([The hypertrophy series： volume vs intensity, 2020-04](https://youtu.be/UQguwgxTC9E?t=191); [The hypertrophy series： the hypertrophy rep range conundrum, 2020-05](https://youtu.be/Vw9MhD5Amfw?t=257); [Push Pull Legs Upper Lower 5 days split Program review, 2020-05](https://youtu.be/0yIieHQjEiA?t=881); [The hypertrophy series： the impact of sets and reps on intensity, 2020-09](https://youtu.be/ZPps_9IGdhc?t=450))

## Intensity windows: loads and rep ranges

<a id="INT-15"></a>
### INT-15 · Work mostly between ~60% and ~95% of 1RM
- **Statement:** The productive window is roughly 60-95% of 1RM; below ~60% is junk volume, and true maxes above ~95% aren't worth the injury risk or the lost tonnage.
- **Numbers:** 70-90% (2020-02); 60-95% (2020-09); 60-95/96% with 20-60% junk (2021-11); 70-90% for bodybuilders (2022-03); 60-90% (2022-12); 65-95% (2023-03). His own: 70-90/95%, ~90% for most lifts (2020). Absolute floor ~40% 1RM (2020).
- **Scope:** Bodybuilding, naturals. Exception: nucleus overload (VOL-55).
- **Confidence:** high — ~12 videos, 2020→2023
- **Status:** current
- **Check:** Is the bulk of working-set load between about 60% and 95% of 1RM?
- **Sources:** ([When are you intermediate and what it means programming wise (for bodybuilding), 2020-02](https://youtu.be/y_lPAdWi4sU?t=318); [The hypertrophy series： intensity windows and their applications, 2020-09](https://youtu.be/K-iofHQxDsA?t=312); [No one understands training intensity, 2021-11](https://youtu.be/UrFS3Gs5zh0?t=1352); [What everyone gets WRONG about Range of Motion, 2023-03](https://youtu.be/1apseBbt0-o?t=250))

<a id="INT-16"></a>
### INT-16 · Average intensity about 85%
- **Statement:** ~85% is the average across training, not a per-set target; individual days can swing as long as the bulk averages ~85%, and that average sets fatigue, frequency, sets and reps.
- **Numbers:** ~85% average; a day at 95% and the next at 65% is fine.
- **Scope:** Program-level planning.
- **Confidence:** medium — ~3 videos, 2020→2022
- **Status:** contradicted — 2020 he said steady 85-95% beats swinging between 99% and 60%; 2022 he allows swings around an 85% average.
- **Sources:** ([The hypertrophy series： deloading without wasting tonnage, 2020-12](https://youtu.be/7ZS-mGePFXw?t=480); [How to Get Bigger by Doing Less (The 85% Rule), 2022-12](https://youtu.be/z2uzpl_smSg?t=442); [How to Get Bigger by Doing Less (The 85% Rule), 2022-12](https://youtu.be/z2uzpl_smSg?t=820); [How to Get Bigger by Doing Less (The 85% Rule), 2022-12](https://youtu.be/z2uzpl_smSg?t=946))

<a id="INT-17"></a>
### INT-17 · Rep range: mostly 6-12, all work 3-15
- **Statement:** Bodybuilding work sits mostly at 6-12 reps within an overall 3-15 span; above 15-20 is junk, and singles to triples should not make up the bulk.
- **Numbers:** 20-35 cap (2020-02); 2-15 (2020-09; core 3-9 for tall lanky lifters); 2-12 (2021-06); 6-12 with extremes 3-4 and 15-20 (2022-12); 6-15 most work (2023-01); 3-15, mostly 6-12, >20 junk, "never 20+" (2024).
- **Scope:** Looks-focused trainees; only some forearm and neck work goes higher.
- **Confidence:** high — ~12 videos, 2020→2024
- **Status:** changed — upper limit fell from 20-35 reps (early 2020) to ~15 (2020-09) and "never 20+" (2024).
- **Check:** Do most working sets fall in 6-12 reps, with almost none above 15-20?
- **Sources:** ([Transcendent training review (from an hypertrophy standpoint), 2020-02](https://youtu.be/uTHCzF7Exck?t=760); [How to start doing more volume in your training, 2020-09](https://youtu.be/p6WcFTOBq3s?t=436); [How to Get Bigger by Doing Less (The 85% Rule), 2022-12](https://youtu.be/z2uzpl_smSg?t=757); [Do you look better than Silver Era lifters? (Physique Review LIVE), 2024-12](https://youtu.be/ZLheQPgEfoA?t=2535))

<a id="INT-18"></a>
### INT-18 · High-rep sets rarely reach real failure
- **Statement:** Above ~15-20 reps each extra rep adds little intensity, and cardio, lactic burn or technique stop you before the muscle does. In 2025 he adds that true failure is reachable at 12-15, and higher ranges are more forgiving for grinding.
- **Numbers:** First compound of the day ~10 reps, not 15; 10-15 hammer curls are worse than 8-12; 35 reps is "ridiculous"; 3x6-10 DB press beats 180 reps of raises.
- **Scope:** All trainees; boredom in high-rep sets is a load-selection problem (2025).
- **Confidence:** high — ~14 videos, 2020→2025
- **Status:** current
- **Sources:** ([Hypertrophy Q&A #4, 2020-12](https://youtu.be/ZScs2L9rero?t=1129); [The BEST Workout if you like to waste time for no results (Ryan Humiston Split/P, 2022-02](https://youtu.be/wLx5BRx8AaU?t=535); [The Monster Natty that trains EVERY DAY (Geoffrey Verity Schofield), 2023-04](https://youtu.be/aJ1e41y8Na4?t=1511); [New Hypertrophy Gimmick™ just dropped 🤡, 2025-03](https://youtu.be/ACFKXT44BzM?t=1063))

<a id="INT-19"></a>
### INT-19 · Low reps build size too
- **Statement:** Low reps (3-5, 4-8) work for size and help naturals by raising the absolute intensity used for higher-rep work; he rejects the claim that anything under 5 (or 7-8) reps is useless.
- **Numbers:** EZ curls 3x5-8; weighted fat-grip pull-ups 4-8; naturals need 6-10, 4-8 and the occasional 3x5; "low reps" means under 5-6.
- **Scope:** Naturals.
- **Confidence:** high — ~6 videos, 2020→2023
- **Status:** current
- **Sources:** ([4 days Upper Lower + 1 Arm day Program review, 2020-11](https://youtu.be/xQQJUXf58ZE?t=1890); [Analyzing the Rock's ＂Black Adam＂ training program, 2021-03](https://youtu.be/BnzVYV9_IQc?t=316); [The Natty Arnold? (Joel Kellett aka Overkell), 2023-07](https://youtu.be/Mn34v5Y1d-0?t=2261); [Giants DO Exist (Tom Haviland), 2023-12](https://youtu.be/hEuy__sCbZA?t=1891))

<a id="INT-20"></a>
### INT-20 · Never test true 1RMs for hypertrophy
- **Statement:** True 1RMs have an atrocious fatigue-to-stimulus ratio, give little tonnage and raise injury risk; working up to a max and stopping gives you only the warm-up.
- **Numbers:** Curls never below 3-4 reps; weighted dips never need true 1RMs.
- **Scope:** Hypertrophy training; rare testing builds strength better than constant maxing.
- **Confidence:** high — ~10 videos, 2020→2024
- **Status:** current
- **Check:** Does the program avoid true 1RM attempts and keep singles-to-triples out of the bulk of the work?
- **Sources:** ([How to program an arm day (the Natural Hypertrophy example), 2020-01](https://youtu.be/gVVj9QuCyFM?t=631); [Is CNS fatigue out to get you?, 2022-03](https://youtu.be/NPlGK0-7h0A?t=374); [How to Get Bigger by Doing Less (The 85% Rule), 2022-12](https://youtu.be/z2uzpl_smSg?t=569); [This Calisthenics Freak Makes Bodybuilders Look Small (Baki_HD), 2024-06](https://youtu.be/2LoP6-KdEx4?t=1005))

<a id="INT-21"></a>
### INT-21 · Low-rep work is a tonnage trap if overdone
- **Statement:** A true 3RM gives little tonnage and can't be repeated for four sets, while many easy triples aren't truly intense; with low reps, fewer sets are better.
- **Numbers:** 2x3 or 2x5 may beat 3x3 or 5x5 for hypertrophy (2023); only the last set of a 3x3 is near failure.
- **Scope:** Naturals using low reps.
- **Confidence:** medium — ~3 videos, 2020→2023
- **Status:** current
- **Sources:** ([The hypertrophy series： the issue of intensity without volume, 2020-07](https://youtu.be/7dqBu5KLIoQ?t=66); [The hypertrophy series： the optimal number of sets per muscle group, 2020-10](https://youtu.be/82CguFy4piw?t=501); [Giants DO Exist (Tom Haviland), 2023-12](https://youtu.be/hEuy__sCbZA?t=2018))

<a id="INT-22"></a>
### INT-22 · Fixed rep "zones" are myths
- **Statement:** "6-8 strength / 8-12 size / 12+ endurance", "10-15 is best, never below 8" and "compounds low, isolations high" are wrong as fixed rules; choose 6-10, 8-12 or 10-15 by preference and by what lets you progress.
- **Numbers:** —
- **Scope:** All trainees.
- **Confidence:** medium — ~3 videos, 2023

<a id="INT-23"></a>
### INT-23 · Still, match the rep range to the lift
- **Statement:** Each lift and muscle has its own best window found by experiment; compounds usually go lower and isolations higher, and heavy/medium/light ranges should stay close together.
- **Numbers:** Heavy 3-6/2-5/3-5, medium 6-10/6-12, light 8-10/8-12/8-15; never a 1-rep heavy day with a 20-rep light day; 1-15 is too wide to be useful; rear delts at 3-5 or weighted dips at 10-15 are mismatches.
- **Scope:** All trainees.
- **Confidence:** medium — ~3 videos, 2020→2024
- **Status:** current

(Physique Review LIVE), 2024-12](https://youtu.be/ZLheQPgEfoA?t=2472))

<a id="INT-24"></a>
### INT-24 · A rep range is a bracket around near-failure
- **Statement:** Pick the weight so the target rep lands near failure; without high intensity you plateau in any range.
- **Numbers:** Lowering rep ranges ~12-20% across the board raises intensity; 6-10 is more intense than 10-15, and grinding 2 more reps past "failure" at 15 means the load isn't challenging.

- **Confidence:** medium — ~4 videos, 2020→2024

## Failure and reps in reserve

Failure is defined narrowly (the muscle stops), used selectively, and never means missing a rep.

<a id="INT-25"></a>
### INT-25 · The target is muscular failure
- **Statement:** Count only failure where the target muscle is the limit. Cardio, lactic burn, pump, occlusion or a structural breakdown (artificial or mechanical failure) feel hard but build little and cap tonnage.
- **Numbers:** He curls 135 lb for 8 but can't do 40 empty-bar reps (pump fatigue, not muscular failure); 20% of your squat for max reps gives a pump but little stimulus.
- **Scope:** All trainees; novices often mistake cardio fatigue for failure. A few artificial-failure sets are acceptable, not as the focus.
- **Confidence:** high — ~14 videos, 2020→2024
- **Status:** contradicted — terminology only: "mechanical failure" means structural breakdown in 2020-21 but in 2023 he "defines failure as mechanical failure" (stop when body English appears).
- **Sources:** ([The hypertrophy series： volume vs intensity, 2020-04](https://youtu.be/UQguwgxTC9E?t=319); [The hypertrophy series： artificial vs organical failure, 2020-07](https://youtu.be/zyjCsFRlBT0?t=191); [The Hypertrophy Iceberg Explained (a complete guide to muscle growth), 2021-07](https://youtu.be/8ELQ2XZgpls?t=850); [I was… wrong? (Giving Mike Israetel a Fair Review of RP’s Mass Gain Training, 2022-09](https://youtu.be/gizylGr0ebo?t=1001))

<a id="INT-26"></a>
### INT-26 · Failure = no further clean rep
- **Statement:** Failure is the point where you cannot do another rep with clean form; the set ends as soon as you need body English or a torso shift, and partials after failure only move the standard.
- **Numbers:** —
- **Scope:** Bodybuilding.
- **Confidence:** medium — ~4 videos, 2020→2024
- **Status:** current
- **Sources:** ([Hypertrophy Q&A #3, 2020-11](https://youtu.be/6sFaB3rAY1A?t=2700); [Training for Aesthetics： You're doing it WRONG., 2023-05](https://youtu.be/Zqv7KVsmu78?t=695); [SAVAGE PUSH DAY 🔥 (Hypertrophy Log #3), 2023-07](https://youtu.be/0X2PxuT3tuE?t=380); [Why everyone HATES Paul Carter (liftrunbang1), 2024-02](https://youtu.be/ZRNSc-xBVnc?t=1702))

<a id="INT-27"></a>
### INT-27 · Never actually miss a rep
- **Statement:** "Going to failure" means hitting the last rep you can complete; a missed rep is a programming error that raises injury risk, hurts morale and ruins the rest of the session.
- **Numbers:** —
- **Scope:** Bodybuilders; missed reps may belong in powerlifting. Failing weekly means the program is wrong.
- **Confidence:** high — ~10 videos, 2020→2021
- **Status:** current
- **Check:** Are loads chosen so that reps are reached at or near failure but never actually missed?
- **Sources:** ([The hypertrophy series： the importance of going to failure for muscle building, 2020-05](https://youtu.be/UpbamnOFaZw); [Smolov program review (from an hypertrophy standpoint), 2020-08](https://youtu.be/N8Dp4inzHog?t=822); [The issue with HIT (the intensity meme), 2020-11](https://youtu.be/LqsqSGZooR0?t=937); [The Educated Barbarian： An introduction to Stoicism (Enchiridion analysis part. , 2021-06](https://youtu.be/p42qv-VEEOk?t=1323))

<a id="INT-28"></a>
### INT-28 · Selective failure: isolations yes, squats and hinges no
- **Statement:** Take isolation, upper-body presses, rows, pulldowns and other low-risk lifts to failure on every set; keep 1-2 reps in reserve on squats, deadlifts, good mornings and other risky lower-body compounds.
- **Numbers:** 0 RIR on isolation, presses, rows; 1-2 RIR on squats and hinges. He personally takes 1 RIR on presses because of a neck/upper-back nerve issue.
- **Scope:** All trainees.
- **Confidence:** high — ~22 videos, 2020→2024
- **Status:** changed — 2020 "every working set goes to failure" (with a rep kept on strength compounds); from 2022 failure only where it is safe and recoverable.
- **Check:** Do isolation and upper-body sets end at 0-1 RIR while squats, deadlifts and good mornings stop 1-2 reps short?

<a id="INT-29"></a>
### INT-29 · Isolation lifts deserve full intensity
- **Statement:** Isolations have the best stimulus-to-fatigue ratio and low injury risk, so push them as hard as a deadlift; small muscles respond to intensity like big ones.
- **Numbers:** 10-12 cable curls with 10 RIR stimulate nothing; 5x10-15 easy arm work is junk.

<a id="INT-30"></a>
### INT-30 · Failure is a calibration tool, not the goal
- **Statement:** Proximity to failure is what matters; failure is the baseline for judging effort, and failing on everything misallocates recovery ("always training to failure is stupid").
- **Numbers:** Sets at 70-90% also grow muscle.
- **Scope:** All trainees; the opposite swing, fear of failure, is just as wrong.
- **Confidence:** high — ~6 videos, 2022→2023
- **Status:** current
- **Sources:** ([3 YEARS WITHOUT INJURIES： How I bulletproofed myself (and how you can do it too), 2022-06](https://youtu.be/qrBLykvU_EE?t=188); [How to Get Bigger by Doing Less (The 85% Rule), 2022-12](https://youtu.be/z2uzpl_smSg?t=507); [The Ten 𝐋𝐀𝐖𝐒 of HYPERTROPHY (that you MUST break to grow), 2022-08](https://youtu.be/yUecX6qONXg?t=506); [The Most IMPORTANT Methods for Muscle Growth (Hypertrophy Tier-List), 2023-11](https://youtu.be/SxqjF2oPasg?t=378))

<a id="INT-31"></a>
### INT-31 · Decide where to fail by recoverability
- **Statement:** Failure is fine where you can train the muscle again soon (curls, laterals), not where it blocks a pattern for a week; recovery cost depends on the load at which you fail.

### INT-32 · Hard sets must be repeatable within 2-3 days
- **Statement:** Keep enough in the tank to train the muscle again in 2-3 days; a set you can only recover from every 15 days is not a good hard set. Repeatability is "the bread and butter of natural bodybuilding".

### INT-33 · Reps in reserve on squats and deadlifts
- **Statement:** On heavy squats, deadlifts and their variations leave the "danger rep" in the tank for form and injury prevention.

<a id="INT-37"></a>
### INT-37 · Percentages vs RPE vs feel
- **Statement:** Percentages, RPE and RIR are interchangeable A-tier tools and he recommends % of an estimated 1RM, yet in his own training he uses none of them: a rep range from experience, push to failure, add weight when the top gets easy.

## Hard sets, repeatability and sandbagging

<a id="INT-40"></a>
### INT-40 · Hard sets are the most important sets
- **Statement:** A hard set uses a challenging load, ends at muscular failure and is repeatable enough to accumulate tonnage; make as much of your tonnage as possible come from hard sets, including accessories, not only strength work.
- **Numbers:** ~10 hard sets fit in one workout across different planes; S tier (2023), "king" (2024).
- **Scope:** All trainees.
- **Confidence:** high — ~8 videos, 2020→2024
- **Status:** current
- **Check:** Are most of the program's sets hard sets ending near muscular failure?
- **Sources:** ([The hypertrophy series： defining hard sets, 2020-07](https://youtu.be/RgYzmTnuwro); [The hypertrophy series： volume vs tonnage, 2020-03](https://youtu.be/dpwvdQqKxQI?t=186); [The Most IMPORTANT Methods for Muscle Growth (Hypertrophy Tier-List), 2023-11](https://youtu.be/SxqjF2oPasg?t=440); [New hypertrophy study just dropped (And Basically You're F＊cking Stupid), 2024-01](https://youtu.be/vVQmYGw7Kj8?t=2205))

<a id="INT-41"></a>
### INT-41 · A growth set moves the muscle off its baseline
- **Statement:** A set that produces growth leaves the muscle unable to repeat the same effort within the session; it needs days, not 3-4 minutes, to recover. Too light and the muscle returns to baseline too easily.
- **Numbers:** After one all-out set you still get ~80% of the reps, so keep working until loads become irrelevant (VOL-04).
- **Scope:** All trainees.
- **Confidence:** medium — ~7 videos, 2020→2021
- **Status:** current
- **Sources:** ([The hypertrophy series： strength baseline control for recovery & gains, 2020-05](https://youtu.be/Vbk_2AALm3M); [The hypertrophy series： strength baseline control for recovery & gains, 2020-05](https://youtu.be/Vbk_2AALm3M?t=570); [Hypertrophy Q&A #3, 2020-11](https://youtu.be/6sFaB3rAY1A?t=3077); [The hypertrophy series： determining the optimal workout length, 2021-01](https://youtu.be/UprNxHue9d0?t=250))

<a id="INT-42"></a>
### INT-42 · Repeatability tests show whether a set was hard
- **Statement:** If you can nearly match a set shortly after, it wasn't hard enough.
- **Numbers:** 55 push-ups then 53 two minutes later = not damaging; baseline 30, post-bench 30/29 = no stimulus, 30/20 = stimulus; after 12 to failure you should still get ≥8; a true max double shouldn't repeat after 10-15 min.
- **Scope:** All trainees.
- **Confidence:** high — ~10 videos, 2020→2023
- **Status:** current
- **Sources:** ([Nucleus overload guide (part. 2)： Which body parts, how to target them & impact , 2020-05](https://youtu.be/4rjywMLXt98?t=441); [The hypertrophy series： why using metabolic stress for muscle growth fails, 2021-02](https://youtu.be/gjZ6qGRxS10?t=437); [The hypertrophy series： stimulus to fatigue ratio, 2020-06](https://youtu.be/boPKiKE26Rw?t=127); [How BAD is Hamza's Fitness Advice? (5 BIGGEST Reasons You Can’t Gain Muscle), 2023-01](https://youtu.be/h3U30oRVrMU?t=1074))

<a id="INT-43"></a>
### INT-43 · Load checks for too-light work
- **Statement:** If you still hit the same back-off numbers after the main work, or the bar flies on squats and deadlifts, the weight is too light; if you could do 7 sets instead of 5 with the same reps, add load.
- **Numbers:** Front squat 200x5 fresh and still 200x5 easily after back squats means raise it.
- **Scope:** All trainees.
- **Confidence:** medium — ~3 videos, 2020→2021
- **Status:** current
- **Sources:** ([The hypertrophy series： the optimal number of sets per muscle group, 2020-10](https://youtu.be/82CguFy4piw?t=252); [Hypertrophy Q&A #7, 2021-05](https://youtu.be/D1_tXh-Kp9Y?t=1010); [Hypertrophy Q&A #7, 2021-05](https://youtu.be/D1_tXh-Kp9Y?t=1572))

<a id="INT-44"></a>
### INT-44 · Sandbagging: when it is fine and when it isn't
- **Statement:** Sandbagging is giving less than full effort without a reason. Chosen sandbagging (warm-ups, planned RIR, a muscle trained again in 2 days) is fine; sandbagging forced by the scheme wastes quality tonnage.
- **Numbers:** —
- **Scope:** All trainees; it belongs at the start (strength work) and, involuntarily, at the end of a session, not in the middle.
- **Confidence:** high — ~6 videos, 2020→2021
- **Status:** current
- **Sources:** ([The hypertrophy series： understanding sandbagging to promote qualitative sets, 2020-11](https://youtu.be/S8T3hQgsrko); [The hypertrophy series： understanding sandbagging to promote qualitative sets, 2020-11](https://youtu.be/S8T3hQgsrko?t=100); [The hypertrophy series： understanding sandbagging to promote qualitative sets, 2020-11](https://youtu.be/S8T3hQgsrko?t=371); [Hypertrophy Q&A #7, 2021-05](https://youtu.be/D1_tXh-Kp9Y?t=1448))

<a id="INT-45"></a>
### INT-45 · Fixed multi-set schemes force sandbagging
- **Statement:** 5x5, 5x10, 10x10, 4x10 and fixed 8s or 12s force you to hold back early sets; with real effort reps decline across sets.
- **Numbers:** If set 1 of 5x5 were a true 5RM, set 2 would be 3-4 reps; 10 then 9-8 is real; 3x5 beats 5x5; 3x8 bench invites more sandbagging than 3x4.
- **Scope:** All trainees.
- **Confidence:** high — ~14 videos, 2020→2021
- **Status:** current
- **Sources:** ([The hypertrophy series： understanding sandbagging to promote qualitative sets, 2020-11](https://youtu.be/S8T3hQgsrko?t=80); [The issue with 10x10 / German Volume Training, 2020-11](https://youtu.be/s8mGWwTGLOo?t=790); [The problem with 5x5/3x5, 2020-06](https://youtu.be/k3O630Nz4B8?t=1260); [The Smartest Push Pull Legs Routine by Jeff Nippard review, 2021-06](https://youtu.be/Mq2TaHm_ySI?t=634))

<a id="INT-46"></a>
### INT-46 · Use evolving (declining) rep ranges
- **Statement:** Write ranges so reps trickle down toward failure each set; small brackets mean more intensity and more sandbagging risk, wide ones the reverse.
- **Numbers:** 6-10 should read 10/9/8; 8/7/6/5; at low reps a 2-rep window (6-8, not fixed 8 or a wide 5-8); 6-5-4 matches 5-5-5 tonnage with a more intense first set.
- **Scope:** All trainees.
- **Confidence:** high — ~9 videos, 2020→2021
- **Status:** current
- **Sources:** ([How to start using evolving rep ranges in your training, 2020-09](https://youtu.be/HpEz3fFWEeA?t=568); [Kizen Strength & Aesthetics Powerbuilding program review, 2020-09](https://youtu.be/-banYSTnkq4?t=1050); [Synchronizing evolving rep range with movement patterns, variations & rotations , 2020-12](https://youtu.be/twgzqTg4nug?t=315); [How to use Evolving Rep Ranges for Hypertrophy, 2021-10](https://youtu.be/X8WMlqP6M78?t=425))

<a id="INT-47"></a>
### INT-47 · Too much work forces survival pacing
- **Statement:** Piling exercises or huge volume into a session makes you pace and sandbag the top work, turning lifting into cardio with weights; if you pace sets to survive later exercises, the program is badly built.
- **Numbers:** Four heavy chest compounds in one session is an example; beginners on 15-rep machine work stop pushing by rep 8.
- **Scope:** All trainees.
- **Confidence:** medium — ~10 videos, 2020→2023
- **Status:** current

## Intensity techniques

<a id="INT-55"></a>
### INT-55 · Techniques are the cherry on top
- **Statement:** Drop sets, clusters, tempo, short rests, rest-pause and myo-reps are added to a quality set, never replacing it or hurting the hard sets.
- **Numbers:** Myo-reps programmed as top sets are unacceptable.
- **Scope:** All trainees.
- **Confidence:** high — ~7 videos, 2021→2024
- **Status:** current
- **Sources:** ([Hypertrophy Q&A #7, 2021-05](https://youtu.be/D1_tXh-Kp9Y?t=1198); [The Natty Arnold? (Joel Kellett aka Overkell), 2023-07](https://youtu.be/Mn34v5Y1d-0?t=2450); [Arnold trained like an idiot?, 2024-04](https://youtu.be/-OYtq2AHGX8?t=1769); [New hypertrophy study just dropped (And Basically You're F＊cking Stupid), 2024-01](https://youtu.be/vVQmYGw7Kj8?t=2205))

<a id="INT-56"></a>
### INT-56 · Rest-pause is his preferred technique
- **Statement:** At failure, rest briefly while focusing on the muscle, then add reps; post-pause reps must be the hardest of the set. It works best at higher reps, so it pushes rep ranges up.
- **Numbers:** Rest 10-20 s (range 3-30 s) → +2-5 reps, ~+10-50% hyper-intense volume; after 8 reps and 15 s ~4 more, on a 3-5 set barely one; start with 1-2 rest-pause sets, on the last set.
- **Scope:** Introduce on isolations first, then upper-body compounds, only later lower-body compounds; advanced lifters especially.
- **Confidence:** high — ~16 videos, 2020→2025
- **Status:** changed — 2020-21 skeptical, ranked last ("leaks tonnage", "three sets in disguise"); 2023-25 his favourite technique, preferred over drop sets.
- **Sources:** ([5 Ways to shock the muscle (GONE WRONG), 2020-07](https://youtu.be/RqS8AxVE28I?t=697); [I'm BACK! (Hypertrophy Log #4), 2023-08](https://youtu.be/B5eAFxfON3A?t=1013); [20 inch arms CMON (Hypertrophy Log #9), 2024-12](https://youtu.be/qvWxIzhT1QU?t=696); [New Hypertrophy Gimmick™ just dropped 🤡, 2025-03](https://youtu.be/ACFKXT44BzM?t=1250))

<a id="INT-57"></a>
### INT-57 · Drop sets and forced reps: occasional at most
- **Statement:** Drop sets on every set are pump-chasing junk; use them only to reach target reps once rest-pause fails. Forced reps, forced negatives and beyond-failure work are an extra set in disguise with a poor stimulus-to-fatigue ratio.
- **Numbers:** Drop 5-10 lb on cable triceps extensions after failing at 10 of 15; beyond-failure work max 1 set per muscle per day (C tier); drop sets never on strength or main lifts.
- **Scope:** Accessories; forced negatives once called "amazing" for biceps (2020).
- **Confidence:** high — ~17 videos, 2020→2024
- **Status:** current
- **Sources:** ([5 Ways to shock the muscle (GONE WRONG), 2020-07](https://youtu.be/RqS8AxVE28I?t=505); [The issue with HIT (the intensity meme), 2020-11](https://youtu.be/LqsqSGZooR0?t=960); [The Most IMPORTANT Methods for Muscle Growth (Hypertrophy Tier-List), 2023-11](https://youtu.be/SxqjF2oPasg?t=314); [Arnold trained like an idiot?, 2024-04](https://youtu.be/-OYtq2AHGX8?t=1894))

## Focus and non-bodybuilders

<a id="INT-63"></a>
### INT-63 · Train with focus, save the hype
- **Statement:** No phone, chatting or dates in the gym; think about the next set between sets. Save loud music for top sets so you don't desensitize.

- **Scope:** All trainees; he PRs whenever he trains with his gym buddy.

## Junk volume

Junk volume is his main tool for cutting programs down: work that adds sets without adding relevant tonnage.

<a id="VOL-07"></a>
### VOL-07 · What junk volume is
- **Statement:** Junk volume is work outside a relevant intensity window: unchallenging loads, pump chasing, and sets ended by cardio or pump rather than muscular failure.
- **Numbers:** Typical case: a 30-rep weight stopped at ~20 by pump; BFR or pump drop sets; 25-rep machine sets.
- **Scope:** All trainees.
- **Confidence:** high — ~20 videos, 2020→2024
- **Status:** current
- **Check:** Is the program free of sets that end from burn, pump or breathlessness rather than muscle failure?
- **Sources:** ([The hypertrophy series： nucleus overload vs junk volume, 2020-10](https://youtu.be/T0QddSpwwdc?t=380); [Kizen Strength & Aesthetics Powerbuilding program review, 2020-09](https://youtu.be/-banYSTnkq4?t=1330); [The hypertrophy series： why using metabolic stress for muscle growth fails, 2021-02](https://youtu.be/gjZ6qGRxS10?t=330); [WEIGHTS vs MACHINES： Which one is better for muscle gains?, 2022-01](https://youtu.be/O5xVdqgt8Uo?t=1507))

<a id="VOL-08"></a>
### VOL-08 · Junk is relative and mainly hurts when it replaces hard sets
- **Statement:** Junk volume depends on your muscular endurance and is mainly a problem when it replaces hard sets or takes time from other muscles; calling every set after a top set junk is Mentzer logic.
- **Numbers:** A second set costs about 3-4 minutes.
- **Scope:** All trainees.
- **Confidence:** medium — ~6 videos, 2021→2024
- **Status:** changed — 2021 he called the junk-volume concept "overblown"; 2022-24 he applies the label widely and asks for the "bare effective minimum".
- **Sources:** ([The Hypertrophy Iceberg Explained (a complete guide to muscle growth), 2021-07](https://youtu.be/8ELQ2XZgpls?t=3452); [Pushing progression and avoiding plateaus using evolving rep ranges, 2021-04](https://youtu.be/C86TMVYGu0M?t=554); [Jeff Nippard & Minimalism： Working Hard or Hardly Working?, 2022-10](https://youtu.be/Zv9QAIb5nGk?t=1701); [This Calisthenics Freak Makes Bodybuilders Look Small (Baki_HD), 2024-06](https://youtu.be/2LoP6-KdEx4?t=504))

<a id="VOL-09"></a>
### VOL-09 · Typical junk schemes, including 10x10
- **Statement:** 10x10/GVT, 5x10 and 5x20 schemes, 25 chest sets, 13+ biceps sets in a session, 10x20 cable work and many sets of light laterals are typical junk. 10x10 is a band-aid: if you can repeat 10 reps for 10 sets the load is uninteresting.
- **Numbers:** On 25 chest sets 60-70% of reps do nothing; on a ~300-rep push day 65-75% is junk; true GVT forces ~55-60% 1RM instead of 70-75%; 3 sets in a relevant window may beat it.
- **Scope:** All trainees; 2024: "10x10 is sandbagging".
- **Confidence:** high — ~25 videos, 2020→2024
- **Status:** current
- **Sources:** ([The issue with 10x10 / German Volume Training, 2020-11](https://youtu.be/s8mGWwTGLOo?t=688); [Good chest day vs Bad chest day, 2022-05](https://youtu.be/k9_dDbGLFZQ?t=248); [The BEST Workout if you like to waste time for no results (Ryan Humiston Split/P, 2022-02](https://youtu.be/wLx5BRx8AaU?t=379); [Your lifting program SUCKS! (Hypertrophy Q&A / Program review), 2024-10](https://youtu.be/c7hl9u3h_s0?t=767))

<a id="VOL-10"></a>
### VOL-10 · Most programs are too greedy
- **Statement:** He trims most reviewed programs and says most bodybuilders could cut a fifth to a third of their training for the same results.
- **Numbers:** Typical cut 20-30% (sometimes 40-80%); arm programs of 21-30 sets cut by 80%; a chest+biceps day for naturals could lose 45%.
- **Scope:** All trainees, especially program reviews.
- **Confidence:** high — ~10 videos, 2020→2024
- **Status:** current
- **Sources:** ([5 days Upper Lower program review (part. 1), 2020-10](https://youtu.be/TD9SB9Bt45o?t=1478); [How to modify any training program, 2021-03](https://youtu.be/o05wgvQtSMc?t=191); [Good arm day Vs Bad arm day, 2021-01](https://youtu.be/RSkzA1l5jlk?t=441); [Your lifting program SUCKS! ## How much volume

<a id="VOL-11"></a>
### VOL-11 · Do the least volume that keeps you progressing
- **Statement:** Do as little as needed for as much growth as possible: the minimal sets that keep you progressing and injury-free, leaving room to add later. Volume "only serves the purpose of progression".
- **Numbers:** By 2024 he places himself "closer to HIT than to 18-20 sets" per muscle.
- **Scope:** All trainees.
- **Confidence:** high — ~16 videos, 2020→2025
- **Status:** changed — 2020-22 maximalist ("more work always gives more" if you recover, sit at the brink of overtraining, 2-3 h sessions); from 2021 minimal-effective, and by 2024 low on the volume spectrum.
- **Check:** Is each muscle's weekly volume the lowest that still produces progress?
- **Sources:** ([The hypertrophy series： maximum recoverable volume, 2020-04](https://youtu.be/tZ9CSu2DMIE?t=61); [The hypertrophy series： the optimal number of sets for muscle growth, 2021-02](https://youtu.be/QL9Dh9CGOBQ?t=114); [BACK 2 THE GYM STREAM (Program reviews & Answering training questions), 2024-09](https://youtu.be/okm6bZHKHI4?t=5998); [New Hypertrophy Gimmick™ just dropped 🤡, 2025-03](https://youtu.be/ACFKXT44BzM?t=751))

<a id="VOL-12"></a>
### VOL-12 · Both extremes fail: one set and 10x10
- **Statement:** HIT's single set is too little for naturals and GVT/10x10 too much; naturals grow in the middle. Multiple hard sets compound reps and give room to modulate effort.
- **Numbers:** One set of 17 can't beat 13+10+10+10; 3-4 sets at 240 lb beat 1 at 250; 2024: HIT still beats GVT because it leaves room to add.
- **Scope:** Naturals.
- **Confidence:** high — ~16 videos, 2020→2024
- **Status:** current
- **Sources:** ([Hypertrophy Q&A #2, 2020-10](https://youtu.be/MIHPylz3f7Q?t=290); [Minimalist training bad, 2021-06](https://youtu.be/w4-2c3iWvDQ?t=2085); [1st Natural Hypertrophy stream! ASK YOUR QUESTIONS AND I SHALL ANSWER, 2024-09](https://youtu.be/bRKQIOYo2u4?t=461); [So you think you can lift? (Program Review LIVE), 2024-11](https://youtu.be/6p2x4kDDjzs?t=6511))

<a id="VOL-13"></a>
### VOL-13 · Minimalism is a tool, not an ideology
- **Statement:** Minimal programs fit strength, athletes, beginners and busy people, but tend to build unbalanced physiques for bodybuilders; at an advanced level the maximalist's last ~20% decides things.
- **Numbers:** Cuts hurt maximalists more in absolute tonnage (50,000 → 25,000 vs 10,000 → 5,000).
- **Scope:** Advanced bodybuilders vs everyone else.
- **Confidence:** medium — ~8 videos, 2021→2024
- **Status:** contradicted — in 2024 he calls maximalist whole-body isolation the best, yet places himself closer to HIT and says most could cut 20-30%.
- **Sources:** ([Minimalist training bad, 2021-06](https://youtu.be/w4-2c3iWvDQ?t=2605); [Jeff Nippard & Alec Enkiri Want Me To Deload... - **Statement:** Some respond more to volume and others to intensity; a muscle that won't grow may need more volume, and someone who can't recover needs less volume and more intensity.

<a id="VOL-16"></a>
### VOL-16 · Train between medium and maximum recoverable volume
- **Statement:** Maximum recoverable volume (MRV) is the most work you can recover and grow from; aim between medium and maximum. MRV is individual, found by experiment and only diagnosable after the fact, and it rises with training age.
- **Numbers:** ~25% above minimum without passing the max is fine; most people don't overshoot.
- **Scope:** All trainees.
- **Confidence:** medium — ~12 videos, 2020→2021
- **Status:** current
- **Sources:** ([The hypertrophy series： maximum recoverable volume, 2020-04](https://youtu.be/tZ9CSu2DMIE); [The Recovery Pot Explained (a complete guide to muscle recuperation), 2021-02](https://youtu.be/p-kR3RfGBHw?t=285); [The hypertrophy series： determining the optimal workout length, 2021-01](https://youtu.be/UprNxHue9d0?t=375); [The Hypertrophy Iceberg Explained (a complete guide to muscle growth), 2021-07](https://youtu.be/8ELQ2XZgpls?t=3301))

<a id="VOL-17"></a>
### VOL-17 · Signs of too much volume
- **Statement:** Lingering soreness or failing to repeat performance session to session signals too much volume; at high weekly sets with slow strength gains, try less volume and more intensity.
- **Numbers:** 15-20 weekly sets with slow strength gains → try less.
- **Scope:** All trainees.
- **Confidence:** medium — 1 video, 2022
- **Status:** current
- **Sources:** ([Hypertrophy Q&A #10, 2022-06](https://youtu.be/QfHfxLYRu88?t=1384); [Hypertrophy Q&A #10, 2022-06](https://youtu.be/QfHfxLYRu88?t=1822))

<a id="VOL-18"></a>
### VOL-18 · Manual laborers need less gym volume
- **Statement:** Office workers can aim at their MRV; manual laborers should stay lower with high intensity and low frequency, and athletes must count the volume from their sport.
- **Numbers:** 2 heavy sets of a compound instead of 4-8.
- **Scope:** Physical jobs, athletes.
- **Confidence:** medium — ~3 videos, 2021→2024

## Weekly sets per muscle

<a id="VOL-19"></a>
### VOL-19 · A weekly set count means little on its own
- **Statement:** Arbitrary weekly numbers ignore frequency, rep range and distribution; the optimal count is whatever produces growth, and ±1-2 sets don't matter. Different body parts naturally take different counts.
- **Numbers:** The 10-20 guideline is "mathematically sound but not a hard rule".
- **Scope:** All trainees.
- **Confidence:** high — ~9 videos, 2020→2022
- **Status:** current
- **Sources:** ([Natural Q&A #2, 2020-09](https://youtu.be/Zg0oUngwPK4?t=874); [The hypertrophy series： the optimal number of sets for muscle growth, 2021-02](https://youtu.be/QL9Dh9CGOBQ?t=51); [How often should you train for 𝐁𝐎𝐃𝐘𝐁𝐔𝐈𝐋𝐃𝐈𝐍𝐆 , 2022-07](https://youtu.be/iDua_rNsBO8); [How often should you train for 𝐁𝐎𝐃𝐘𝐁𝐔𝐈𝐋𝐃𝐈𝐍𝐆 , 2022-07](https://youtu.be/iDua_rNsBO8?t=758))

<a id="VOL-20"></a>
### VOL-20 · If you need a number: 8-14 hard sets a week
- **Statement:** As a rough answer, 8-14 weekly sets per muscle; at 3x/week and high intensity, 9-15 hard sets is enough to keep growing.
- **Numbers:** 8-14 (rough math ~7-14: about 4 sessions per 8 days x 2-4 sets, 2022); 9-15 at 3x/wk (2023).
- **Scope:** Intermediate and advanced naturals; back is an exception (VOL-45).
- **Confidence:** medium — ~3 videos, 2022→2023
- **Status:** current
- **Check:** Do most muscles get roughly 8-14 hard sets a week?
- **Sources:** ([How often should you train for 𝐁𝐎𝐃𝐘𝐁𝐔𝐈𝐋𝐃𝐈𝐍𝐆 , 2022-07](https://youtu.be/iDua_rNsBO8?t=506); [How often should you train for 𝐁𝐎𝐃𝐘𝐁𝐔𝐈𝐋𝐃𝐈𝐍𝐆 , 2022-07](https://youtu.be/iDua_rNsBO8?t=632); [ULTIMATE HYPERTROPHY PROGRAMS (Novice to Advanced), 2023-06](https://youtu.be/gpFdh0eBMGc?t=2128))

<a id="VOL-21"></a>
### VOL-21 · Weekly sets by training level
- **Statement:** Novices need few weekly sets and build up; intermediates build toward a cap of about 12.
- **Numbers:** Novice 3-6/wk (3 once or twice a week, never 6 at once); intermediate 6-12, cap 12, +2 at a time; 2020: 3 → 9 → 12 hard sets by level.
- **Scope:** Novice → intermediate; see ch. 12.
- **Confidence:** high — ~4 videos, 2020→2023
- **Status:** current
- **Sources:** ([Hypertrophy Q&A #3, 2020-11](https://youtu.be/6sFaB3rAY1A?t=3013); [Come with me if you want massive arms (Step by Step MASSterplan), 2023-01](https://youtu.be/HXoY7xzHlWU?t=312); [Come with me if you want massive arms (Step by Step MASSterplan), 2023-01](https://youtu.be/HXoY7xzHlWU?t=943))

<a id="VOL-22"></a>
### VOL-22 · Almost no one needs 16-20 weekly sets
- **Statement:** 16-20 weekly sets per muscle is more than almost anyone needs and is impractical to schedule.
- **Numbers:** 20 sets/wk would mean 5 sessions x 4 sets or 2 x 10; most lifters do 12-20, about 10 can work for intermediates; an advanced natural on ~4 hard sets/wk may only maintain.

## Adding and cutting volume

<a id="VOL-29"></a>
### VOL-29 · Add volume only on a stall, two sets at a time
- **Statement:** Add volume only when load, reps and tonnage stall, in small steps; past a point progress should come from intensity rather than more sets.
- **Numbers:** About +2 sets per body part (2-4 max) per adjustment.
- **Scope:** All trainees.
- **Confidence:** high — ~6 videos, 2021→2025
- **Status:** current
- **Check:** Are sets added only after progress stalls, and only about two at a time?

<a id="VOL-30"></a>
### VOL-30 · Never jump volume
- **Statement:** Volume spikes bring no results, sickness or overuse injury, and people then wrongly blame volume.
- **Numbers:** You can't jump from 9 to 16 sets; don't double volume on becoming intermediate.
- **Scope:** All trainees.
- **Confidence:** high — ~7 videos, 2020→2024
- **Status:** current
- **Sources:** ([The hypertrophy series： maintaining tonnage stability for long term progress, 2020-05](https://youtu.be/Z1xF6eFUdBQ?t=63); [How to start doing more volume in your training, 2020-09](https://youtu.be/p6WcFTOBq3s?t=40); [Escape Intermediate Hell (Path to Exceptional Physique), 2023-10](https://youtu.be/16fjHEtZTCA?t=1336); [TIME TO GROW BOYS (Live Q&A / Self-Improvement), 2024-09](https://youtu.be/lyj1BFZ85Dg?t=4866))

<a id="VOL-31"></a>
### VOL-31 · Introducing a new exercise
- **Statement:** Start a new exercise at low volume and build up, trimming other work to make room; or use several sets with very light weight.
- **Numbers:** 1-2 sets (~50% of the main lift's volume), trim others to 2, then +1 set every week or two up to 4; adding 4 sets of a brand-new exercise exhausts you.
- **Scope:** All trainees.
- **Confidence:** medium — ~3 videos, 2020→2023
- **Status:** current
- **Sources:** ([The hypertrophy series： maintaining tonnage stability for long term progress, 2020-05](https://youtu.be/Z1xF6eFUdBQ?t=63); [The hypertrophy series： maintaining tonnage stability for long term progress, 2020-05](https://youtu.be/Z1xF6eFUdBQ?t=128); [How to Keep Growing FOREVER (Unlimited Hypertrophy Method), 2023-07](https://youtu.be/1TKqwXCge9E?t=1706); [Come with me if you want a BIG BACK (4 steps MASSterplan), 2023-09](https://youtu.be/7uBT8vp0lNw?t=882))

<a id="VOL-32"></a>
### VOL-32 · Bringing in a new small muscle
- **Statement:** Start direct work for a newly trained small muscle at 2-3 weekly sets and build.
- **Numbers:** Biceps 3 → 4 → 6; neck 3 → 6 → 9 → 10-12; abs 2-3; small muscles 3 → 6; weak arms 3 sets then 7-8.
- **Scope:** Muscles not trained directly before; see also FRQ-27.
- **Confidence:** high — ~6 videos, 2021→2023
- **Status:** current

<a id="VOL-33"></a>
### VOL-33 · Add conservatively, cut liberally
- **Statement:** Programming is subtraction as well as addition: be conservative when adding and liberal when removing. "If you can shrink a day, always shrink it."
- **Numbers:** If you still progress at 12 sets, drop from 15.
- **Scope:** All trainees.
- **Confidence:** medium — ~5 videos, 2021→2022
- **Status:** current

<a id="VOL-34"></a>
### VOL-34 · Cut sets, not reps; cut strength sets first
- **Statement:** To reduce fatigue, cut sets rather than reps, and cut strength-work sets (to 1-3) before lowering back-off intensity.
- **Numbers:** Strength work is a small share of tonnage, so cutting it barely matters.

- **Statement:** Budget weekly volume: take some from a dominant muscle and spend it on weak points or recovery; dominant parts won't shrink.
- **Numbers:** Take 30-40% from a dominant muscle; cutting 20% of dominant-leg volume "makes no difference" (2024).

## Work capacity

<a id="VOL-38"></a>
### VOL-38 · Work capacity is built gradually
- **Statement:** Work capacity is what lets you do the volume that drives growth; it is built and lost gradually, and more muscle raises it.
- **Numbers:** Building capacity for 2 h of heavy work may take 3-4 years.
- **Scope:** All trainees.
- **Confidence:** high — ~8 videos, 2020→2024
- **Status:** current
- **Sources:** ([The hypertrophy series： surpassing cardiovascular limitations, 2020-05](https://youtu.be/LCpa0h89TJM?t=192); [How to start doing more volume in your training, 2020-09](https://youtu.be/p6WcFTOBq3s?t=374); [Going to WAR over Giant Sets (Response to Bald Omni Man), 2022-09](https://youtu.be/nqzVqvMvQ1s?t=680); [Your lifting program SUCKS! ## Distribution of volume

<a id="VOL-41"></a>
### VOL-41 · Strength work is ~20%, the rest makes you grow
- **Statement:** Strength work opens the session and gives the highest-quality tonnage but is a minority; the variations and accessories that follow provide most of the growth stimulus.
- **Numbers:** ~20% strength vs ~80% variations and accessories; typical 2020 day: 1-3 strength sets + 6-8 back-off/variation/accessory sets.
- **Scope:** All trainees.
- **Confidence:** high — ~12 videos, 2020→2022
- **Status:** current
- **Sources:** ([How I utilize body part splits for maximum muscle hypertrophy (versus upper lowe, 2020-01](https://youtu.be/4FY2Ct22qXU?t=376); [The hypertrophy series： programming strength work to bolster tonnage quality & p, 2020-11](https://youtu.be/A-asa7QMiG0?t=520); [How to structure a Gentleman split (volume & intensity), 2020-12](https://youtu.be/ehxjCB_MdKc?t=1068); [Going to WAR over Giant Sets (Response to Bald Omni Man), 2022-09](https://youtu.be/nqzVqvMvQ1s?t=438))

<a id="VOL-42"></a>
### VOL-42 · Most tonnage at moderate reps; offset heavy and volume work
- **Statement:** The bulk of tonnage sits at 4-12 reps, and "volume work" means above 6 reps. When the strength set is heaviest, the following volume work should be lightest, offsetting tonnage swings with variations.
- **Numbers:** 4x6-10 or 4x8-12 beats 4x5; evolving sets swing tonnage hugely (1x4 vs 8-6-4).
- **Scope:** All trainees.
- **Confidence:** medium — ~10 videos, 2020→2021
- **Status:** current
- **Sources:** ([Synchronizing evolving rep range with movement patterns, variations & rotations , 2020-11](https://youtu.be/mbtAKsbDz9I?t=90); [Synchronizing evolving rep range with movement patterns, variations & rotations , 2020-11](https://youtu.be/mbtAKsbDz9I?t=600); [The hypertrophy series： developing the values of size and strength, 2020-10](https://youtu.be/k8k1PycHKDI?t=100); [How to progress forward with evolving rep ranges, 2020-09](https://youtu.be/65rLZe9cz_0?t=440))

<a id="VOL-43"></a>
### VOL-43 · Count indirect volume
- **Statement:** Compounds spread tonnage across several muscles, so count it: bench is triceps and front-delt volume, and a 300 lb squat isn't 300 lb of quad tonnage. Shared structures such as the lower back cap how much you can send through them.
- **Numbers:** Send part of back volume through legless moves (~300/700 of 1000 lb).
- **Scope:** All trainees.
- **Confidence:** medium — ~8 videos, 2020→2024
- **Status:** current
- **Sources:** ([The hypertrophy series： diffuse vs targeted tonnage, 2020-07](https://youtu.be/x3YHLNqftr4?t=63); [𝙃𝙊𝙍𝙍𝙄𝙁𝙄𝘾 𝙡𝙞𝙛𝙩𝙞𝙣𝙜 𝙞𝙣𝙟𝙪, 2022-08](https://youtu.be/yoROLGGUPXU?t=627); [Level up your back, 2022-02](https://youtu.be/dVssxcEh1UQ?t=1628); [Why you shouldn't listen to Genetic Freaks (The Joel Williams Example), 2024-02](https://youtu.be/GyK1Y6WTR-g?t=887))

<a id="VOL-44"></a>
### VOL-44 · Isolation vs compound share
- **Statement:** He has given both an isolation-heavy and a compound-heavy ratio.
- **Numbers:** About 2:1 isolation:compound per muscle (2023); compounds should be the program's bulk (2024).
- **Scope:** Program design.
- **Confidence:** low — ~2 videos, 2023→2024
- **Status:** contradicted — 2023 isolation 2:1 vs 2024 compounds as the bulk.

## Body-part volume

Per-muscle detail lives in ch. 6; these are the volume rules he states in general terms.

<a id="VOL-45"></a>
### VOL-45 · Upper back is a volume black hole
- **Statement:** The upper back takes huge volume and recovers fast, so it gets the most sets, as long as the lower back isn't taxed; most people undertrain it.
- **Numbers:** Weekly caps rise by stage: 12 → 20 → 12-24 → 14-28 (covers 99.9% of lifters); arms would not tolerate 20. Naturals start with 1-2 pulls per session (one vertical, one horizontal) at ~4 sets each.
- **Scope:** All trainees.
- **Confidence:** high — ~13 videos, 2020→2023
- **Status:** current
- **Sources:** ([Upper Body dominant 4 Days split review, 2020-06](https://youtu.be/PYmr91aELnE?t=1287); [Does Mr. Olympia know how to train BACK? <a id="VOL-46"></a>
### VOL-46 · Legs respond to minimal, hard volume
- **Statement:** Legs grow from intensity and progression, not "a million sets": one quad movement plus one hinge or knee-flexion movement at about 3 hard sets each.
- **Numbers:** 2022: 6-7 heavy knee-flexion sets/wk; 2023: ~9 quad + 8 posterior hard sets/wk is enough, 18-24 total at 3x/wk is plenty; 2024: 6 quad + 6 posterior sets/wk for himself.
- **Scope:** Naturals.
- **Confidence:** high — ~10 videos, 2020→2024
- **Status:** changed — 2020 at least 11-12 heavy squat sets per squat day plus giant-set finishers; 2022-24 minimal hard sets.
- **Sources:** ([My sets/frequency for Natural Hypertrophy, 2020-01](https://youtu.be/m_IGaiqrCvA?t=191); [Hypertrophy Q&A #9, 2022-01](https://youtu.be/9y2s6kyFkPc?t=189); [The PERFECT Hybrid Calisthenics Program (Feat Bald Omni Man), 2023-01](https://youtu.be/_P0-kYyVMn4?t=1384); [So you think you can lift? (Program Review LIVE), 2024-11](https://youtu.be/6p2x4kDDjzs?t=1680))

<a id="VOL-47"></a>
### VOL-47 · Chest grows on modest volume, but presses need enough
- **Statement:** Chest grows on modest weekly volume and about three exercises is the session limit; still, very low pressing volume (3x5 bench) is too little.
- **Numbers:** ~6-8 sets/wk; he does 8-12/wk (2023) then 6/wk (2024); four horizontal presses in a session exceed most people's weekly need; 3x5 bench (15 reps) too little, ≥60 working bench reps wanted (2020).
- **Scope:** All trainees; add push-ups or dips, which are easier to recover from.
- **Confidence:** high — ~14 videos, 2020→2024
- **Status:** current

<a id="VOL-48"></a>
### VOL-48 · Vertical presses and shoulders tolerate more
- **Statement:** Vertical pressing tolerates up to double the horizontal press sets; shoulders get 1-2 isolations plus 1-2 vertical presses per day, and more after a press plus one isolation is junk.

<a id="VOL-49"></a>

- **Statement:** Treat arms as main lifts with 2-4 hard sets per muscle per session; bro-style 20 sets/wk per arm muscle is junk. If ~12 weekly arm sets don't grow arms, check progression first, then change exercises or even lower volume.

- **Statement:** Small muscles take fewer sets per session but recover quickly; feed them through varied angles, frequency and supersets.
- **Numbers:** See the small-muscle reference table at the end of this part.

## Set structures

<a id="VOL-51"></a>
### VOL-51 · Back-off sets: two or three after the work sets
- **Statement:** After 1-3 strength sets, usually 2-3 back-off sets of the same pattern with a modest drop. After a 3x3, a heavy 3x8-12 back-off on the same lift is too much, so use a variation.
- **Numbers:** 2-3 (sometimes 3-4) back-offs, never 10; after 275 lb work sets go to ~245, not 185 (2024).
- **Scope:** Compounds.
- **Confidence:** medium — ~12 videos, 2020→2024
- **Status:** changed — 2020 back-offs are "a must… free tonnage"; 2023 B tier, better as a variation; 2024 he skips them on dips and non-priority squats.
- **Sources:** ([The hypertrophy series： utilizing back-off sets to accumulate quality tonnage, 2020-10](https://youtu.be/Rz4uzjM068M?t=942); [Hypertrophy Q&A #8, 2021-09](https://youtu.be/P89o8FBSWDI?t=838); [The Most IMPORTANT Methods for Muscle Growth (Hypertrophy Tier-List), 2023-11](https://youtu.be/SxqjF2oPasg?t=1761); [The WORST Bodybuilding Program Ever Created (my bad), 2024-04](https://youtu.be/Ft039H8jzXU?t=439))

<a id="VOL-52"></a>
### VOL-52 · Evolving sets: keep the span narrow
- **Statement:** When the number of sets evolves, keep the span to 2-4 sets; it is an advanced tool because swinging sets changes volume far more than swinging reps.
- **Numbers:** 2-4 sets (2-5 or 2-6 max, never 1-8); 3-6 bench sets "is already a big range".
- **Scope:** Advanced lifters.
- **Confidence:** medium — ~4 videos, 2020→2024
- **Status:** current
- **Sources:** ([How to progress forward with evolving rep ranges, 2020-09](https://youtu.be/65rLZe9cz_0?t=565); [How to Keep Growing FOREVER (Unlimited Hypertrophy Method), 2023-07](https://youtu.be/1TKqwXCge9E?t=828); [How often should you train for 𝐁𝐎𝐃𝐘𝐁𝐔𝐈𝐋𝐃𝐈𝐍𝐆 , 2022-07](https://youtu.be/iDua_rNsBO8?t=1444); [BACK 2 THE GYM STREAM (Program reviews & Answering training questions), 2024-09](https://youtu.be/okm6bZHKHI4?t=12516))

<a id="VOL-53"></a>
### VOL-53 · Match total reps when changing schemes
- **Statement:** When swapping set/rep schemes keep total reps similar, or know why you are changing volume.
- **Numbers:** 5x5 = 25 ≈ 3x8; 4x4 = 16 ≈ 3x5; replace 5x5 with 5x3-6 or 4x4-7.
- **Scope:** All trainees.
- **Confidence:** medium — ~3 videos, 2020→2021
- **Status:** current
- **Sources:** ([How to modify any training program, 2021-03](https://youtu.be/o05wgvQtSMc?t=254); [Icecream Fitness Program review, 2020-06](https://youtu.be/5Wz0xTfWOOs?t=563); [The problem with 5x5/3x5, 2020-06](https://youtu.be/k3O630Nz4B8?t=1384))

<a id="VOL-54"></a>
### VOL-54 · Finishers and pyramids drift into junk
- **Statement:** Pyramids and drop-set finishers drift toward junk; weight progression builds quality tonnage. A finisher only makes sense after real work has used up the muscle.
- **Numbers:** Max 2-3 finishers per session (2021); drop sets C tier, finishers D tier (2023).
- **Scope:** All trainees.
- **Confidence:** medium — ~6 videos, 2021→2023
- **Status:** changed — 2021 finishers are fine and build work capacity; 2023 "textbook junk volume" or active recovery at best.
- **Sources:** ([Hypertrophy Q&A #8, 2021-09](https://youtu.be/P89o8FBSWDI?t=99); [The Hypertrophy Iceberg Explained (a complete guide to muscle growth), 2021-07](https://youtu.be/8ELQ2XZgpls?t=1891); [The hypertrophy series： the most reliable way to progressively overload, 2021-03](https://youtu.be/Em00Z8i8V7c?t=64); [The Most IMPORTANT Methods for Muscle Growth (Hypertrophy Tier-List), 2023-11](https://youtu.be/SxqjF2oPasg?t=1889))

<a id="VOL-55"></a>
### VOL-55 · Nucleus overload: a light complement, later rated minor
- **Statement:** Nucleus overload (NO) is frequent, high-volume, very light work kept easy enough to repeat, used to complement strength work for the same muscle, never to replace it. It is the one exception to intensity windows.
- **Numbers:** ~15-30% intensity, 4-25 reps (he corrected an earlier 40-60), ≥5 reps left; months (4-5) to show; spread through other days as supersets, never on the day the muscle gets hard sets; traps NO 2-4x/wk.
- **Scope:** Lats, shoulders, abs, forearms, traps.
- **Confidence:** medium — ~20 videos, 2020→2023
- **Status:** changed — 2020-22 an advocated accessory method for most body parts; 2023 D tier, ~1-2% of results. Also contradicted on whether NO reaches failure.
- **Sources:** ([Nucleus overload guide (part. 1)： What it is & how to implement it, 2020-05](https://youtu.be/T74sR7AIOZc?t=568); [Nucleus overload guide (part. 4)： Reps, sets and frequency schemes, 2020-10](https://youtu.be/ZXFj-taKBis?t=316); [☣️ Biohacking Muscle Growth with Nucleus Overload 💪, 2022-03](https://youtu.be/LNggSj0WBd8?t=502); [The Most IMPORTANT Methods for Muscle Growth (Hypertrophy Tier-List), 2023-11](https://youtu.be/SxqjF2oPasg?t=2959))

## Session length

<a id="VOL-56"></a>
### VOL-56 · Train until the day's stimulus is done, then leave
- **Statement:** There is no fixed time cap: train as long as the day's stimulus takes, don't drag sessions into junk, and cram the necessary work into the least time.
- **Numbers:** 2021: 1h15 target, 10 saved minutes ≈ 2 extra quality sets; a 25-35 min session is fine if you progress; 2024: 45-60 min of hard sets exhausts most people.
- **Scope:** All trainees.
- **Confidence:** high — ~14 videos, 2020→2024
- **Status:** changed — 2020 advanced lifters must lengthen sessions and naturals "cannot just train an hour a day"; 2021 as short as possible; 2024 don't train to a clock.
- **Sources:** ([Hypertrophy Q&A #3, 2020-11](https://youtu.be/6sFaB3rAY1A?t=2823); [The hypertrophy series： determining the optimal workout length, 2021-01](https://youtu.be/UprNxHue9d0); [The hypertrophy series： determining optimal training durations, 2020-06](https://youtu.be/7e0gcEEa-ms?t=188); [Don't be THAT GUY in 2024, 2024-01](https://youtu.be/uOAia_t5c_I?t=1067))

<a id="VOL-57"></a>
### VOL-57 · Normal sessions run 60-90 minutes
- **Statement:** About 60-90 min is a normal session and 90 min is "pushing it"; if you're done after 60 min of a planned 90, cut the day. Saying training past 1.5 h is pointless is a myth.
- **Numbers:** A program that takes 2 h on paper takes ~30 min more in the gym; giant sets compress sessions to 60-70 min; novices: 3 x 1 h beats 2 x 2 h; ~80% of results come from the first 60-70% of a program (2022).
- **Scope:** All trainees.
- **Confidence:** medium — ~7 videos, 2020→2024
- **Status:** current
- **Sources:** ([Icecream Fitness Program review, 2020-06](https://youtu.be/5Wz0xTfWOOs?t=188); [The hypertrophy series： modulating session timeframe to control volume/intensity, 2020-08](https://youtu.be/QAgxfDd4kWY?t=440); [Jeff Nippard & Minimalism： Working Hard or Hardly Working?, 2022-10](https://youtu.be/Zv9QAIb5nGk?t=251); [Better than 90% of bodybuilding routines： 4 HORSEMEN by Brian Alsruhe, 2021-10](https://youtu.be/OWbmOI3cuNs?t=251))

- **Scope:** Him (descriptive).
- **Confidence:** medium — ~6 videos, 2020→2024
- **Status:** changed — longer sessions in 2020, fewer sets by 2024.

## Frequency as a variable

Frequency is how he fits volume in: the same weekly sets work better spread over several sessions.

<a id="FRQ-01"></a>
### FRQ-01 · Frequency is the pillar naturals ignore most
- **Statement:** Frequency is one of the three pillars with volume and intensity and the most ignored, so for naturals it matters most; when sets happen comes before how many.
- **Numbers:** Frequency rated S tier (2023).
- **Scope:** Naturals; a coach who says "do 12 sets whenever" doesn't understand programming.
- **Confidence:** high — ~9 videos, 2020→2023
- **Status:** current
- **Sources:** ([The hypertrophy series： modifying sessions frequency to control volume/intensity, 2020-09](https://youtu.be/sfUkrygYNiU); [The hypertrophy series： the inevitability of frequency control for optimal progr, 2021-01](https://youtu.be/0YrBT05ZwYM?t=190); [How often should you train for 𝐁𝐎𝐃𝐘𝐁𝐔𝐈𝐋𝐃𝐈𝐍𝐆 , 2022-07](https://youtu.be/iDua_rNsBO8?t=63); [The Most IMPORTANT Methods for Muscle Growth (Hypertrophy Tier-List), 2023-11](https://youtu.be/SxqjF2oPasg?t=1637))

<a id="FRQ-02"></a>
### FRQ-02 · Spread weekly sets over several sessions
- **Statement:** The same weekly sets give better results spread out: lumping them forces lighter loads and adds cardio limits and junk, while spreading allows heavier loads, more tonnage and better recovery. Frequency exists to fit volume in.
- **Numbers:** 3x3 sets beat 9 in one session; 5+5+5 beats 15 on Monday; 4 back sets 3x/wk beat 10 once; 12 back sets in one day after deadlifts is wasted; 15 sets in one day might need ~100 h of recovery.
- **Scope:** All trainees beyond novice; front-loading early in the week is fine unless it turns into junk.
- **Confidence:** high — ~14 videos, 2020→2024
- **Status:** current
- **Sources:** ([The hypertrophy series： the optimal number of sets for muscle growth, 2021-02](https://youtu.be/QL9Dh9CGOBQ?t=70); [How often should you train for 𝐁𝐎𝐃𝐘𝐁𝐔𝐈𝐋𝐃𝐈𝐍𝐆 , 2022-07](https://youtu.be/iDua_rNsBO8?t=253); [Level up your back, 2022-02](https://youtu.be/dVssxcEh1UQ?t=947); [So you think you can lift? (Program Review LIVE), 2024-11](https://youtu.be/6p2x4kDDjzs?t=6449))

<a id="FRQ-03"></a>
### FRQ-03 · Once a week is suboptimal unless you are coasting
- **Statement:** Training a muscle once a week is always suboptimal for a natural unless you are deliberately coasting on it; it leaves the muscle idle most of the week and brings soreness and poor work capacity.
- **Numbers:** Once-a-week all-out = 4 sessions a month, and a lifter training 4x/week beats you on tonnage.
- **Scope:** Naturals. Exceptions he admits: a friend's legs growing on 1x/week (2023) and legs 1x/week while fixing an upper-body weakness (2024).
- **Confidence:** high — ~11 videos, 2020→2024
- **Status:** current
- **Check:** Is every muscle you want to grow trained at least twice a week?
- **Sources:** ([The issue with HIT (the intensity meme), 2020-11](https://youtu.be/LqsqSGZooR0?t=1340); [The hypertrophy series： the inevitability of frequency control for optimal progr, 2021-01](https://youtu.be/0YrBT05ZwYM?t=190); [Minimalist training bad, 2021-06](https://youtu.be/w4-2c3iWvDQ?t=2129); [How I Built Monster Legs, 2024-12](https://youtu.be/-OjJEzZTXtQ?t=883))

<a id="FRQ-04"></a>
### FRQ-04 · Frequency is a recovery schedule
- **Statement:** There is no universally optimal frequency, only one that matches the work done to its recovery time; retrain a muscle once it is ready, because leaving it dormant leads to stagnation.
- **Numbers:** No hard 72 h rule; 24 or 48 h works if volume and intensity are managed.
- **Scope:** All trainees; paper math fails because recovery fluctuates.
- **Confidence:** medium — ~6 videos, 2021→2023
- **Status:** current
- **Sources:** ([The Best/Worst of Reddit Fitness - The Ten Commandments of Lifting, 2021-10](https://youtu.be/THV7B11oalk?t=447); [How to Get Bigger by Doing Less (The 85% Rule), 2022-12](https://youtu.be/z2uzpl_smSg?t=1893); [Why I never deload (and why you shouldn't either), 2022-02](https://youtu.be/BJXFeQWGUuY?t=1265); [Why spamming lateral raises won't work, 2023-12](https://youtu.be/yRRXCYcgzJs?t=317))

- **Statement:** Pick frequency first; templates mostly dictate frequency and grouping, and per-session numbers must scale to the number of days.
- **Numbers:** A rep range that works on a 6-day PPL fails on a 3-day one.
- **Scope:** Program design.
- **Confidence:** medium — ~5 videos, 2020→2023

### FRQ-06 · Higher frequency, less per session
- **Statement:** The more often you train a muscle, the less volume (and the shorter the session) each time; low frequency needs high volume and intensity per session.
