### FRQ-07 · Take only part of the recovery "pot" each session
- **Statement:** Recovery is a fixed-size tub: fill it with quality tonnage as often as possible, taking only part of it per session; training once a week doesn't make the tub bigger.
- **Numbers:** Take ~30-40% per session; if legs recover in 2 days, train them again after 2 days.

- **Statement:** Technique and strength depend on frequency: every movement pattern should return at least once a week, and compounds should be practised 2-3x a week. Once a lift is automatic, heavy-work frequency can drop.

## Spacing between sessions for the same muscle

<a id="FRQ-14"></a>
### FRQ-14 · At least ~48 hours between hard sessions for a muscle
- **Statement:** ~48 h is the default and minimum between hard sessions for the same muscle; don't hit a muscle hard two days in a row.
- **Numbers:** 48 h ("a bare minimum", 2024); benching two days in a row is bad even with different variations.
- **Scope:** All trainees; light hits are treated separately (FRQ-15).
- **Confidence:** high — ~8 videos, 2020→2024
- **Status:** contradicted — he also calls two days in a row and 90/80/70% Mon-Wed valid (2020, 2022); likely hard vs light hits, not always stated.
- **Check:** Are hard sessions for the same muscle at least 48 h apart?

## Frequency by muscle and lift

<a id="FRQ-19"></a>
### FRQ-19 · Legs about every 48 hours, later twice a week
- **Statement:** Legs grow from volume spread out, not a weekly crushing day: a heavy knee flexion or hip hinge about every 2 days, with two leg days a week as the minimum beyond novices.
- **Numbers:** ~3x/wk with 3-4 sets for quads or hamstrings per session (2024-05); 2x/wk with 72-96 h between sessions (2024-12), because 3x becomes unrecoverable at ~400s squat / ~500s RDL.
- **Scope:** Naturals beyond novice; the lower back is usually what stops people training legs that often.
- **Confidence:** high — ~20 videos, 2020→2024
- **Status:** changed — 2020-2024-05 every 48 h / 3x a week; 2024-12 2x a week for strong advanced lifters.
- **Check:** Are legs trained at least twice a week?
- **Sources:** ([How I utilize body part splits for maximum muscle hypertrophy (versus upper lowe, 2020-01](https://youtu.be/4FY2Ct22qXU?t=503); [This is Peak Bulk (Hypertrophy Log #6), 2024-05](https://youtu.be/l6L6HlGM4F0?t=189); [How the King of Zoomers Trains to Look like a Greek God (Alex Eubank Program Rev, 2022-12](https://youtu.be/0pKnDucWcDc?t=1127); [How I Built Monster Legs, 2024-12](https://youtu.be/-OjJEzZTXtQ?t=945))

<a id="FRQ-20"></a>
### FRQ-20 · Upper body about three times a week
- **Statement:** Upper-body muscles are numerous, less taxing and recover fast, so train them about every 2 days; chest does better 2-3x a week with fewer, more precise sets than on one chest day.
- **Numbers:** Upper ~3x/wk; chest 2-3x/wk with 2-3 sets per session; 2024: forearms 3-4x, biceps and chest 2-3x weekly.
- **Scope:** All trainees.
- **Confidence:** high — ~7 videos, 2020→2024
- **Status:** current
- **Sources:** ([Free novice program for hypertrophy, 2020-02](https://youtu.be/_4wWgin1dVY?t=317); [Response to Husaka - CHEST - Bench vs Ring Push Ups, 2020-03](https://youtu.be/K4UBm1dV6WM?t=755); [Good chest day vs Bad chest day, 2022-05](https://youtu.be/k9_dDbGLFZQ?t=685); [How I Built Monster Legs, 2024-12](https://youtu.be/-OjJEzZTXtQ?t=1009))

<a id="FRQ-21"></a>
### FRQ-21 · Horizontal press at least twice, bench under three times
- **Statement:** Bench once a week doesn't progress the bench, but raw bench 3+ times a week brings shoulder overuse; press horizontally at least twice and use push-ups, flies or close-grip for extra frequency.
- **Numbers:** ≥2x/wk horizontal pressing; bench <3x/wk; 3x/wk as in novice programs is too much; at 5x/wk use shoulder-sparing variations.
- **Scope:** All trainees.
- **Confidence:** high — ~10 videos, 2020→2022
- **Status:** current
- **Sources:** ([FREE 4/5 days Gentleman split (part. 1), 2020-10](https://youtu.be/cGzlMRCxvxo?t=1403); [Tips to combat shoulder pain, 2020-02](https://youtu.be/IahVc0kbGOU?t=189); [𝙃𝙊𝙍𝙍𝙄𝙁𝙄𝘾 𝙡𝙞𝙛𝙩𝙞𝙣𝙜 𝙞𝙣𝙟𝙪, 2022-08](https://youtu.be/yoROLGGUPXU?t=580); [𝙃𝙊𝙍𝙍𝙄𝙁𝙄𝘾 𝙡𝙞𝙛𝙩𝙞𝙣𝙜 𝙞𝙣𝙟𝙪, 2022-08](https://youtu.be/yoROLGGUPXU?t=605))

### FRQ-22 · Vertical pressing about twice a week
- **Statement:** Vertical pressing ~2x a week is needed for big shoulders; 3x OHP is overcorrection and once a week at 5x5 is too little. Do both a vertical and a horizontal press on each press day.
- **Numbers:** 2x/wk; 2023: the vertical pattern 2-3x/wk, not the same lift.
- **Scope:** Lifters wanting big shoulders.
- **Confidence:** medium — ~6 videos, 2020→2023
- **Status:** current

### FRQ-23 · Squat twice a week long term
- **Statement:** Once a week is not enough, 2x a week is the long-term sweet spot and 3x is hard to sustain; daily squatting works but builds strength more than size.
- **Numbers:** 2x/wk; novices 1-2x; heavy squats 4x/wk was more than he could handle.
- **Scope:** All trainees.
- **Confidence:** medium — ~9 videos, 2020→2022
- **Status:** current

<a id="FRQ-24"></a>
### FRQ-24 · Deadlift rarely, the hinge pattern more often
- **Statement:** The conventional deadlift needs the least frequency of the big lifts (low frequency, high intensity, moderate volume), while the hinge pattern can return every 2-3 days with variations.
- **Numbers:** Deadlift every 7-10 days, 1x4-6 is excellent; 2024: max 1-2x/wk after 2+ years of pushing it. Hinge pattern every 2-3 days; he hinged heavy every 2 days (2022).
- **Scope:** All trainees; he claims pulling heavy several times a week "just means you're still weak".
- **Confidence:** high — ~14 videos, 2020→2024
- **Status:** contradicted — 2020 "only a few times a month" alongside heavy deadlifts 2x/week, and heavy hinging every 2 days in 2022; partly deadlift vs hinge variations.

### FRQ-25 · Upper back: most frequency-tolerant, spread over days
- **Statement:** The upper back tolerates training nearly every day with varied angles and intensities; train back at least 3x a week, add back movements to the split "as Lego blocks", and never put all back volume on one day.
- **Numbers:** ≥3x/wk; per session ≤3 exercises / ~10 sets; e.g. 6 back exercises as 2/2/2 over Mon/Wed/Sat; ~6 sets per day instead of 30 once; no horizontal pull on consecutive days.

- **Confidence:** high — ~16 videos, 2020→2024

- **Statement:** Pull-ups are low-impact and the upper back recovers fast, so they can be done daily, even to failure; grease-the-groove works for them as an exception.

- **Statement:** For a neglected or small muscle, raise frequency (1x → 2x → 3x a week) before adding sets per session.

- **Statement:** Arm intensity is fixed at failure and per-session volume is limited, so arm growth comes from frequency; put biceps work on every upper day, and isolations need more frequency than the compounds they accompany.

## Days per week

<a id="FRQ-30"></a>
### FRQ-30 · Four days a week is the sustainable sweet spot
- **Statement:** 4 training days a week is his favourite and sustainable for life; 3 is fine, and intermediates need at least 3.
- **Numbers:** 4 ideal (4-5 range, 2020); 3 or 6 days are "sub-extreme" (2021); 3 days "perfectly fine" (2024).
- **Scope:** Most lifters.
- **Confidence:** high — ~5 videos, 2020→2024
- **Status:** current

<a id="FRQ-31"></a>
### FRQ-31 · Advanced means more sessions
- **Statement:** Advancing means more sessions per year, not just more sets.
- **Numbers:** Intermediate 3 sessions/wk (12/month, 140-150/yr); advanced every other day (~4/wk, 15/month, ~180/yr), about 30 extra sessions a year.
- **Scope:** Intermediate → advanced; a regular extra rest day puts you back on the intermediate program.

- **Statement:** Start with 3-4 days and expand; add a day by spreading existing tonnage, not by piling on more, and never jump from 3 to 6 days at the same per-day volume.

- **Statement:** If sessions run too long, add a day; if days are thin or redundant, compress them.

## Split templates

<a id="FRQ-37"></a>
### FRQ-37 · The bro split is the worst template for naturals
- **Statement:** One muscle per day once a week gives too little frequency and too much per-session volume, which fills sessions with junk; the fix is to hit each muscle twice a week.
- **Numbers:** 2024 example: six back exercises for 25 sets, where 20% of the work gives ~95% of the gains.
- **Scope:** Naturals. In his opinion enhanced lifters can recover from it, and would still grow more with more frequency.
- **Confidence:** high — ~15 videos, 2020→2024
- **Status:** current
- **Check:** Does the split avoid giving any muscle a single big session per week?
- **Sources:** ([Body parts split： bro split vs Gentleman Split, 2020-09](https://youtu.be/A4KNy_uMCRM?t=86); [Analyzing the Rock's ＂Black Adam＂ training program, 2021-03](https://youtu.be/BnzVYV9_IQc?t=378); [Does Mr. Olympia know how to train BACK? <a id="FRQ-38"></a>
### FRQ-38 · The gentleman split is his favourite
- **Statement:** His preferred template is an upper/lower skeleton whose days are built around synergistic muscle groups and a main compound, with flexible boundaries.

- **Scope:** Intermediate and advanced bodybuilders.
- **Confidence:** high — ~12 videos, 2020→2023
- **Status:** changed — terminology: in 2020 he praised a well-built "body-part split" as the best natural template; from 2021 that label means one-muscle-per-day splits and he condemns it, while the same idea lives on as the gentleman split.

<a id="FRQ-69"></a>

- **Statement:** Open with the most demanding, most important lift (heavy low-rep strength work while fresh), then lighter compounds, then isolation; if time runs short, cut from the bottom, never the top.
- **Numbers:** Cutting the bottom loses only ~10-20% of gains.
- **Scope:** All trainees; exception: a priority muscle can go first.
- **Confidence:** high — ~16 videos, 2020→2023
- **Status:** current

<a id="FRQ-73"></a>
### FRQ-73 · Upper days long, lower days short
- **Statement:** Lower lifts hit more muscle and move more tonnage per set, so lower days carry fewer exercises; upper days have many small muscles that need isolation and should look about twice as long on paper.
- **Numbers:** Lower 3-5 movements (≤2 giant-set lines), upper 6-8 up to 10 (lower ≈ 60-70% of upper); 2022: 4-6 exercises per day with ≥4 low-fatigue isolations; in PPL legs are the shortest, most intense day.
- **Scope:** All trainees.
- **Confidence:** high — ~16 videos, 2020→2024

## Frequency for special populations

<a id="FRQ-79"></a>
### FRQ-79 · Fighters and athletes: lifting is secondary
- **Statement:** For fighters, lifting is minimal and scheduled away from the sport; an upper-dominant split suits them because lower lifts tax the CNS and tendons more.
- **Numbers:** Purists 2 sessions/wk (~1.5 h each); hybrids 3-4x/wk with rotated variations; time split ~70% sport / 20% drills / 10% hypertrophy (advanced 60/20/20); upper-dominant e.g. 4 upper, 2 lower.
- **Scope:** Combat athletes and other athletes.
- **Confidence:** medium — ~5 videos, 2021→2022
- **Status:** current
- **Sources:** ([Lifting plans for Athletes (programming for sports), 2021-09](https://youtu.be/cNGPCn9Uupc); [Lifting plans for Athletes (programming for sports), 2021-09](https://youtu.be/cNGPCn9Uupc?t=1004); [Bodybuilders can't FIGHT (but martial artists should lift), 2022-01](https://youtu.be/v-F3QHSM2hg?t=876); [FREE Lifting Plans for Fighters (Martial Arts Weight Training Programs), 2022-01](https://youtu.be/3JNwlqx3Z6w?t=969))

## Rest between sets

Rest only as long as the next set needs; heavy strength work gets full rest as straight sets, and nearly everything else is supersetted.

<a id="RST-01"></a>
### RST-01 · Rest about 2-3 minutes, never more than 5
- **Statement:** Rest as little as possible while staying performant; more than 5 min is overkill. He doesn't time rests and goes roughly by feel.
- **Numbers:** 2020: 3-5 min strength, 1-2 min straight-set accessories, 3-4 min between heavy low-rep evolving sets; 2021: 2-3 min for strength, 1.5-3 up to 5; 2023: "2 or 3 is fine as long as you recover"; 2024: ~3 min by feel or a song.
- **Scope:** All trainees; heavy Bulgarian split squats: he sits 3 min.
- **Confidence:** high — ~8 videos, 2020→2024
- **Status:** changed — mild drift from 3-5 min for strength sets (2020) to 2-3 min by feel (2021-24).
- **Check:** Do straight sets get roughly 2-3 minutes of rest (not under ~90 s, not over ~5 min)?
- **Sources:** ([AlphaDestiny Novice Program review (part. 2： FAQ), 2020-04](https://youtu.be/T_DyRlu3Y7I); [Icecream Fitness FAQ review, 2020-06](https://youtu.be/MCUpClPnPkQ?t=1126); [Hypertrophy Q&A #6, 2021-03](https://youtu.be/pvpf7Yuayco?t=356); [The Most IMPORTANT Methods for Muscle Growth (Hypertrophy Tier-List), 2023-11](https://youtu.be/SxqjF2oPasg?t=3276))

<a id="RST-02"></a>
### RST-02 · Rest so the muscle returns to baseline
- **Statement:** The aim of rest is for the muscle to be back to baseline for the next set; too-short rests wreck performance and turn training into cardio.
- **Numbers:** 20 s between curl sets gives a third of the reps; 15 s with a challenging weight isn't enough; 60-90 s improves conditioning but hurts performance; 100 reps is like 10x10 with no rest.
- **Scope:** All trainees; rest-pause is the deliberate exception (INT-56).
- **Confidence:** high — ~5 videos, 2020→2024
- **Status:** current
- **Sources:** ([Transcendent training review (from an hypertrophy standpoint), 2020-02](https://youtu.be/uTHCzF7Exck?t=448); [Hypertrophy Q&A #6, 2021-03](https://youtu.be/pvpf7Yuayco?t=400); [Hypertrophy Q&A #10, 2022-06](https://youtu.be/QfHfxLYRu88?t=3141); [Another 𝐻𝒪𝑅𝑅𝐼𝐵𝐿𝐸 Bodybuilding Program (HYPERMASS by Noel, 2022-06](https://youtu.be/uYRIWAKlA0c?t=689))

<a id="RST-03"></a>
### RST-03 · Same-muscle exercises still need full rest
- **Statement:** Between two exercises for the same muscle, rest 2-3 min; performance matters for biceps as much as for quads.
- **Numbers:** 2-3 min.
- **Scope:** All trainees; supersets of different muscles are fine.
- **Confidence:** medium — 1 video, 2024
- **Status:** current
- **Sources:** ([Why you shouldn't listen to Genetic Freaks (The Joel Williams Example), 2024-02](https://youtu.be/GyK1Y6WTR-g?t=1197))

<a id="RST-04"></a>
### RST-04 · Low reps get straight sets and long rests
- **Statement:** Low-rep sets run as straight sets with long rests; higher-rep sets can use rest-pause and shorter rests.
- **Numbers:** —
- **Scope:** All trainees.
- **Confidence:** medium — 1 video, 2025
- **Status:** current
- **Sources:** ([New Hypertrophy Gimmick™ just dropped 🤡, 2025-03](https://youtu.be/ACFKXT44BzM?t=1316))

<a id="RST-05"></a>
### RST-05 · Rest-based tests
- **Statement:** Redoing a set after 3 min should give fewer reps; but a big crash means poor work capacity, and a 1RM you can repeat after 10 min wasn't a true max.
- **Numbers:** 6 reps falling to 3-4 after 3 min signals poor work capacity (unless technique or context changed).
- **Scope:** All trainees (not nucleus overload).
- **Confidence:** medium — ~3 videos, 2020→2021
- **Status:** current
- **Sources:** ([The hypertrophy series： strength baseline control for recovery & gains, 2020-05](https://youtu.be/Vbk_2AALm3M?t=506); [Building work capacity with cardio specificity, 2021-02](https://youtu.be/BBqiphYfqMA?t=150); [Hypertrophy Q&A #6, 2021-03](https://youtu.be/pvpf7Yuayco?t=380))

## Supersets and giant sets

<a id="RST-06"></a>
### RST-06 · Don't superset the opening strength work
- **Statement:** Heavy opening lifts (squat, deadlift, bench, hinges, heavy knee flexion, weighted chins) run as straight sets with full rest to keep focus and energy; at most pair them with small non-bracing work (neck, abs, curls, rear delts).
- **Numbers:** 2024: bench and pull-ups standalone, the rest supersetted, ~1h10 session. Overhead press paired with a pull is an exception.
- **Scope:** All trainees.
- **Confidence:** high — ~19 videos, 2020→2025
- **Status:** contradicted — he also says resting 5 min after bench is wasted and supersets bench (and his bench back-offs) with rows or pull-ups.
- **Check:** Are the session's heavy opening lifts done as straight sets with full rest?
- **Sources:** ([Why I superset EVERYTHING (the giant sets principle), 2020-01](https://youtu.be/Z-D9kRwK90I); [5 days Upper Lower program review (Week 1), 2020-07](https://youtu.be/du7JYCA2pa4?t=874); [Greek Aesthetics Bodybuilding Program (Apollonian Physique Workout), 2022-05](https://youtu.be/SPicD3F686s?t=629); [So you think you can lift? (Program Review LIVE), 2024-11](https://youtu.be/6p2x4kDDjzs?t=1460))

<a id="RST-07"></a>
### RST-07 · Never superset two movements for the same muscle
- **Statement:** Pairing two lifts for the same muscle is pre-fatigue or a finisher, a different tool, and a last resort otherwise.
- **Numbers:** No face pulls with reverse flies, dips with shoulder press, OHP with lateral raises, or two biceps movements back to back.
- **Scope:** All trainees.
- **Confidence:** high — ~8 videos, 2020→2024
- **Status:** current
- **Sources:** ([The hypertrophy series： multiplying tonnage accumulation using supersets, 2020-09](https://youtu.be/l3tsyzKEktQ?t=189); [5 days Upper Lower program review (Week 1), 2020-07](https://youtu.be/du7JYCA2pa4?t=1255); [Push Pull Legs Upper Lower 5 days split Program review, 2020-05](https://youtu.be/0yIieHQjEiA?t=629); [BACK 2 THE GYM STREAM (Program reviews & Answering training questions), 2024-09](https://youtu.be/okm6bZHKHI4?t=2558))

<a id="RST-08"></a>
### RST-08 · Leg exercises don't chain into each other
- **Statement:** Lower-body supersets are harder because leg lifts tax the cardiovascular system; pair leg lifts with static or non-leg moves, and moving straight from one leg exercise to another is "a cardinal sin of hypertrophy". Keep ab work away from heavy bracing lifts.
- **Numbers:** Front squats + leg raises or pull-ups, not + deficit deadlifts.
- **Scope:** Lower-body days.
- **Confidence:** medium — ~6 videos, 2020→2024
- **Status:** contradicted — he has also paired leg press with leg curl and leg extension with calf raises; probably circuits vs paired isolation, a distinction he doesn't make.
- **Sources:** ([Push/Pull Pull/Legs Legs/Push 3 days program review, 2020-05](https://youtu.be/eFhwWirR70o?t=1307); [Going to WAR over Giant Sets (Response to Bald Omni Man), 2022-09](https://youtu.be/nqzVqvMvQ1s?t=501); [The Smartest Push Pull Legs Routine by Jeff Nippard review, 2021-06](https://youtu.be/Mq2TaHm_ySI?t=503); [Judging and Grading every Fitness Channel (Sam Sulek, Max Euceda, Lex Little), 2024-01](https://youtu.be/jDk3LytTEjA?t=1726))

<a id="RST-09"></a>
### RST-09 · Superset all accessory and isolation work
- **Statement:** Sitting idle between sets of curls, shrugs, laterals, pushdowns or leg extensions wastes time and tonnage; the target muscle needs rest, the rest of the body doesn't. He uses supersets in all programs, even for novices.
- **Numbers:** "An arm day without supersets is wasted time"; without supersets an advanced program would take 5 h. He giant-sets ~80% of his training (2020), "100% giant sets" (2023).
- **Scope:** All trainees.
- **Confidence:** high — ~22 videos, 2020→2024
- **Status:** current
- **Check:** Is accessory and isolation work supersetted rather than run as straight sets with long rests?
- **Sources:** ([Why I superset EVERYTHING (the giant sets principle), 2020-01](https://youtu.be/Z-D9kRwK90I?t=317); [Good arm day Vs Bad arm day, 2021-01](https://youtu.be/RSkzA1l5jlk?t=800); [The Monster Natty that trains EVERY DAY (Geoffrey Verity Schofield), 2023-04](https://youtu.be/aJ1e41y8Na4?t=630); [Going to WAR over Giant Sets (Response to Bald Omni Man), 2022-09](https://youtu.be/nqzVqvMvQ1s?t=1508))

<a id="RST-10"></a>
### RST-10 · Pair unrelated or antagonist muscles
- **Statement:** Supersets of non-competing muscles cost little or no performance, only cardiovascular capacity; the loss grows in a long full-body day.
- **Numbers:** Curls have no effect on calf raises right after; a long-head triceps exercise after a press costs at most one rep (he tested it).
- **Scope:** All trainees.
- **Confidence:** high — ~12 videos, 2020→2024
- **Status:** changed — 2020 he recommended long-head triceps work between press back-off sets; 2024 he no longer believes in that pairing.
- **Sources:** ([Want to save some time AND grow your muscles? Supersets are your best friends, 2021-09](https://youtu.be/XncJr9uMpWo?t=107); [Fullbody template review, 2021-01](https://youtu.be/G7rVTseabFU?t=430); [Greek Aesthetics Bodybuilding Program (Apollonian Physique Workout), 2022-05](https://youtu.be/SPicD3F686s?t=691); [BACK 2 THE GYM STREAM (Program reviews & Answering training questions), 2024-09](https://youtu.be/okm6bZHKHI4?t=7431))

<a id="RST-11"></a>
### RST-11 · Default pairings: press with pull
- **Statement:** Pair a horizontal press with a horizontal pull and a vertical press with a vertical pull; such a superset is part of a day, not its emphasis.
- **Numbers:** Other pairings he gives: curls + face pulls; skullcrushers + dips; weighted pull-ups/dips + calves, neck, forearms or shoulders; RDL + chin-ups, shrugs, calves or rear delts; leg raises after each bench set.
- **Scope:** All trainees.
- **Confidence:** high — ~18 videos, 2020→2023
- **Status:** current
- **Sources:** ([Push/Pull Pull/Legs Legs/Push 3 days program review, 2020-05](https://youtu.be/eFhwWirR70o?t=316); [Kizen Strength & Aesthetics Powerbuilding program review, 2020-09](https://youtu.be/-banYSTnkq4?t=330); [Program critique #1 (Upper Lower Push Pull), 2020-02](https://youtu.be/np9LdwTPfNs?t=1078); [We're turning Alan Thrall into a bodybuilder!, 2023-05](https://youtu.be/d1eLAd5WvIA?t=1880))

<a id="RST-12"></a>
### RST-12 · Near-free volume to fill rests
- **Statement:** Rear delts, leg curls, wrist curls, calves, traps, biceps and abs add stimulus with almost no systemic fatigue, so they slot into rest periods; use machine and warm-up downtime too.
- **Numbers:** 3x10-15 leg curls at session end at zero systemic cost; reverse curls right after the last squat warm-up.

- **Confidence:** medium — ~5 videos, 2020→2024

<a id="RST-13"></a>
### RST-13 · No rest inside a superset, rest after the round
- **Statement:** A superset is exercises back to back with no planned rest, then rest before repeating the round; walking between stations is fine.
- **Numbers:** Within: 0 rest (up to ~1 min to walk). After a round: 3-4 min (2021-24), 2-4 min (2022), 2-3 min (2021, 2024), ~2 min (2023); 90 s between rounds is valid, he gives more.

<a id="RST-14"></a>
### RST-14 · Giant sets: 4-5 exercises, most intense first
- **Statement:** A giant set is 4+ exercises; 4-5 is the sweet spot and longer ones eat time instead of saving it. Order them from most to least intense, and the last exercise is the one to cut.
- **Numbers:** 4-5 exercises, 6 is overkill; 3-4 rounds (2-4 while learning); at most 2 giant-set lines or 4-5 exercises on leg day; arm giant sets 3 exercises x 3-4 rounds.
- **Scope:** All trainees; 2023 he rated giant sets C tier for commercial gyms and low capacity.

<a id="RST-15"></a>
### RST-15 · Nonstop giant sets for conditioned lifters
- **Statement:** Advanced, conditioned lifters can cycle giant sets nonstop, since with 5 exercises the first has recovered by the time you loop back; isolation-only giant sets work because isolation isn't systemically fatiguing.

<a id="RST-16"></a>
### RST-16 · Build up to giant sets gradually
- **Statement:** Progress from easy supersets to hard giant sets, or you'll be cooked and wrongly blame the system; beginners who can't superset yet use short gaps instead of dropping supersets.
- **Numbers:** Easy supersets (biceps + triceps) → easy giant sets (+ rear delts) → hard supersets (press + pull) → hard giant sets (press + pull + abs); 1-2 weeks to adapt with ~4 min rest after the giant set; beginner fallback: set, 1 min, next set, then 2-3 min.

<a id="RST-17"></a>
### RST-17 · Superset only what is logistically close
- **Statement:** In commercial gyms superset equipment that sits close together and accept the gamble when it doesn't; never force supersets that don't fit, and if you can't superset, split the exercises.
- **Numbers:** —
- **Scope:** Commercial-gym lifters.

# 4. Progression, fatigue & recovery

This chapter covers how a lift, a program and a lifter move forward over months and years (progression), how he manages the fatigue that training creates without deload weeks (fatigue, deloads, breaks), and what happens outside the gym (sleep and recovery). His stance: progressive overload is mandatory for naturals, best done through evolving rep ranges with small, steady, never-stopping progress and stable tonnage. He rejects scheduled deloads, blocks and peaking for bodybuilders and builds fatigue management into every week instead. Sleep and passive rest are the base of recovery; soreness and "feel" are poor guides.

## Why progression matters

He treats rising tonnage as the target and getting stronger as the main way to raise it. Rep ranges and intensity windows themselves are in ch. 3.

<a id="PRG-01"></a>
### PRG-01 · Progressive overload is non-negotiable
- **Statement:** Without progressive overload there is no muscle gain; something has to go up for the muscles to go up, and a coach who never mentions it is a "hack".
- **Numbers:** —
- **Scope:** All trainees, especially naturals.
- **Confidence:** high — ~15 videos, 2020→2024
- **Status:** current
- **Check:** Does the program have a defined way for load, reps or sets to rise over time?
- **Sources:** ([The hypertrophy series： promoting progression in your training, 2020-06](https://youtu.be/ML5AQa9THHI); [The hypertrophy series： the most reliable way to progressively overload, 2021-03](https://youtu.be/Em00Z8i8V7c); [The Most IMPORTANT Methods for Muscle Growth (Hypertrophy Tier-List), 2023-11](https://youtu.be/SxqjF2oPasg?t=1132); [Don't be THAT GUY in 2024, 2024-01](https://youtu.be/uOAia_t5c_I?t=62))

## Overload levers and their order

Load, reps, sets and frequency are all overload, but he insists the bar weight never leaves the mix.

<a id="PRG-11"></a>
### PRG-11 · Overload has many modes
- **Statement:** Overload can come from load, reps, sets, frequency, rest, technique/variation or range of motion; weight on the bar is just "the tip of the iceberg", and more sets and reps at the same weight are valid overload.
- **Numbers:** —
- **Scope:** All trainees.
- **Confidence:** high — ~8 videos, 2020→2023
- **Status:** current
- **Sources:** ([Should bodybuilders care about strength?, 2020-02](https://youtu.be/xn8RN9807Ns?t=318); [The Hypertrophy Iceberg Explained (a complete guide to muscle growth), 2021-07](https://youtu.be/8ELQ2XZgpls?t=638); [The Ten 𝐋𝐀𝐖𝐒 of HYPERTROPHY (that you MUST break to grow), 2022-08](https://youtu.be/yUecX6qONXg?t=1015); [Come with me if you want a BIG BACK (4 steps MASSterplan), 2023-09](https://youtu.be/7uBT8vp0lNw?t=882))

<a id="PRG-12"></a>
### PRG-12 · Bar weight must stay in the mix
- **Statement:** Weight on the bar is the simplest, most reliable and easiest lever to log and must stay in the mix, but load-only progression is "designed to fail" because the ability to add weight outpaces recovery (the "Milo paradox").
- **Numbers:** —
- **Scope:** All trainees past the novice stage.
- **Confidence:** high — ~10 videos, 2020→2024
- **Status:** changed — 2020-21: bar weight is the simplest and best method; 2022: weight is the "tip of the iceberg", most natural gains come from accumulated volume; 2024: his own bar-weight obsession caused progression anxiety, yet you must still get stronger.
- **Check:** Does the program raise load as well as reps or sets, without relying on load alone?
- **Sources:** ([The hypertrophy series： promoting progression in your training, 2020-06](https://youtu.be/ML5AQa9THHI?t=63); [The hypertrophy series： controlling volume & intensity to promote progression, 2020-05](https://youtu.be/l9iNYJtRrD8?t=187); [No one understands progressive overload, 2022-03](https://youtu.be/YIIWlqhoNA0?t=1009); [Escape Intermediate Hell (Path to Exceptional Physique), 2023-10](https://youtu.be/16fjHEtZTCA?t=1209))

## Evolving rep ranges (double progression)

His main tool: each lift gets a fixed range, reps climb week to week, and weight goes up when the first set reaches the ceiling. Ch. 3 (INT-46) covers why declining reps across sets matter for intensity.

<a id="PRG-20"></a>
### PRG-20 · Evolving rep ranges are the core method
- **Statement:** Give each lift a fixed rep range, start near the bottom, add reps weekly, add weight at the top and stay in the same range. He calls it the best way to progress.
- **Numbers:** 6-10 example: 6,5 → … → 10,9,8 → jump; ~90-95% of his lifts (2020); "every one of his programs" (2024).
- **Scope:** All lifts past the novice stage (see PRG-36 for novices).
- **Confidence:** high — ~15 videos, 2020→2025
- **Status:** current
- **Check:** Does each lift have a rep range with a rule for when to add weight?
- **Sources:** ([Pull Push Legs 6 days Program Review, 2020-05](https://youtu.be/rucwL-SIefg?t=314); [Hypertrophy Q&A #10, 2022-06](https://youtu.be/QfHfxLYRu88?t=2765); [We're turning Alan Thrall into a bodybuilder!, 2023-05](https://youtu.be/d1eLAd5WvIA?t=3817); [Do you look better than Silver Era lifters? (Physique Review LIVE), 2024-12](https://youtu.be/ZLheQPgEfoA?t=504))

<a id="PRG-21"></a>
### PRG-21 · Add weight when the first set hits the ceiling
- **Statement:** Only the first (top) set needs to reach the top of the range, with the others close; waiting for every set to hit the top turns the range back into a static scheme.
- **Numbers:** 6-10×4: 10-10-10-10 = should have jumped long ago, 10-9-8-7 = ready; 5-10: 8-7-7-5 → 9-8-7-6 → 10 → +5 lb.
- **Scope:** All lifts on evolving ranges.
- **Confidence:** high — ~8 videos, 2020→2024
- **Status:** changed — Jan 2020: on 4×12, go up only if all four sets of 12 are comfortable; from Aug 2020: waiting for all sets makes ranges static; 2024: one set at the top is enough.
- **Check:** Is weight added once the first set reaches the top of the range, not only when every set does?
- **Sources:** ([Free 3 times a week full body hypertrophy program, 2020-01](https://youtu.be/xFVva4-swKc?t=188); [When to progress forward with evolving rep ranges, 2020-08](https://youtu.be/CrT1WOhxLqU?t=64); [When to progress forward with evolving rep ranges, 2020-08](https://youtu.be/CrT1WOhxLqU?t=190); [Do you look better than Silver Era lifters? (Physique Review LIVE), 2024-12](https://youtu.be/ZLheQPgEfoA?t=566))

<a id="PRG-22"></a>
### PRG-22 · Readiness depends on the range
- **Statement:** On a heavy low range less is needed to add weight; you needn't max every set.
- **Numbers:** On 3-5, 5,4 is enough; on an 8-12 isolation, 11,10; 5-4 or 5-4-3 can be enough.
- **Scope:** All lifts on evolving ranges.
- **Confidence:** medium — 2 videos, 2021→2022
- **Status:** current
- **Sources:** ([How to use Evolving Rep Ranges for Hypertrophy, 2021-10](https://youtu.be/X8WMlqP6M78?t=308); [Hypertrophy Q&A #10, 2022-06](https://youtu.be/QfHfxLYRu88?t=2640))

<a id="PRG-23"></a>
### PRG-23 · Reps should fall across sets
- **Statement:** At the same weight, reps should drop from set to set; identical reps on three or more sets mean sandbagging or too light a load.
- **Numbers:** E.g. 12 → 7; 10, 9-8, 8-7; 4×10 repeated after 3 min rest = add weight; 7,7,7 → 8,7,7 is fine if the top set progresses.
- **Scope:** All working sets.
- **Confidence:** high — ~10 videos, 2020→2024
- **Status:** current
- **Sources:** ([When to progress forward with evolving rep ranges, 2020-08](https://youtu.be/CrT1WOhxLqU?t=127); [Rep Goal System (by Steve Shaw of Massive Iron) review, 2020-07](https://youtu.be/LYBdXCcmOO0?t=691); [Hypertrophy Q&A #8, 2021-09](https://youtu.be/P89o8FBSWDI?t=997); [BACK 2 THE GYM STREAM (Program reviews & Answering training questions), 2024-09](https://youtu.be/okm6bZHKHI4?t=4888))

<a id="PRG-24"></a>
### PRG-24 · Straight sets, no pyramids
- **Statement:** Use the same weight on all working sets; pyramids and reverse pyramids ("D tier") pile up junk volume.
- **Numbers:** —
- **Scope:** All working sets.
- **Confidence:** high — ~5 videos, 2020→2023
- **Status:** current
- **Sources:** ([Rep Goal System (by Steve Shaw of Massive Iron) review, 2020-07](https://youtu.be/LYBdXCcmOO0?t=502); [The hypertrophy series： utilizing tonnage for muscle growth, 2021-01](https://youtu.be/_2M6FhWuIvs?t=220); [Superhero Aesthetics Bodybuilding Program (Kinobody Hollywood Physique Workout), 2022-08](https://youtu.be/o_x3Ij2GBXM?t=120); [The Most IMPORTANT Methods for Muscle Growth (Hypertrophy Tier-List), 2023-11](https://youtu.be/SxqjF2oPasg?t=692))

<a id="PRG-25"></a>
### PRG-25 · Every set stays inside the range
- **Statement:** If a set falls below the floor after a jump, drop the next set and win it back next session; if the first set misses, return to the previous weight. Falling below means the jump was too big or the range was badly set ("too greedy").
- **Numbers:** E.g. 7 then 6 on 6-10 after a jump.
- **Scope:** All lifts on evolving ranges.
- **Confidence:** high — ~6 videos, 2020→2023
- **Status:** current
- **Sources:** ([When to progress forward with evolving rep ranges, 2020-08](https://youtu.be/CrT1WOhxLqU?t=376); [Hypertrophy Q&A #9, 2022-01](https://youtu.be/9y2s6kyFkPc?t=315); [Everything I do to get HUGE (Split, Reps, Lifts), 2023-09](https://youtu.be/43F9unmSc_I?t=1007); [How to Keep Growing FOREVER (Unlimited Hypertrophy Method), 2023-07](https://youtu.be/1TKqwXCge9E?t=638))

<a id="PRG-26"></a>
### PRG-26 · Evolving sets: add a set, then weight
- **Statement:** When the first set tops the range, add a set; at the top set count, add weight and drop back a set, then rebuild.
- **Numbers:** OHP 4×8-12 at 100 lb: at 12/11/10 add 2.5 lb and go to 3 sets; if 3 sets can't stay in range after a jump do 2 (e.g. 7, 6), then add the third back; 12 → 15-16 weekly sets, then add load and return to 12.
- **Scope:** Compounds and isolation, intermediates.
- **Confidence:** high — ~6 videos, 2022→2024
- **Status:** changed — 2020: he avoided evolving set ranges because removing both limits removes structure; 2021: advanced tools that destabilize programs; 2022-24: standard in his programs.
- **Sources:** ([Rep Goal System (by Steve Shaw of Massive Iron) review, 2020-07](https://youtu.be/LYBdXCcmOO0?t=940); [How to use Evolving Rep Ranges for Hypertrophy, 2021-10](https://youtu.be/X8WMlqP6M78?t=720); [Come with me if you want big shoulders (JOIN THE CHALLENGE!), 2022-10](https://youtu.be/BhOuuyriBDw?t=1383); [Your lifting program SUCKS! (Hypertrophy Q&A / Program review), 2024-10](https://youtu.be/c7hl9u3h_s0?t=5990))

## Range width

<a id="PRG-37"></a>
### PRG-37 · Ranges that are too narrow fail
- **Statement:** Narrow ranges leave no room for set evolution and drift toward sandbagged 5x5; keep at least 4 reps between floor and ceiling.
- **Numbers:** Too narrow: 5-6, 6-8, 8-10 ×4 sets, 10-12 ×2-3 sets, 4×8-10 squat; good: 6-10, 8-12; 4-6 "a recipe for plateaus" (2025).
- **Scope:** All lifts.
- **Confidence:** high — ~10 videos, 2020→2025
- **Status:** changed — 2020 he often prescribed 4-6 (4×4-6 pull-ups/dips, 3×4-6 squat); 2023-25: ≥4 reps between floor and ceiling, 4-6 plateaus.
- **Sources:** ([Push Pull Legs Upper Lower 5 days split Program review, 2020-05](https://youtu.be/0yIieHQjEiA?t=64); [2 days Upper (Torso/Arm dominant) split program review, 2020-04](https://youtu.be/87CMjYjX2jY?t=125); [How to Keep Growing FOREVER (Unlimited Hypertrophy Method), 2023-07](https://youtu.be/1TKqwXCge9E?t=638); [New Hypertrophy Gimmick™ just dropped 🤡, 2025-03](https://youtu.be/ACFKXT44BzM?t=498))

<a id="PRG-38"></a>
### PRG-38 · Ranges that are too wide fail
- **Statement:** Very wide ranges (top more than 2× the bottom) take forever to earn a jump and invite laziness; 6-12 is about the widest he allows (2024).
- **Numbers:** Too wide: 2-20, 2-12, 3×3-20, 8-16, 8-18; 10-20 only with 4 sets; replace 8-20 with 10-15 or 14-20.
- **Scope:** All lifts.
- **Confidence:** high — ~8 videos, 2020→2024
- **Status:** contradicted — 8-15: too wide because reaching 15 means you'll get 12-13 (2020) vs hitting 15 lets you add ~10 lb and still get 8 (2023).
- **Sources:** ([How to set up evolving rep ranges (theoretical aspects), 2020-06](https://youtu.be/0O0wnhU3g-8?t=129); [4 days Body parts split program review, 2020-10](https://youtu.be/sCMGXCXKVjs?t=252); [How to Keep Growing FOREVER (Unlimited Hypertrophy Method), 2023-07](https://youtu.be/1TKqwXCge9E?t=574); [Your lifting program SUCKS! (Hypertrophy Q&A / Program review), 2024-10](https://youtu.be/c7hl9u3h_s0?t=3261))

<a id="PRG-39"></a>
### PRG-39 · Wide ranges for lifts where reps fall fast
- **Statement:** Use a wide range like 6-12 where reps drop fast across sets or the lift is hard to progress; incline and preacher curls plateau easily and need it.
- **Numbers:** 5×6-12 drops 12 → 6-7; 8 reps at 40 lb won't survive a jump to 4 reps.
- **Scope:** Spoto press, incline/preacher curls and similar lifts.
- **Confidence:** medium — ~5 videos, 2020→2025
- **Status:** current
- **Sources:** ([My rep ranges for Natural Hypertrophy, 2020-01](https://youtu.be/t_RZT-AkjhE?t=380); [4 days Upper Lower + 1 Arm day Program review, 2020-11](https://youtu.be/xQQJUXf58ZE?t=1177); [The ULTIMATE PPL Program (Doom Slayer Physique), 2023-11](https://youtu.be/DA7QvIAyptw?t=1326); [New Hypertrophy Gimmick™ just dropped 🤡, 2025-03](https://youtu.be/ACFKXT44BzM?t=434))

<a id="PRG-40"></a>
### PRG-40 · Higher ranges: easy reps, hard jumps
- **Statement:** Wider or higher ranges make each added rep easier, but the higher the range, the harder it is to clear and add weight.
- **Numbers:** Bottom is 50% of top in 4-8, 60% in 6-10.
- **Scope:** All lifts.
- **Confidence:** medium — 2 videos, 2024→2025
- **Status:** current
- **Sources:** ([New Hypertrophy Gimmick™ just dropped 🤡, 2025-03](https://youtu.be/ACFKXT44BzM?t=498); [So you think you can lift? (Program Review LIVE), 2024-11](https://youtu.be/6p2x4kDDjzs?t=5730))

<a id="PRG-41"></a>
### PRG-41 · Adjust the range to a plateau
- **Statement:** When stalled in a range, adjust it to the exercise: widen if low reps stall, shrink if high reps stall; try widening first so tonnage climbs at the same weight.
- **Numbers:** —
- **Scope:** Stalled lifts.
- **Confidence:** medium — 2 videos, 2021→2025
- **Status:** current
- **Sources:** ([Pushing progression and avoiding plateaus using evolving rep ranges, 2021-04](https://youtu.be/C86TMVYGu0M?t=328); [New Hypertrophy Gimmick™ just dropped 🤡, 2025-03](https://youtu.be/ACFKXT44BzM?t=1250))

### PRG-42 · When testing a range, start wide
- **Statement:** When beta-testing a new range, start wider and narrow it; shrinking is safer than expanding.
- **Numbers:** Close-grip bench 6-12 → 6-10.

## Strength-work progression schemes

Fixed-weight schemes for the heavy opening lift, where reps and sets evolve before the load moves. Lift-specific programming is in ch. 7.

<a id="PRG-43"></a>
### PRG-43 · The "543" elevator scheme
- **Statement:** For heavy deadlifts and OHP, keep the weight and build sets and reps up a ladder, then add weight and restart at the bottom.
- **Numbers:** 1-3 sets of 2-5: 2; 3,2; 4,3,2; 5,4,3; then +10 lb and restart at 2. Deadlift variant 2-3-2-4-3-2-5-3-2; a tight 1, 2-1, 3-2-1 version moves slower but may allow 10 lb jumps.
- **Scope:** His 2020 deadlift and OHP.
- **Confidence:** medium — ~4 videos, 2020
- **Status:** changed — 2020 schemes of 2-5 reps; by 2022 compounds never go below 4 (see PRG-102).
- **Sources:** ([My rep ranges for Natural Hypertrophy, 2020-01](https://youtu.be/t_RZT-AkjhE?t=318); [How to set up evolving rep ranges (practical aspects), 2020-06](https://youtu.be/4Dop4_sIWn4?t=64); [How to progress forward with evolving rep ranges, 2020-09](https://youtu.be/65rLZe9cz_0?t=314); [Weight progression on evolving rep ranges, 2020-07](https://youtu.be/6lggo2XPomI?t=377))

<a id="PRG-44"></a>
### PRG-44 · Fixed-weight squat and bench ladder
- **Statement:** For squat and bench, keep the weight and climb a rep ladder, then add weight and return to the start; a failed session is repeated.
- **Numbers:** 4 → 5,4 → 6,5,4 → 7,5,3 → 8,6,4, then +5 lb/side; 6-5-4 (15 reps) isn't enough to jump, 8-6-4 (18) is. Higher-volume version where form breaks at high intensity: 4; 5,4; 6,5,4; 7,6,5; 8,7,6.
- **Scope:** His squat and bench, 2020-21.
- **Confidence:** medium — ~4 videos, 2020→2021
- **Status:** current
- **Sources:** ([My rep ranges for Natural Hypertrophy, 2020-01](https://youtu.be/t_RZT-AkjhE?t=255); [How to set up evolving rep ranges (practical aspects), 2020-06](https://youtu.be/4Dop4_sIWn4?t=126); [When to progress forward with evolving rep ranges, 2020-08](https://youtu.be/CrT1WOhxLqU?t=252); [Hypertrophy Q&A #5, 2021-01](https://youtu.be/-anA4CV2SVU?t=1317))

<a id="PRG-45"></a>
### PRG-45 · Strength work: 1-3 sets
- **Statement:** Keep strength work to 1-3 sets (4 max); 5-6 sets means sandbagging. Descending reps (5-4-3) keep the tonnage high-quality.
- **Numbers:** 1-3 sets, max 4.
- **Scope:** The heavy opening lift.
- **Confidence:** medium — ~3 videos, 2020→2021
- **Status:** current
- **Sources:** ([The hypertrophy series： programming strength work to bolster tonnage quality & p, 2020-11](https://youtu.be/A-asa7QMiG0?t=425); [How to use Evolving Rep Ranges for Hypertrophy, 2021-10](https://youtu.be/X8WMlqP6M78?t=210); [When to progress forward with evolving rep ranges, 2020-08](https://youtu.be/CrT1WOhxLqU?t=439))

<a id="PRG-46"></a>
### PRG-46 · Autoregulate strength work by sets, not load
- **Statement:** Keep the strength-lift weight and autoregulate through sets and reps; a weak day is made up with same-pattern back-offs.
- **Numbers:** E.g. 420 lb for 1-3 sets of 4-8; a day of one set of 2 → back-offs 3-4×8-12.
- **Scope:** Intermediates with a heavy opening lift.
- **Confidence:** medium — ~3 videos, 2020→2022
- **Status:** current
- **Sources:** ([2 days Upper (Torso/Arm dominant) split program review, 2020-04](https://youtu.be/87CMjYjX2jY?t=561); [Why I never deload (and why you shouldn't either), 2022-02](https://youtu.be/BJXFeQWGUuY?t=1453); [Jeff Nippard & Alec Enkiri Want Me To Deload... I Don't Wanna (Size vs Strength , 2022-03](https://youtu.be/PuIp9cGKMHo?t=3524))

<a id="PRG-47"></a>
### PRG-47 · Top sets plus lighter volume sets
- **Statement:** Pair a few top-intensity sets with lighter volume or back-off sets; how heavy the strength sets are decides the back-off reps.
- **Numbers:** OHP: 2-3 top sets (or 3×2-5) + 3×5 ~20-25 lb lighter, 6 sets total (e.g. 135×5, 155×3, 145×5, 155×2); bench: top set 2-4 then 3×5; strength sets at 3s → back-offs toward 8, at 4s → heavier back-offs (5-8); deadlift 1-3/2-4 with RDL 5-7, 5-8 or 5-10.
- **Scope:** Heavy compounds, mostly 2020.
- **Confidence:** medium — ~6 videos, 2020
- **Status:** current
- **Sources:** ([Push Pull Legs Upper Lower 5 days split Program review, 2020-05](https://youtu.be/0yIieHQjEiA?t=193); [Coolcicada 6 Days PPL Program review, 2020-05](https://youtu.be/GClcGq2tIDU?t=253); [4 days Upper Lower program review, 2020-06](https://youtu.be/ZKgM-tX_ODU?t=735); [Synchronizing evolving rep range with movement patterns, variations & rotations , 2020-12](https://youtu.be/twgzqTg4nug?t=189))

## Rule-based alternatives he endorses

<a id="PRG-48"></a>
### PRG-48 · The 85% rule (step loading)
- **Statement:** Build reps and sets at a load until it feels like ~70% effort, then add weight to get back to ~85%, cut sets or reps, and rebuild; never keep piling volume at 70%. Your 85% grows with you.
- **Numbers:** Close-grip bench 200 lb at 7/6/5 → build until the first set hits 10 and the last still gets 6 with a 4th set added → 10/9/8 at 200 → 205 lb gives ~7/6/6.
- **Scope:** General, arms included.
- **Confidence:** medium — ~3 videos, 2022→2023
- **Status:** current
- **Sources:** ([How to Get Bigger by Doing Less (The 85% Rule), 2022-12](https://youtu.be/z2uzpl_smSg?t=1070); [How to Get Bigger by Doing Less (The 85% Rule), 2022-12](https://youtu.be/z2uzpl_smSg?t=1259); [How to Get Bigger by Doing Less (The 85% Rule), 2022-12](https://youtu.be/z2uzpl_smSg?t=1511); [Come with me if you want massive arms (Step by Step MASSterplan), 2023-01](https://youtu.be/HXoY7xzHlWU?t=1451))

<a id="PRG-49"></a>
### PRG-49 · Rep-goal system
- **Statement:** Maxing every set at the same weight toward a total rep goal, then adding ~5 lb, is "excellent" and essentially evolving ranges by another name; he later prefers RIR for clearer brackets.
- **Numbers:** 5x5 → 25-rep goal; 25 reps over 3 sets forces ~7-8 per set; when tired he'd use a 35-rep goal.
- **Scope:** General.
- **Confidence:** medium — ~2 videos, 2020→2021
- **Status:** changed — 2020: rep goals excellent; 2021: RIR preferred; 2023: day-chosen RIR autoregulation "S tier".
- **Sources:** ([Rep Goal System (by Steve Shaw of Massive Iron) review, 2020-07](https://youtu.be/LYBdXCcmOO0); [Rep Goal System (by Steve Shaw of Massive Iron) review, 2020-07](https://youtu.be/LYBdXCcmOO0?t=1445); [Viking's the Bare Bones Series Program review, 2021-03](https://youtu.be/8mGHG5C-EPE?t=312); [The Most IMPORTANT Methods for Muscle Growth (Hypertrophy Tier-List), 2023-11](https://youtu.be/SxqjF2oPasg?t=755))

<a id="PRG-50"></a>
### PRG-50 · Eastern-style big jumps
- **Statement:** Keep a weight challenging for 4 reps until easy, then make a big jump; leaving reps in reserve doesn't slow progress.
- **Numbers:** RIR may cost ~300 lb tonnage now but avoids plateaus and injuries.
- **Scope:** General, mainly strength work.
- **Confidence:** medium — ~3 videos, 2020
- **Status:** current
- **Sources:** ([Why you should leave reps in the tank (Reps in Reserve), 2020-02](https://youtu.be/QiOh8SF-UxQ); [Why you should leave reps in the tank (Reps in Reserve), 2020-02](https://youtu.be/QiOh8SF-UxQ?t=364); [The hypertrophy series： applying reps in reserve while minimizing tonnage loss, 2020-11](https://youtu.be/JmowZI5YiAk?t=189))

## Static schemes (5x5, 3x5, 10x10)

See ch. 3 (INT-44, INT-45) for sandbagging and intensity.

<a id="PRG-51"></a>
### PRG-51 · Static schemes force sandbagging
- **Statement:** With static schemes the first set is too easy or the last is ground out; 5x5 progresses fast early, then plateaus hard, and is not a good hypertrophy reference.
- **Numbers:** —
- **Scope:** Past the novice stage.
- **Confidence:** high — ~15 videos, 2020→2025
- **Status:** current
- **Check:** Past the novice stage, does the program avoid fixed set×rep targets like 5x5 on its main lifts?
- **Sources:** ([My rep ranges for Natural Hypertrophy, 2020-01](https://youtu.be/t_RZT-AkjhE?t=240); [4 days Upper Lower split Program review, 2020-04](https://youtu.be/fSOiGuUPqBc?t=187); [The Great MOGGING of Bodybuilding： How Strength Came to DOMINATE Fitness, 2022-02](https://youtu.be/GNJkAcgUJ_0?t=5772); [New Hypertrophy Gimmick™ just dropped 🤡, 2025-03](https://youtu.be/ACFKXT44BzM?t=186))

<a id="PRG-52"></a>
### PRG-52 · Static schemes can only add weight
- **Statement:** Static schemes progress only by adding weight, force conservative jumps, make tonnage jump in steps, and after a miss you deload below where you started; they never teach plateau handling ("5x5 syndrome").
- **Numbers:** Repeating 5x5 needs a PR on five sets at once, which stops working after noob gains.
- **Scope:** Past the novice stage.
- **Confidence:** high — ~8 videos, 2020→2023
- **Status:** current
- **Sources:** ([5 Ways to shock the muscle (GONE WRONG), 2020-07](https://youtu.be/RqS8AxVE28I?t=188); [The problem with 5x5/3x5, 2020-06](https://youtu.be/k3O630Nz4B8?t=378); [The issue with Novice Programs, 2021-03](https://youtu.be/S0qBQppUtTQ?t=900); [How to Get Bigger by Doing Less (The 85% Rule), 2022-12](https://youtu.be/z2uzpl_smSg?t=1382))

<a id="PRG-53"></a>
### PRG-53 · Where static ranges are fine
- **Statement:** Static ranges are fine for novices (weight keeps rising regardless) and as deliberate tools: back-off or accessory volume after strength work, a secondary lift you don't push, chin-ups, or the only horizontal press of a low-volume day.
- **Numbers:** 3x5 > 5x5 as back-off after an AMRAP top set; he uses 5×4 as a mental break on feeder lifts.
- **Scope:** Novices; deliberate secondary work.
- **Confidence:** high — ~10 videos, 2020→2023
- **Status:** current
- **Sources:** ([Ivysaur Novice program review, 2020-08](https://youtu.be/QKpAtCK6oPQ?t=375); [The hypertrophy series： understanding sandbagging to promote qualitative sets, 2020-11](https://youtu.be/S8T3hQgsrko?t=380); [Upper Body focused 5 days PPL + sprints program review, 2020-09](https://youtu.be/aaQr-Av0x9Y?t=691); [The Best Natural Lifter You've NEVER Heard Of (Hersovyac), 2023-04](https://youtu.be/-sf34ScWLK8?t=1899))

<a id="PRG-54"></a>
### PRG-54 · An evolving version always beats static
- **Statement:** An evolving version of a scheme always beats its static form, and static targets should not be used past the beginner phase.
- **Numbers:** 3×4-6 over 3x5; 3-5 sets of 3-5 over 5x5; 3×3-5 over 3x3; 3×6 → use 6-10.
- **Scope:** Past the beginner phase.
- **Confidence:** high — ~10 videos, 2020→2025
- **Status:** current

## Weight jumps

<a id="PRG-55"></a>
### PRG-55 · Default jump sizes
- **Statement:** The default jump is 5 lb per side on barbell lifts and 2.5 lb per side on OHP and curls, with "5 lb per hand" logic for dumbbells.
- **Numbers:** 5 lb/side (10 lb total); 2.5 lb/side OHP and curls; intermediate range 2.5-10 lb/side; 5 lb/side proved too much for his curls and OHP.
- **Scope:** Intermediates.
- **Confidence:** high — ~6 videos, 2020→2023
- **Status:** current

<a id="PRG-56"></a>
### PRG-56 · No universal jump
- **Statement:** Jump size depends on the lift, the range and the whole program; decide plate loading before choosing the range, and if they don't match change one.

- **Scope:** Program design.
- **Confidence:** high — ~5 videos, 2020→2023
- **Status:** current

<a id="PRG-62"></a>
### PRG-62 · Slow, steady, uninterrupted progress
- **Statement:** Slow, steady, uninterrupted progress beats fast gains followed by stalls, injury or regression ("not a shooting star"; the tortoise beats the hare).
- **Numbers:** 3 fast months then 3 stalled months kills motivation.
- **Scope:** All trainees.
- **Confidence:** high — ~12 videos, 2020→2024
- **Status:** current
- **Check:** Is the program built for small, regular increases rather than fast jumps that end in resets?

## Plateaus

<a id="PRG-71"></a>
### PRG-71 · What counts as a plateau
- **Statement:** Repeating a weight or reps for 2-3 sessions is the "breaking point" where gains happen, not a plateau; months at the same weight is one. Plateaus are normal and PRs every session are unrealistic (2023).
- **Numbers:** 2-3 sessions = normal; ~6 months = plateau; no lift should stagnate more than ~1 month vs 4-5 months on a compound means the program is wrong (both June 2020).
- **Scope:** All lifts.
- **Confidence:** medium — ~5 videos, 2020→2024
- **Status:** contradicted — stall tolerance of ~1 month vs 4-5 months, both June 2020.
- **Sources:** ([The hypertrophy series： promoting progression in your training, 2020-06](https://youtu.be/ML5AQa9THHI?t=63); [How to set up evolving rep ranges (theoretical aspects), 2020-06](https://youtu.be/0O0wnhU3g-8?t=245); [How to Keep Growing FOREVER (Unlimited Hypertrophy Method), 2023-07](https://youtu.be/1TKqwXCge9E?t=1327); [Don't be THAT GUY in 2024, 2024-01](https://youtu.be/uOAia_t5c_I?t=62))

<a id="PRG-72"></a>
### PRG-72 · Plateaus are a recovery or programming problem
- **Statement:** Plateaus come from poor recovery or diet, low effort, bad programming or a bad lift; in bodybuilding they usually mean too much volume to recover from or too little stimulus.
- **Numbers:** Outside old age (65-70), regression means program or diet.
- **Scope:** All lifters. See SLP-48.
- **Confidence:** high — ~4 videos, 2020→2024
- **Status:** current
- **Sources:** ([The hypertrophy series： using volume to assess recovery abilities, 2020-06](https://youtu.be/B4aHn6pXfTo?t=443); [Hypertrophy Q&A #9, 2022-01](https://youtu.be/9y2s6kyFkPc?t=1250); [Your lifting program SUCKS! ### PRG-73 · First response: manipulate volume and intensity
- **Statement:** Answer a plateau first with new rep ranges, more volume, widened ranges or frequency, not with new exercises; volume, intensity or supersets bypass the law of accommodation.
- **Numbers:** —
- **Scope:** Stalled lifts.
- **Confidence:** high — ~6 videos, 2020→2023

<a id="PRG-74"></a>
### PRG-74 · Never deload and re-run the progression
- **Statement:** Taking weight off and re-running the same progression is "a longer run-up at the same wall" and wastes quality tonnage; only drop weight if you hit failure mid-session. A missed 3x5 should become 5,4,3 instead.
- **Numbers:** E.g. -10% or back to 70% resets.
- **Scope:** All lifts; reset-and-retry is why many quit.
- **Confidence:** high — ~8 videos, 2020→2023
- **Status:** current
- **Check:** Does the program handle stalls without resetting the load and re-running the same progression?
- **Sources:** ([The problem with 5x5/3x5, 2020-06](https://youtu.be/k3O630Nz4B8?t=378); [Hypertrophy Q&A #8, 2021-09](https://youtu.be/P89o8FBSWDI?t=2755); [5 Things I Wish I Knew Before I Started Lifting, 2022-09](https://youtu.be/6HGBdDOAReA?t=568); [The Most IMPORTANT Methods for Muscle Growth (Hypertrophy Tier-List), 2023-11](https://youtu.be/SxqjF2oPasg?t=755))

<a id="PRG-75"></a>
### PRG-75 · Don't swap a lift because it stalled
- **Statement:** Swapping a stalled lift dodges the plateau; the "progress" on the new lift is neural relearning, and stalling is when the body must build muscle. Letting failure trigger rotation hurts mental strength.
- **Numbers:** —
- **Scope:** All lifts.
- **Confidence:** high — ~6 videos, 2020→2023
- **Status:** changed — 2020: never let a stall trigger rotation; 2023: only add a variation if you truly can't break the plateau; 2024: move to or add another variation of the pattern when a lift stalls.
- **Sources:** ([Push/Pull Pull/Legs Legs/Push 3 days program review, 2020-05](https://youtu.be/eFhwWirR70o?t=127); [Rotating lifts： What it should & shouldn't be, 2020-05](https://youtu.be/z9MDwMO8K4Y?t=190); [The ULTIMATE PPL Program (Doom Slayer Physique), 2023-11](https://youtu.be/DA7QvIAyptw?t=1641); [Exercise Tier Lists are STUPID, 2024-11](https://youtu.be/6yW3GSskl8g?t=1581))

## Tonnage stability and strength work

<a id="PRG-82"></a>
### PRG-82 · Tonnage rises steadily, no roller-coaster
- **Statement:** Bodybuilding tonnage should rise steadily with only small planned dips, neither flat nor a roller-coaster; powerlifters wave and peak, bodybuilders don't.
- **Numbers:** Never deadlift 40 lb less than last session; after each jump tonnage stays above the previous cycle's low.
- **Scope:** Bodybuilders.
- **Confidence:** high — ~10 videos, 2020→2022
- **Status:** current

## Fatigue: against deload weeks and time off

He sees deloads as a powerlifting peaking tool; a bodybuilder who needs one has a program that overshoots recovery.

<a id="FAT-01"></a>
### FAT-01 · Scheduled deloads are unnecessary for bodybuilders
- **Statement:** Scheduled deloads are unnecessary or harmful for bodybuilders; needing one means you are "digging a hole" with too much frequency, volume or strength work. A deload is an emergency response to a programming mistake and useless unless injured.
- **Numbers:** —
- **Scope:** Bodybuilders (not strength athletes peaking).
- **Confidence:** high — ~16 videos, 2020→2024
- **Status:** changed — 2020: "I never deload"; 2022: he deloads constantly through set/rep management, just not the powerlifter way (see FAT-13).
- **Check:** Does the program run without scheduled deload weeks?
- **Sources:** ([The training principles series： deloads, 2020-06](https://youtu.be/CRXE2gFfwcs?t=188); [The hypertrophy series： deloading without wasting tonnage, 2020-12](https://youtu.be/7ZS-mGePFXw?t=312); [Jeff Nippard & Alec Enkiri Want Me To Deload... <a id="FAT-02"></a>
### FAT-02 · Deloads exist for peaking
- **Statement:** Deloads are for strength athletes who peak; bodybuilders never peak, so only the recovery half could matter. The term spread with the internet and powerlifting and is absent from earlier bodybuilding eras.
- **Numbers:** Term spread ~20 years ago.
- **Scope:** Bodybuilders.
- **Confidence:** high — ~9 videos, 2020→2024
- **Status:** current
- **Sources:** ([The hypertrophy series： deloading without wasting tonnage, 2020-12](https://youtu.be/7ZS-mGePFXw?t=62); [Why I never deload (and why you shouldn't either), 2022-02](https://youtu.be/BJXFeQWGUuY?t=255); [The Great MOGGING of Bodybuilding： How Strength Came to DOMINATE Fitness, 2022-02](https://youtu.be/GNJkAcgUJ_0?t=5585); [Why everyone HATES Paul Carter (liftrunbang1), 2024-02](https://youtu.be/ZRNSc-xBVnc?t=691))

<a id="FAT-03"></a>
### FAT-03 · Trim the program instead of deloading
- **Statement:** Reduce workload yourself before a deload would be needed; doing slightly less means you never need a week off and lose less tonnage than a deload costs.
- **Numbers:** Cutting 40-50 min from your week beats a deload; ~25% more work across two weeks (2024).

- **Confidence:** high — ~5 videos, 2020→2024

- **Statement:** A week off, or 3-4 days fully off, is detraining, not deloading; you can only deload from a load. Time off is for injury or when away from the gym.
- **Numbers:** Needing 3-4 days off every 2 months means intensity/volume is wrong; a 13-day break is planned detraining.

## The built-in "bodybuilding deload"

His alternative: small, continuous adjustments that keep tonnage stable and every muscle stimulated.

<a id="FAT-13"></a>
### FAT-13 · The deload is built into every week
- **Statement:** Evolving reps and sets plus rotations vary volume, intensity and frequency slightly while tonnage stays stable; small dips from rep ranges are the only variation he allows. He opposes blast/cruise, polarized volume/intensity days and clear hard/easy weeks.
- **Numbers:** —
- **Scope:** Bodybuilders.
- **Confidence:** high — ~8 videos, 2020→2022
- **Status:** current
- **Sources:** ([Kizen Strength & Aesthetics Powerbuilding program review, 2020-09](https://youtu.be/-banYSTnkq4?t=1210); [Hypertrophy Q&A #2, 2020-10](https://youtu.be/MIHPylz3f7Q?t=697); [Doggcrapp Training review, 2021-01](https://youtu.be/A55c7v1yMn4?t=937); [Jeff Nippard & Alec Enkiri Want Me To Deload... I Don't Wanna (Size vs Strength , 2022-03](https://youtu.be/PuIp9cGKMHo?t=6605))

<a id="FAT-14"></a>
### FAT-14 · Micro-deloads by muscle, on the day
- **Statement:** Picture each body part flashing red (needs work) or green (needs recovery); reduce a muscle that needs rest or rotate it out, and train a fresh muscle even if a rotation planned rest, so every muscle stays continuously stimulated.
- **Numbers:** A muscle needing rest gets one evolving-rep set or is rotated out.
- **Scope:** Autoregulated programs.
- **Confidence:** medium — ~3 videos, 2022
- **Status:** current
- **Sources:** ([Why I never deload (and why you shouldn't either), 2022-02](https://youtu.be/BJXFeQWGUuY?t=951); [Why I never deload (and why you shouldn't either), 2022-02](https://youtu.be/BJXFeQWGUuY?t=1766); [Why I never deload (and why you shouldn't either), 2022-02](https://youtu.be/BJXFeQWGUuY?t=1828); [Why I never deload (and why you shouldn't either), 2022-02](https://youtu.be/BJXFeQWGUuY?t=1890))

<a id="FAT-15"></a>
### FAT-15 · Volume, intensity and frequency manage fatigue
- **Statement:** Volume, intensity and frequency are one thing: tools to manage fatigue. Any program is a block of fatigue, so get the most from the least.
- **Numbers:** —
- **Scope:** Program design (see ch. 3, VOL-01).
- **Confidence:** medium — ~2 videos, 2021→2022
- **Status:** current
- **Sources:** ([How to modify any training program, 2021-03](https://youtu.be/o05wgvQtSMc?t=379); [Why I never deload (and why you shouldn't either), 2022-02](https://youtu.be/BJXFeQWGUuY?t=2203))

<a id="FAT-16"></a>
### FAT-16 · Autoregulation needs built-in mechanisms

## Recovery timing

<a id="SLP-22"></a>
### SLP-22 · A muscle needs ~48-72 hours
- **Statement:** A muscle needs about 48 h, up to 72 h, and even a fully trashed muscle is fresh in 4-5 days; no muscle needs a full week off. Avoid the same isolation lift on consecutive days.
- **Numbers:** ~48 h, up to 72 h; trashed max 4-5 days; ≥48 h between an arm day and the next upper day; same isolation ≥48 h apart.
- **Scope:** General.
- **Confidence:** high — ~5 videos, 2020→2024
- **Status:** current
- **Sources:** ([Programming rest days, 2020-09](https://youtu.be/y-Z49WlVV84?t=360); [4 days Body parts split program review, 2020-10](https://youtu.be/sCMGXCXKVjs?t=502); [Why I never deload (and why you shouldn't either), 2022-02](https://youtu.be/BJXFeQWGUuY?t=635); [Your lifting program SUCKS! (Hypertrophy Q&A / Program review), 2024-10](https://youtu.be/c7hl9u3h_s0?t=8149))

<a id="SLP-23"></a>
### SLP-23 · You don't need 100% recovery
- **Statement:** You can retrain before full recovery; a muscle can only be restored to 100%, never beyond, so waiting for or emptying it fully gains nothing, and waiting for 100% pushes people to bro splits. Training early adds fatigue and lengthens the next recovery, a problem only if constant.
- **Numbers:** 90-95% (or 90-100%) recovered is enough; even 20% can still grow.
- **Scope:** Bodybuilders.
- **Confidence:** high — ~5 videos, 2021→2022
- **Status:** contradicted — 2020: training again before full recovery "steals gains" (SLP-24); 2021-22: 20% or 90-95% recovery still grows; reconcilable only as "not constantly".
- **Sources:** ([The Recovery Pot Explained (a complete guide to muscle recuperation), 2021-02](https://youtu.be/p-kR3RfGBHw); [The Recovery Pot Explained (a complete guide to muscle recuperation), 2021-02](https://youtu.be/p-kR3RfGBHw?t=470); [Why I never deload (and why you shouldn't either), 2022-02](https://youtu.be/BJXFeQWGUuY?t=1016); [Jeff Nippard & Alec Enkiri Want Me To Deload... I Don't Wanna (Size vs Strength , 2022-03](https://youtu.be/PuIp9cGKMHo?t=1706))

## The recovery pot

<a id="SLP-30"></a>
### SLP-30 · The recovery pot model
- **Statement:** Training damage drains a recovery pot whose size is your maximum recoverable volume; keep it relatively full and never empty outside a powerlifting peak. Each muscle and tendon has a pot, pots feed each other (legs also drain the lower-back pot), and time spent with the pot low wastes gains.
- **Numbers:** —
- **Scope:** General model.
- **Confidence:** medium — ~3 videos, 2021
- **Status:** current
- **Sources:** ([The Recovery Pot Explained (a complete guide to muscle recuperation), 2021-02](https://youtu.be/p-kR3RfGBHw?t=40); [The Recovery Pot Explained (a complete guide to muscle recuperation), 2021-02](https://youtu.be/p-kR3RfGBHw?t=240); [The Recovery Pot Explained (a complete guide to muscle recuperation), 2021-02](https://youtu.be/p-kR3RfGBHw?t=330); [Fullbody template review, 2021-01](https://youtu.be/G7rVTseabFU?t=1695))

<a id="SLP-31"></a>
### SLP-31 · Spread volume rather than empty the tank
- **Statement:** Several partial drains a week give more quality work than one crash to zero; junk volume is lots of fatigue for little stimulus.
- **Numbers:** Drain to 40 and refill to 100 twice (120 points) beats one 100-to-0 crash; 9 sets once a week drain to zero, 3 sets ×3/week each drain ~30% for roughly double the quality work.
- **Scope:** Frequency design (see ch. 3).
- **Confidence:** medium — ~3 videos, 2022→2025
- **Status:** current
- **Sources:** ([Why I never deload (and why you shouldn't either), 2022-02](https://youtu.be/BJXFeQWGUuY?t=762); [How often should you train for 𝐁𝐎𝐃𝐘𝐁𝐔𝐈𝐋𝐃𝐈𝐍𝐆 , 2022-07](https://youtu.be/iDua_rNsBO8?t=253); [New Hypertrophy Gimmick™ just dropped 🤡, 2025-03](https://youtu.be/ACFKXT44BzM?t=939))

<a id="SLP-32"></a>
### SLP-32 · The CNS bucket holds the muscle buckets
- **Statement:** The big CNS bucket spends more than any muscle but refills no faster, so leave water in the tank; it keeps refilling while you train other muscles, and its capacity is large and trainable.
- **Numbers:** People historically did 8-12 h/day of labour without deloads.
- **Scope:** General model.
- **Confidence:** medium — 1 video, 2022
- **Status:** current
- **Sources:** ([Is CNS fatigue out to get you?, 2022-03](https://youtu.be/NPlGK0-7h0A?t=564); [Is CNS fatigue out to get you?, 2022-03](https://youtu.be/NPlGK0-7h0A?t=813); [Is CNS fatigue out to get you?, 2022-03](https://youtu.be/NPlGK0-7h0A?t=1626))

## Soreness

<a id="SLP-42"></a>
### SLP-42 · Soreness is not a sign of growth
- **Statement:** Soreness isn't a growth signal; strength and tonnage over time are. Constant heavy soreness signals poor adaptation, new programs make you sore from adapting, and trembling or flu-like symptoms aren't growth signs.
- **Numbers:** C tier (2023); last, 10th (2024).
- **Scope:** All trainees.
- **Confidence:** high — ~9 videos, 2020→2024
- **Status:** current
- **Check:** Is the program judged without using soreness as a measure of success?
- **Sources:** ([Hypertrophy Q&A #2, 2020-10](https://youtu.be/MIHPylz3f7Q?t=420); [The issue with HIT (the intensity meme), 2020-11](https://youtu.be/LqsqSGZooR0?t=1150); [The Most IMPORTANT Methods for Muscle Growth (Hypertrophy Tier-List), 2023-11](https://youtu.be/SxqjF2oPasg?t=1385); [Exercise Tier Lists are STUPID, 2024-11](https://youtu.be/6yW3GSskl8g?t=633))

<a id="SLP-43"></a>
### SLP-43 · Soreness should fade with training
- **Statement:** Soreness should fade with training age and frequency; still being routinely sore after 5 years means program hopping, and once-weekly muscles stay unconditioned. Once you reach no-soreness, soreness becomes meaningful.
- **Numbers:** He trains legs every 2 days and is never sore; new high-volume trainees will be sore 4-7 days; 7 days of leg soreness is a bad sign unless a total beginner, so fix frequency.
- **Scope:** Past the beginner stage.

# 5. Exercise selection & technique

This chapter covers how Natural Hypertrophy picks exercises in general (compounds vs isolation, how many lifts, rotations, order, equipment) and how he wants lifts performed (form, spine, tempo, range of motion, cheating, warm-ups) plus the technique of the main lifts, with a cue table at the end. His stance: a small, stable roster of compounds plus serious isolation, chosen to fit your build and trained for months. Every rep should be controlled, aimed at the target muscle and the same from first to last. Over time he moved toward stretch-heavy, stable lifts and strict reps. Which exercise to pick for each body part is in ch. 6; strength-specific programming of the big lifts is in ch. 7.

## Compounds and isolation

Compounds give the tonnage and isolation fills what compounds miss. He counts both as required.

<a id="EXS-01"></a>
### EXS-01 · Compounds plus isolation, neither alone
- **Statement:** A hypertrophy program is compounds for most of the tonnage plus isolation for whatever the compounds miss. Compounds are the "shotgun", isolation the "sniper", and neither works alone.
- **Numbers:** —
- **Scope:** All lifters training for size.
- **Confidence:** high — ~25 videos, 2020→2024
- **Status:** current
- **Check:** Does the program combine compound lifts for most of the tonnage with isolation for the muscles they miss?
- **Sources:** ([Isolation movements benefits： attacking muscles more precisely, 2020-03](https://youtu.be/QwoBxHI7NBU?t=312); [＂Isolation movements are useless because you can't really isolate a muscle＂, 2020-03](https://youtu.be/g4N7gpzHm5k?t=126); [Biomechanics Gurus™ need to 𝚂𝙷𝚄𝚃 𝚄𝙿 about Optimal Training, 2022-10](https://youtu.be/nmgidpn3DNM?t=1516); [Hypertrophy training is CANCELLED, 2024-06](https://youtu.be/jUMmu583w34?t=1420))

- **Numbers:** —
- **Scope:** All; aimed at strength-template followers with small arms.
- **Confidence:** high — ~8 videos, 2021→2024

## How many exercises, variations and rotations

Variety should come from how a few lifts are trained, not from many lifts. Rotations swap close variations for a reason.

<a id="EXS-13"></a>
### EXS-13 · Keep the exercise list short
- **Statement:** Variety comes from what you do with a few lifts, not from many lifts. Too many exercises means each is trained too rarely, technique and tonnage become unstable, and you become "a technician of new tricks rather than a master".
- **Numbers:** 20, 45 or 55 lifts named as too many
- **Scope:** All.
- **Confidence:** high — ~15 videos, 2020→2024
- **Status:** current
- **Check:** Is each muscle trained with a small set of lifts done often enough to progress?
- **Sources:** ([The hypertrophy series： using lifting rotations to maximize quality tonnage, 2020-05](https://youtu.be/uRWgz3nhqds?t=127); [Is shocking the muscle a thing?, 2020-07](https://youtu.be/Zkhc-j-6ptU?t=735); [The Specificity Tree Explained (a complete guide to muscle specialization), 2021-01](https://youtu.be/dyeeKOQJhrM?t=620); [Your lifting program SUCKS! (Hypertrophy Q&A / Program review), 2024-10](https://youtu.be/c7hl9u3h_s0?t=4087))

<a id="EXS-14"></a>
### EXS-14 · Exercise and variation counts by level
- **Statement:** The number of exercises per muscle and variations per lift grows with training age but stays small.
- **Numbers:** 2020: one method keeps a list of 15-20 lifts per body part to choose from. 2022: he rotates 6-7 favourites per muscle; biceps: beginner 1 exercise, NH 4-6. 2023: variations per lift novice 0-1, intermediate 1-2, advanced 3-5, max 5 "hard" variations per pattern. 2024: novices 1-2 exercises per muscle, never more than 4-5; small variations unlimited.
- **Scope:** Novice → advanced.
- **Confidence:** medium — ~6 videos, 2020→2024
- **Status:** current
- **Check:** Does a novice program use 1-2 exercises per muscle (never more than 4-5)?
- **Sources:** ([4 ways to rotate lifts effectively, 2020-05](https://youtu.be/wJTax5ziJUY?t=125); [🌌5 BIG BRAIN TRAINING TIPS TO 🆄🅽🅵🆄🅲🅺 YOUR PROGRAM🧠, 2022-05](https://youtu.be/BW-32tYoNxw?t=759); [How to Keep Growing FOREVER (Unlimited Hypertrophy Method), 2023-07](https://youtu.be/1TKqwXCge9E?t=1960); [Do you look better than Silver Era lifters? (Physique Review LIVE), 2024-12](https://youtu.be/ZLheQPgEfoA?t=1974))

<a id="EXS-15"></a>
### EXS-15 · Hard vs soft variations
- **Statement:** A soft variation keeps the pattern and changes the implement, grip, pause or rep range (near-full carryover, unlimited). A hard variation is a different pattern (pull-up vs pulldown, squat vs leg press), is a new skill, and should be capped. Rotate soft variations to prevent overuse without changing the pattern.
- **Numbers:** max ~5 hard variations
- **Scope:** All, especially intermediate+.
- **Confidence:** high — ~5 videos, 2023→2024
- **Status:** current
- **Sources:** ([How to Keep Growing FOREVER (Unlimited Hypertrophy Method), 2023-07](https://youtu.be/1TKqwXCge9E?t=1899); [How to Keep Growing FOREVER (Unlimited Hypertrophy Method), 2023-07](https://youtu.be/1TKqwXCge9E?t=2273); [Everything I do to get HUGE (Split, Reps, Lifts), 2023-09](https://youtu.be/43F9unmSc_I?t=695); [Your lifting program SUCKS! (Hypertrophy Q&A / Program review), 2024-10](https://youtu.be/c7hl9u3h_s0?t=6814))

<a id="EXS-16"></a>
### EXS-16 · Change a lift only for a reason
- **Statement:** Add or swap a variation only for a reason: a stall despite changing rep ranges, technique, overuse or injury. Never for boredom-driven novelty or to "shock the muscle" (he rates that D tier); constant switching keeps you relearning.
- **Numbers:** —
- **Scope:** All.
- **Confidence:** high — ~12 videos, 2020→2023
- **Status:** current
- **Check:** Does every exercise change have a stated reason (stall, overuse, injury, technique) rather than "muscle confusion"?
- **Sources:** ([The hypertrophy series： shocking the muscle synergistically & optimally, 2020-07](https://youtu.be/FtwMg4iM5kA); [Everything wrong with Online Masculinity and Modern Bodybuilding all in one meat, 2022-02](https://youtu.be/5ANLeP4QvX8?t=1767); [How to Keep Growing FOREVER (Unlimited Hypertrophy Method), 2023-07](https://youtu.be/1TKqwXCge9E?t=1516); [The Ten 𝐋𝐀𝐖𝐒 of HYPERTROPHY (that you MUST break to grow), 2022-08](https://youtu.be/yUecX6qONXg?t=990))

<a id="EXS-17"></a>
### EXS-17 · Rotation options must hit the muscle the same way
- **Statement:** Rotations alternate close variations in one slot (week A / week B). Good pairs: Kroc/Meadows rows, RDL/stiff-leg, V-bar/rope pushdowns, bench/close-grip, dips/pause dips. Bad pairs: bench vs OHP, floor press vs paused bench, deadlift vs RDL, close-grip vs skull crusher, sumo vs conventional deficit. An "or" in his programs means pick one or rotate weekly, never both in one session.
- **Numbers:** —
- **Scope:** All.

## Choosing and dropping lifts

No lift is mandatory; lifts are judged by fit, enjoyment, stretch, stability and stimulus-to-fatigue over months of use.

<a id="EXS-23"></a>
### EXS-23 · No lift is mandatory
- **Statement:** For a bodybuilder every lift, including squat, bench and deadlift, can be replaced by another in the same pattern. If a lift hurts after a fair try, plenty of others do the job.
- **Numbers:** —
- **Scope:** Bodybuilders; powerlifters must do competition lifts.
- **Confidence:** high — ~12 videos, 2020→2024
- **Status:** current
- **Sources:** ([Any movement with a pain byproduct is a bad exercise (for you), 2020-02](https://youtu.be/Eh0fnXIyDMc?t=188); [Make training fun again, 2021-05](https://youtu.be/0RoULYC_tao?t=188); [No such thing as a dangerous lift (the good morning example), 2021-04](https://youtu.be/sFMQj4Lflk0?t=756); [So you think you look good? - **Statement:** Leverages, height and mobility decide which lifts suit you; the program adapts to the lifter. Drop lifts that don't suit you instead of clinging to them (sunk cost).
- **Numbers:** —
- **Scope:** All; tall lifters often do better with sumo, low-bar to parallel, RDL/stiff-leg, block pulls, OHP.
- **Confidence:** high — ~10 videos, 2020→2024
- **Status:** current
- **Check:** Were the main lifts chosen to suit the lifter's build and pain-free history?

- **Statement:** Start a new lift light and judge it only after training it seriously for about three months, by progress rather than feel; allow a tuning phase. Only program lifts you have done regularly for 3+ months. Keep a ranked list of lifts done, a "to try" list and an "exercise graveyard".

- **Statement:** His criteria: stretch under load, high stability, good stimulus-to-fatigue (judged per target muscle), low cardio cost, quick setup, and progressable. A lift without a stretch can't rank above "decent"; if form breaks as soon as you load it, it's useless for hypertrophy.
- **Numbers:** setup under ~3 min or it gets skipped
- **Scope:** All, 2023-24 framework.
- **Confidence:** high — ~8 videos, 2020→2024
- **Status:** current

## What good form is

Technique is how tonnage gets directed into the target muscle. Form rules exist, but they adapt to the individual.

<a id="TEC-01"></a>
### TEC-01 · Bodybuilding form: target, pain-free, reproducible
- **Statement:** Good bodybuilding form targets the intended muscle, is pain-free and is reproducible every rep; how much you lift is not a criterion. It may mean lifting less at first, but it recovers better and correlates with long-term progress.
- **Numbers:** —
- **Scope:** Bodybuilders.
- **Confidence:** high — ~8 videos, 2020→2023
- **Status:** current
- **Check:** Is every rep aimed at the target muscle, pain-free and repeatable?
- **Sources:** ([The training principles series： good form, 2020-02](https://youtu.be/M-a4cj1yFX8); [How to deadlift to maximize muscle growth and minimize injury risks, 2021-03](https://youtu.be/FIaOVjDHT4k?t=590); [Surviving Novice Syndrome (a beginner's guide to lifting), 2021-08](https://youtu.be/9mnLRQsrs9k?t=2965); [Training for Aesthetics： You're doing it WRONG., 2023-05](https://youtu.be/Zqv7KVsmu78?t=632))

<a id="TEC-02"></a>
### TEC-02 · Execution is half the result
- **Statement:** Execution is about half of results and programming the other half; a great program executed badly won't deliver. Form is "mandatory" to lift for years without setbacks.
- **Numbers:** ~50% execution / 50% programming
- **Scope:** All.
- **Confidence:** high — ~3 videos, 2020→2024
- **Status:** current
- **Sources:** ([Can injuries be attributed to bad luck?, 2020-04](https://youtu.be/qqAw6s-_l3o?t=74); [Training for Aesthetics： You're doing it WRONG., 2023-05](https://youtu.be/Zqv7KVsmu78); [Judging and Grading every Fitness Channel (Sam Sulek, Max Euceda, Lex Little), 2024-01](https://youtu.be/jDk3LytTEjA?t=2459))

<a id="TEC-03"></a>
### TEC-03 · Technique sits between load and range
- **Statement:** Technique is S tier because it directs stress to the muscle, but it is individual. His 2024 order: load as the precondition, then technique, range of motion and tempo; time under tension is just a by-product of tempo.
- **Numbers:** —
- **Scope:** All.
- **Confidence:** medium — ~3 videos, 2023→2024
- **Status:** current
- **Sources:** ([The Most IMPORTANT Methods for Muscle Growth (Hypertrophy Tier-List), 2023-11](https://youtu.be/SxqjF2oPasg?t=2644); [What everyone gets WRONG about Range of Motion, 2023-03](https://youtu.be/1apseBbt0-o?t=124); [New hypertrophy study just dropped (And Basically You're F＊cking Stupid), 2024-01](https://youtu.be/vVQmYGw7Kj8?t=1074))
