## Form breakdown, load and ego lifting

<a id="TEC-14"></a>
### TEC-14 · The last rep looks like the first
- **Statement:** Bodybuilders own technique from the first rep to the last: the 10th rep looks as crisp as the first, only slower. Near failure only speed changes, never form. Form breakdown is acceptable in strength sport, not for size.
- **Numbers:** —
- **Scope:** Bodybuilders.
- **Confidence:** high — ~5 videos, 2020→2025
- **Status:** current
- **Check:** Does the last rep of a set look like the first, only slower?
- **Sources:** ([Where Snap City occurs, 2020-12](https://youtu.be/UzTfF1VduxM?t=320); [When Snap City occurs, 2021-03](https://youtu.be/Z35bJjrc_MY?t=64); [The hypertrophy series： handling lower body volume & intensity, 2020-08](https://youtu.be/pUpQypTV3Ck?t=61); [10 years of lifting for this (Hypertrophy Log #10), 2025-01](https://youtu.be/waeSP7DBmig?t=730))

<a id="TEC-15"></a>
### TEC-15 · Avoid mechanical failure
- **Statement:** Mechanical failure (your structure gives out before the muscle) is bad mainly because tonnage stops going to the target. You want to be limited by the muscle, never by structure. It comes from fixable weak links: thoracic extension, setup, technique (e.g. good-morning squats, hips shooting up on deadlifts).
- **Numbers:** —
- **Scope:** All.
- **Confidence:** high — ~6 videos, 2020→2022
- **Status:** current
- **Sources:** ([The hypertrophy series： mechanical vs muscular fatigue, 2020-06](https://youtu.be/T_ZMmSNmLbs?t=63); [The hypertrophy series： mechanical vs muscular fatigue, 2020-06](https://youtu.be/T_ZMmSNmLbs?t=381); [Using the lower back as a bridge (the new lift with your legs), 2020-12](https://youtu.be/QLUXXk0OtX4?t=438); [The Hypertrophy Iceberg Explained (a complete guide to muscle growth), 2021-07](https://youtu.be/8ELQ2XZgpls?t=975))

<a id="TEC-16"></a>
### TEC-16 · Artificial vs organic mechanical failure
- **Statement:** "Artificial" mechanical failure (bad technique or bar placement) is correctable. "Organic" mechanical failure is a deliberately weak position (e.g. a crane-style stiff-leg with the bar near the toes) used to fail the target sooner.
- **Numbers:** —
- **Scope:** Advanced.
- **Confidence:** low — 1 video, 2020
- **Status:** current
- **Sources:** ([The hypertrophy series： artificial vs organical failure, 2020-07](https://youtu.be/zyjCsFRlBT0?t=316); [The hypertrophy series： artificial vs organical failure, 2020-07](https://youtu.be/zyjCsFRlBT0?t=381))

<a id="TEC-17"></a>
### TEC-17 · Weight selection makes or breaks form
- **Statement:** Structural integrity comes mostly from weight selection: perfect form at 400 lb can fall apart at 450. Good technique won't save a bad loading decision, and "there is no bad form" ignores this.
- **Numbers:** 400 vs 450 lb example
- **Scope:** All.
- **Confidence:** medium — ~3 videos, 2020→2021
- **Status:** current
- **Sources:** ([Programming for people with limited mobility, 2020-11](https://youtu.be/sK78-yohV1s?t=857); [Why do injuries happen?, 2020-07](https://youtu.be/rsbqqfM6ZFM?t=189); [When Snap City occurs, 2021-03](https://youtu.be/Z35bJjrc_MY?t=64))

<a id="TEC-18"></a>
### TEC-18 · Stop when form starts to break
- **Statement:** If you sense form breaking, stop and put the bar down. If a squat rep would turn into a good morning or the hips shoot up, rack it and keep that rep in reserve for a later exercise.
- **Numbers:** —
- **Scope:** All, especially squat and deadlift.
- **Confidence:** medium — ~3 videos, 2020→2023
- **Status:** current
- **Sources:** ([Natural Hypertrophy： my lifting philosophy, 2020-01](https://youtu.be/IR-YS-TGGx0?t=251); [3 YEARS WITHOUT INJURIES： How I bulletproofed myself (and how you can do it too), 2022-06](https://youtu.be/qrBLykvU_EE?t=629); [Training for Aesthetics： You're doing it WRONG., 2023-05](https://youtu.be/Zqv7KVsmu78?t=759))

<a id="TEC-19"></a>
### TEC-19 · Ego lifting defined
- **Statement:** Ego lifting is using more weight than the exercise can turn into a justified stimulus; cutting range to lift more counts. "If 10 lb dumbbells challenge you, use them." Accusing others of ego lifting often reveals insecurity.

## Spine, posture and bracing

<a id="TEC-25"></a>
### TEC-25 · No lumbar flexion under load
- **Statement:** Any lumbar flexion under load is form breakdown and wrong for bodybuilders. It is a correctable flaw, not inevitable, and it also kills leg drive. Anyone without a severe spinal condition can find a variation with a fully neutral back.
- **Numbers:** —
- **Scope:** All loaded squats, hinges and rows.
- **Confidence:** high — ~5 videos, 2020→2022
- **Status:** current
- **Check:** Does the lower back stay neutral on every loaded squat, hinge and row rep?
- **Sources:** ([Using the lower back as a bridge (the new lift with your legs), 2020-12](https://youtu.be/QLUXXk0OtX4?t=562); [Using the lower back as a bridge (the new lift with your legs), 2020-12](https://youtu.be/QLUXXk0OtX4?t=374); [Using the lower back as a bridge (the new lift with your legs), 2020-12](https://youtu.be/QLUXXk0OtX4?t=940); [𝙃𝙊𝙍𝙍𝙄𝙁𝙄𝘾 𝙡𝙞𝙛𝙩𝙞𝙣𝙜 𝙞𝙣𝙟𝙪, 2022-08](https://youtu.be/yoROLGGUPXU?t=1380))

<a id="TEC-26"></a>
### TEC-26 · The lower back is a bridge, not a crane
- **Statement:** The lower back is a rigid, neutral bridge between legs and upper body; only its angle changes during a rep, never its flexion. The legs produce the power. Lower-back pain the day after deadlifts means you aren't pulling with the legs.
- **Numbers:** —
- **Scope:** All.
- **Confidence:** high — ~7 videos, 2020→2022
- **Status:** current
- **Sources:** ([Using the lower back as a bridge (the new lift with your legs), 2020-12](https://youtu.be/QLUXXk0OtX4?t=689); [How to avoid hamstring pulls during deadlifts, 2020-11](https://youtu.be/YtNUZjBxdtE?t=450); [How to deadlift to maximize muscle growth and minimize injury risks, 2021-03](https://youtu.be/FIaOVjDHT4k?t=40); [Level up your legs, 2021-06](https://youtu.be/ANvvVrMqF7Y?t=2504))

<a id="TEC-27"></a>
### TEC-27 · Upper-back rounding is tolerable, but drags the lower back
- **Statement:** Thoracic rounding is less dangerous than lumbar rounding and acceptable in some contexts, but it tends to pull the lower back into rounding. The spine follows the neck: head down starts the chain.
- **Numbers:** —
- **Scope:** All.
- **Confidence:** high — ~6 videos, 2020→2024

### TEC-28 · Rounding is usually not a choice
- **Statement:** On squats and deadlifts the back usually rounds because the body can't stay upright and reshapes around the bar on the positive. It is a technique and intention issue more than weak muscles; causes include weak core, glutes or thoracic extension, setup and poor cues.

- **Statement:** The torso can be angled, even horizontal as in Pendlay rows, as long as the spine stays straight. The more the torso leans forward, the more potential for rounding.

<a id="TEC-34"></a>

- **Statement:** A negative that gravity does for you doesn't count; resist it. "The weight should not lead you." Cables and machines invite dropping it; free weights force control.

- **Scope:** All lifts except the deadlift (TEC-87).
- **Confidence:** high — ~10 videos, 2020→2024
- **Status:** current
- **Check:** Is the eccentric of every rep (deadlifts excepted) controlled rather than dropped?

## Range of motion and partials

<a id="TEC-45"></a>
### TEC-45 · ROM is distance under load, relative to leverages
- **Statement:** For hypertrophy, range of motion is how far the load travels under tension, and it depends on leverages; there is no objective "full ROM" (standards come from competition). A tall lifter's parallel squat can travel more than a short lifter's ass-to-grass.
- **Numbers:** —
- **Scope:** All.
- **Confidence:** high — ~7 videos, 2020→2023
- **Status:** current
- **Sources:** ([The training principles series： full range of motion, 2020-04](https://youtu.be/-wk3jSpm434); [The training principles series： full range of motion, 2020-04](https://youtu.be/-wk3jSpm434?t=65); [The form p＊lice is under arrest, 2021-07](https://youtu.be/GH8tqzGTgH8?t=829); [What everyone gets WRONG about Range of Motion, 2023-03](https://youtu.be/1apseBbt0-o?t=439))

<a id="TEC-46"></a>
### TEC-46 · Full range by default, within comfort
- **Statement:** Longer range generally means more hypertrophy (more stretch, more travel), so full range is the default, but use the range you can do comfortably and sustainably. Trimming a little barely matters; keep at least one full-range leg lift.
- **Numbers:** —
- **Scope:** All.
- **Confidence:** high — ~7 videos, 2020→2024
- **Status:** current
- **Check:** Is full range (or lengthened-biased range) the default for the main lifts?
- **Sources:** ([The training principles series： full range of motion, 2020-04](https://youtu.be/-wk3jSpm434?t=381); [Should you lock out your lifts?, 2020-10](https://youtu.be/iEKSZ806mrc?t=790); [The Ten 𝐋𝐀𝐖𝐒 of HYPERTROPHY (that you MUST break to grow), 2022-08](https://youtu.be/yUecX6qONXg?t=634); [New hypertrophy study just dropped (And Basically You're F＊cking Stupid), 2024-01](https://youtu.be/vVQmYGw7Kj8?t=380))

<a id="TEC-47"></a>
### TEC-47 · Effective range is what counts
- **Statement:** What matters is the part of the range where the target is under the most stress; extra range only helps if the load challenges the muscle through it.
- **Numbers:** pullover example: ~30% effective, trimmed to 70-80% effective
- **Scope:** All.
- **Confidence:** medium — ~3 videos, 2023
- **Status:** current
- **Sources:** ([What everyone gets WRONG about Range of Motion, 2023-03](https://youtu.be/1apseBbt0-o?t=565); [What everyone gets WRONG about Range of Motion, 2023-03](https://youtu.be/1apseBbt0-o?t=1761); [What everyone gets WRONG about Range of Motion, 2023-03](https://youtu.be/1apseBbt0-o?t=1887); [The ULTIMATE Abs Exercises Tier-List (Greek God-tier to Scrawny-tier), 2023-06](https://youtu.be/JSOvpTDcSvA?t=943))

<a id="TEC-48"></a>
### TEC-48 · Range dictates load, never the reverse
- **Statement:** "Let ROM dictate the load, never the load dictate the ROM." There are two valid reasons to limit range: more target recruitment, or better performance (tempo, load, reps). Cutting range to add weight usually removes the most stimulating part.
- **Numbers:** if a shallower squat allows more than ~20% extra load vs below parallel, you cut too much
- **Scope:** All.

## Lockout and the top squeeze

<a id="TEC-56"></a>
### TEC-56 · The lockout adds almost nothing
- **Statement:** At lockout the joints are stacked and the skeleton holds the load, so it contributes almost nothing to hypertrophy (C tier). Lockout and depth standards exist for judging; "joints are meant to lock" is an appeal to nature.
- **Numbers:** ~1% of hypertrophy; ~2% extra triceps work on OHP
- **Scope:** All except deadlift (TEC-86).
- **Confidence:** high — ~7 videos, 2020→2023
- **Status:** current
- **Sources:** ([Should you lock out your lifts?, 2020-10](https://youtu.be/iEKSZ806mrc?t=188); [Should you lock out your lifts?, 2020-10](https://youtu.be/iEKSZ806mrc?t=63); [The form p＊lice is under arrest, 2021-07](https://youtu.be/GH8tqzGTgH8?t=2894); [What everyone gets WRONG about Range of Motion, 2023-03](https://youtu.be/1apseBbt0-o?t=1322))

<a id="TEC-57"></a>
### TEC-57 · Lock out only when it helps
- **Statement:** Lock out if it keeps you in the groove, is pain-free and earns more reps or load; skip it if it throws off technique or hurts. Never locking out "to keep tension" can reduce total tension if it costs reps. Lock out dips for stability.
- **Numbers:** —
- **Scope:** All.
- **Confidence:** high — ~4 videos, 2020→2024
- **Status:** current
- **Sources:** ([Should you lock out your lifts?, 2020-10](https://youtu.be/iEKSZ806mrc?t=568); [Should you lock out your lifts?, 2020-10](https://youtu.be/iEKSZ806mrc?t=590); [What everyone gets WRONG about Range of Motion, 2023-03](https://youtu.be/1apseBbt0-o?t=1635); [Your lifting program SUCKS! (Hypertrophy Q&A / Program review), 2024-10](https://youtu.be/c7hl9u3h_s0?t=1523))

<a id="TEC-58"></a>
### TEC-58 · The top squeeze is low value
- **Statement:** Squeezing at the top is C/D tier: the muscle is least active there, and removing it doesn't reduce growth. A squeeze only helps you feel the muscle; holding lockout for 2 s is just resting, and thrusting the hips at the top of a squat or deadlift does nothing.
- **Numbers:** —
- **Scope:** All.
- **Confidence:** high — ~6 videos, 2020→2024
- **Status:** changed — 2020: squeeze at the top (slow curl positives for the squeeze; on calf raises the squeeze matters more than the stretch); 2021-24: the squeeze gives no tension, C/D tier.

<a id="TEC-60"></a>

- **Statement:** Pause until momentum is gone, keeping the stretch, with no rocking or heaving; no 20 s pauses. Pauses add a small stretched-tension bonus, not a major driver.

- **Scope:** Paused work.

- **Statement:** Pause reps (B tier) clean up form, protect the red zone and cure fear of the hole, but the stretch reflex adds hypertrophy, so use them sparingly. Pause squat is the best paused lift, paused bench second (a lifesaver for shoulder pain); pause without pins to keep control.

## Mind-muscle connection

### TEC-68 · What mind-muscle connection is
- **Statement:** Mind-muscle connection is the ability to prioritise a target within a compound so stronger muscles don't take the work: feeling fibres stretch and contract, not the pump. Pump doesn't prove a muscle worked, nor does its absence prove it didn't.

- **Scope:** All.
- **Confidence:** medium — ~3 videos, 2020

Warm-up reps use the same tempo and technique as top sets and are the place to fix technique (e.g. spotting too much lower back at 135).

<a id="TEC-91"></a>
### TEC-91 · Straps, not mixed grip
- **Statement:** Bodybuilders pull double overhand until grip fails, then strap up. Mixed grip creates imbalance and biceps-tear risk, and hook and mixed grips exist for competition (one deadlift video calls hook grip acceptable). Never mixed grip with straps or on shrugs/rows.

## Deadlift technique

The deadlift is a leg-driven pull with a rigid back, done positive-only. Its place in his programs is covered in ch. 7.

<a id="TEC-96"></a>
### TEC-96 · The legs move the deadlift
- **Statement:** The deadlift is "a leg press against the floor" with the back as a rigid bridge: neutral spine, very deep hips, knee flexion, strong hip drive. "Lift with your legs" is a poor cue because you always do; the problem is overusing the lower back.
- **Numbers:** —
- **Scope:** All floor pulls.
- **Confidence:** high — ~8 videos, 2020→2021
- **Status:** current
- **Sources:** ([Using the lower back as a bridge (the new lift with your legs), 2020-12](https://youtu.be/QLUXXk0OtX4?t=62); [Using the lower back as a bridge (the new lift with your legs), 2020-12](https://youtu.be/QLUXXk0OtX4?t=124); [Lower back rounding： The Good, the Bad and the Ugly, 2020-09](https://youtu.be/rIngKQqTJMs?t=1190); [How to deadlift to maximize muscle growth and minimize injury risks, 2021-03](https://youtu.be/FIaOVjDHT4k?t=560))

<a id="TEC-97"></a>
### TEC-97 · Deadlift setup
- **Statement:** Bar over the whole foot, close to but not touching the shins. Bend the knees slightly, push the butt back and reach, then pull yourself into position so the hamstrings are tense, take the slack out, shoulders over the bar. Torso between vertical and horizontal, never parallel. Dragging the bar up the shins means you sat back too much; shoulders behind the bar means you're squatting it.
- **Numbers:** —
- **Scope:** Conventional deadlift.
- **Confidence:** high — ~5 videos, 2020→2021
- **Status:** current
- **Sources:** ([How to deadlift to maximize muscle growth and minimize injury risks, 2021-03](https://youtu.be/FIaOVjDHT4k?t=150); [How to deadlift to maximize muscle growth and minimize injury risks, 2021-03](https://youtu.be/FIaOVjDHT4k?t=251); [Properly applying the protective and hypertrophic properties of lower body movem, 2020-10](https://youtu.be/u9OoRQOC3G0?t=757); [Can lift variations/accessories affect your form on the main lifts?, 2020-03](https://youtu.be/_iaU9_rM1QQ?t=185))

<a id="TEC-98"></a>
### TEC-98 · Patient off the floor
- **Statement:** Break the bar from the floor with steadily increasing leg pressure and a neutral spine, not "grip and rip". The bar leaves slowly but never slows down, and everything locks out together. People bend over to fake explosiveness off the floor.
- **Numbers:** —
- **Scope:** All floor pulls.
- **Confidence:** medium — ~3 videos, 2020→2021
- **Status:** current
- **Sources:** ([The most common deadlift form mistake (fishing rod syndrome), 2020-02](https://youtu.be/iY2uzM3vlBA?t=318); [⚠️ Don't make this mistake ⚠️, 2021-09](https://youtu.be/twEeL-z4Zug?t=1082); [⚠️ Don't make this mistake ⚠️, 2021-09](https://youtu.be/twEeL-z4Zug?t=1333); [Lower back rounding： The Good, the Bad and the Ugly, 2020-09](https://youtu.be/rIngKQqTJMs?t=1634))

<a id="TEC-99"></a>
### TEC-99 · The "fishing rod" deadlift
- **Statement:** When the knees lock early with a rounded back, the legs leave the lift and the back finishes it, causing the struggle past the knees. Most people who fail at the knee have a setup problem, not a strength problem.
- **Numbers:** —
- **Scope:** Floor pulls.
- **Confidence:** high — ~5 videos, 2020→2021
- **Status:** current
- **Sources:** ([Lower back rounding： The Good, the Bad and the Ugly, 2020-09](https://youtu.be/rIngKQqTJMs?t=1570); [The most common deadlift form mistake (fishing rod syndrome), 2020-02](https://youtu.be/iY2uzM3vlBA?t=126); [Using the lower back as a bridge (the new lift with your legs), 2020-12](https://youtu.be/QLUXXk0OtX4?t=814); [Conventional VS Sumo VS Trap bar： Which deadlift style is best for you?, 2021-08](https://youtu.be/lG5SZbRdOjA?t=689))

<a id="TEC-100"></a>
### TEC-100 · No rounded-back deadlifting
- **Statement:** No one benefits from a rounded lower back on deadlifts; it is defensible only for elite lifters or a competition PR. Olympic lifters who round do so deliberately with light, controllable weight. Abort the pull if the back rounds.
- **Numbers:** —
- **Scope:** All non-elite lifters.
- **Confidence:** high — ~5 videos, 2020→2021

<a id="TEC-101"></a>
### TEC-101 · Full deadlift lockout
- **Statement:** Unlike other lifts, the deadlift locks out fully: hips, knees and shoulders together with a neutral spine. No leaning back, hip thrusting or hyperextension. A soft lockout usually means thoracic rounding.
- **Numbers:** —
- **Scope:** Deadlift.
- **Confidence:** high — ~6 videos, 2020→2021
- **Status:** current

<a id="TEC-102"></a>
### TEC-102 · Deadlifts are positive-only
- **Statement:** Don't fight the deadlift negative: put the bar down and reset. Slow negatives tire you and sandbag the positive; a controlled negative gives slightly more hypertrophy, but the concentric-only puller gets more reps and fewer injuries. Use RDLs for eccentric work; no touch-and-go.
- **Numbers:** 4 s negatives wreck a novice's core within 3 reps
- **Scope:** Deadlift (not RDL).
- **Confidence:** high — ~5 videos, 2020→2022

<a id="TEC-103"></a>
### TEC-103 · Low deadlift reps because structure fails first
- **Statement:** Keep deadlift sets low-rep: at high reps thoracic extension gives out before the legs, so 15-rep deadlifts are junk volume. With shaky form, do a few sets of 4-5 and add weight only when confident. Place deadlifts early, not at the end of back day.
- **Numbers:** 4-6 reps max, stop around 5-6; shaky form 2-3×4-5
- **Scope:** Conventional deadlift.
- **Confidence:** medium — ~4 videos, 2020
- **Status:** current

<a id="TEC-104"></a>
### TEC-104 · Pick a variation that keeps the back neutral
- **Statement:** If the floor is a problem, choose a stance or variation that allows a neutral back: sumo, trap bar, blocks/rack (max work off blocks, submax from the floor). No cat-back floor pulls; behind-the-back deadlifts not recommended. Deadlift range is arbitrary anyway (set by plate diameter).

- **Scope:** Lifters who can't pull neutral from the floor.

<a id="TEC-105"></a>
### TEC-105 · How deadlift variations differ
- **Statement:** Variations differ in torso angle and knee and hip flexion, and torso angle plus knee flexion decide what's trained. Sumo's sticking point is off the floor, conventional's near lockout; the trap bar has more quad drive.
- **Numbers:** —
- **Scope:** Floor pulls.
- **Confidence:** medium — ~4 videos, 2020→2021
- **Status:** current

<a id="TEC-106"></a>
### TEC-106 · Deadlift odds and ends
- **Statement:** Learn leg drive with submaximal conventional deficit deadlifts for about 10 reps, and finish deadlift day with light hyperextensions. No heeled shoes for floor pulls (they add a deficit). If the hips shift, move one foot slightly out; a staggered stance only matters if it hurts.

- **Scope:** Floor pulls.

## Squat technique

<a id="TEC-108"></a>
### TEC-108 · Squat with the knees first
- **Statement:** The squat is knee flexion first: break at the knees and let the hips hinge naturally at depth (limit it, don't resist it). Hinging first turns it into a good morning. Torso angle changes come from the hip, never spinal flexion, and should match on the way down and up.
- **Numbers:** —
- **Scope:** All squats.
- **Confidence:** high — ~6 videos, 2020→2021
- **Status:** current
- **Sources:** ([Properly applying the protective and hypertrophic properties of lower body movem, 2020-10](https://youtu.be/u9OoRQOC3G0?t=632); [How to squat to maximize muscle growth and minimize injury risks, 2021-07](https://youtu.be/3bEkmyM8NBQ?t=61); [Using the lower back as a bridge (the new lift with your legs), 2020-12](https://youtu.be/QLUXXk0OtX4?t=689); [Hypertrophy Q&A #3, 2020-11](https://youtu.be/6sFaB3rAY1A?t=64))

<a id="TEC-109"></a>
### TEC-109 · The good-morning squat is the cardinal fault
- **Statement:** When the hips rise first and the squat becomes a good morning, the tonnage number stays the same but the lower back takes the load instead of the quads, and it leads to injury. Fix it with technique, thoracic extension, core and glute work and 1 s paused squats, not a box.
- **Numbers:** 1 s pause squats
- **Scope:** All squats.
- **Confidence:** high — ~6 videos, 2020→2022
- **Status:** current
- **Check:** Do squat reps rise with chest and hips together rather than turning into a good morning?
- **Sources:** ([The hypertrophy series： using mind muscle connection for tonnage quality control, 2020-06](https://youtu.be/Hn3oGdUUhic?t=64); [The utility of lifting gear, 2020-08](https://youtu.be/f_ElXUd7LHE?t=56); [Why Novices shouldn't do Box Squats, 2021-01](https://youtu.be/bTin_tBGoVo?t=676); [Biomechanics Gurus™ need to 𝚂𝙷𝚄𝚃 𝚄𝙿 about Optimal Training, 2022-10](https://youtu.be/nmgidpn3DNM?t=380))

<a id="TEC-110"></a>
### TEC-110 · Knee-dominant stance for size
- **Statement:** For size keep the squat knee-dominant: medium-to-narrow stance, toes forward, knees allowed forward (knees past toes is fine); heel elevation or a slant board helps. Very wide stances raise the number but cut quad work, and a copied wide, toes-out stance repeatedly injured him.
- **Numbers:** —
- **Scope:** Hypertrophy squatting.
- **Confidence:** high — ~7 videos, 2020→2024
- **Status:** changed — 2020: slightly wider stance with knees out spares the knee; 2021-24: narrow/medium stance, toes forward, knees forward.
- **Sources:** ([Curing patellar tendinitis (part. 2)： Rehab & precautions, 2020-05](https://youtu.be/vHf2ZoHWHQs?t=690); [How to do squats for SIZE, 2022-09](https://youtu.be/XAcv427WvMw?t=300); [Your lifting program SUCKS! (Hypertrophy Q&A / Program review), 2024-10](https://youtu.be/c7hl9u3h_s0?t=951); [How I Built Monster Legs, 2024-12](https://youtu.be/-OjJEzZTXtQ?t=190))

<a id="TEC-111"></a>
### TEC-111 · Squat depth
- **Statement:** Squat as deep as you can without back or knee pain or butt wink (a "power leak"); stop before it. Parallel or a hair below is a fine heavy standard, the last few inches add little, and quarter squats stress the knees and grow nothing. Safety and repeatability beat depth.
- **Numbers:** parallel or slightly below
- **Scope:** All squats.
- **Confidence:** high — ~10 videos, 2020→2024
- **Status:** current
- **Sources:** ([Hypertrophy Q&A #3, 2020-11](https://youtu.be/6sFaB3rAY1A?t=190); [Injury Q&A #4, 2021-06](https://youtu.be/9kIIW251uiI?t=2390); [How to do squats for SIZE, 2022-09](https://youtu.be/XAcv427WvMw?t=813); [Don't be THAT GUY in 2024, 2024-01](https://youtu.be/uOAia_t5c_I?t=564))

<a id="TEC-112"></a>
### TEC-112 · Quads are stretched below parallel
- **Statement:** Quads keep stretching below parallel; the idea that quads only need a short range is a myth. Graduate to free squats once you can go below parallel, since half squats shear the knee.
- **Numbers:** —
- **Scope:** All squats.
- **Confidence:** low — ~2 videos, 2020
- **Status:** current
- **Sources:** ([Hypertrophy Q&A #3, 2020-11](https://youtu.be/6sFaB3rAY1A?t=163); [Curing patellar tendinitis (part. 2)： Rehab & precautions, 2020-05](https://youtu.be/vHf2ZoHWHQs?t=753))

<a id="TEC-113"></a>
### TEC-113 · Controlled descent, no dive-bombing
- **Statement:** Control the descent; never dive-bomb (patellar tendinitis, knees shooting forward). The bottom should feel rock solid, like sitting; reverse with a controlled bounce, practised light.
- **Numbers:** —
- **Scope:** All squats.
- **Confidence:** high — ~6 videos, 2020→2024
- **Status:** current
- **Sources:** ([Curing patellar tendinitis (part. 2)： Rehab & precautions, 2020-05](https://youtu.be/vHf2ZoHWHQs?t=501); [Hypertrophy Q&A #3, 2020-11](https://youtu.be/6sFaB3rAY1A?t=241); [How to use pause reps for SIZE, 2021-05](https://youtu.be/MP01uQbcoLc?t=374); [Bodybuilding is killing me (Hypertrophy Log #8), 2024-09](https://youtu.be/JW73oft8Q60?t=720))

<a id="TEC-114"></a>
### TEC-114 · Bar and upper back on the back squat
- **Statement:** No pad: the bar sits tight on the skin. Use as narrow a grip as you can to pack the upper back (narrow it set by set in warm-ups), never relax thoracic extension, and drive the bar into the traps out of the hole. Grip width still depends on proportions; pad pain fades within 2 weeks to 2 months.
- **Numbers:** —
- **Scope:** Back squat.
- **Confidence:** medium — ~5 videos, 2020→2021
- **Status:** current

### TEC-115 · Unrack and walk out
- **Statement:** Unrack from directly under the bar with minimal knee bend and walk out in about four steps, widening into your stance.

### TEC-116 · High bar vs low bar
- **Statement:** Try both. Low bar suits tall, lanky lifters (bar over midfoot, back a rigid bridge); high bar suits heeled shoes and knee flexion. On low bar use a thumbless grip and press up from under the bar to spare the wrists.

### TEC-117 · Box squats don't fix squats
- **Statement:** On a box most people sit back, rock and good-morning up; the box catches you where the squat gets hard and reinforces forward lean. If used, go straight down and up. Touch-and-go SSB box squats are fine for glutes.

<a id="TEC-118"></a>
### TEC-118 · No knee valgus
- **Statement:** Push the knees out and press through the whole foot. Valgus may be acceptable for a one-rep max athlete but harms tendons over a bodybuilder's many reps; light paused or higher-rep squats help control it.

### TEC-119 · Front squat is a rack-and-thoracic lift
- **Statement:** Most front squatters (he says 80%) are limited by thoracic extension and the rack, not the legs; the lift fails when the bar dumps. Elbows high, wrists not cocked back, fingers only stop the roll (a three-finger grip is fine), torso upright. It took him about two years to learn, and he'd tell his past self not to bother.

- **Statement:** The SSB pushes you forward (the opposite of a front squat), taxing the posterior chain. Never use your normal working weight the first time, and don't flip the bar.

- **Statement:** Smith machine squats are S tier with feet and hips forward, since the machine replaces the hip hinge; don't copy free-weight form on it, and novices should learn free squats. Belt squats: close stance, vertical torso, knees forward, heels elevated, not too low; wide toes-out stance is misuse.

### TEC-122 · Split squats for quads vs glutes
- **Statement:** For quads: front foot close, knee travelling past the toes and tracking the foot, foot straight, slow reps unless you're an athlete. For glutes: front foot further out and the torso leaning onto the thigh as you descend. Prefer split squats to lunges.

## Pressing technique

<a id="TEC-123"></a>
### TEC-123 · Bench: shoulder safety first
- **Statement:** On bench, protect the shoulders first: arch, shoulders back and tight, leg drive, elbows tucked not flared. The arch shortens the range and keeps the shoulders "in the pocket"; leg drive adds stability, not magic force. He avoids feet-up bench.
- **Numbers:** —
- **Scope:** Barbell bench.
- **Confidence:** high — ~7 videos, 2020→2022
- **Status:** current
- **Check:** Is the bench done with shoulders set back and down and elbows tucked?

Grip slightly wider than the shoulders; parallel bars are most shoulder-friendly. Lock out at the top for stability.

## Pulling technique

<a id="TEC-137"></a>
### TEC-137 · Pull with the back, arms are hooks
- **Statement:** Rows and pulls are done with the back; the arms are hooks, and the back moves and stretches with the weight. Arm-only rowing is a hammer curl.
- **Numbers:** —
- **Scope:** All pulls.
- **Confidence:** high — ~6 videos, 2020→2024
- **Status:** current

<a id="TEC-138"></a>
### TEC-138 · Let the shoulder blades travel on rows
- **Statement:** On rows let the scapulae protract so the back gets stretched; the bottom stretch matters most and pulling all the way back can be counterproductive. Constant "shoulders back" is the wrong cue for rows (pull-ups keep scapular engagement).
- **Numbers:** —
- **Scope:** Rows.
- **Confidence:** high — ~7 videos, 2020→2024
- **Status:** changed — 2020-21: retract the scapulae, novices fail by not retracting; 2024: protraction for the stretch matters more.
- **Check:** Do rows let the shoulder blades move forward into a stretch at the bottom?
- **Sources:** ([Fierce 5 novice program review (from an hypertrophy standpoint), 2020-02](https://youtu.be/OATtf3kPtdI?t=439); [Dumbbell rows Tutorial for a Bigger Back, 2020-12](https://youtu.be/YDTUYiKFcFo?t=440); [Arnold trained like an idiot?, 2024-04](https://youtu.be/-OYtq2AHGX8?t=193); [How to get buff GF (Dating & Relationships Q&A), 2024-11](https://youtu.be/o40xCjIzl14?t=278))

<a id="TEC-139"></a>
### TEC-139 · A row is a held deadlift position
- **Statement:** On bent-over rows the hamstrings, glutes and lower back hold rigid while the back pulls; floor or touch-and-go rows drift into hip hinges (his own cheat rows turned into RDLs). Novices who can't deadlift can't row safely.
- **Numbers:** —
- **Scope:** Bent-over rows.
- **Confidence:** high — ~6 videos, 2020→2023

### TEC-140 · Barbell rows: moderate reps, pronated grip
- **Statement:** Below 6 reps you jerk the bar with the legs. Barbell rows are somewhat full-body: not too strict, not too cheated. Pronated grip, no supinated or mixed grip.
- **Numbers:** 3×6-10, never below 6; 5×5 "terrible"
- **Scope:** Barbell rows.

- **Statement:** Dumbbell rows: both feet on the floor (staggered/tripod), no knee on the bench; pull in an arc so the lat stretches and the weight travels forward; no hip shifts to heave. Kroc rows: weight in front, pronated wrists, upright torso, not too few reps (5-8 invites cheating).

- **Statement:** Start from the top with the negative, lower more slowly than you pull, keep the scapulae engaged, stay under the bar in line with the body, and pull with the back. No dangling or kipping, and don't force the head over the bar. Strict reps cost load but give better hypertrophy; keep the same grip and tempo when loaded.

### TEC-146 · No dead hang at the bottom of a pull-up
- **Statement:** A dead hang at the bottom disengages the lats and scapulae. The lat's maximum stretch is just before you lose retraction, so train that "striking range". Dead hangs are a separate tendon drill; weighted hangs don't grow lats.
- **Numbers:** 8 reps in the striking range beat 4 full reps
- **Scope:** Pull-ups.
- **Confidence:** high — ~7 videos, 2020→2024

### TEC-149 · Pullovers: stretch the rib cage, not the shoulder
- **Statement:** Lie across the bench with the hips dropped below the shoulders, slight elbow bend, elbows turned in overhead, inhale on the negative. Stretch the rib cage, not the shoulder: stop when the lat stops stretching, no full shoulder extension, and skip the dead top. If the triceps take over, bend the elbows more or use an EZ bar. Not on the floor or a bed.

## Hinge accessories

<a id="TEC-150"></a>
### TEC-150 · RDL: bent-knee, negative-first hinge
- **Statement:** The RDL is a negative-first hinge with bent knees: start from a rack, push the hips back, keep the bar close (or slightly floating with the weight still under you), go until the plates nearly kiss the floor, no bounce. A stiff-leg lets the bar float away. Most people's RDLs are partials or stiff-legs.
- **Numbers:** floating the bar so far that it costs >30% load is too far
- **Scope:** RDL, stiff-leg.
- **Confidence:** high — ~6 videos, 2020→2024
- **Status:** current

- **Scope:** Good mornings.
- **Confidence:** medium — ~7 videos, 2020→2024

- **Statement:** Keep the elbows at the sides and move only the forearm. Raising the elbows makes it a front raise, and hip drive turns it into a "supinated clean"; this explains poor biceps more than genetics does.

- **Scope:** Curls.

<a id="TEC-161"></a>
### TEC-161 · Forearms, traps and neck
- **Statement:** Forearms: train the muscle, not the tendon; keep the wrist stacked; on finger curls let the bar roll to the fingertips. Traps: let the shoulders protract so the traps catch the bar in a stretch, squeeze back rather than up, torso vertical. Neck: chin tucked, spine stacked, clean slow reps per direction, with a harness rather than plates on the head.

- **Scope:** Forearms, traps, neck.

# 6. Body-part playbook

This chapter goes through his rules one body part at a time: what each muscle needs, his rep and frequency numbers, and the exercises he prefers for it. His main point is that every muscle you want big has to be trained directly. For naturals, compounds leave the arms, forearms, abs, calves, neck, side and rear delts and the triceps long head small, while quads, glutes and hamstrings can grow mostly from compounds. His latest prescriptions (2023-2024) are more moderate than his 2020 high-volume "nucleus overload" (NO) phase: weighted, progressively overloaded isolation in roughly the 6-15 rep range.

## Rules that apply to every body part

These cross-cutting rules come from the general section of his muscle-specific teaching. They apply to every section below, so they are kept here as reference rather than as numbered principles.

## Chest

He treats the chest as one muscle built by a press you actually feel. Bench pressing is optional, and dips and ring push-ups do just as well.

<a id="CHE-01"></a>
### CHE-01 · No separate upper chest; build the whole chest
- **Statement:** There is no separate "upper chest" to chase; bench and dips develop it, and people who obsess over it usually have no chest. Splitting the chest into regions is an "isolationist mindset".
- **Numbers:** —
- **Scope:** All lifters; novices especially shouldn't worry about it. Multi-height cable flies are gimmicky.
- **Confidence:** high — ~5 videos, 2020→2024
- **Status:** current
- **Sources:** ([The Most Important Muscles to Look JACKED (Aesthetics Tier-List), 2024-03](https://youtu.be/fycepPpxN_k?t=444); [𝐄𝐗𝐏𝐋𝐎𝐃𝐄 your Chest Gains (3 𝐊𝐈𝐋𝐋𝐄𝐑 Pec Ex, 2022-11](https://youtu.be/WKy2C8JoltU?t=883); [The BEST Workout if you like to waste time for no results (Ryan Humiston Split/P, 2022-02](https://youtu.be/wLx5BRx8AaU?t=100); [The PERFECT Chest Workout by Athlean-X Review, 2021-04](https://youtu.be/62OBPecQPnM?t=64))

<a id="CHE-02"></a>
### CHE-02 · A stubborn chest needs a press you feel
- **Statement:** Grip, arch and dominant delts or triceps can steal bench work ("225 on the bar isn't 225 on the chest"). If you don't feel a press in your chest, switch to push-ups, dumbbells or dips for a while, or superset flies or band work between bench sets.
- **Numbers:** —
- **Scope:** Lifters whose chest lags despite a decent bench.
- **Confidence:** high — ~5 videos, 2020→2024
- **Status:** current
- **Check:** If the chest lags, is the main press one the lifter actually feels in the chest (or has it been swapped)?
- **Sources:** ([Response to Husaka - CHEST - Bench vs Ring Push Ups, 2020-03](https://youtu.be/K4UBm1dV6WM?t=499); [Don't turn your back on calisthenics, 2021-06](https://youtu.be/HrUPp573ki0?t=771); [Your lifting program SUCKS! (Hypertrophy Q&A / Program review), 2024-10](https://youtu.be/c7hl9u3h_s0?t=385); [Activate your chest for the bench and keep your pectoral tendons healthy in less, 2020-01](https://youtu.be/vLAhljbROlk))

<a id="CHE-03"></a>
### CHE-03 · Bench press is not mandatory
- **Statement:** Dips, push-ups and ring push-ups can replace the bench with no other change to the program. Choose by what agrees with you, and swap the bench if it doesn't hit your chest or keeps injuring you. His chest first grew from home push-ups, and by 2024 he had dropped the bench himself.
- **Numbers:** —
- **Scope:** All lifters with a muscle goal; not powerlifters.
- **Confidence:** high — ~12 videos, 2020→2024
- **Status:** current
- **Sources:** ([Any movement with a pain byproduct is a bad exercise (for you), 2020-02](https://youtu.be/Eh0fnXIyDMc?t=125); [Good chest day vs Bad chest day, 2022-05](https://youtu.be/k9_dDbGLFZQ?t=498); [So you think you look good? (Physique Critique Chad Edition), 2024-12](https://youtu.be/pt4mbNb7NJ0?t=821); [Your lifting program SUCKS! (Hypertrophy Q&A / Program review), 2024-10](https://youtu.be/c7hl9u3h_s0?t=1205))

<a id="CHE-04"></a>
### CHE-04 · Weighted dips are top tier
- **Statement:** Weighted dips ("squat of the upper body") are top tier for chest, triceps and shoulders. They give more pec and shoulder stretch than bench and may stress the pecs more. The shoulder risk is slightly higher, with no safety net.
- **Numbers:** He does 3 plates + 2×10 lb for 5.
- **Scope:** Those whose shoulders and ribcage tolerate them; growing young men should watch for sternum or rib pain.
- **Confidence:** high — ~9 videos, 2020→2024
- **Status:** changed — in 2020 he would not recommend dips over bench; later he ranks them equal or better for hypertrophy.

## Back, lats and traps

The upper back is where he sees the most untapped potential in naturals. A complete back needs a hinge, a vertical pull and a horizontal pull. Lats come from pull-ups and pullovers, not deadlifts, and traps come from heavy load held in the hands.

<a id="BAK-01"></a>
### BAK-01 · The upper back has the most growth potential in naturals
- **Statement:** The upper back is the most underdeveloped area in naturals and the slowest to mature; the best natural backs belong to lifters in their 30s-40s. After 10 years of training, adding upper-back volume made his grow "like weeds".
- **Numbers:** —
- **Scope:** Natural lifters, all levels.
- **Confidence:** high — ~12 videos, 2020→2023
- **Status:** current
- **Sources:** ([Candito Upper Lower Hypertrophy Program review, 2020-05](https://youtu.be/4aThavRpYLw?t=1385); [My philosophy regarding upper back training (part. 2), 2020-11](https://youtu.be/3JBjFKI4PmQ); [Good back day Vs Bad back day, 2021-05](https://youtu.be/qDH088UUiMA?t=13); [This is why you don't have a Demon Back (Advanced Tips), 2023-11](https://youtu.be/4t72r8Q0vXQ?t=1130))

<a id="BAK-02"></a>
### BAK-02 · The upper back tolerates the most volume and frequency
- **Statement:** The upper back is a "glutton for volume"; train it almost every session. Its limits are the shoulder, biceps and elbow tendons and lower-back fatigue, so favour rows and pulls that spare the lower back. 4 sets of pulldowns won't build big lats.
- **Numbers:** —
- **Scope:** Intermediate and up.
- **Confidence:** high — ~12 videos, 2020→2023
- **Status:** current
- **Sources:** ([My philosophy regarding upper back training (part. 1), 2020-02](https://youtu.be/3oZD6Hk525A); [6 days french bodybuilding split review, 2020-07](https://youtu.be/eaXDVkHjsZQ?t=751); [The Best/Worst of Reddit Fitness - The Ten Commandments of Lifting, 2021-10](https://youtu.be/THV7B11oalk?t=1576); [The OPTIMAL 6D/WEEK Hypertrophy Program by Mike Israetel Review, 2022-09](https://youtu.be/JnWWva91QUM?t=1900))

<a id="BAK-03"></a>
### BAK-03 · Push/pull balance: from "pull more" to "many need more front"
- **Statement:** He now sees many lifters as back-dominant from the "pull twice as much as you push" advice; they need less back and more front volume. Everyone should still do plenty of back work.
- **Numbers:** —
- **Scope:** Judged per physique.
- **Confidence:** high — ~5 videos, 2020→2024
- **Status:** changed — 2020: do more pulling than pushing; 2024: many reviewees need more pushing.
- **Sources:** ([Upper Lower 2 days Program review, 2020-05](https://youtu.be/CFlRdyLiWOo?t=313); [So you think you can lift? (Program Review LIVE), 2024-11](https://youtu.be/6p2x4kDDjzs?t=2500); [So you think you look good? (Physique Critique Chad Edition), 2024-12](https://youtu.be/pt4mbNb7NJ0?t=2347); [Do you look better than Silver Era lifters? (Physique Review LIVE), 2024-12](https://youtu.be/ZLheQPgEfoA?t=1335))

<a id="BAK-04"></a>
### BAK-04 · A complete back needs a hinge, a vertical pull and a horizontal pull
- **Statement:** The back is several areas, each needing its own pattern; vertical and horizontal pulls are not interchangeable. Deadlifts alone give a thick "fridge" back with no width; pull-ups were the only difference between his flat and his detailed back at the same 210 lb. 6-7 back exercises is "bro-split garbage".
- **Numbers:** Masterplan: 1 hinge + 1 vertical + 1 horizontal pull on different days, then +1 pull or shrug; a new hinge alternates weekly (A: deadlift 3x3, B: RDL 3x8-12); 1-2 exercises per area.
- **Scope:** All lifters wanting a full back.
- **Confidence:** high — ~6 videos, 2020→2024
- **Status:** current
- **Check:** Does each week include a hip hinge, a vertical pull and a horizontal pull?
- **Sources:** ([How to do deadlifts for SIZE, 2020-12](https://youtu.be/3IMgRqcRN4Y?t=812); [Don't turn your back on calisthenics, 2021-06](https://youtu.be/HrUPp573ki0?t=1803); [Come with me if you want a BIG BACK (4 steps MASSterplan), 2023-09](https://youtu.be/7uBT8vp0lNw?t=1198); [The ULTIMATE PPL Program (Doom Slayer Physique), 2023-11](https://youtu.be/DA7QvIAyptw?t=1261))

<a id="BAK-05"></a>
### BAK-05 · Open the back day with a heavy pull
- **Statement:** Open with a floor pull/hinge, a heavy row or a weighted pull-up, never a light pulldown or machine. Don't burn out on the opener; it doubles as a warm-up.

## Shoulders

Delt size comes mainly from vertical pressing. Side and rear delts are what naturals lack, so they get isolation on top, but the raises support the press and never replace it.

<a id="SHO-01"></a>
### SHO-01 · Vertical pressing is the bread and butter of delt size
- **Statement:** Most shoulder gains come from presses; the incline press is a hybrid and a delt movement first. All his recent shoulder gains came from "spamming" overhead presses. Judge by delt size, not pressing load.
- **Numbers:** 70-80% of shoulder gains can come from presses.
- **Scope:** All, except shoulder-dominant lifters (SHO-05).
- **Confidence:** high — ~10 videos, 2020→2024
- **Status:** current
- **Check:** Does the program include at least one vertical press a week (unless the lifter is shoulder-dominant)?
- **Sources:** ([Powerlifting centric Sheiko program review (part. 1, hypertrophy assessment), 2020-09](https://youtu.be/oLm1CDuY9zg?t=932); [Arnold raises tutorial, 2020-09](https://youtu.be/01jOBsrQCPg?t=100); [These Lifts BUILT My Physique (Top 10 Hypertrophy List), 2023-02](https://youtu.be/ABTeMrXdgI4?t=188); [Your lifting program SUCKS! (Hypertrophy Q&A / Program review), 2024-10](https://youtu.be/c7hl9u3h_s0?t=2406))

<a id="SHO-02"></a>
### SHO-02 · Lateral raises support pressing; they don't replace it
- **Statement:** Big round natural shoulders come from pressing plus isolation; spamming raises at the cost of presses is a trendy mistake. Press before laterals, and never put raises right before or after a press.
- **Numbers:** —
- **Scope:** All.
- **Confidence:** high — ~5 videos, 2022→2024
- **Status:** current
- **Check:** Are lateral raises added after pressing rather than replacing it?
- **Sources:** ([The Best Natural Lifter You've NEVER Heard Of (Hersovyac), 2023-04](https://youtu.be/-sf34ScWLK8?t=1582); [Why spamming lateral raises won't work, 2023-12](https://youtu.be/yRRXCYcgzJs); [Come with me if you want big shoulders (JOIN THE CHALLENGE!), 2022-10](https://youtu.be/BhOuuyriBDw?t=1632); [BACK 2 THE GYM STREAM (Program reviews & Answering training questions), 2024-09](https://youtu.be/okm6bZHKHI4?t=10267))

- **Statement:** Vertical presses at least twice a week, building toward three; by 2024, 1-2 vertical presses plus 1-2 isolations.

## Arms: biceps and triceps

Arms grow from isolation trained as seriously as the big lifts. For the triceps this means extensions with the shoulder flexed for the long head. Forearms have their own section.

<a id="ARM-01"></a>
### ARM-01 · Arms need isolation; compounds alone leave them small
- **Statement:** He has never seen a natural with big biceps from chin-ups alone; at the bottom of a chin-up the back takes the stretch. If rowing 3 plates didn't grow your biceps, 4 plates won't. "70% of arm gains come from compounds" is made up.
- **Numbers:** He reached 16 in arms without a chin-up.
- **Scope:** Natural lifters, all levels.
- **Confidence:** high — ~20 videos, 2020→2024
- **Status:** current
- **Check:** Does the program include direct biceps and triceps isolation?

## Forearms and grip

Grip strength and forearm size are separate things. Forearms grow from isolation of every wrist and elbow function plus heavy weighted stretch. By 2023-2024 they were the one body part he says to "spam".

<a id="FOR-01"></a>
### FOR-01 · Pulling doesn't build big forearms; isolate them
- **Statement:** Elite 600-900 lb pullers often have thin forearms. His raw-pulling years stalled his forearms; direct work made them "blow up". His big forearms come from years of isolation, not genetics.
- **Numbers:** About 13.5 → 15 in after direct flexion work.
- **Scope:** All naturals.
- **Confidence:** high — ~25 videos, 2020→2025
- **Status:** current
- **Check:** Is there direct forearm isolation, not just pulling and grip work?
- **Sources:** ([Having a strong grip won't give you big forearms, 2020-02](https://youtu.be/lq_qgThCqHY?t=187); [Using straps will help you grow your forearms, 2020-02](https://youtu.be/sT8z3ENnqAQ?t=631); [Come with me if you want big forearms (7 Steps MASSterplan), 2023-02](https://youtu.be/clzLnKrm6Ao?t=317); [10 years of lifting for this (Hypertrophy Log #10), 2025-01](https://youtu.be/waeSP7DBmig?t=1070))

- **Confidence:** high — ~7 videos, 2020→2024

## Legs: quads, hamstrings and glutes

Legs are the exception to "isolate everything": they grow mostly from a heavy knee-flexion pattern plus a heavy hip hinge. Over the years he moved from back squats and deadlifts toward heel-elevated, hack and split squats and the RDL.

<a id="LEG-01"></a>
### LEG-01 · Big legs need a heavy knee flexion plus a heavy hip hinge
- **Statement:** Any squat pattern, hack, belt squat or leg press plus any heavy hinge. You can grow huge legs without squats or deadlifts specifically, but never without these patterns. The lower body needs few exercises.
- **Numbers:** Squat + RDL ≈ 80-90% of the gains; a leg day = 1 big quad move, 1 posterior-chain move, 1-2 isolations.
- **Scope:** All.
- **Confidence:** high — ~12 videos, 2020→2024
- **Status:** current
- **Check:** Does each week include a heavy knee-flexion (squat-pattern) lift and a heavy hip hinge?
- **Sources:** ([Level up your legs, 2021-06](https://youtu.be/ANvvVrMqF7Y?t=1314); [The Smartest Push Pull Legs Routine by Jeff Nippard review, 2021-06](https://youtu.be/Mq2TaHm_ySI?t=376); [These Lifts BUILT My Physique (Top 10 Hypertrophy List), 2023-02](https://youtu.be/ABTeMrXdgI4?t=313); [Arnold trained like an idiot?, 2024-04](https://youtu.be/-OYtq2AHGX8?t=1393))

- **Numbers:** He built 26-26.5 in thighs with almost only squats.
- **Scope:** Naturals.
- **Confidence:** high — ~8 videos, 2020→2021
- **Status:** current
- **Sources:** ([The training principles series： bodybuilder proportions, 2020-04](https://youtu.be/WZH2K6er7cA?t=186); [Isolation movements benefits： attacking muscles more precisely, 2020-03](https://youtu.be/QwoBxHI7NBU?t=108); [Why you will NEVER have freaky, thick forearms if your wrists are small (Natty o, 2021-02](https://youtu.be/YHm-qSHgGSk?t=920); [Nucleus overload guide (part. 2)： Which body parts, how to target them & impact , 2020-05](https://youtu.be/4rjywMLXt98?t=188))

## Calves and tibialis

Calves stay small because people don't train them, not because of genetics. They need load, several sessions a week, and a place early in the session or in supersets.

<a id="CLF-01"></a>
### CLF-01 · Calves stay small because they aren't trained
- **Statement:** Once trained, calves grow; small calves are bad training, not genetics. Squats don't grow calves.
- **Numbers:** His calves: 16 in (2020) → 17 (2022) → ~17.8 in; an inch a year is possible. He waited nine years before training them.
- **Scope:** All.
- **Confidence:** high — ~12 videos, 2020→2024
- **Status:** current
- **Sources:** ([Why you will NEVER have freaky, thick forearms if your wrists are small (Natty o, 2021-02](https://youtu.be/YHm-qSHgGSk?t=790); [3 YEAR RECOMP TRANSFORMATION (From Husky to Jacked) - 50K SPECIAL, 2022-08](https://youtu.be/O9txIDHBBIk?t=1100); [So you think you look good? - **Confidence:** high — ~8 videos, 2020→2024
- **Status:** current

## Abs, obliques and core

Abs need direct, loaded, stretched isolation. Bracing in compounds doesn't build them and diet only reveals them. He moved from daily high-rep work to weighted, progressive sets a few times a week.

<a id="ABS-01"></a>
### ABS-01 · Abs need direct isolation
- **Statement:** Compounds and bracing don't build a six-pack; bracing gives an isometric contraction with no stretch. Ab isolation is "non-negotiable", and every program of his includes at least one.
- **Numbers:** ≥1 ab isolation per program.
- **Scope:** All.
- **Confidence:** high — ~25 videos, 2020→2024
- **Status:** current
- **Check:** Does the program include at least one direct, stretch-based ab exercise?
- **Sources:** ([My favorite ab isolation exercises, 2020-04](https://youtu.be/uf3-n8CFeu0); [Level up your abs, 2021-10](https://youtu.be/f-XiVNy25tw?t=3013); [Stop falling for these Ab Training Myths, 2023-03](https://youtu.be/-izcpmcGs-c?t=255); [Bodybuilding is killing me (Hypertrophy Log #8), 2024-09](https://youtu.be/JW73oft8Q60?t=430))

## Neck

Everyone should train the neck directly. It grows fast on little volume. His latest prescription is 1-2 sessions a week of neck curls and extensions in the 10-20 rep range, supersetted on lower days.

# 7. Strength & the big lifts

This chapter covers how strength relates to size, where strength work sits in a bodybuilding program, his rep schemes for the main lifts, max testing, carryover between lifts, strength standards, powerlifting and powerbuilding, and strength for other athletes. His stance: for a bodybuilder, strength is a means, not the goal. You must get stronger to grow, but chasing 1RMs, big-three numbers or standards costs size. His own lift numbers over time are in ch. 1 and Appendix C and are not repeated here.

## Strength vs size

Strength and size are linked but separate qualities. Within one person they move together, but between people leverages, skill and bodyweight blur the link.

<a id="STR-01"></a>
### STR-01 · Strength and size are different qualities
- **Statement:** Strength and size are different qualities with some crossover, and training for one is not training for the other. Two lifters who add the same amount to a lift end up different sizes, and the one focused on volume and tonnage is bigger.
- **Numbers:** example: two lifters taking a squat from 100 to 300 lb, or reaching a 250 lb bench
- **Scope:** all lifters, and especially bodybuilders choosing what to train for
- **Confidence:** high — ~15 videos, 2020→2024
- **Status:** current
- **Check:** Is the program built to add muscle (volume, tonnage) rather than to raise lift numbers for their own sake?
- **Sources:** ([Why your strength potential might be limiting your size gains, 2020-11](https://youtu.be/-1dECrWYeFk); [The hypertrophy series： developing the values of size and strength, 2020-10](https://youtu.be/k8k1PycHKDI?t=340); [The hypertrophy series： the primordial metric for muscle growth, 2021-01](https://youtu.be/V4aBuYpdY34?t=300); [How to Get Bigger by Doing Less (The 85% Rule), 2022-12](https://youtu.be/z2uzpl_smSg?t=1702))

<a id="STR-02"></a>
### STR-02 · You can't grow without getting stronger
- **Statement:** Strength is not the bodybuilder's goal, but you will have to get stronger to grow. Size and strength both rise, one faster than the other.
- **Numbers:** —
- **Scope:** bodybuilders at every level
- **Confidence:** high — ~8 videos, 2020→2024
- **Status:** current
- **Check:** Does the program expect loads or reps on its lifts to go up over time?
- **Sources:** ([The hypertrophy series： developing the values of size and strength, 2020-10](https://youtu.be/k8k1PycHKDI); [The hypertrophy series： developing the values of size and strength, 2020-10](https://youtu.be/k8k1PycHKDI?t=220); [Tips to Avoid a Mediocre Physique, 2022-11](https://youtu.be/JgAoGDmM4n4?t=497); [Hypertrophy training is CANCELLED, 2024-06](https://youtu.be/jUMmu583w34?t=1030))

<a id="STR-03"></a>
### STR-03 · Within a person, strength reflects muscle
- **Statement:** For one person on long-practised lifts, strength gains reflect muscle gains (bigger legs mean a bigger squat), and small size increases bring surprisingly large strength increases. Between people, leverages dominate, so you can't read strength from size.
- **Numbers:** legs from 20 to 25 in means the squat went up; between people: 20 in legs squatting ~400 vs 22 in legs squatting 500
- **Scope:** comparing yourself over time; not for comparing different lifters
- **Confidence:** high — ~8 videos, 2020→2022
- **Status:** changed — 2020: he rejected the idea that strength can rise while muscles shrink, and said size can't rise while strength stays flat; 2022: citing Candito losing size while his total rose, he said you can trade one for the other. Later view: correlated within a person, but tradeable.
- **Sources:** ([Response to Migan (Team3DAlpha) - PROGRESSIVE OVERLOAD IS NOT THE DRIVER OF MUSC, 2020-03](https://youtu.be/VVckf4vyYPE?t=260); [＂What is the point of lifting natty past 30 if test levels crash?＂, 2020-04](https://youtu.be/TIsnQ03FegQ?t=338); [Strength standards are useless, 2022-04](https://youtu.be/LxGdGChvk2c?t=3139); [Strength standards are useless, 2022-04](https://youtu.be/LxGdGChvk2c?t=3076))

## Neural adaptation vs muscle

Early strength gains on a lift are mostly skill. Once the skill is learned, strength added at the same technique and bodyweight is muscle.

<a id="STR-10"></a>
### STR-10 · Neural gains are front-loaded and capped
- **Statement:** Neural and technical gains on a new lift mostly arrive early. After that you are at 95-100% technical mastery, and further strength at the same technique is muscle. Saying all strength gains could be neural is "wrong and demoralizing".
- **Numbers:** ~6 months of weekly practice (2020); "a month to a year" (2021); 95-100% technical mastery
- **Scope:** any lift practised regularly, past the learning phase
- **Confidence:** high — ~6 videos, 2020→2021
- **Status:** current — the window was refined from ~6 months (2020) to a month to a year (2021), with the same conclusion
- **Check:** Once a lift has been practised for ~6-12 months, is further strength at the same technique and bodyweight treated as muscle gain?
- **Sources:** ([Strength training is for SUCKERS (Natty or not.com), 2020-07](https://youtu.be/7XqE7GhDsgc?t=938); [Is shocking the muscle a thing?, 2020-07](https://youtu.be/Zkhc-j-6ptU?t=519); [The hypertrophy series： the optimal measure of progression for muscle growth, 2020-10](https://youtu.be/ISLtO-xJbYo?t=252); [The hypertrophy series： pairing neurological adaptation and muscle gains, 2021-02](https://youtu.be/AeIKc3A2FiY?t=270))

<a id="STR-11"></a>
### STR-11 · Learning or rotating lifts gives artificial progress
- **Statement:** Progress on a new or rotated lift is mostly relearning, not muscle. A box lets you think you are stronger at the squat. A second +100 lb on the bench brings far more muscle than the first.
- **Numbers:** his SSB box squat 185→365 lb in under a year, mostly relearning
- **Scope:** judging progress on new variations
- **Confidence:** medium — ~4 videos, 2020→2021
- **Status:** current
- **Sources:** ([Is shocking the muscle a thing?, 2020-07](https://youtu.be/Zkhc-j-6ptU?t=399); [Is shocking the muscle a thing?, 2020-07](https://youtu.be/Zkhc-j-6ptU?t=450); [The problem with 5x5/3x5, 2020-06](https://youtu.be/k3O630Nz4B8?t=188); [Why Novices shouldn't do Box Squats, 2021-01](https://youtu.be/bTin_tBGoVo?t=395))

<a id="STR-12"></a>
### STR-12 · Strength is largely skill
- **Statement:** Strength is largely the skill of recruiting motor units in a pattern, and it needs a fresh nervous system. High-frequency programs (daily squatting, Bulgarian or Wisconsin-style) raise one lift without much muscle, and he never prescribes them for size.
- **Numbers:** —
- **Scope:** specialised strength programs
- **Confidence:** medium — ~6 videos, 2020→2022
- **Status:** current

<a id="STR-13"></a>

- **Statement:** Past the novice stage, a big percentage strength gain with no muscle gain is biologically impossible. Strength that jumps while nothing visibly changes is a red flag.

### STR-14 · Strength detrains faster than size
- **Statement:** Time off costs strength and work capacity well before it costs size. Presses, especially the OHP, regress quickly when not practised.

## Bodyweight, fat and leverage

Bodyweight makes you stronger, but strength that comes from fat is leverage, not progress.

<a id="STR-15"></a>
### STR-15 · Fat-driven strength isn't real progress
- **Statement:** Mass moves mass, but strength gained by adding mostly fat raises absolute strength, not pound-for-pound strength. It is leverage, and it disappears on a cut.
- **Numbers:** +20 lb on the bench with +20 lb bodyweight = no real progress; +100 lb of mostly fat raises absolute strength only
- **Scope:** judging progress during bulks
- **Confidence:** high — ~6 videos, 2020→2022
- **Status:** current
- **Check:** Is strength progress judged at a stable bodyweight (or alongside lean gain), not credited when it only follows fat gain?
- **Sources:** ([Response to Migan (Team3DAlpha) - PROGRESSIVE OVERLOAD IS NOT THE DRIVER OF MUSC, 2020-03](https://youtu.be/VVckf4vyYPE?t=322); [BLOATMAXX： the Kyriakos Grizzly example, mogging general & potential downsides, 2020-12](https://youtu.be/so6MbvvtM1w?t=242); [Don't fall for the bulking meme, 2022-11](https://youtu.be/h7D6CB4p1oU?t=1580); [Don't fall for the bulking meme, 2022-11](https://youtu.be/h7D6CB4p1oU?t=1139))

<a id="STR-16"></a>
### STR-16 · Bodyweight helps presses far more than hinges
- **Statement:** Extra bodyweight helps pressing through leverage (a shorter range of motion) and helps hinges much less. In a deficit, hinges barely suffer while bench and OHP drop a lot.
- **Numbers:** "put 50 lb on your frame, add ~100 lb to your bench"; he benched 315 at ~220 lb, 335 when fatter, and lost it when the fat came off
- **Scope:** pressing vs hinging lifts across bulks and cuts
- **Confidence:** medium — ~5 videos, 2020→2021
- **Status:** current
- **Sources:** ([BLOATMAXX： the Kyriakos Grizzly example, mogging general & potential downsides, 2020-12](https://youtu.be/so6MbvvtM1w?t=902); [Crazy bulks： secret for INSANE gains?, 2021-11](https://youtu.be/-T8qWCI4_No?t=616); [Crazy bulks： secret for INSANE gains?, 2021-11](https://youtu.be/-T8qWCI4_No?t=668); [The reason people lose so much strength/size on cuts, 2020-09](https://youtu.be/e3KPnpnfbxc?t=316))

<a id="STR-17"></a>
### STR-17 · Pure strength needs mass, preferably muscle
- **Statement:** For pure strength, carry as much mass as possible, preferably muscle. Getting really strong means letting bodyweight rise, so staying very lean ("otter mode") means never getting really strong or reaching full size.
- **Numbers:** 400 lb at 10% body fat beats 400 lb at 20%
- **Scope:** lifters whose goal is maximal strength
- **Confidence:** medium — ~2 videos, 2020→2023
- **Status:** current
- **Sources:** ([Can you modify the bodyfat range in which building muscle is most comfortable?, 2020-08](https://youtu.be/mUAHGlseeyk?t=502); [Is THIS the most attractive body type? (Ottermode Physique), 2023-03](https://youtu.be/HOgwZO70z_M?t=878))

<a id="STR-18"></a>
### STR-18 · You can get stronger without gaining weight
- **Statement:** Strength can keep rising at a stable bodyweight. He uses his own lifts as proof.
- **Numbers:** all his lifts rose at ≤210 lb (2020); in 2024 he beat his old 240 lb lifts at 220 lb, except the bench
- **Scope:** lifters at stable bodyweight
- **Confidence:** medium — ~2 videos, 2020→2024

- **Statement:** Long femurs or a long torso make squats hard and deadlifts easier, and arms past the knees would make a deadlift world-record holder. ## Strength work inside a bodybuilding program

Strength work is a small, focused part of a bodybuilding program. It opens the session, is done as solo sets, and serves the tonnage. His later practice moved the heavy work to less risky movements.

<a id="STR-21"></a>
### STR-21 · Strength work is a year-round pillar
- **Statement:** A small dose of heavy strength work is the backbone of hypertrophy training and stays in all year, not only in a block. It is little tonnage, but its high-intensity peaks drive progression.
- **Numbers:** —
- **Scope:** all bodybuilding programs
- **Confidence:** medium — ~10 videos, 2020→2021 (strongly stated early, less emphasised later)
- **Status:** changed — 2020-21: the backbone, "the one cornerstone you never cut"; 2024-25: high-bar squat and bench only 3-5 times a year, he "doesn't care about strength", and his heavy work moved to dips and weighted pull-ups. Later view: keep getting stronger, through less risky movements.
- **Check:** Does the program keep some heavy, low-rep work all year rather than only in phases?
- **Sources:** ([How to progress forward with evolving rep ranges, 2020-09](https://youtu.be/65rLZe9cz_0?t=251); [The hypertrophy series： utilizing tonnage for muscle growth, 2021-01](https://youtu.be/_2M6FhWuIvs?t=314); [You know what time it is... STORY TIME, 2025-01](https://youtu.be/0O0nG2jLadU?t=572); [3 hours of Story Time, 2025-02](https://youtu.be/-7bzbmL-x3Q?t=748))

<a id="STR-22"></a>
### STR-22 · Strength work opens the session
- **Statement:** Strength work comes first, and a day with zero strength work is bad, with occasional exceptions. Pre-activation must be light: an explosive opener taken short of failure (a kettlebell swing) primes you, while a leg-curl opener only fatigues. A small dose fires up the nervous system for the accessories.
- **Numbers:** —
- **Scope:** session structure
- **Confidence:** medium — ~5 videos, 2020→2022
- **Status:** current
- **Check:** Does the heavy strength work come first in the session, after only light warm-ups?
- **Sources:** ([Kizen Strength & Aesthetics Powerbuilding program review, 2020-09](https://youtu.be/-banYSTnkq4?t=230); [The hypertrophy series： using strength work to control tonnage without sacrifice, 2020-07](https://youtu.be/zCo31HKOsIY?t=317); [The PERFECT Chest Workout by Athlean-X Review, 2021-04](https://youtu.be/62OBPecQPnM?t=440); [Going to WAR over Giant Sets (Response to Bald Omni Man), 2022-09](https://youtu.be/nqzVqvMvQ1s?t=1196))

## Rep schemes for the main lifts

His rep ranges for the main strength lifts. A summary table follows the principles.

<a id="STR-34"></a>
### STR-34 · Deadlift: few sets, never more than 5 reps
- **Statement:** Deadlift for 1-3 sets of 2-5 reps, never more than 5, and a single heavy set of 5 is often enough. 3x3 works very well if you leave reps in the tank.
- **Numbers:** 1-3 x 2-5; often 1x5; 3x3 with reps in reserve; 3x5 is a good volume for floor pulls; back-offs 4x3 at a comfortable triple or 3x3 submax
- **Scope:** heavy floor pulls, intermediate and up
- **Confidence:** high — ~14 videos, 2020→2024
- **Status:** current
- **Check:** Are heavy deadlift sets kept at 5 reps or fewer, for only a few sets?

- **Statement:** His later practice is to deadlift from the floor rarely and get most posterior-chain volume from RDLs, good mornings and hyperextensions.

## Max testing

Bodybuilders build strength and estimate it from reps. They don't test it.

<a id="STR-44"></a>
### STR-44 · Never test 1RMs as a bodybuilder
- **Statement:** Maxing out is a powerlifting skill for peaking and brings no hypertrophy benefit. 1RMs don't even build strength (2-3RMs or 1 rep in reserve might), and every max-out uses up muscle-building capacity.
- **Numbers:** —
- **Scope:** bodybuilders
- **Confidence:** high — ~7 videos, 2020→2024
- **Status:** current
- **Check:** Does the program avoid 1RM testing?
- **Sources:** ([AlphaDestiny Novice Program review (part. 2： FAQ), 2020-04](https://youtu.be/T_DyRlu3Y7I?t=317); [5 reasons to only lift heavy weight DEBUNKED, 2021-01](https://youtu.be/CTMwuqNsY9Q?t=498); [No one understands training intensity, 2021-11](https://youtu.be/UrFS3Gs5zh0?t=763); [Powerbuilding is an Abomination., 2023-10](https://youtu.be/x9GNS5HBZ_4?t=1262))

<a id="STR-45"></a>
### STR-45 · Estimate your max from reps
- **Statement:** Estimate your max from rep performance and program by intensity. A double just under your max beats a single: double the tonnage, with less risk and fatigue.
- **Numbers:** e.g. 200x10; 485x2 vs 500x1; by 2021 he hadn't tested a 1RM in ~4 years
- **Scope:** bodybuilders
- **Confidence:** medium — 1 video, 2021
- **Status:** current
- **Sources:** ([No one understands training intensity, 2021-11](https://youtu.be/UrFS3Gs5zh0?t=1054); [No one understands training intensity, 2021-11](https://youtu.be/UrFS3Gs5zh0?t=665); [No one understands training intensity, 2021-11](https://youtu.be/UrFS3Gs5zh0?t=922))

<a id="STR-46"></a>
### STR-46 · Constant max testing stalls progress
- **Statement:** Testing your max often "smashes the piggy bank": it spends what you have built instead of building more.
- **Numbers:** testing a deadlift 1RM every 2 weeks kept him at 465-485 lb for a year
- **Scope:** anyone who tests maxes frequently
- **Confidence:** medium — 1 video, 2024
- **Status:** current
- **Sources:** ([The WORST Bodybuilding Program Ever Created (my bad), 2024-04](https://youtu.be/Ft039H8jzXU?t=1822))

## Carryover between lifts

The best way to improve a lift is to do that lift. Variations help, but partials, machines and odd lifts can hide your real strength.

<a id="STR-47"></a>

- **Statement:** The best way to bench more is to bench, and the best deadlift accessory is more deadlifting.
- **Numbers:** —
- **Scope:** improving a specific lift
- **Confidence:** medium — ~3 videos, 2020→2024

- **Statement:** Close-grip bench carries over and skull crushers barely do. Push-ups and ring push-ups don't build bench strength, but dips carry over a lot. A slingshot carries over little to raw benching, and using only a slingshot for 2 months could cost raw strength.
- **Numbers:** he was advanced at push-ups yet benched ~145 lb the first time; a lifter hit a 4-plate bench after 6 weeks thanks to dip strength
- **Scope:** bench accessories

## Strength standards

He mostly dismisses strength standards, with a few minimum baselines he does endorse.

<a id="STR-57"></a>
### STR-57 · Strength standards are C-tier
- **Statement:** He ignores strength standards unless you compete. They rest on unverified self-reports or powerlifter data and round plate numbers, and they ignore leverages, experience, the nervous system and timeline. They compare you to weak people and turn hypertrophy training into number-chasing. If you compete, use your sport's competition standards.
- **Numbers:** —
- **Scope:** non-competing lifters; competitors use their sport's standards
- **Confidence:** high — ~10 videos, 2020→2024
- **Status:** current
- **Check:** Does the program avoid generic strength standards as targets (unless the lifter competes)?

The fix is to drop the 1RM training, and then you are just bodybuilding the silver/bronze-era way. He debated Dr. Milo Wolf on this.

# 8. Aesthetics & the gym look

This chapter covers what NH thinks a physique should look like and how to judge one: body fat, proportions, which muscles matter most to the eye, frame, measuring and the social side of looking muscular. His stance is that bodybuilding is an art of illusion aimed at beauty. Every muscle should be trained with aesthetic intent, imbalances should be deliberate, and a natural should carry a moderate body fat over a lot of muscle. He also holds that big limbs, a developed core, a thick neck and upper back count for more than stage leanness. How to train each muscle is in ch. 6; bulking and cutting are in ch. 11.

## What bodybuilding is for

His starting point: looks are a legitimate goal, they come from function that you point toward appearance, and the goal is personal as long as it is chosen on purpose.

<a id="AES-01"></a>

- **Statement:** Bodybuilding pursues beauty through illusion, not a pile of mass or big measurements; flow, insertions and posing beat raw size.

- **Scope:** All lifters training for looks.
- **Confidence:** high — ~10 videos, 2020→2024
- **Status:** current
- **Sources:** ([Natty or not (.com)： Jeff Nippard, 2020-05](https://youtu.be/f0vdsC2yyhY?t=1012); [Don't fall for the bulking meme, 2022-11](https://youtu.be/h7D6CB4p1oU?t=1645); [Don't let this man ruin your physique, 2023-01](https://youtu.be/elk4uYvjXos?t=378); [So you think you look good? ## Body fat and leanness

He wants lots of muscle at a moderate body fat. Fat, muscle size and fat pattern all change how lean someone looks.

- **Numbers:** 12-18% (old-school naturals); 10-16% (era competitors); abs look good at 10, 15 or 17%; 15% looks good; 6-8% "achievable but not reasonable"; 5% is masochism; 8% standards make men look like skeletons

## Proportions and his ideal physique

He frames ideals through Greek statues and the classical era, prefers a limb-heavy Herculean look for himself, and insists that neighbouring muscles grow together.

<a id="AES-20"></a>
### AES-20 · Apollonian V-taper vs Herculean X-taper
- **Statement:** The Greek tradition has two branches: Apollonian (wide shoulders and lats, small waist, smaller legs, low fat) and Herculean/Farnese (thicker waist, big limbs, legs and core). He prefers the Herculean, ancient "bear mode"; the Farnese Hercules is closer to his ideal.
- **Numbers:** —
- **Scope:** Goal-setting; he has written programs for both.
- **Confidence:** high — ~7 videos, 2020→2022
- **Status:** current
- **Sources:** ([The training principles series： aesthetics, 2020-02](https://youtu.be/4IhOKe7lo_s); [The training principles series： aesthetics, 2020-02](https://youtu.be/4IhOKe7lo_s?t=189); [Greek Lifting Wisdom, 2021-08](https://youtu.be/Zt6bvNqnJmA?t=516); [Farnese Hercules Bodybuilding Program (Ancient Greek Herculean Physique Workout), 2022-03](https://youtu.be/IYobXlRVLd0?t=309))

<a id="AES-21"></a>
### AES-21 · His "Berserker" ideal: big limbs, strong core, upper back
- **Statement:** Massive arms, forearms and legs slightly out of proportion with the trunk, a strong core, developed upper back and smaller shoulders. Big limbs pull attention from the torso, an illusion.
- **Numbers:** —
- **Scope:** His personal goal.
- **Confidence:** high — ~8 videos, 2020→2023
- **Status:** changed — 2020-22 the trunk and chest stay comparatively small (2021 "Buddha physique": big limbs, small shoulders and chest, very developed core); 2023 the Berserker includes a big chest; 2025, being narrow, he chases a Bizu-style physique with huge traps.
- **Sources:** ([Going Berserker mode (Berserk physique introduction), 2020-03](https://youtu.be/NTMGQPjpP00?t=126); [Why you NEED a goal body, 2021-09](https://youtu.be/PYICG0hBlVo?t=446); [Everything I do to get HUGE (Split, Reps, Lifts), 2023-09](https://youtu.be/43F9unmSc_I); [10 years of lifting for this (Hypertrophy Log #10), 2025-01](https://youtu.be/waeSP7DBmig?t=270))

<a id="AES-22"></a>
### AES-22 · Arms should look bigger than the shoulders
- **Statement:** He dislikes big round delts on smaller limbs; the arm should dominate the shoulder.

### AES-68 · Measurements: objective but misleading
- **Statement:** Tape measurements track progress objectively, but pump and fat inflate them and big numbers can look worse than smaller ones. Use a locking tape and measure on dates fixed in advance. He claims Blaha's "18 in" arms are really 14-15 in and that Blaha wears a belt shirtless to fake a V-taper (his unverified opinion).
- **Numbers:** +10% body fat raises all measurements; measure one part every 2-3 months on pre-set dates (e.g. 6 months); 22 in arms can look worse than smaller ones
- **Scope:** Progress tracking.
- **Confidence:** medium — ~4 videos, 2020
- **Status:** current
- **Sources:** ([How to body measurements & discussing my weak points, 2020-02](https://youtu.be/KlSyeS0R9FE); [How to body measurements & discussing my weak points, 2020-02](https://youtu.be/KlSyeS0R9FE?t=61); [How to body measurements & discussing my weak points, 2020-02](https://youtu.be/KlSyeS0R9FE?t=126); [Fake Merc Character Study (part. 1)： Entering the Blohoverse, 2020-06](https://youtu.be/g4mX62QGzTo?t=1564))

# 9. Injuries

This chapter covers why lifters get hurt, how to read pain, how to treat tendinitis, how to program to avoid injury, and joint-by-joint rules for the back, knees, shoulders, elbows, wrists and other sites. His stance: injuries are almost never bad luck. They come from mismanaged load, fatigue, volume and repetition, so they are the lifter's responsibility. Tendinitis is treated by training around the pain, not by rest or drugs. For a natural, staying injury-free is the best way to keep growing.

## Why injuries happen

He puts nearly every injury down to variables the lifter controls: load and fatigue, grinding reps, and repeating the same pattern.

<a id="INJ-01"></a>
### INJ-01 · Injuries are preventable, not bad luck
- **Statement:** Injuries come from variables you failed to control, so they are preventable; calling them bad luck is lazy and irresponsible.
- **Numbers:** —
- **Scope:** All lifters. Only things like being tackled mid-lift are truly out of your control; skipping a warm-up or slipping on ice still counts as yours.
- **Confidence:** high — ~14 videos, 2020→2023
- **Status:** current
- **Sources:** ([Why do injuries happen?, 2020-07](https://youtu.be/rsbqqfM6ZFM); [Did I just snap my sh＊t up? (an injury assessment guide & pain psychology discus, 2021-09](https://youtu.be/Z90VsPDV__U?t=492); [𝙃𝙊𝙍𝙍𝙄𝙁𝙄𝘾 𝙡𝙞𝙛𝙩𝙞𝙣𝙜 𝙞𝙣𝙟𝙪, 2022-08](https://youtu.be/yoROLGGUPXU?t=64); [5 Secrets of Elite Natural Lifters, 2023-10](https://youtu.be/iU-oYc8fbEM?t=632))

<a id="INJ-02"></a>
### INJ-02 · Volume/intensity mismanagement is the top cause
- **Statement:** Ego, too much load and forcing the extra rep cause most injuries; together with poor positioning they account for the "vast majority". Perfect form cannot save poor volume/intensity management.
- **Numbers:** —
- **Scope:** All lifters.
- **Confidence:** high — ~8 videos, 2020→2023
- **Status:** current
- **Sources:** ([Why do injuries happen?, 2020-07](https://youtu.be/rsbqqfM6ZFM?t=62); [The hypertrophy series： handling lower body volume & intensity, 2020-08](https://youtu.be/pUpQypTV3Ck?t=124); [Injury Q&A #2, 2020-10](https://youtu.be/W-s1ft_HqYE?t=1061); [5 Secrets of Elite Natural Lifters, 2023-10](https://youtu.be/iU-oYc8fbEM?t=632))

<a id="INJ-03"></a>
### INJ-03 · Injury = load and fatigue exceeding tissue capacity
- **Statement:** An injury is pressure exceeding what the tissue can handle, a failure to adapt to a cycle of stress. Risk depends on load and accumulated fatigue together.
- **Numbers:** 50% of max is "baby weight"; 5 reps at 80% to failure every day raises risk daily as fatigue builds.
- **Scope:** All lifters.
- **Confidence:** medium — ~4 videos, 2020→2021
- **Status:** current
- **Sources:** ([Did I just snap my sh＊t up? (an injury assessment guide & pain psychology discus, 2021-09](https://youtu.be/Z90VsPDV__U?t=423); [Did I just snap my sh＊t up? (an injury assessment guide & pain psychology discus, 2021-09](https://youtu.be/Z90VsPDV__U?t=189); [Injuries as a result of cyclical adaptation failure, 2020-07](https://youtu.be/iCWUcBy7Vxs?t=62); [No such thing as a dangerous lift (the good morning example), 2021-04](https://youtu.be/sFMQj4Lflk0?t=1320))

<a id="INJ-04"></a>
### INJ-04 · The "red zone" is where injuries happen
- **Statement:** Acute injuries happen where the negative reverses into the positive; almost nobody gets hurt at lockout. Negative-first lifts (squat, bench) are the most dangerous at high intensity, and a controlled negative is injury prevention.
- **Numbers:** "99%" of injuries in the red zone (2020); 95-98% (2021).
- **Scope:** All lifts, especially heavy squat and bench.
- **Confidence:** high — ~10 videos, 2020→2021
- **Status:** current
- **Sources:** ([The hypertrophy series： using intensity to assess risk to reward ratios, 2020-06](https://youtu.be/2hwj-NEebj8?t=126); [Blood and Guts program review, 2020-10](https://youtu.be/6kRRzKx7lKs?t=1600); [Where Snap City occurs, 2020-12](https://youtu.be/UzTfF1VduxM?t=382); [The Hypertrophy Iceberg Explained (a complete guide to muscle growth), 2021-07](https://youtu.be/8ELQ2XZgpls?t=2531); [Injury Q&A #4, 2021-06](https://youtu.be/9kIIW251uiI?t=2140))

<a id="INJ-05"></a>
### INJ-05 · Grinding the last rep causes most injuries
- **Statement:** Most gym injuries come in the last grindy reps of heavy sets. With no grinding, staying in the rep range and no last-rep chasing, risk is "almost zero". All his own past injuries came from grinding reps he wasn't capable of.
- **Numbers:** Cutting 3-4 grinder squat reps gave him 3 years with no squat injury.
- **Scope:** All lifters, heavy compound sets.
- **Confidence:** high — ~10 videos, 2020→2022
- **Status:** current
- **Check:** Does the program avoid grinding ugly reps and chasing the extra rep on heavy sets?
- **Sources:** ([Why you should leave reps in the tank (Reps in Reserve), 2020-02](https://youtu.be/QiOh8SF-UxQ?t=300); [Why do injuries happen?, 2020-07](https://youtu.be/rsbqqfM6ZFM?t=125); [3 YEARS WITHOUT INJURIES： How I bulletproofed myself (and how you can do it too), 2022-06](https://youtu.be/qrBLykvU_EE?t=253); [3 YEARS WITHOUT INJURIES： How I bulletproofed myself (and how you can do it too), 2022-06](https://youtu.be/qrBLykvU_EE?t=568); [Injury Q&A #4, 2021-06](https://youtu.be/9kIIW251uiI?t=692))
