## Reading pain

He separates muscle pain from tendon/joint pain, separates "hurt" from "injured", and judges a lift by how it feels the next day.

<a id="INJ-23"></a>
### INJ-23 · Never train through joint or tendon pain
- **Statement:** Joint/tendon pain is a warning; pushing through turns minor issues into lifelong ones, and joint pain never goes away by itself. If a movement hurts, stop and re-check form; if form changes don't fix it, drop the lift, since there is "always a way around".
- **Numbers:** —
- **Scope:** All lifters; applies to tendon/joint pain, not muscle soreness (INJ-24).
- **Confidence:** high — ~14 videos, 2020→2025
- **Status:** changed — 2020: absolute "never lift through pain; if it hurts, stop". 2021: graded pain scales where minor pain can be pushed aside (INJ-26). 2022-2025: tendon/joint pain is still a stop signal.
- **Check:** Is any lift that causes joint or tendon pain modified or dropped rather than pushed through?
- **Sources:** ([How to work around pain, 2020-01](https://youtu.be/1R42snjAX4I); [Any movement with a pain byproduct is a bad exercise (for you), 2020-02](https://youtu.be/Eh0fnXIyDMc?t=382); [3 YEARS WITHOUT INJURIES： How I bulletproofed myself (and how you can do it too), 2022-06](https://youtu.be/qrBLykvU_EE); [10 years of lifting for this (Hypertrophy Log #10), 2025-01](https://youtu.be/waeSP7DBmig?t=370))

<a id="INJ-24"></a>

- **Statement:** There are two kinds of pain: pump and muscle soreness (fine) versus tendon, ligament or joint pain (alarm). Tendons have more nerve endings because they repair poorly. Tension in the muscle is "more painful than dangerous"; pain at the tendon insertion is not.
- **Numbers:** —
- **Scope:** All lifters.
- **Confidence:** high — ~6 videos, 2020→2021
- **Status:** current
- **Sources:** ([Any movement with a pain byproduct is a bad exercise (for you), 2020-02](https://youtu.be/Eh0fnXIyDMc); [ANIME WORKOUTS - Would Jack Hanma's Transformation in Grappler Baki be possible , 2020-12](https://youtu.be/WyxeMHovPJ8?t=290); [TENDINITIS, BEGONE! <a id="INJ-26"></a>
### INJ-26 · Graded pain scales: occurrence and aftermath
- **Statement:** He grades pain during the lift (occurrence) and after the session (aftermath), each with a matching response; see the table below.
- **Numbers:** Level 1 in-set pain: one more rep; if it persists, stop, walk 2 min, do another set ("99%" gone). Aftermath level 3+ is usually injury.
- **Scope:** All lifters.
- **Confidence:** medium — 1 video, 2021
- **Status:** current
- **Sources:** ([Did I just snap my sh＊t up? (an injury assessment guide & pain psychology discus, 2021-09](https://youtu.be/Z90VsPDV__U?t=1528); [Did I just snap my sh＊t up? (an injury assessment guide & pain psychology discus, 2021-09](https://youtu.be/Z90VsPDV__U?t=1665); [Did I just snap my sh＊t up? (an injury assessment guide & pain psychology discus, 2021-09](https://youtu.be/Z90VsPDV__U?t=1760); [Did I just snap my sh＊t up? (an injury assessment guide & pain psychology discus, 2021-09](https://youtu.be/Z90VsPDV__U?t=2024))

| scale | level | sign | response |
|---|---|---|---|
| Occurrence | 0 | noise | nothing |
| Occurrence | 1 | pain on a rep | do one more rep; if it persists, stop, walk 2 min, do another set ([Did I just snap my sh＊t up? (an injury assessment guide & pain psychology discus, 2021-09](https://youtu.be/Z90VsPDV__U?t=1528)) |
| Occurrence | 2 | pain all workout | small strain or nocebo; push through or go home ([Did I just snap my sh＊t up? (an injury assessment guide & pain psychology discus, 2021-09](https://youtu.be/Z90VsPDV__U?t=1590)) |
| Occurrence | 4 | shift + pain | walk it off; if still there, likely injured ([Did I just snap my sh＊t up? (an injury assessment guide & pain psychology discus, 2021-09](https://youtu.be/Z90VsPDV__U?t=1665)) |
| Occurrence | 5 | shift + pain + snap | injury |
| Occurrence | 6 | structural failure | freak accident, avoidable ([Did I just snap my sh＊t up? (an injury assessment guide & pain psychology discus, 2021-09](https://youtu.be/Z90VsPDV__U?t=1760)) |
| Aftermath | 0 | soreness | nothing ([Did I just snap my sh＊t up? (an injury assessment guide & pain psychology discus, 2021-09](https://youtu.be/Z90VsPDV__U?t=1915)) |
| Aftermath | 1 | pain only lifting heavy | change angle or go lighter that day |
| Aftermath | 2 | pain with any weight | change movement/ROM, keep moving ([Did I just snap my sh＊t up? (an injury assessment guide & pain psychology discus, 2021-09](https://youtu.be/Z90VsPDV__U?t=1962)) |
| Aftermath | 3 | pain walking | usually injury, often tendinitis |
| Aftermath | 4-6 | pain to the touch / at rest or waking you / can't move | structural damage ([Did I just snap my sh＊t up? (an injury assessment guide & pain psychology discus, 2021-09](https://youtu.be/Z90VsPDV__U?t=2024)) |

## Tendinitis: diagnosis and treatment

Tendinitis is his most-discussed injury. His treatment is to keep training in a pain-free range, change angles, push blood to the tendon and build the surrounding muscle, with little rest and no painkillers.

<a id="INJ-32"></a>
### INJ-32 · Tendinitis is a spectrum ending in rupture
- **Statement:** Tendinitis is the most common lifting injury, ranging from occasional pain to deep all-day pain. Ruptures (biceps, patellar, hip labrum) usually follow months or years of ignored tendinitis.
- **Numbers:** —
- **Scope:** All lifters.
- **Confidence:** high — ~5 videos, 2020→2022
- **Status:** current
- **Sources:** ([Serious injuries don't just ＂happen＂, 2020-01](https://youtu.be/9c7O0jjeR5Q?t=126); [TENDINITIS, BEGONE! (Healing Tendinopathy / Tendon Pain Rehab for Lifters), 2021-11](https://youtu.be/KzXUgd-SnMw?t=64); [TENDINITIS, BEGONE! <a id="INJ-33"></a>
### INJ-33 · Rest does not cure tendinitis
- **Statement:** Rest only seems to cure tendinitis; it returns because the movement cause is unchanged. Immobility "fossilizes" the tendon and atrophies the muscle that shares its load. Take at most 1-2 days off when pain is bad, mainly to get over the emotional hump; longer builds a fear association.
- **Numbers:** Max 1-2 days off; 3-4 weeks is far too long; 2 weeks off still re-flares.
- **Scope:** Any tendinitis.
- **Confidence:** high — ~10 videos, 2020→2024
- **Status:** current
- **Check:** Is tendinitis handled with at most 1-2 days off followed by modified training, rather than weeks of rest?
- **Sources:** ([Natural Q&A #1, 2020-08](https://youtu.be/3dLu3VQinL8?t=1386); [Curing patellar tendinitis (part. 2)： Rehab & precautions, 2020-05](https://youtu.be/vHf2ZoHWHQs?t=312); [TENDINITIS, BEGONE! ## Programming for prevention

Most of his prevention is programming: rotating variations, keeping risky lifts at higher reps, ordering the session, balancing push and pull, and ramping in changes slowly.

<a id="INJ-46"></a>
### INJ-46 · Rotate variations, grips and stances
- **Statement:** Rotating variations, grips and stances prevents overuse and is how he gains year-round; small joint-angle changes shift strain while training the same muscle. On machines, rotate grips and machines too.
- **Numbers:** —
- **Scope:** All lifters, especially intermediate/advanced.
- **Confidence:** high — ~14 videos, 2020→2024
- **Status:** current
- **Check:** Does the program rotate variations, grips or stances rather than repeating one identical pattern for long?
- **Sources:** ([How I split up my week for Natural Hypertrophy, 2020-01](https://youtu.be/cHYOYTgiRlM?t=187); [The hypertrophy series： shocking the muscle synergistically & optimally, 2020-07](https://youtu.be/FtwMg4iM5kA?t=65); [How to add variations/rotations to your Gentleman split, 2021-06](https://youtu.be/7n8RMhsxEB4?t=626); [WEIGHTS vs MACHINES： Which one is better for muscle gains?, 2022-01](https://youtu.be/O5xVdqgt8Uo?t=2130))

<a id="INJ-47"></a>
### INJ-47 · Risky lifts at higher reps
- **Statement:** Put risky lifts in higher rep ranges so you can sense the bad rep coming. A 1RM concentrates risk into one all-or-nothing rep; an injury on rep 3 at 70% is milder, and a rounded 8RM deadlift is far less risky than at 1RM. 3RM and 10RM give the same hypertrophy, so pick the one you can progress safely.
- **Numbers:** 10-15 reps instead of 3-5; burnouts with ~20RM weight, never an 8RM; lunges and good mornings never below 8; hypers ~15, never 3×3.
- **Scope:** Injury-prone lifts; hypertrophy goal.
- **Confidence:** high — ~10 videos, 2020→2024
- **Status:** current
- **Check:** Are injury-prone lifts (good mornings, lunges, pullovers, weighted dips/chins, etc.) kept at moderate-to-high reps rather than low-rep maxes?
- **Sources:** ([Why do injuries happen?, 2020-07](https://youtu.be/rsbqqfM6ZFM?t=125); [3 days Upper 2 days Lower program review (for an advanced calisthenics guy part., 2020-11](https://youtu.be/9jAjNyxeiXc?t=565); [4 days Upper Lower split Program review, 2020-04](https://youtu.be/fSOiGuUPqBc?t=692); [So you think you can lift? (Program Review LIVE), 2024-11](https://youtu.be/6p2x4kDDjzs?t=5600))

<a id="INJ-48"></a>
### INJ-48 · Small muscles and fragile structures get higher reps
- **Statement:** Small muscles and tendon-heavy movements skew to the volume end; don't carry low isolation-style rep choices onto the wrong lifts.
- **Numbers:** Biceps: no 2-5 (2020-11); 3-5 only for very experienced lifters, carefully (2020-09).
- **Scope:** Small muscles, tendon-heavy lifts.
- **Confidence:** medium — ~3 videos, 2020
- **Status:** contradicted — biceps low reps: allowed for very experienced lifters (2020-09) vs no 2-5 at all (2020-11).
- **Sources:** ([How to start using evolving rep ranges in your training, 2020-09](https://youtu.be/HpEz3fFWEeA?t=400); [Synchronizing evolving rep range with movement patterns, variations & rotations , 2020-11](https://youtu.be/mbtAKsbDz9I?t=220); [How to start using evolving rep ranges in your training, 2020-09](https://youtu.be/HpEz3fFWEeA?t=230))

<a id="INJ-51"></a>
### INJ-51 · No heavy squat then heavy deadlift
- **Statement:** Heavy back squat then heavy deadlift in one day is a "death combo": squat fatigue rounds the thoracic spine on the pull. Don't progress squat and deadlift simultaneously; a heavy low-back lift followed by a floor pull, or barbell rows after deadlifts, is how people get hurt.
- **Numbers:** —
- **Scope:** Lower-body programming.
- **Confidence:** high — ~5 videos, 2020→2021
- **Status:** current
- **Check:** Does the program avoid heavy squats and heavy deadlifts on the same day?
- **Sources:** ([Boring but Big program review, 2020-11](https://youtu.be/hT4zgNcMOBY?t=760); [Viking's the Bare Bones Series Program review, 2021-03](https://youtu.be/8mGHG5C-EPE?t=1061); [The hypertrophy series： picking your progression battles to push tonnage, 2020-06](https://youtu.be/dI07ARtmDsc?t=256); [Upper Lower Light/Heavy 4 days split with mirror Week program review (part. 1), 2020-12](https://youtu.be/niD0UuwTUvg?t=942))

<a id="INJ-52"></a>
### INJ-52 · Pull more than you press
- **Statement:** Balance the body: pull more than you press, more posterior chain than quads, and hinges at least equal to knee flexion. There is no perfect ratio (not necessarily 2:1), but heavy pressers must pull roughly as much, and the type of pull matters, since weighted chins and plate rows don't train the scapular girdle.
- **Numbers:** —
- **Scope:** All lifters, especially heavy pressers.
- **Confidence:** high — ~6 videos, 2020→2023
- **Status:** current
- **Check:** Does pulling volume at least match pressing volume, with hinges at least equal to knee-dominant work?
- **Sources:** ([5 days Upper Lower program review (Week 1), 2020-07](https://youtu.be/du7JYCA2pa4?t=1191); [Injury Q&A #4, 2021-06](https://youtu.be/9kIIW251uiI?t=379); [The Best Natural Lifter You've NEVER Heard Of (Hersovyac), 2023-04](https://youtu.be/-sf34ScWLK8?t=1137); [Push Pull 3 days Program review, 2020-05](https://youtu.be/-6i7xt92Khg?t=632))

## Knees and patellar tendinitis

<a id="INJ-80"></a>
### INJ-80 · Patellar tendinitis: pattern, frequency, muscle
- **Statement:** Patellar tendinitis is fixed in three parts: correct the movement pattern, manage frequency and tonnage, and build the muscles that unload the tendon. Never by rest. Even perfect form wears tendons if frequency is too high.
- **Numbers:** —
- **Scope:** Patellar tendinitis.
- **Confidence:** high — ~4 videos, 2020→2021
- **Status:** current
- **Sources:** ([Curing patellar tendinitis (part. 2)： Rehab & precautions, 2020-05](https://youtu.be/vHf2ZoHWHQs?t=125); [Curing patellar tendinitis (part. 1)： Causes & symptoms, 2020-05](https://youtu.be/awroGsPwNPU?t=444); [The Hypertrophy Iceberg Explained (a complete guide to muscle growth), 2021-07](https://youtu.be/8ELQ2XZgpls?t=2592); [Injury Q&A #2, 2020-10](https://youtu.be/W-s1ft_HqYE?t=999))

<a id="INJ-81"></a>
### INJ-81 · Box-squat and widowmaker rehab
- **Statement:** His knee rehab: box squats progressed by reps then load, then "widowmakers"; stay in the widowmaker phase as long as possible and keep the rebuild maximally conservative. See the table below.
- **Numbers:** Every 2-3 days, never daily; details in the table.
- **Scope:** Patellar tendinitis.
- **Confidence:** medium — 1-2 videos, 2020
- **Status:** current
- **Sources:** ([Curing patellar tendinitis (part. 2)： Rehab & precautions, 2020-05](https://youtu.be/vHf2ZoHWHQs?t=312); [Curing patellar tendinitis (part. 2)： Rehab & precautions, 2020-05](https://youtu.be/vHf2ZoHWHQs?t=877); [Curing patellar tendinitis (part. 2)： Rehab & precautions, 2020-05](https://youtu.be/vHf2ZoHWHQs?t=941); [Icecream Fitness FAQ review, 2020-06](https://youtu.be/MCUpClPnPkQ?t=500))

| phase | protocol | cites |
|---|---|---|
| Box squat start | tallest box that allows a knee break, empty bar, very slow negative, 5×5 | ([Curing patellar tendinitis (part. 2)： Rehab & precautions, 2020-05](https://youtu.be/vHf2ZoHWHQs?t=312); [Curing patellar tendinitis (part. 2)： Rehab & precautions, 2020-05](https://youtu.be/vHf2ZoHWHQs?t=376)) |
| Box squat build | add reps to 12-15 × 5-6 sets, then add weight; at 135×~15 easy, go to a lower box and restart | ([Curing patellar tendinitis (part. 2)： Rehab & precautions, 2020-05](https://youtu.be/vHf2ZoHWHQs?t=440)) |
| Widowmakers | 135 lb × 25-30 reps × 5-6 sets, then ~185 lb at lower reps | ([Curing patellar tendinitis (part. 2)： Rehab & precautions, 2020-05](https://youtu.be/vHf2ZoHWHQs?t=877); [Curing patellar tendinitis (part. 2)： Rehab & precautions, 2020-05](https://youtu.be/vHf2ZoHWHQs?t=1004)) |
| Frequency | every 2-3 days, not daily | ([Curing patellar tendinitis (part. 2)： Rehab & precautions, 2020-05](https://youtu.be/vHf2ZoHWHQs?t=312)) |

<a id="INJ-82"></a>
### INJ-82 · Knee rehab habits and wraps
- **Statement:** Morning knee extensions from small to full range, then knee bends; avoid impact sports, running on concrete and cat-style stretches that overextend the knee. Use short elastic wraps angled onto the tendon, not sleeves or hole-braces, and never too tight: X-shape for pain below the kneecap, around the kneecap for kneecap pain, wrapped inside → out. He still tapes his previously torn left knee when it flares.
- **Numbers:** —
- **Scope:** Knee pain/tendinitis.
- **Confidence:** medium — ~4 videos, 2020→2024
- **Status:** current

- **Statement:** Signs: pain at the knee break (not the rest of the rep), worse going up stairs, a warm/tender knee, sudden "giving way" when walking. Pain that fades once warm suggests tendinitis; pain that keeps rising suggests a tear.

- **Scope:** Knee pain.

## Shoulders

<a id="INJ-87"></a>
### INJ-87 · Frequent heavy flat bench injures shoulders
- **Statement:** Frequent heavy horizontal pressing is the main cause of shoulder injury regardless of form, unless you're an outlier. Injuries are almost always to the rotator cuff/AC joint, not the delts; he claims they are the #1 injury in retired powerlifters. The tell is an achy soreness between pec and shoulder the next day.
- **Numbers:** Benching 3×/wk (or 10×10) smoked his shoulders; 3×/wk flat bench = shoulder pain for many intermediates.
- **Scope:** Heavy pressers, intermediates and up.
- **Confidence:** high — ~14 videos, 2020→2023
- **Status:** current
- **Check:** Is heavy flat bench kept infrequent (not 3×/wk) or rotated with other horizontal variations?
- **Sources:** ([Tips to combat shoulder pain, 2020-02](https://youtu.be/IahVc0kbGOU?t=126); [Response to Husaka - CHEST - Bench vs Ring Push Ups, 2020-03](https://youtu.be/K4UBm1dV6WM?t=819); [𝙃𝙊𝙍𝙍𝙄𝙁𝙄𝘾 𝙡𝙞𝙛𝙩𝙞𝙣𝙜 𝙞𝙣𝙟𝙪, 2022-08](https://youtu.be/yoROLGGUPXU?t=503); [The Best Natural Lifter You've NEVER Heard Of (Hersovyac), 2023-04](https://youtu.be/-sf34ScWLK8?t=1074))

- **Scope:** Pressers with shoulder issues.

- **Statement:** Touch-and-go bench protracted his right shoulder until at 24 he could barely raise his arm; paused bench, Spoto press and the Slingshot let him bench pain-free again.

<a id="INJ-92"></a>
### INJ-92 · External rotation and upper back for pressers
- **Statement:** External rotation, rear delt and upper-back work keep shoulders healthy, and heavy pressing needs it directly: an upper-back movement every push day. Keep rehab movements in even when pain is gone.
- **Numbers:** Face pulls 15-20+ or AMRAP with a band (2020); 4×15-20 (2022); 20-25 between pressing sets (2023).
- **Scope:** Heavy pressers.
- **Confidence:** high — ~14 videos, 2020→2024

Both views value rear delts.
- **Check:** Do push days include direct rear-delt/external-rotation/upper-back work (e.g. face pulls)?

## Elbows, biceps, triceps

<a id="INJ-101"></a>
### INJ-101 · Never overextend the elbow under heavy curls
- **Statement:** Never fully extend or overextend the elbow under heavy load in curls; stop the negative short and keep a slight bend. Bouncing off the tendon at full extension does nothing for growth and causes distal tears. If the shoulder moves with the arm, overextension is safe; with the shoulder frozen (preacher curls) it is not.
- **Numbers:** ~45° short of extension on concentration-type curls.
- **Scope:** Heavy curls.
- **Confidence:** high — ~10 videos, 2020→2023
- **Status:** current
- **Sources:** ([The training principles series： full range of motion, 2020-04](https://youtu.be/-wk3jSpm434?t=445); [Arm-wrestling style preacher curls tutorial, 2020-08](https://youtu.be/nHt2c7PIGME?t=63); [𝙃𝙊𝙍𝙍𝙄𝙁𝙄𝘾 𝙡𝙞𝙛𝙩𝙞𝙣𝙜 𝙞𝙣𝙟𝙪, 2022-08](https://youtu.be/yoROLGGUPXU?t=1822); [Why you should STOP doing incline curls, 2023-02](https://youtu.be/CGhPZ9AxBJE?t=126))

<a id="INJ-102"></a>
### INJ-102 · No heavy supinated pulling, no mixed grip
- **Statement:** No supinated/Yates rows, supinated shrugs, or mixed-grip deadlifts or rows: the biceps gives before the back. Bodybuilders should use double overhand, then straps; straps prevent tears and asymmetry. He claims he's never seen a tear with double overhand; mixed grip also causes bar rotation, uneven traps and lower-back torsion. Vertical supinated pulls are generally fine.
- **Numbers:** If you insist on supinated rows: 4×10-12, not 3×6-8.
- **Scope:** Bodybuilders; heavy pulls.
- **Confidence:** high — ~16 videos, 2020→2023
- **Status:** current
- **Check:** Are heavy pulls done double overhand or with straps, never mixed grip or heavy supinated rows?
- **Sources:** ([How to avoid bicep tears, 2020-03](https://youtu.be/1roZlKwps8Y?t=127); [Push/Pull Pull/Legs Legs/Push 3 days program review, 2020-05](https://youtu.be/eFhwWirR70o?t=1053); [Stop using a mixed grip, 2020-02](https://youtu.be/eU_f4lGi9vA?t=63); [The Streetlifting MUTANT w/ Steel Cable Tendons (Artem Shirokov), 2023-12](https://youtu.be/M2yqxp4IHXg?t=1760))

# 10. Nutrition & supplements

This chapter covers what NH says about food, energy balance, protein and macros, meal timing, fasting, food quality, individual food choices, drinks, the psychology of eating, and supplements. His stance: for naturals, training drives growth and diet only fuels it, though diet is the top factor for long-term health. He eats mostly whole, home-cooked, carb-heavy food with modest protein, tailors it to his own body and ancestry, and treats supplements as "D tier", taking only creatine, MSM, bee pollen and a little whey. Bulking, cutting and cardio strategy are in ch. 11.

## Where diet ranks

He ranks training above diet for building muscle, but diet above everything for health and longevity. Once a diet works, it should run on autopilot.

<a id="NUT-01"></a>
### NUT-01 · Training matters more than diet for naturals
- **Statement:** For a natural lifter, training drives muscle growth and diet only fuels it; the "diet is 70-80%" line is nonsense that comes from drug users. Nutrition only matters once training is on point.
- **Numbers:** Training is "at least 50%" (2020), "80% or more" (2023)
- **Scope:** Naturals, all levels; training's share grows as you advance
- **Confidence:** high — ~15 videos, 2020→2024
- **Status:** changed — 2020: training is at least 50%; 2023: training is 80% or more
- **Check:** Does the program treat training, not diet, as the main driver of muscle gain?
- **Sources:** ([Should natural lifters bulk / cut?, 2020-02](https://youtu.be/VpPf9o5923k?t=253); [Supplements are (mostly) useless, 2020-06](https://youtu.be/dgxdlxNZUUs?t=437); [Stop falling for these Ab Training Myths, 2023-03](https://youtu.be/-izcpmcGs-c?t=191); [Everything I eat to get HUGE (Full Bulking Plan), 2024-03](https://youtu.be/SV5rA-iMHRE))

# 11. Bulking, cutting & cardio

This chapter covers how NH thinks a natural should manage bodyweight (bulking, cutting, recomposition, body-fat ranges) and how cardio fits into bodybuilding. His default is a very slow lean bulk on a small surplus, judged by gym progress, waist, mirror and calisthenics rather than the scale. He cuts only if you start fat or compete, and he calls dirty bulks, crash cuts and yo-yo cycles his own biggest mistake. On cardio he moved from "not necessary" (2020-21) to advocate (2023+): short hard sessions after lifting so that your lungs never end a set before your muscles do.

## Who should bulk, cut or recomp

His starting question is where you are now: skinny, skinny-fat, lean but small, or fat. Over time he widened the group he tells to bulk.

<a id="BLK-01"></a>
### BLK-01 · Default for naturals: small permanent surplus
- **Statement:** Men who are not very over- or underweight should stay in a small surplus for their whole career ("perma-bulk"), unless they start out fat; overshooting body fat once ruins it.
- **Numbers:** "permabulk from day one for 15 years"
- **Scope:** Natural men not at a bodyweight extreme; fat starters cut first (BLK-04).
- **Confidence:** high — ~5 videos, 2020→2024, still said in 2024
- **Status:** current
- **Check:** Is the default plan a small, continuous surplus rather than repeated bulk/cut phases?
- **Sources:** ([What you should NOT be doing during a bulk, 2020-02](https://youtu.be/VAblRcVMjqw?t=248); [Should natural lifters bulk / cut?, 2020-02](https://youtu.be/VpPf9o5923k?t=379); [Can you modify the bodyfat range in which building muscle is most comfortable?, 2020-08](https://youtu.be/mUAHGlseeyk?t=566); [So you think you look good? (Physique Review LIVE), 2024-11](https://youtu.be/yZC3Nsmmzb8?t=6575))

- **Statement:** In 2020 only extremes should bulk or cut (very skinny bulk, very fat cut, everyone else near maintenance). By 2024 lean, small and formerly chubby lifters must lean bulk, and maintaining or cutting is a mistake for them; moving past the lean "auto mode" physique requires an awkward bulking phase.
- **Numbers:** example lean-but-small lifter: ~15% at 190 cm/81 kg (2024)
- **Scope:** Naturals who are lean but not big, including escaped skinny-fat and formerly chubby lifters.
- **Confidence:** high — ~10 videos, 2020→2024
- **Status:** changed — 2020: only very skinny people should bulk; 2024: lean/small lifters must bulk.

## Surplus size

The body can only turn so much food into muscle; past a small surplus the rest is fat.

<a id="BLK-12"></a>
### BLK-12 · Keep the surplus small
- **Statement:** Bulk on a small surplus; a few hundred calories is enough and more is pointless for a natural past beginner.
- **Numbers:** +200-400 kcal (2020); under 10%, "4% beats 40%" (2021); his own +300 (2022); ~500 kcal gets ~95-98% of possible gains (2022); 200 kcal "enough" (2024-09); 300 "plenty", 500 "pointless" (2024-12)
- **Scope:** Naturals past the beginner stage; see BLK-15 for the hardgainer exception.
- **Confidence:** high — ~9 videos, 2020→2024, still said in 2024
- **Status:** changed — the advised surplus shrank: 10-15% ceiling (2020) and ~500 kcal near-optimal (2022) → 200-300 kcal, 500 "pointless" (2024).
- **Check:** Is the bulking surplus around 200-300 kcal rather than 500+?
- **Sources:** ([Nutrition Q&A #1, 2020-11](https://youtu.be/vC9cKh9tFxs?t=1253); [Don't fall for the bulking meme, 2022-11](https://youtu.be/h7D6CB4p1oU?t=318); [BACK 2 THE GYM STREAM (Program reviews & Answering training questions), 2024-09](https://youtu.be/okm6bZHKHI4?t=8320); [Do you look better than Silver Era lifters? (Physique Review LIVE), 2024-12](https://youtu.be/ZLheQPgEfoA?t=8625))

<a id="BLK-13"></a>
### BLK-13 · Big surplus = fat; big deficit = muscle loss
- **Statement:** A big surplus doesn't build more natural muscle, only fat; a big deficit burns muscle as well as fat. Protein synthesis is limited, your capacity to get fat is not.
- **Numbers:** no muscle benefit above ~10-15% surplus (2020); 1000-2000 kcal does not double muscle (2022)
- **Scope:** Naturals.
- **Confidence:** high — ~8 videos, 2020→2023
- **Status:** current
- **Sources:** ([STORY TIME： My entire diet history, 2020-10](https://youtu.be/NpIo8tFRESg?t=700); [What you should NOT be doing during a bulk, 2020-02](https://youtu.be/VAblRcVMjqw?t=248); [My Nightmare Bulk (Story Time), 2023-09](https://youtu.be/XK9KjVP-5Wo?t=941); [Don't fall for the bulking meme, 2022-11](https://youtu.be/h7D6CB4p1oU?t=318))

- **Statement:** Novices should eat at maintenance and raise calories slowly as appetite grows; a big surplus is a waste.
- **Numbers:** +500 kcal or more is a waste
- **Scope:** Novices.
- **Confidence:** medium — 1 video, 2021
- **Status:** current
- **Sources:** ([The issue with Novice Programs, 2021-03](https://youtu.be/S0qBQppUtTQ?t=1670))

## Rate of gain

He measures a bulk by how slowly the scale moves, and the advised rate tightened over the years.

<a id="BLK-19"></a>
### BLK-19 · Gain about 0.5-1.5 lb per month
- **Statement:** Bulk slowly; past the beginner stage, more than a pound or so a month is mostly fat.
- **Numbers:** under 4 lb/month (2020-08); 1-2 lb/month (2020-12); 0.5-1 lb/month or ~10 lb/year (2023-07); ~1 lb/month (2023-10); 1.5 lb/month "good" on a lean bulk (2024-11)
- **Scope:** Intermediate and advanced naturals; true beginners can gain faster (BLK-21).
- **Confidence:** high — ~6 videos, 2020→2024
- **Status:** changed — 1-2 lb/month (2020) tightened to 0.5-1 lb/month after his own too-fast 2023 bulk (20-30 lb in a year); 1.5 lb/month called good in 2024.
- **Check:** Is the target gain about 0.5-1.5 lb per month (less if advanced)?
- **Sources:** ([Can you modify the bodyfat range in which building muscle is most comfortable?, 2020-08](https://youtu.be/mUAHGlseeyk?t=566); [BLOATMAXX： the Kyriakos Grizzly example, mogging general & potential downsides, 2020-12](https://youtu.be/so6MbvvtM1w?t=865); [Leg Day + Bulk Update (Hypertrophy Log #2), 2023-07](https://youtu.be/6KA80BQ9W3k?t=1317); [Therapy is CANCELLED (Jung ｜ Modern Man in Search of a Soul), 2024-11](https://youtu.be/fPU3nRIH8sM?t=9349))

- **Scope:** Advanced naturals.

- **Sources:** ([Leg Day + Bulk Update (Hypertrophy Log #2), 2023-07](https://youtu.be/6KA80BQ9W3k?t=1193); [Everything I do to get HUGE (Split, Reps, Lifts), 2023-09](https://youtu.be/43F9unmSc_I?t=2136); [BACK 2 THE GYM STREAM (Program reviews & Answering training questions), 2024-09](https://youtu.be/okm6bZHKHI4?t=9103))

Calories only fuel what the training creates.

- **Scope:** All bulking lifters.
- **Confidence:** high — ~9 videos, 2021→2023

Rising scale and bar weight do not prove muscle; he uses calisthenics, waist, mirror and the ratio of strength to bodyweight.

- **Statement:** If bench rises while push-ups regress, or rows rise while pull-ups drop, you're gaining fat: slow down or stop the bulk. Keep calisthenics in while bulking.

- **Scope:** Bulking lifters.
- **Confidence:** high — 3 videos, 2021→2024

- **Check:** Do push-ups and pull-ups hold or improve while the bulk continues?

## Dirty bulking and GOMAD

<a id="BLK-41"></a>
### BLK-41 · Dirty bulking is mostly fat
- **Statement:** Dirty bulking adds mostly fat and leverage, not muscle. Junk food is low in protein and micronutrients, so you feel sluggish and bloated; whatever muscle you keep would have come from any surplus. Big naturals got big in spite of it.

- **Scope:** Naturals.

## Recomposition

A recomp trades fat for muscle at a fixed bodyweight. He ran one for three years and then concluded a slow bulk grows you faster.

<a id="BLK-54"></a>
### BLK-54 · Recomp is real but slower than a bulk
- **Statement:** A recomp is its own thing, not a bulk/cut hybrid: heavy training at maintenance makes the body draw on fat stores, like sculpting a statue. It is slow but real; for growth, a slow bulk beats it.
- **Numbers:** his recomp: 3 years at 210 lb (2019-2022)
- **Scope:** Lifters with both muscle and fat (BLK-55).
- **Confidence:** high — ~10 videos, 2020→2024
- **Status:** changed — 2020-2021: recomp is "the future", better than bulk/cut, planned 4-5 more years; 2022-08: recomp growth "minimal compared" to a bulk, switched to a slow lean bulk; 2024: "perma-bulker is the way to go unless you start out fat".

## Cardio: purpose

For a bodybuilder, cardio exists so your heart and lungs never cut a set short.

<a id="CAR-01"></a>
### CAR-01 · Lungs must never end a set first
- **Statement:** Never end a squat or deadlift set out of breath with reps left in the muscles. Getting winded after one rep, on curls or after a bench set means poor conditioning; fix it with conditioning work or a slower tempo.
- **Numbers:** he squats 8 reps to failure and deadlifts 5 heavy without breathing hard
- **Scope:** All lifters, especially on lower-body compounds.
- **Confidence:** high — ~16 videos, 2020→2024, still said in 2024
- **Status:** current
- **Check:** Can the lifter finish hard squat and deadlift sets limited by muscle rather than breath?
- **Sources:** ([The hypertrophy series： surpassing cardiovascular limitations, 2020-05](https://youtu.be/LCpa0h89TJM?t=380); [The importance of cardio for bodybuilding & overall health, 2020-10](https://youtu.be/ckDmNEFcwW8?t=189); [Level up your legs, 2021-06](https://youtu.be/ANvvVrMqF7Y?t=1880); [Exercise Tier Lists are STUPID, 2024-11](https://youtu.be/6yW3GSskl8g?t=887))

- **Scope:** All lifters.
- **Confidence:** high — ~5 videos, 2020→2022
- **Status:** current

## Does cardio kill gains?

<a id="CAR-09"></a>
### CAR-09 · Cardio done right helps gains
- **Statement:** Cardio doesn't kill gains or testosterone. Good cardio boosts gains through more volume, better pumps and faster recovery.
- **Numbers:** biking 30 min each way to the gym didn't hurt his squat/deadlift; low-intensity running 2x/week for 20-30 min doesn't hurt
- **Scope:** Lifters.
- **Confidence:** high — ~7 videos, 2021→2024
- **Status:** changed — 2020: cardio kills gains indirectly via calories; 2024: good cardio boosts gains.
- **Sources:** ([Level up your legs, 2021-06](https://youtu.be/ANvvVrMqF7Y?t=1691); [We're turning Alan Thrall into a bodybuilder!, 2023-05](https://youtu.be/d1eLAd5WvIA?t=1630); [The ULTIMATE Cardio/Calves Exercises Tier-List, 2024-02](https://youtu.be/ryWJV6yN3ZE?t=189); [How I Built Monster Legs, 2024-12](https://youtu.be/-OjJEzZTXtQ?t=1134))

<a id="CAR-10"></a>
### CAR-10 · Cardio's real cost is calories
- **Statement:** Cardio doesn't cannibalise muscle but uses calories meant for recovery, so how much you can do depends on intake. Skinny men prioritising muscle should avoid cardio-focused activity; long slow distance limits growth only through calorie shortfall.

- **Statement:** Do a short block of high-intensity cardio after each session (it replaces pump finishers), plus low-intensity walking, hiking or swimming.

# 12. Beginners, training levels & equipment

This chapter covers how he defines novice, intermediate and advanced lifters, what he wants a novice to do, and his views on gear, straps and building or choosing a gym. On beginners, his stance is that "anything works", so a novice should play the long game: a minimal, written full-body program with isolation from day one, free weights and calisthenics, few hard sets, and adherence above all. On equipment, he says straps are a must whenever grip limits a pulling set and most other gear is optional. His gym advice moved from home-gym evangelism (2020-2021) to a hybrid home/commercial view (2023-2025).

## Why the novice phase matters

He treats the novice phase as a foundation for a long career rather than a race, and novice results as proof of nothing.

<a id="BEG-01"></a>
### BEG-01 · Anything works, so choose for the long term
- **Statement:** Almost any program works for novices. That should free them to pick what sets up the rest of their career, not justify random programs, and novice results prove nothing about a program, coach or channel.
- **Numbers:** —
- **Scope:** novices; it becomes "a game of inches" only later
- **Confidence:** high — ~18 videos, 2020→2025
- **Status:** current
- **Check:** Is the novice phase judged by skill, habits and base built rather than by how fast the numbers rise?
- **Sources:** ([How to program for novices (with an hypertrophy bias), 2020-02](https://youtu.be/QpTHtmI8nrU); [The issue with Novice Programs, 2021-03](https://youtu.be/S0qBQppUtTQ?t=442); [Surviving Novice Syndrome (a beginner's guide to lifting), 2021-08](https://youtu.be/9mnLRQsrs9k?t=2514); [RIP Natural Hypertrophy; Welcome School of Strategy!, 2025-01](https://youtu.be/J9_udWdk6ZM?t=1050))

<a id="BEG-02"></a>

- **Statement:** Novice status is short but you are an intermediate or advanced lifter for life, so use the novice period to build a base, prevent injuries and form habits rather than to chase numbers.
- **Numbers:** noob gains may be only 3-4% of your lifting time
- **Scope:** novices
- **Confidence:** medium — ~6 videos, 2020→2021
- **Status:** current
- **Sources:** ([The training principles series： noob gains, 2020-02](https://youtu.be/d7441LfRS9s?t=63); [AlphaDestiny Novice Program review (part. 1： training), 2020-03](https://youtu.be/Tw8qA93Gf58?t=1196); [How often should you change programs?, 2020-08](https://youtu.be/o9uDgF5J89U?t=313); [The issue with Novice Programs, 2021-03](https://youtu.be/S0qBQppUtTQ))

## Frequency, session length and volume

Novices lack work capacity, so he keeps their frequency moderate, sessions short and hard sets few, but not easy.

<a id="BEG-11"></a>
### BEG-11 · Three full-body days a week by default
- **Statement:** The novice default is 3 full-body days a week, 48 h apart (Mon/Wed/Fri); 2-3 days works.
- **Numbers:** 4 days is the high end; 5-6 days is "very hard to justify"; 2024: "tremendous results" on 2-3 days of ~1 h; floating rest days are for advanced lifters
- **Scope:** novices
- **Confidence:** high — ~14 videos, 2020→2024
- **Status:** contradicted — elsewhere he prefers "full body every day" with one heavy compound per day and says novices can recover from daily calisthenics, while also saying full body needs programming knowledge novices lack
- **Check:** Does the novice train 2-3 (at most 4) full-body days a week?

## Program structure and content

His novice template: a written full-body program with supersets, 2-3 compounds a day, isolation for the rest, every movement pattern, and no powerlifting bias.

<a id="BEG-23"></a>
### BEG-23 · Novices need written, rigid structure
- **Statement:** Novices need a written, fixed structure; flexibility is earned. They can't be trusted with lift rotations or optional exercises, and should start on an established program because they lack the data to program for themselves.
- **Numbers:** —
- **Scope:** novices; training by template or instinct comes later

## Reps, loading and progression

Novices start light, build skill before load, and learn overload methods beyond adding weight.

<a id="BEG-40"></a>
### BEG-40 · Start light and accumulate quality reps
- **Statement:** Start light, even with the empty bar, and accumulate quality reps without struggling or compromising the next session. Repeat a hard weight before adding more; no PR is worth an injury.
- **Numbers:** —
- **Scope:** novices
- **Confidence:** medium — ~4 videos, 2020→2021
- **Status:** current
- **Sources:** ([Free novice program for hypertrophy, 2020-02](https://youtu.be/_4wWgin1dVY?t=317); [Surviving Novice Syndrome (a beginner's guide to lifting), 2021-08](https://youtu.be/9mnLRQsrs9k?t=2885); [Ivysaur Novice program review, 2020-08](https://youtu.be/QKpAtCK6oPQ?t=563))

<a id="BEG-41"></a>
### BEG-41 · Fixed schemes first, evolving ranges on accessories
- **Statement:** Fixed schemes (5x5, 3x5) are fine at first; use evolving ranges on accessories, then spread them. If every lift uses evolving ranges, tonnage collapses when all hit their low point at once.
- **Numbers:** evolving ranges 6-10, 8-12; turning a 3x3 into a 3x3-5 takes ~2 weeks to learn
- **Scope:** novices
- **Confidence:** medium — ~6 videos, 2020→2021
- **Status:** contradicted — "evolving ranges are not suitable for beginners" vs "teach them early so they become second nature"
- **Sources:** ([How to progress forward with evolving rep ranges, 2020-09](https://youtu.be/65rLZe9cz_0?t=63); [How to progress forward with evolving rep ranges, 2020-09](https://youtu.be/65rLZe9cz_0?t=502); [The benefits of evolving rep ranges, 2020-05](https://youtu.be/2QnD9k0SbwA); [The hypertrophy series： the perfect progression scheme for muscle growth, 2021-08](https://youtu.be/ulwUVDK7RUk?t=314))

<a id="BEG-42"></a>
### BEG-42 · Use rep ranges where form stays clean
- **Statement:** Novices should use higher reps in a range where form stays clean; back work that loads the lower back and hamstrings needs at least 6-10 reps.
- **Numbers:** ≥6-10 reps; 3x6 rows get butchered; 4x8 squats are risky because of grinding and ugly reps
- **Scope:** novices
- **Confidence:** medium — ~3 videos, 2020
- **Status:** current
- **Sources:** ([Ivysaur Novice program review, 2020-08](https://youtu.be/QKpAtCK6oPQ?t=438); [Candito Upper Lower Hypertrophy Program review, 2020-05](https://youtu.be/4aThavRpYLw?t=631))

- **Statement:** Early strength gains are mostly neural and technical, not muscle.
- **Numbers:** 5-10 lb per session for a long time; +10 lb/week is mostly neural; 60 → 200 lb squat in year one is "a given"; adding 200 lb in 6 months is pointless
- **Scope:** novices
- **Confidence:** medium — ~3 videos, 2020→2021
- **Status:** current
- **Sources:** ([The problem with 5x5/3x5, 2020-06](https://youtu.be/k3O630Nz4B8?t=126); [The hypertrophy series： pairing neurological adaptation and muscle gains, 2021-02](https://youtu.be/AeIKc3A2FiY?t=250); [The issue with Novice Programs, 2021-03](https://youtu.be/S0qBQppUtTQ?t=610); [How to never have to buy a training program again in your life, 2020-11](https://youtu.be/gWdAfpJIXbc?t=247))

## Exercise selection for novices

Novice-specific choices; general exercise selection is in ch. 5 and body-part detail in ch. 6.

<a id="BEG-47"></a>
### BEG-47 · Free weights and bodyweight before machines
- **Statement:** Novices should learn on free weights and bodyweight; machines, cables and the Smith are for advanced lifters. Novices on machines "stay small for years", and a machine-and-cable novice program is a bad sign.
- **Numbers:** —
- **Scope:** novices; exception from 2024: the Smith vertical press, which handles stabilisation
- **Confidence:** high — ~9 videos, 2020→2024
- **Status:** changed — 2020-2023: the Smith is useless or harmful for beginners (never learn squat or bench on it); 2024: novices should lean on the Smith vertical press
- **Check:** Does the novice learn the main lifts with free weights or bodyweight rather than machines or the Smith?
- **Sources:** ([Is the smith machine completely useless?, 2020-02](https://youtu.be/TrU2m-4yZT0?t=627); [Fierce 5 novice program review (from an hypertrophy standpoint), 2020-02](https://youtu.be/OATtf3kPtdI?t=187); [The ULTIMATE Quads/Legs Exercises Tier-List (Platz-tier to Chicken-tier), 2023-07](https://youtu.be/_IBSNO56zuE?t=437); [1st Natural Hypertrophy stream! <a id="BEG-49"></a>
### BEG-49 · Pull-ups over pulldowns; vertical over horizontal
- **Statement:** For novices, vertical pulls matter more than horizontal pulls and pull-ups beat pulldowns, which are accessories. Vertical pulls decompress the shoulders and spine when benching often.
- **Numbers:** anyone who can do 3+ pull-ups should do them
- **Scope:** novices
- **Confidence:** medium — ~5 videos, 2020→2021
- **Status:** current

<a id="BEG-50"></a>
### BEG-50 · Pull-up progression for novices
- **Statement:** Use negatives if you can't do a pull-up, then many low-rep sets or AMRAP sets, and stay at bodyweight until a clean 15. No weighted chins for novices.
- **Numbers:** many sets of 2-3 (novice max ~5); 3 sets AMRAP; negatives 3 x 5-8 (can go first in the session, straps for grip); 15 clean reps before adding weight; 1-2 grips (pronated plus chin-up)
- **Scope:** novices
- **Confidence:** medium — ~7 videos, 2020→2021
- **Status:** current
- **Sources:** ([Free novice program for hypertrophy, 2020-02](https://youtu.be/_4wWgin1dVY?t=127); [AlphaDestiny Novice Program review (part. 1： training), 2020-03](https://youtu.be/Tw8qA93Gf58?t=819); [Hypertrophy Q&A #5, 2021-01](https://youtu.be/-anA4CV2SVU?t=567); [Joe Fazer's Workout program for Skinny guys trying to get Bigger review, 2021-06](https://youtu.be/ZkQZPnTVKpg?t=315))

<a id="BEG-51"></a>
### BEG-51 · No barbell or Pendlay rows for novices
- **Statement:** Novices can't pull from the floor well yet, so use cable or dumbbell rows; cable rows teach the lower back before it must bridge a row. Most intermediates should skip barbell rows too.
- **Numbers:** —
- **Scope:** novices and most intermediates
- **Confidence:** high — ~5 videos, 2020→2021
- **Status:** current
- **Sources:** ([Fierce 5 novice program review (from an hypertrophy standpoint), 2020-02](https://youtu.be/OATtf3kPtdI?t=375); [6 days Pull Push Legs program review, 2020-08](https://youtu.be/jSUmn33lmlI?t=376); [Why Novices shouldn't do Barbell Rows, 2021-08](https://youtu.be/Q5y4wM8zcWY?t=631); [Why Novices shouldn't do Barbell Rows, 2021-08](https://youtu.be/Q5y4wM8zcWY?t=1764))

<a id="BEG-52"></a>
### BEG-52 · A full-ROM floor pull, at low volume
- **Statement:** A full-ROM pull from the floor is mandatory for novices, but deadlift volume stays low. Any full hip hinge counts (conventional, sumo, trap bar, Atlas stones).
- **Numbers:** 1x5 is "excellent"; 1x5, 3x3 or 3x5 is enough; 3-4 x 6-10 or 4 x 6-12 is too much; once a week keeps novices coming back for PRs
- **Scope:** novices
- **Confidence:** high — ~5 videos, 2020→2024
- **Status:** contradicted — one video says novices should squat and deadlift several times a week (with deloads), while his own routine deliberately deadlifts once a week
- **Check:** Does the novice pull a full-ROM hip hinge from the floor about once a week at low volume (about 1x5 to 3x5)?
- **Sources:** ([Fierce 5 novice program review (from an hypertrophy standpoint), 2020-02](https://youtu.be/OATtf3kPtdI?t=439); [Starting Strength - novice program review (ft. Pepe), 2020-07](https://youtu.be/et6AylDr1uk?t=253); [The issue with Novice Programs, 2021-03](https://youtu.be/S0qBQppUtTQ?t=1540); [Who can afford to only squat and deadlift once a week?, 2020-03](https://youtu.be/awNEfmfGkmY?t=189))

<a id="BEG-53"></a>
### BEG-53 · Deadlift entry points and grip
- **Statement:** Ways in: trap bar (high → low handles → conventional), rack pulls to learn the hinge, deficits to teach leg drive, dumbbell deadlifts. No Jefferson or snatch-grip deadlifts for novices; grip double overhand with straps (see EQP-07).
- **Numbers:** no mixed grip at least until a 300 lb deadlift
- **Scope:** novices, non-competitors
- **Confidence:** medium — ~4 videos, 2020→2024
- **Status:** current
- **Sources:** ([Conventional VS Sumo VS Trap bar： Which deadlift style is best for you?, 2021-08](https://youtu.be/lG5SZbRdOjA?t=1575); [Programming for people with limited mobility, 2020-11](https://youtu.be/sK78-yohV1s?t=785); [AlphaDestiny Novice Program review (part. 2： FAQ), 2020-04](https://youtu.be/T_DyRlu3Y7I?t=696); [Stop using a mixed grip, 2020-02](https://youtu.be/eU_f4lGi9vA?t=440))

- **Statement:** Novices should squat free and unsupported, to parallel. A box fixes depth instead of mobility and box squatters can't reach parallel later, so squat higher and deepen over months; mobility is innate, just unpracticed.

- **Scope:** novices
- **Confidence:** high — ~5 videos, 2020→2021
- **Status:** current

- **Statement:** The paused back squat is the one novice variation. No front squats, which need thoracic mobility and front-rack time, unless the lifter loves them.
- **Numbers:** squat 2x/week (once regular, once paused); 1-3 heavy sets of 4-8 plus 3 back-off sets

- **Confidence:** high — ~5 videos, 2020→2022

## Learning to program

He sees learning to write your own program as the real exit from the novice phase, and optimisation as a novice trap.

<a id="BEG-63"></a>
### BEG-63 · Learn by modifying the program you run
- **Statement:** Learn to program by modifying the novice program you run, then use it as a skeleton: copy its rep ranges, match its tonnage, stay minimalist. The first draft will look terrible; if the base program is very bad, start from scratch.
- **Numbers:** run it 3-6 months with fixes; drafting your own while on it may take a year
- **Scope:** late novices
- **Confidence:** high — ~9 videos, 2020→2024
- **Status:** changed — 2020: novices shouldn't write programs (theirs are almost always bad); 2021: draft your own while running the novice program; 2024: start on an established program, then write your own and have a coach review it (a refinement, not a flip)
- **Sources:** ([How to never have to buy a training program again in your life, 2020-11](https://youtu.be/gWdAfpJIXbc?t=123); [How often should you change programs?, 2020-08](https://youtu.be/o9uDgF5J89U?t=376); [How to program your training yourself, 2021-02](https://youtu.be/rlWIogS2Qho?t=340); [So you think you look good? (Physique Review LIVE), 2024-11](https://youtu.be/yZC3Nsmmzb8?t=8488))

<a id="BEG-64"></a>

- **Numbers:** sessions jump from 45 to 90 min
- **Scope:** novice → intermediate transition
- **Confidence:** medium — ~4 videos, 2020→2021
- **Status:** current
- **Sources:** ([Alpha/Beta testing your program, 2021-05](https://youtu.be/8A7hSygtWfM?t=125); [How to program your training yourself, 2021-02](https://youtu.be/rlWIogS2Qho?t=360); [The Bridge (by Austin Baraki & Jordan Feigenbaum ft Alan Thrall) Program review, 2020-07](https://youtu.be/YcHkXwsIOI8?t=125); [How to start doing more volume in your training, 2020-09](https://youtu.be/p6WcFTOBq3s?t=134))

## Quitting, burnout and adherence

He attributes most novice dropout to doing too much too soon, and puts adherence first.

<a id="BEG-70"></a>
### BEG-70 · About 90% of lifters quit, mostly as novices
- **Statement:** Most people who start lifting quit, mostly in the novice phase.
- **Numbers:** 90% (2020, 2021, 2022); 95% during the novice-to-intermediate move (2020, "made up"); 80-90% as novices (2023)
- **Scope:** novices
- **Confidence:** high — ~5 videos, 2020→2023
- **Status:** current
- **Sources:** ([When are you intermediate and what it means programming wise (for bodybuilding), 2020-02](https://youtu.be/y_lPAdWi4sU?t=507); [Candito Upper Lower Hypertrophy Program review, 2020-05](https://youtu.be/4aThavRpYLw?t=125); [How to stop being a lazy slob (According to Reddit), 2022-03](https://youtu.be/Jdv6dG_Stzw?t=1972); [Escape Intermediate Hell (Path to Exceptional Physique), 2023-10](https://youtu.be/16fjHEtZTCA))

<a id="BEG-71"></a>
### BEG-71 · "Novice syndrome": overdoing it is the main crash cause
- **Statement:** Overdoing it, not lack of potential, is the top reason novices crash, and it is mostly mental. Burnout is over-stimulation (e.g. 2 h sessions), not overtraining; a program that stops you training for a full week is bad for you.
- **Numbers:** a year mildly intense beats six months super intense
- **Scope:** novices
- **Confidence:** high — ~8 videos, 2020→2022
- **Status:** current
- **Check:** Is the novice workload modest enough that it never forces a full week off training?

## Straps, grip and hand care

Straps are his strongest equipment position: grip should never be what ends a back set.

<a id="EQP-01"></a>
### EQP-01 · Strap up when grip limits a pulling set
- **Statement:** Use straps as soon as grip limits a back or pulling set, and spend the saved grip on direct forearm work. "Letting grip limit the back is criminal"; straps let you isolate the back better and don't hurt forearm growth.
- **Numbers:** forearm isolation costs only 10-15 min/week
- **Scope:** non-powerlifters with a hypertrophy goal, once grip limits (not novices at first, see EQP-04)
- **Confidence:** high — ~10 videos, 2020→2025
- **Status:** current
- **Check:** Are straps used on back and pull sets where grip would otherwise end the set, with forearms trained directly?

## Home gym vs commercial gym

His view moved from "you eventually need your own gym" (2020-2021) to a hybrid in which commercial gyms are optimal for hypertrophy (2023-2025).

<a id="EQP-20"></a>
### EQP-20 · Commercial gyms are optimal; train hybrid
- **Statement:** His current view is that commercial gyms are optimal for building muscle. He trains about 50/50: legs at home; pull-ups, overhead and isolation at the gym. He joined a gym because home limits explained his lagging triceps and delts.

## Minimal-equipment training

You can grow with little equipment, but calisthenics alone makes legs and big size hard.

- **Statement:** A pull-up bar, wooden gymnastic rings and bands are enough for excellent gains; rings are invaluable without a gym. Add a dip station.

- **Scope:** no-gym trainees

## Platform, floor and mats

<a id="EQP-52"></a>
### EQP-52 · Build your own platform
- **Statement:** Don't lift on bare concrete (drops damage it, and it's hard on knees and stability); build your own platform for a fraction of retail.
- **Numbers:** DIY <$150 vs ~$1000 retail (2020); $100 at Home Depot vs $1000 Rogue (2023); his 16x8 ft platform ~$500 vs ≥$4000 custom (Feb 2020); his 16x9 ft one $800-900 vs $5-6k contracted (Dec 2020); ~$3000 saved
- **Scope:** garage and home lifters
- **Confidence:** high — ~5 videos, 2020→2023
- **Status:** current
- **Sources:** ([Equipment you can afford to go cheap on for your home gym, 2020-02](https://youtu.be/Lg0FY5wzMqw?t=248); [The logistics of building a weight lifting platform to save money, 2020-05](https://youtu.be/j0UMvyV80VY); [10 000$ Home Gym Tour - 10k subs special, 2020-12](https://youtu.be/SbPaZ5giUNs?t=123); [HELP! I'm getting too BIG (Hypertrophy Log #5), 2023-11](https://youtu.be/6YC_gmRNhPo?t=1325))

<a id="EQP-53"></a>
### EQP-53 · How to build the platform
- **Statement:** Plan on paper and do a mock assembly; buy plywood in person (online stock is warped). Use mid-quality wood for the base and the best wood for the top; glue the base layers but screw the mats and top wood so damaged pieces can be swapped. Shim sloped garage floors, add a vapour barrier in arctic climates, and use wood screws if bolting a rack.
- **Numbers:** plan 1-2 months ahead; top wood ~3x the price; glue dries ~40 min; swapping a damaged piece ~$30
- **Scope:** platform builders
- **Confidence:** medium — ~3 videos, 2020
- **Status:** current
- **Sources:** ([The logistics of building a weight lifting platform to save money, 2020-05](https://youtu.be/j0UMvyV80VY?t=256); [The logistics of building a weight lifting platform to save money, 2020-05](https://youtu.be/j0UMvyV80VY?t=820); [The logistics of building a weight lifting platform to save money, 2020-05](https://youtu.be/j0UMvyV80VY?t=692); [10 000$ Home Gym Tour - 10k subs special, 2020-12](https://youtu.be/SbPaZ5giUNs?t=308))

<a id="EQP-54"></a>
### EQP-54 · Horse stall mats, with drawbacks
- **Statement:** Horse stall mats are the best and cheapest mats; avoid online puzzle mats. Use two layers or screw them to wood on sensitive floors. Drawbacks: slippery for squat, OHP and bench leg drive (wood is "night and day" better), they crease, shift and collect moisture.
- **Numbers:** the wood under his deadlift spot sank after ~7 months
- **Scope:** home gym floors
- **Confidence:** medium — ~2 videos, 2020
- **Status:** current
- **Sources:** ([The cheapest gym floor option： stall mats, 2020-04](https://youtu.be/vW-SG1vMgHQ?t=62); [The cheapest gym floor option： stall mats, 2020-04](https://youtu.be/vW-SG1vMgHQ?t=436); [The cheapest gym floor option： stall mats, 2020-04](https://youtu.be/vW-SG1vMgHQ?t=185); [The cheapest gym floor option： stall mats, 2020-04](https://youtu.be/vW-SG1vMgHQ?t=374))

- **Scope:** home gym builders
- **Confidence:** medium — ~3 videos, 2020

### EQP-67 · Dumbbell-only training is less efficient
- **Statement:** Dumbbell-only training is limited: you outgrow them on deadlifts, goblet squats aren't back squats, and isolating legs and triceps is hard. Cables are a big upgrade, and barbells offer more than dumbbells (load aside).
- **Numbers:** you outgrow 100 lb DBs on deadlifts
- **Scope:** dumbbell-only trainees
- **Confidence:** medium — ~3 videos, 2020→2024

### EQP-68 · Adjustable dumbbells are a trap
- **Statement:** Adjustable dumbbells are a "trap" (pricey base and plates), worth it only with frequent use. Buy used dumbbells from closing gyms or private sellers instead, but avoid cheap junk dumbbells, which can cause wrist tendonitis.
- **Numbers:** worth it only if used ≥3x/week (2024); junk DBs ~$30-50 a pair
- **Scope:** home gym buyers
- **Confidence:** medium — ~4 videos, 2020→2024

# 13. The fitness industry & reading science

This chapter covers how NH sees the fitness business (programs, coaching, supplements, influencers, YouTube itself), how to judge whom to trust, and how he weighs scientific evidence against lived experience. His stance: the industry exists to sell, hard work can't be sold, and lifting knowledge should be free, so learn to program for yourself and question anyone who profits from you. On science he calls himself experience-based rather than "science-based": he is against scientism and the "science-based" brand, not against the scientific method. Everything said here about named people and brands is his unverified opinion. PEDs and natural limits as such are in ch. 2, training variables in ch. 3-4, supplements in ch. 10.

## Selling knowledge: programs and coaching

He holds that knowledge you got for free should stay free, that a lifter who can program needs no one, and that most paid programs and coaching exploit beginners. His own paid tier from late 2024 is the main exception (see IND-21).

<a id="IND-01"></a>
### IND-01 · Lifting knowledge should be free
- **Statement:** Charging for knowledge you got for free is unjust; all his own programs are free, and he likens paid plans to selling festival water when free water is hidden nearby.
- **Numbers:** ~30 free programs by 2023; a $50-100 non-personalised program or ebook is "ridiculous"; $1000 for plans is overpriced
- **Scope:** Non-personalised programs, ebooks and plans
- **Confidence:** high — ~12 videos, 2020→2023
- **Status:** changed — he stayed opposed to selling generic programs, but from Dec 2024 runs a paid personalised tier (see IND-21)
- **Sources:** ([RANT： You don't need a coach, 2020-02](https://youtu.be/UKr-dWXa73Q?t=125); [Vertical diet review, 2020-06](https://youtu.be/YVxYG7FhlVE); [Censorship on Youtube： How Greg Doucette betrayed the entire Fitness community b, 2021-05](https://youtu.be/vVlpg3202Uw?t=2936); [HUGE ANNOUNCEMENT 🎁 (You're gonna love this), 2023-12](https://youtu.be/Rc9jhSVGoxM?t=64))

## How he weighs evidence

He ranks your own tested experience above studies, pooled experience above single papers, and treats science as a bonus that is useful only if it improves training.

<a id="SCI-01"></a>
### SCI-01 · Your own body is the best evidence
- **Statement:** Your own body's data is the most valid evidence; studies are group generalisations that are worthless until tested on yourself, and your experience matters more than his or all the science. "Optimal" is whatever you've proven works on your body.
- **Numbers:** —
- **Scope:** All lifters
- **Confidence:** high — ~7 videos, 2020→2023
- **Status:** current
- **Check:** Is the method judged by how the lifter actually responded to it, not only by what studies say?
- **Sources:** ([You don't need science to see results, 2020-04](https://youtu.be/37WbiLy4Dkc?t=63); [The hypertrophy series： using mind muscle connection for tonnage quality control, 2020-06](https://youtu.be/Hn3oGdUUhic?t=253); [The impact of exogenous estrogen on the male body (from a broscientist perspecti, 2020-03](https://youtu.be/j2DCJGxIE-s); [5 Secrets of Elite Natural Lifters, 2023-10](https://youtu.be/iU-oYc8fbEM?t=1328))

<a id="SCI-02"></a>
### SCI-02 · He doesn't cite studies
- **Statement:** He never cites or links studies or uses them as arguments of authority; his channel shares experience, and a natural with a good physique is "a mine of knowledge" as valuable as peer review.
- **Numbers:** —
- **Scope:** His channel
- **Confidence:** high — ~5 videos, 2020→2024
- **Status:** contradicted — he invokes specific studies when they support him (tempo, ROM, boxers, 500 mg testosterone, lengthened vs 90°), close to the cherry-picking he criticises (SCI-12)
- **Sources:** ([The impact of exogenous estrogen on the male body (from a broscientist perspecti, 2020-03](https://youtu.be/j2DCJGxIE-s?t=505); [The Galaxy Brains of YT Fitness have ruined science, 2021-01](https://youtu.be/662MjNpnQcw?t=190); [The ULTIMATE Triceps Exercises Tier-List (Mythical-tier to Toothpick-tier), 2022-10](https://youtu.be/ylmTf9Qb6jg?t=1067); [New hypertrophy study just dropped (And Basically You're F＊cking Stupid), 2024-01](https://youtu.be/vVQmYGw7Kj8?t=508))

# 14. Life philosophy, culture & manga

This chapter covers what NH teaches beyond training: how to live, what to value, how to handle relationships, and the anime, manga, books and physical-culture history that shaped him. His core position is that lifting is one half of a complete life: body and mind must be built together, struggle beats comfort, you own your life completely, and strength only counts once it serves others. His philosophy moved from Stoicism (2020) through Nietzsche (2022-23) to Jung (2024), and much of this chapter is opinion, not training method. Claims about real people are his unverified opinions.

## Body and mind: the complete man

The base of his worldview is that the body is not secondary. Training is a spiritual practice, but it does not fix your life by itself.

<a id="PHI-01"></a>
### PHI-01 · Build body and mind together
- **Statement:** Body and spirit must be developed together; the ideal is the "complete man" or "educated barbarian". Training without reading and thinking is as unbalanced as theory without a body.
- **Numbers:** Training 10 h/day without reading "won't even produce proper gains".
- **Scope:** Everyone, especially men; applies to lifters and to intellectuals alike.
- **Confidence:** high — ~20 videos, 2020→2023
- **Status:** changed — 2020: the body is "the lesser part", an envelope ("you are not your body"); 2021-23: body and soul are one coin and the body belongs at the centre of life (see PHI-03).
- **Check:** Does the program or advice treat training as part of a whole life that also includes reading, thinking and other people?
- **Sources:** ([The Educated Barbarian： Book of Five Rings analysis (part. 4), 2020-05](https://youtu.be/j2u5TzD5fGg?t=442); [The Educated Barbarian： Book of Five Rings analysis (part. 6), 2020-06](https://youtu.be/QTxLU8WTx6g?t=64); [The Educated Barbarian： Hagakure analysis (part. 5), 2020-08](https://youtu.be/O-x2v688wrg?t=1070); [The Problematic Masculinity of 300, 2023-01](https://youtu.be/TPcnP8Tvj5E?t=307))

<a id="PHI-02"></a>

- **Statement:** Modern life is almost all mind and little body, while antiquity was balanced. He blames mind-body dualism (traced to Christianity's view of the body as impure) and schools built to train desk workers, and wants physical education restored.
- **Numbers:** ~95% mind / 5% body today vs ~50/50 in antiquity; 2 h of school PE a week is not enough.
- **Scope:** Society, schools, children.
- **Confidence:** medium — ~4 videos, 2022→2023
- **Status:** current
- **Sources:** ([Indian Lifting Wisdom, 2022-07](https://youtu.be/4W_D07eE29I?t=563); [Medieval Lifting Wisdom, 2022-04](https://youtu.be/3W-yE2pgTec?t=696); [Are you too smart to lift?, 2023-01](https://youtu.be/pBszDfFvoVI?t=190); [Are you too smart to lift?, 2023-01](https://youtu.be/pBszDfFvoVI?t=317))

## Health, longevity and aging

Health comes before muscle, and the purpose of a lifetime of lifting is to stay strong and mobile into old age.

<a id="PHI-11"></a>
### PHI-11 · Health comes before muscle
- **Statement:** Being muscular is pointless if you die in your 50s; sickness takes the muscle anyway. Natural bodybuilding is also about a long life. Great genetics don't excuse neglecting health (he cites Apollon, a lifelong smoker who died young of throat cancer).
- **Numbers:** 350 lb isn't healthy even at 6% body fat.
- **Scope:** All lifters, especially naturals.
- **Confidence:** high — ~8 videos, 2020→2024
- **Status:** current
- **Check:** Does the approach put long-term health ahead of maximal size?
- **Sources:** ([Assessing your ancestry/DNA to hone in your diet, 2020-10](https://youtu.be/ylbxNE-2Im0?t=1040); [How to do squats for SIZE, 2022-09](https://youtu.be/XAcv427WvMw?t=1230); [BLOATMAXX： the Kyriakos Grizzly example, mogging general & potential downsides, 2020-12](https://youtu.be/so6MbvvtM1w?t=1045); [How I Built Monster Legs, 2024-12](https://youtu.be/-OjJEzZTXtQ?t=1324))

<a id="PHI-12"></a>
### PHI-12 · Muscle is your lifeline in old age
- **Statement:** People lose the ability to walk without glute, hamstring and quad muscle. He wants to be mobile and strong at 70-80 and keep the ability to squat and hinge heavy, even with less volume and intensity. "We all age but we don't have to get old."
- **Numbers:** Lifelong trainees should live healthy to 80-85; dying at 70 is "a tragedy"; mobile and strong at 70-80.
- **Scope:** Lifelong trainees.

# Appendix A. Contradictions & how his views changed

Collected by script from the topic syntheses: where NH changed his mind over time, and where he said conflicting things without a clear evolution. The principles in the chapters carry the same information in their **Status** field; this appendix shows it all in one place.

## Aesthetics

**Changed over time**

- **Shoulders**: 2020-2022 kept delts deliberately small, cut shoulder tonnage, wanted arms bigger than delts ([Road to bigger shoulders update, 2021-05](https://youtu.be/MkhKlZeBpg4); [Hypertrophy Q&A #8, 2021-09](https://youtu.be/P89o8FBSWDI?t=2037); [My Program to go BERSERKER MODE (BODYBUILDING GOAL PHYSIQUE), 2022-06](https://youtu.be/itnjfi6RYtY?t=63)) → 2023 shoulders are his weak point and must catch up with his huge upper back; 2024 priorities: rounder shoulders via vertical presses and isolation ([Wild Man Training (Hypertrophy Log #0), 2023-06](https://youtu.be/P7ADeDVghxg?t=804); [Everything I do to get HUGE (Split, Reps, Lifts), 2023-09](https://youtu.be/43F9unmSc_I?t=62)); 2024 tier list puts shoulders top tier, though he still likes them small next to the arm ([The Most Important Muscles to Look JACKED (Aesthetics Tier-List), 2024-03](https://youtu.be/fycepPpxN_k?t=2706); [Do you look better than Silver Era lifters? (Physique Review LIVE), 2024-12](https://youtu.be/ZLheQPgEfoA?t=877)). Later view: grow them, keep arms dominant.
- **Neck size**: 2020 neck should be wider than the jaw and ≈ arm size (18 in for 19 in arms) ([Road to a bigger neck： 18 inches or bust!, 2020-01](https://youtu.be/PfqgZ3_2EcM?t=128); [How to body measurements & discussing my weak points, 2020-02](https://youtu.be/KlSyeS0R9FE?t=623)) → 2022-2024 in line with the jaw is enough, more looks like a ball ([Most UNDERRATED Muscle for Aesthetics (TAKE THE NECK PILL), 2022-11](https://youtu.be/1U5cgUdos88?t=315); [The Most Important Muscles to Look JACKED (Aesthetics Tier-List), 2024-03](https://youtu.be/fycepPpxN_k?t=3083)). Later view: jaw-line standard.
- **Chest in his ideal**: 2020-2022 trunk/chest comparatively small (Berserker, Buddha physique) ([Going Berserker mode (Berserk physique introduction), 2020-03](https://youtu.be/NTMGQPjpP00?t=126); [Why you NEED a goal body, 2021-09](https://youtu.be/PYICG0hBlVo?t=446); [My Program to go BERSERKER MODE (BODYBUILDING GOAL PHYSIQUE), 2022-06](https://youtu.be/itnjfi6RYtY?t=63)) → 2023 Berserker includes a big chest ([Everything I do to get HUGE (Split, Reps, Lifts), 2023-09](https://youtu.be/43F9unmSc_I)).
- **Abs' importance**: 2020-2023 core is key and ties the physique together ([My philosophy regarding abs training, 2020-03](https://youtu.be/rGt7TWcWD60); [Come with me if you want ABS! (6 PACK MASSterplan), 2023-05](https://youtu.be/7KDB5wzgY4c)) → 2024 tier list: abs bottom tier *for everyday clothed looks* ([The Most Important Muscles to Look JACKED (Aesthetics Tier-List), 2024-03](https://youtu.be/fycepPpxN_k?t=2328)), while he still says never skip core ([1st Natural Hypertrophy stream! ASK YOUR QUESTIONS AND I SHALL ANSWER, 2024-09](https://youtu.be/bRKQIOYo2u4?t=1343)). A refinement by context (clothed vs shirtless).
- **Glutes**: 2022 silver era didn't chase glutes, posterior chain optional ([Silver Era Aesthetics Program (Steve Reeves Physique Workout), 2022-10](https://youtu.be/g-pqgciOSgE?t=695)) → 2024 glutes top tier ([The Most Important Muscles to Look JACKED (Aesthetics Tier-List), 2024-03](https://youtu.be/fycepPpxN_k?t=1579)) (he already said in 2021 they can't hurt a male physique ([Level up your legs, 2021-06](https://youtu.be/ANvvVrMqF7Y?t=248))).
- **His own body fat/weight**: 210 lb at 17-18% (2020) and 16-17% (2021-22) → 220 lb, 17-18% (2024) ([What everyone gets WRONG about bodyfat %, 2020-05](https://youtu.be/JYl3S7yuN6M); [How Big Can You Get Naturally? (Nattyornot.com), 2021-12](https://youtu.be/oAXzDQIwvLg?t=1331); [This Calisthenics Freak Makes Bodybuilders Look Small (Baki_HD), 2024-06](https://youtu.be/2LoP6-KdEx4?t=2269); [10 Signs you might be a Blackpilled Natty, 2024-04](https://youtu.be/loDNjTHZjG4?t=2084)).

**Contradictions**

- **Leanness as a goal**: 2020 "as big as his body allows at the lowest bodyfat possible" ([Seven Deadly Fitness Sins： Lust, 2020-05](https://youtu.be/U7WtpNeiRjI?t=125)) vs 2024 "never cared about being lean and still does not" ([Therapy is CANCELLED (Jung ｜ Modern Man in Search of a Soul), 2024-11](https://youtu.be/fPU3nRIH8sM?t=9411)).
- **Do heavy squats and hinges thicken the waist?** 2022: they develop the waist, don't overdo them ([Greek Aesthetics Bodybuilding Program (Apollonian Physique Workout), 2022-05](https://youtu.be/SPicD3F686s?t=316)) vs 2022: that idea is "mostly nonsense" ([Farnese Hercules Bodybuilding Program (Ancient Greek Herculean Physique Workout), 2022-03](https://youtu.be/IYobXlRVLd0?t=871)).
- **Tight waist**: 2020 he doesn't care about a tiny waist ([Going Berserker mode (Berserk physique introduction), 2020-03](https://youtu.be/NTMGQPjpP00?t=319)) vs 2020 keeps the waist as tight as possible ([Natural Hypertrophy： What I picture as my ideal physique, 2020-01](https://youtu.be/4Js7OkiuuKU?t=126)). Probably both mean "can't be tiny, keep it tight".
- **Upper back and other limbs as priorities for others**: 2020 "never too much upper back" ([Road to a Bigger Back update, 2020-11](https://youtu.be/gxo4R0lHJIk?t=251)) vs 2022 classical statues/Apollonian lack a wide lat flare and have smaller arms and legs ([Farnese Hercules Bodybuilding Program (Ancient Greek Herculean Physique Workout), 2022-03](https://youtu.be/IYobXlRVLd0?t=61); [Greek Aesthetics Bodybuilding Program (Apollonian Physique Workout), 2022-05](https://youtu.be/SPicD3F686s?t=815)). These are goal-dependent, not a real conflict.

## Beginners

**Changed over time**

- **Small muscle groups: "later" → "from day one".** 2020: calves are unimportant for novices, and neck, traps and calves can wait until you have a solid physique ([Fierce 5 novice program review (from an hypertrophy standpoint), 2020-02](https://youtu.be/OATtf3kPtdI?t=626); [Fierce 5 novice program review (from an hypertrophy standpoint), 2020-02](https://youtu.be/OATtf3kPtdI?t=1757)). 2023: forearm isolation is optional ([Come with me if you want big forearms (7 Steps MASSterplan), 2023-02](https://youtu.be/clzLnKrm6Ao?t=758)). 2024 (later view): isolate forearms from day one and catch dormant weak points early ([BACK 2 THE GYM STREAM (Program reviews & Answering training questions), 2024-09](https://youtu.be/okm6bZHKHI4?t=4630); [Do you look better than Silver Era lifters? (Physique Review LIVE), 2024-12](https://youtu.be/ZLheQPgEfoA?t=2410)).
- **What "base" means.** 2020: novices should build a wide base covering all movement patterns, and in one video should focus only on bench, squat and deadlift before hypertrophy work ([Strength training is for SUCKERS (Natty or not.com), 2020-07](https://youtu.be/7XqE7GhDsgc?t=438); [Free 3 times a week full body hypertrophy program, 2020-01](https://youtu.be/xFVva4-swKc?t=627)). 2023 (later view): a real base is push-up and pull-up proficiency, and his programs skew toward bodybuilding because there is "no reason to waste years building a 'base'" ([These Lifts BUILT My Physique (Top 10 Hypertrophy List), 2023-02](https://youtu.be/ABTeMrXdgI4?t=670); [Powerbuilding Drama： The Final Answer, 2023-11](https://youtu.be/SZEjCsuclx8?t=2913)).
- **Length of the novice phase.** 2020-04: novices shouldn't stay novices more than 4-6 months ([Programming for high change personality types, 2020-04](https://youtu.be/TwuT80wJql8?t=125)). 2020-11 → 2021: prolong it to 1-2 years ([How to never have to buy a training program again in your life, 2020-11](https://youtu.be/gWdAfpJIXbc?t=497); [Surviving Novice Syndrome (a beginner's guide to lifting), 2021-08](https://youtu.be/9mnLRQsrs9k?t=916)). 2024: done within a year for many ([So you think you look good? (Physique Review LIVE), 2024-11](https://youtu.be/yZC3Nsmmzb8?t=10549)).
- **Smith machine.** 2020-2023: useless or harmful for beginners ([Is the smith machine completely useless?, 2020-02](https://youtu.be/TrU2m-4yZT0?t=627); [The ULTIMATE Quads/Legs Exercises Tier-List (Platz-tier to Chicken-tier), 2023-07](https://youtu.be/_IBSNO56zuE?t=437)). 2024 (later view, vertical press only): novices should lean heavily on the Smith vertical press because it handles stabilisation ([1st Natural Hypertrophy stream! ASK YOUR QUESTIONS AND I SHALL ANSWER, 2024-09](https://youtu.be/bRKQIOYo2u4?t=4770)).
- **Lateral raises.** 2020: beginners don't need side raises ([Fierce 5 novice program review (from an hypertrophy standpoint), 2020-02](https://youtu.be/OATtf3kPtdI?t=1503)). 2022: they are in his novice shoulder example ([Come with me if you want big shoulders (JOIN THE CHALLENGE!), 2022-10](https://youtu.be/BhOuuyriBDw?t=1321)).
- **Writing your own program.** 2020: novices should not write programs because theirs are almost always bad ([How to never have to buy a training program again in your life, 2020-11](https://youtu.be/gWdAfpJIXbc?t=123)). 2021: draft your own while running the novice program ([How to program your training yourself, 2021-02](https://youtu.be/rlWIogS2Qho)). 2024: start on an established program, then write your own and have a coach review it ([So you think you look good? (Physique Review LIVE), 2024-11](https://youtu.be/yZC3Nsmmzb8?t=8488); [So you think you can lift? (Program Review LIVE), 2024-11](https://youtu.be/6p2x4kDDjzs?t=5434)). This is a refinement, not a flip.

**Contradictions**

- **Daily vs 3x/week full body.** He prefers "full body every day" with one heavy compound per day, and novices can recover from daily calisthenics ([Fullbody template review, 2021-01](https://youtu.be/G7rVTseabFU?t=720); [Don't turn your back on calisthenics, 2021-06](https://youtu.be/HrUPp573ki0?t=1890)). Elsewhere: 3x/week is the default and full body needs programming knowledge novices lack ([Fullbody template review, 2021-01](https://youtu.be/G7rVTseabFU?t=660); [The hypertrophy series： modifying sessions frequency to control volume/intensity, 2020-09](https://youtu.be/sfUkrygYNiU?t=190)).
- **Squat/deadlift frequency.** Novices should squat and deadlift several times a week (using deloads) ([Who can afford to only squat and deadlift once a week?, 2020-03](https://youtu.be/awNEfmfGkmY?t=189)). His own routine deliberately lowers squat and deadlift frequency, and deadlifts once a week ([ANIME WORKOUTS - Can you look like Baki Hanma in real life?, 2020-10](https://youtu.be/dfnn-YdXerg?t=755); [The issue with Novice Programs, 2021-03](https://youtu.be/S0qBQppUtTQ?t=1540)).
- **Intensity.** Lower intensity and volume at first, never struggling ([Your Fitness New Year's Resolution will fail. Here's why：, 2022-01](https://youtu.be/Bg7jQfbI1w8?t=380); [Free novice program for hypertrophy, 2020-02](https://youtu.be/_4wWgin1dVY?t=317)). But the top beginner mistake is training too easy, and novices should go to failure ([Can you look like Kratos from God of War in real life? (RAGNAROK WORKOUT), 2022-11](https://youtu.be/wB-ydKSfQ5k?t=2022); [So you think you look good? (Physique Review LIVE), 2024-11](https://youtu.be/yZC3Nsmmzb8?t=10229)).
- **Variations.** "No variations for novices", with the paused squat as the exception ([How to use pause reps for SIZE, 2021-05](https://youtu.be/MP01uQbcoLc?t=619); [ULTIMATE HYPERTROPHY PROGRAMS (Novice to Advanced), 2023-06](https://youtu.be/gpFdh0eBMGc?t=686)). Yet he likes novices doing variations ([Programming for people with limited mobility, 2020-11](https://youtu.be/sK78-yohV1s?t=1170); [How to add variations/rotations to your Gentleman split, 2021-06](https://youtu.be/7n8RMhsxEB4?t=125)).
- **Evolving rep ranges.** Not suitable for beginners ([The benefits of evolving rep ranges, 2020-05](https://youtu.be/2QnD9k0SbwA)). Teach them early ([The hypertrophy series： the perfect progression scheme for muscle growth, 2021-08](https://youtu.be/ulwUVDK7RUk?t=314); [Fierce 5 novice program review (from an hypertrophy standpoint), 2020-02](https://youtu.be/OATtf3kPtdI?t=1375)).
- **Explore vs repeat.** Beginners should be "tossed into the sea" and explore ([How to program for novices (with an hypertrophy bias), 2020-02](https://youtu.be/QpTHtmI8nrU?t=564)). A good novice program embraces monotony ([Fierce 5 novice program review (from an hypertrophy standpoint), 2020-02](https://youtu.be/OATtf3kPtdI?t=1438); [ANIME WORKOUTS - Can you look like Baki Hanma in real life?, 2020-10](https://youtu.be/dfnn-YdXerg?t=436)).
- **Isolation dose.** "Would never prescribe that much isolation to a novice" ([Jeff Nippard's Push Pull Legs program review, 2021-01](https://youtu.be/pey1Ni6HPlY?t=280)). Isolation in every program from the start ([Isolation movements benefits： attacking muscles more precisely, 2020-03](https://youtu.be/QwoBxHI7NBU?t=375)).

## Bulk cut

**Changed over time**

- **Recomp evangelist → slow bulker.** 2020-2021: recomping is "the future", better than bulk/cut, and "recomp beats bulking for me". He planned to recomp 4-5 more years (2021-05, 2022-03) ([Recomp guide (part. 2)： Who can do it & diet manipulation, 2020-05](https://youtu.be/IeYLu4_hkZY?t=190); [Natural Q&A #2, 2020-09](https://youtu.be/Zg0oUngwPK4?t=850); [Natural Q&A #7, 2021-05](https://youtu.be/QTHtVBP_36g?t=2934); [Nutrition Q&A #3, 2022-03](https://youtu.be/7Sp526pPxEU?t=1570)). August 2022: ended the 3-year 210 lb maintenance and said his recomp growth was "minimal compared" to a bulk. He switched to a 2-3 year slow lean bulk to 215-220 lb ([Building Muscles AND Losing Fat WITHOUT Gaining Weight? (My Best Recomp Lessons), 2022-08](https://youtu.be/9WA6eQODjHQ); [Building Muscles AND Losing Fat WITHOUT Gaining Weight? (My Best Recomp Lessons), 2022-08](https://youtu.be/9WA6eQODjHQ?t=1003); [3 YEAR RECOMP TRANSFORMATION (From Husky to Jacked) - 50K SPECIAL, 2022-08](https://youtu.be/O9txIDHBBIk?t=1565)). 2024: "perma-bulker is the way to go unless you start out fat" ([So you think you look good? (Physique Review LIVE), 2024-11](https://youtu.be/yZC3Nsmmzb8?t=6575)). Later view: slow bulking.
- **Surplus necessity.** 2022: "you do not need a caloric surplus", having gained at maintenance ([Building Muscles AND Losing Fat WITHOUT Gaining Weight? (My Best Recomp Lessons), 2022-08](https://youtu.be/9WA6eQODjHQ?t=315)). 2022-2024: for skinny/lean lifters, a surplus is required ("you must gain weight to gain muscle"), and "a caloric surplus is your best weapon" ([Greg Doucette's MainGaining is keeping you small?! (Analyzing Revival Fitness Ex, 2022-01](https://youtu.be/RryibwmuOWE?t=1596); [How BAD is Hamza's Fitness Advice? (5 BIGGEST Reasons You Can’t Gain Muscle), 2023-01](https://youtu.be/h3U30oRVrMU?t=63); [So you think you look good? (Physique Review LIVE), 2024-11](https://youtu.be/yZC3Nsmmzb8?t=7595)). Later view: a surplus is the main tool except for people with fat to trade.
- **Who should bulk.** 2020: only very skinny people should bulk ([Should natural lifters bulk / cut?, 2020-02](https://youtu.be/VpPf9o5923k?t=63)). 2024: lean/small and formerly chubby lifters must bulk, and maintaining is a mistake ([Do you look better than Silver Era lifters? (Physique Review LIVE), 2024-12](https://youtu.be/ZLheQPgEfoA?t=3039); [So you think you look good? (Physique Critique Chad Edition), 2024-12](https://youtu.be/pt4mbNb7NJ0?t=10484)). Later view: broader bulking.
- **Rate tightened.** 1-2 lb/month (2020-12) ([BLOATMAXX： the Kyriakos Grizzly example, mogging general & potential downsides, 2020-12](https://youtu.be/so6MbvvtM1w?t=865)) → 0.5-1 lb/month after his own too-fast 2023 bulk (20-30 lb in a year) ([Leg Day + Bulk Update (Hypertrophy Log #2), 2023-07](https://youtu.be/6KA80BQ9W3k?t=1317); [My Nightmare Bulk (Story Time), 2023-09](https://youtu.be/XK9KjVP-5Wo?t=691)). In 2024 1.5 lb/month was "good" ([Therapy is CANCELLED (Jung ｜ Modern Man in Search of a Soul), 2024-11](https://youtu.be/fPU3nRIH8sM?t=9349)).
- **Surplus size shrank.** 10-15% ceiling (2020) ([What you should NOT be doing during a bulk, 2020-02](https://youtu.be/VAblRcVMjqw?t=248)) → 200-300 kcal, 500 "pointless" (2024) ([BACK 2 THE GYM STREAM (Program reviews & Answering training questions), 2024-09](https://youtu.be/okm6bZHKHI4?t=8320); [Do you look better than Silver Era lifters? (Physique Review LIVE), 2024-12](https://youtu.be/ZLheQPgEfoA?t=8625)). Note: in 2022 he called ~500 kcal near-optimal ([Don't fall for the bulking meme, 2022-11](https://youtu.be/h7D6CB4p1oU?t=318)).
- **Recomp floor.** 2020: recomp down to ~12-13% ([Recomp guide (part.1)： What it is & isn't, 2020-05](https://youtu.be/qmpvEERwXVI?t=437)). 2022: don't recomp below ~14-15% ([Building Muscles AND Losing Fat WITHOUT Gaining Weight?
