## Progression

**Changed over time**

- **When to add weight:** Jan 2020: on 4×12, go up only if all four sets of 12 are comfortable ([Free 3 times a week full body hypertrophy program, 2020-01](https://youtu.be/xFVva4-swKc?t=188)). From Aug 2020 on: waiting for every set to hit the top turns ERRs static ([When to progress forward with evolving rep ranges, 2020-08](https://youtu.be/CrT1WOhxLqU?t=64)), and by 2024 only one set must reach the top ([Do you look better than Silver Era lifters? (Physique Review LIVE), 2024-12](https://youtu.be/ZLheQPgEfoA?t=566)). Later view: first set at the ceiling.
- **Narrow low ranges:** 2020 he prescribed 4-6 often (4×4-6 pull-ups/dips, 3×4-6 squat) ([2 days Upper (Torso/Arm dominant) split program review, 2020-04](https://youtu.be/87CMjYjX2jY?t=125); [Push Pull Legs Upper Lower 5 days split Program review, 2020-05](https://youtu.be/0yIieHQjEiA?t=1192)). 2023-25: keep ≥4 reps between floor and ceiling, and 4-6 is "a recipe for plateaus" ([How to Keep Growing FOREVER (Unlimited Hypertrophy Method), 2023-07](https://youtu.be/1TKqwXCge9E?t=638); [New Hypertrophy Gimmick™ just dropped 🤡, 2025-03](https://youtu.be/ACFKXT44BzM?t=498)). Later view: wider ranges.
- **Very low reps:** 2020 elevator schemes of 2-5 reps on deadlift and OHP ([How to progress forward with evolving rep ranges, 2020-09](https://youtu.be/65rLZe9cz_0?t=314)). 2022: compounds never below 4 ([Come with me if you want big shoulders (JOIN THE CHALLENGE!), 2022-10](https://youtu.be/BhOuuyriBDw?t=570)); 2023: sub-5 sets ~5% of volume ([Giants DO Exist (Tom Haviland), 2023-12](https://youtu.be/hEuy__sCbZA?t=1955)).
- **Isolation ranges:** 2020: 3×6-10 "great" for isolation ([AlphaDestiny Novice Program review (part. 1： training), 2020-03](https://youtu.be/Tw8qA93Gf58?t=567)). 2024: 6-10 too low, use 8-12/10-15 ([Your lifting program SUCKS! (Hypertrophy Q&A / Program review), 2024-10](https://youtu.be/c7hl9u3h_s0?t=7318)). Exceptions remain for hard curls (6-12, 6-10 in 2023-25) ([The ULTIMATE PPL Program (Doom Slayer Physique), 2023-11](https://youtu.be/DA7QvIAyptw?t=1326); [New Hypertrophy Gimmick™ just dropped 🤡, 2025-03](https://youtu.be/ACFKXT44BzM?t=434)).
- **Evolving sets:** 2020 he hadn't introduced evolving set ranges because removing both limits removes structure ([Rep Goal System (by Steve Shaw of Massive Iron) review, 2020-07](https://youtu.be/LYBdXCcmOO0?t=940)), and 2021 he called them advanced tools that destabilize programs ([How to use Evolving Rep Ranges for Hypertrophy, 2021-10](https://youtu.be/X8WMlqP6M78?t=720)). 2022-24: they are standard in his programs (add a set, then weight, drop a set) ([Come with me if you want big shoulders (JOIN THE CHALLENGE!), 2022-10](https://youtu.be/BhOuuyriBDw?t=1383); [Your lifting program SUCKS! (Hypertrophy Q&A / Program review), 2024-10](https://youtu.be/c7hl9u3h_s0?t=5990)).
- **Final program:** 2021: his "final program" no longer changes ([STORY TIME： My entire training history, 2021-08](https://youtu.be/aIjUTEtXOcM?t=1942); [How to program your training yourself, 2021-02](https://youtu.be/rlWIogS2Qho?t=567)). 2022: no final program exists because the body keeps evolving, and he admits he pushed the idea earlier ([🌌5 BIG BRAIN TRAINING TIPS TO 🆄🅽🅵🆄🅲🅺 YOUR PROGRAM🧠, 2022-05](https://youtu.be/BW-32tYoNxw?t=63); [5 Things I Wish I Knew Before I Started Lifting, 2022-09](https://youtu.be/6HGBdDOAReA?t=379)).
- **Rest-pause:** 2021: an afterthought that complicates rep/set manipulation ([The hypertrophy series： the most reliable way to progressively overload, 2021-03](https://youtu.be/Em00Z8i8V7c?t=190); [The hypertrophy series： the most reliable way to progressively overload, 2021-03](https://youtu.be/Em00Z8i8V7c?t=126)). 2024-25: a recommended plateau-buster for isolation ([Arnold trained like an idiot?, 2024-04](https://youtu.be/-OYtq2AHGX8?t=1833); [10 years of lifting for this (Hypertrophy Log #10), 2025-01](https://youtu.be/waeSP7DBmig?t=443)).
- **Microloading:** 2020: avoid microplates unless really advanced ([Weight progression on evolving rep ranges, 2020-07](https://youtu.be/6lggo2XPomI?t=189)). 2021-22: use ~2 lb jumps for arms; microloading is good for presses ([Good arm day Vs Bad arm day, 2021-01](https://youtu.be/RSkzA1l5jlk?t=540); [Hypertrophy Q&A #10, 2022-06](https://youtu.be/QfHfxLYRu88)).
- **Tempo:** 2020: slower tempo listed as an overload method ([Should bodybuilders care about strength?, 2020-02](https://youtu.be/xn8RN9807Ns?t=318)). 2021-24: tempo is hard to track and should be standardised, not progressed ([The hypertrophy series： the most reliable way to progressively overload, 2021-03](https://youtu.be/Em00Z8i8V7c?t=126); [Do you look better than Silver Era lifters? (Physique Review LIVE), 2024-12](https://youtu.be/ZLheQPgEfoA?t=5701)).
- **Rep goals vs RIR:** 2020: the rep-goal system is excellent ([Rep Goal System (by Steve Shaw of Massive Iron) review, 2020-07](https://youtu.be/LYBdXCcmOO0?t=1445)). 2021: he prefers RIR for clearer brackets ([Viking's the Bare Bones Series Program review, 2021-03](https://youtu.be/8mGHG5C-EPE?t=312)). 2023: autoregulation with RIR chosen on the day is "S tier" ([The Most IMPORTANT Methods for Muscle Growth (Hypertrophy Tier-List), 2023-11](https://youtu.be/SxqjF2oPasg?t=755)).
- **Can plateaus be avoided:** 2021: "fully avoidable" with smart programming ([The Hypertrophy Iceberg Explained (a complete guide to muscle growth), 2021-07](https://youtu.be/8ELQ2XZgpls?t=1827)). 2023: plateaus can't be avoided, so aim for fewer and later ones ([How to Keep Growing FOREVER (Unlimited Hypertrophy Method), 2023-07](https://youtu.be/1TKqwXCge9E?t=190)).
- **Weight on the bar emphasis:** 2020-21: the simplest, most reliable and best method ([The hypertrophy series： promoting progression in your training, 2020-06](https://youtu.be/ML5AQa9THHI?t=63); [The hypertrophy series： the perfect progression scheme for muscle growth, 2021-08](https://youtu.be/ulwUVDK7RUk?t=63)). 2022: weight is the "tip of the iceberg", and most natural gains come from accumulated volume via set multiplication and frequency ([The Ten 𝐋𝐀𝐖𝐒 of HYPERTROPHY (that you MUST break to grow), 2022-08](https://youtu.be/yUecX6qONXg?t=1015); [The Ten 𝐋𝐀𝐖𝐒 of HYPERTROPHY (that you MUST break to grow), 2022-08](https://youtu.be/yUecX6qONXg?t=1079)). 2024: his own obsession with bar weight created progression anxiety ([The WORST Bodybuilding Program Ever Created (my bad), 2024-04](https://youtu.be/Ft039H8jzXU?t=2197)), yet you must eventually get stronger ([Swinging a sword WON'T make you jacked, 2024-02](https://youtu.be/29XrRmOrCMs?t=1067)). Later view: load is one lever among several, but it can't be dropped.
- **Adding a variation on a stall:** 2020: never let a stall trigger rotation ([Rotating lifts： What it should & shouldn't be, 2020-05](https://youtu.be/z9MDwMO8K4Y?t=190)). 2024: if a lift doesn't progress, move to another variation of the pattern, or add a variation when it stalls ([Exercise Tier Lists are STUPID, 2024-11](https://youtu.be/6yW3GSskl8g?t=1581); [Arnold trained like an idiot?, 2024-04](https://youtu.be/-OYtq2AHGX8?t=2021)). The 2023 middle ground: only add a variation if you truly can't break the plateau ([The ULTIMATE PPL Program (Doom Slayer Physique), 2023-11](https://youtu.be/DA7QvIAyptw?t=1641)).

**Contradictions**

- **Evolving ranges for novices:** He says novices should not use them because they're hard to track and need beta-testing ([Hypertrophy Q&A #4, 2020-12](https://youtu.be/ZScs2L9rero?t=1190); [The Best Science-Based Full Body Workout for Size and Strength by Jeremy Ethier , 2021-03](https://youtu.be/_L5wLHlFfI0?t=689)), and that they are dangerous for lazy novices ([The benefits of evolving rep ranges, 2020-05](https://youtu.be/2QnD9k0SbwA?t=127)). He also says a program's 3-5×4-6 evolving scheme is "very intelligent" for novices ([AlphaDestiny Novice Program review (part. 1： training), 2020-03](https://youtu.be/Tw8qA93Gf58?t=692)), novices can handle leeway ([Candito Upper Lower Hypertrophy Program review, 2020-05](https://youtu.be/4aThavRpYLw?t=250)), and ERRs for novices are good ([The Best Science-Based Full Body Workout for Size and Strength by Jeremy Ethier , 2021-03](https://youtu.be/_L5wLHlFfI0?t=627)). All of this is 2020-21 with no clear direction.
- **Order of overload levers (both Dec 2022):** "weight, then reps, then sets, then frequency" ([How the King of Zoomers Trains to Look like a Greek God (Alex Eubank Program Rev, 2022-12](https://youtu.be/0pKnDucWcDc?t=1761)) vs "reps, then sets, then weight" ([How to Get Bigger by Doing Less (The 85% Rule), 2022-12](https://youtu.be/z2uzpl_smSg?t=1195); [☣️ Biohacking Muscle Growth with Nucleus Overload 💪, 2022-03](https://youtu.be/LNggSj0WBd8?t=1887)). The first probably ranks importance and the second gives the order of steps, but he states both as the way to progress.
- **8-15 range:** too wide, since if you can get 15 you'll get 12-13 (2020) ([4 days Body parts split program review, 2020-10](https://youtu.be/sCMGXCXKVjs?t=252)). Later he says hitting 15 lets you add ~10 lb and still get 8 (2023) ([How to Keep Growing FOREVER (Unlimited Hypertrophy Method), 2023-07](https://youtu.be/1TKqwXCge9E?t=574)).
- **Body measurements:** the worst way to judge progress ([The hypertrophy series： the optimal measure of progression for muscle growth, 2020-10](https://youtu.be/ISLtO-xJbYo?t=63)) and too slow to guide programming ([The hypertrophy series： the optimal measure of progression for muscle growth, 2020-10](https://youtu.be/ISLtO-xJbYo?t=189)) vs "the only reliable way to know if a muscle grew" ([Why you will NEVER have freaky, thick forearms if your wrists are small (Natty o, 2021-02](https://youtu.be/YHm-qSHgGSk?t=1040)).
- **Stall tolerance:** no lift should stagnate more than ~1 month ([The hypertrophy series： promoting progression in your training, 2020-06](https://youtu.be/ML5AQa9THHI?t=63)) vs 4-5 months on a compound before the program is wrong ([How to set up evolving rep ranges (theoretical aspects), 2020-06](https://youtu.be/0O0wnhU3g-8?t=245)). Both are from June 2020.
- **Pull-up threshold for adding weight:** 10 clean pull-ups ([FREE 4 days Upper Lower sheiko inspired Bodybuilding Program, 2020-09](https://youtu.be/HVD5j7hOobI?t=260); [Everything I do to get HUGE (Split, Reps, Lifts), 2023-09](https://youtu.be/43F9unmSc_I?t=2072)) vs 15-20 pull-ups / 30 dips ([Come with me if you want a BIG BACK (4 steps MASSterplan), 2023-09](https://youtu.be/7uBT8vp0lNw?t=1007)) vs 25 dips ([So you think you look good? (Physique Review LIVE), 2024-11](https://youtu.be/yZC3Nsmmzb8?t=3587)) vs 30 pull-ups ([3 days Upper 2 days Lower program review (for an advanced calisthenics guy part., 2020-11](https://youtu.be/D3mJh0ZA5nc?t=150)). The thresholds vary, but every version says to add load.

## Rest periods

**Changed over time**

- **Rest length drifts shorter and looser.** 2020: 3-5 min for strength sets ([Icecream Fitness FAQ review, 2020-06](https://youtu.be/MCUpClPnPkQ?t=1126)). 2021-2024: 2-3 min, by feel, "rest times don't matter" as long as you recover ([Doggcrapp Training review, 2021-01](https://youtu.be/A55c7v1yMn4?t=437); [The Most IMPORTANT Methods for Muscle Growth (Hypertrophy Tier-List), 2023-11](https://youtu.be/SxqjF2oPasg?t=3276); [Do you look better than Silver Era lifters? (Physique Review LIVE), 2024-12](https://youtu.be/ZLheQPgEfoA?t=5764)). This is a mild refinement; 3-4 min after giant-set rounds persists through 2024 ([So you think you can lift? (Program Review LIVE), 2024-11](https://youtu.be/6p2x4kDDjzs?t=2690)).

**Contradictions**

- **Supersetting strength work.** "Don't superset strength work such as main bench or weighted chins" ([4 days Upper Lower + 1 Arm day Program review, 2020-11](https://youtu.be/xQQJUXf58ZE?t=580); [5 days Upper Lower program review (Week 1), 2020-07](https://youtu.be/du7JYCA2pa4?t=874)), repeated in 2025 (low reps as straight sets with long rests) ([New Hypertrophy Gimmick™ just dropped 🤡, 2025-03](https://youtu.be/ACFKXT44BzM?t=1316)), vs "even strength work can be supersetted, e.g. bench with rows; resting 5 min after bench is wasted" ([Greek Aesthetics Bodybuilding Program (Apollonian Physique Workout), 2022-05](https://youtu.be/SPicD3F686s?t=629)).
- **Leg pairings.** Pair leg press with leg curl and leg extension with calf raises ([The Smartest Push Pull Legs Routine by Jeff Nippard review, 2021-06](https://youtu.be/Mq2TaHm_ySI?t=503)), or lunges with skull crushers ([Jeff Nippard & Minimalism： Working Hard or Hardly Working?, 2022-10](https://youtu.be/Zv9QAIb5nGk?t=2269)), vs moving straight from one leg exercise to another being "a cardinal sin" ([Judging and Grading every Fitness Channel (Sam Sulek, Max Euceda, Lex Little), 2024-01](https://youtu.be/jDk3LytTEjA?t=1726)). Probably same-region circuits vs paired isolation, but he doesn't make that distinction.
- **Does supersetting hurt performance?** It is "not detrimental" and "costs nothing" ([Why I superset EVERYTHING (the giant sets principle), 2020-01](https://youtu.be/Z-D9kRwK90I); [The Smartest Push Pull Legs Routine by Jeff Nippard review, 2021-06](https://youtu.be/Mq2TaHm_ySI?t=760)) vs the loss growing in a long full-body day ([Fullbody template review, 2021-01](https://youtu.be/G7rVTseabFU?t=430)) and leg circuits destroying performance ([Judging and Grading every Fitness Channel (Sam Sulek, Max Euceda, Lex Little), 2024-01](https://youtu.be/jDk3LytTEjA?t=1726)).

## Science evidence

**Changed over time**

- **Stretch/eccentric versus concentric.** 2020-2021: muscle is gained mostly via weighted stretch, the negative is the key, and weighted stretching is "now backed by studies" ([Hypertrophy Q&A #3, 2020-11](https://youtu.be/6sFaB3rAY1A?t=1194); [The Hypertrophy Iceberg Explained (a complete guide to muscle growth), 2021-07](https://youtu.be/8ELQ2XZgpls?t=1986); [Natty or not (.com)： Alpha Destiny (part. 2), 2020-07](https://youtu.be/XweCS5RdqNk?t=318)). 2023-2024: he cites a ~100-man study where ~90° training outgrew lengthened-only. He calls the stretch-focused trend contrarian and believes the concentric builds more than the eccentric, proposing a partner-removes-the-negative experiment. He notes Milo Wolf says lengthened partials help only a little ([Why you should STOP doing incline curls, 2023-02](https://youtu.be/CGhPZ9AxBJE?t=379); [Your lifting program SUCKS! (Hypertrophy Q&A / Program review), 2024-10](https://youtu.be/c7hl9u3h_s0?t=1141); [New hypertrophy study just dropped (And Basically You're F＊cking Stupid), 2024-01](https://youtu.be/vVQmYGw7Kj8?t=2205)). The later view is current.
- **Rep range and load.** 2020: some studies favour heavy weights, and heavy loads are needed for damage ([The hypertrophy series： the issue of volume without intensity, 2020-05](https://youtu.be/lJyrBDvtQFU?t=319); [The hypertrophy series： why using metabolic stress for muscle growth fails, 2021-02](https://youtu.be/gjZ6qGRxS10?t=110)). 2025: rep range is "mostly dead" as long as you're close to failure ([New Hypertrophy Gimmick™ just dropped 🤡, 2025-03](https://youtu.be/ACFKXT44BzM?t=1694)). This is a refinement.

**Contradictions**

- **Physique as evidence.** "Being bigger is not an argument" ([The Brainlets of YT Fitness don't understand Science, 2021-02](https://youtu.be/EP1Qw9aEKOU?t=2485)) versus judging knowledge by ability to replicate it and science people being small ([Science-Based Fitness needs a reality check., 2023-07](https://youtu.be/Z8Kwk55DxlU?t=125); [The Galaxy Brains of YT Fitness have ruined science, 2021-01](https://youtu.be/662MjNpnQcw?t=2766)). Partly reconciled by his natural-only qualifier ([Jeff Nippard is WRONG about Natty or Nots., 2023-08](https://youtu.be/aOk65xuzIPE?t=2720)).
- **Uses studies while dismissing them.** He never cites studies ([The Galaxy Brains of YT Fitness have ruined science, 2021-01](https://youtu.be/662MjNpnQcw?t=190)), yet he invokes specific studies when they support him (tempo, ROM, boxers, 500 mg testosterone, lengthened versus 90°) ([New hypertrophy study just dropped (And Basically You're F＊cking Stupid), 2024-01](https://youtu.be/vVQmYGw7Kj8?t=508); [Why you should STOP doing incline curls, 2023-02](https://youtu.be/CGhPZ9AxBJE?t=379)). This is close to the cherry-picking he criticises.

## Sleep recovery

**Changed over time**

- **Active vs passive recovery.** In 2020-2021, light blood-flow work, calisthenics and a busy rest day ("not a couch day") aided recovery ( ([The hypertrophy series： maximum recoverable volume, 2020-04](https://youtu.be/tZ9CSu2DMIE?t=186); [Push Pull Legs Upper Lower 5 days split Program review, 2020-05](https://youtu.be/0yIieHQjEiA?t=1319); [3 days Upper 2 days Lower program review (for an advanced calisthenics guy part., 2020-11](https://youtu.be/9jAjNyxeiXc?t=63))). In 2024: "you do not need active recovery", constant active recovery keeps you fatigued, and couch rest matters ( ([BACK 2 THE GYM STREAM (Program reviews & Answering training questions), 2024-09](https://youtu.be/okm6bZHKHI4?t=10132); [You're not hardcore, you're just an idiot., 2024-05](https://youtu.be/Eta-sxecx9E?t=480); [Time to become indestructible (Self-Improvement Q&A), 2024-10](https://youtu.be/wBct3Pl8OY4?t=637))). Later view: passive rest, with light activity allowed.
- **His sleep target rose.** He said 7 h in 2021 ( ([Natural Q&A #7, 2021-05](https://youtu.be/QTHtVBP_36g?t=2998))) and 7-8 h in 2022 ( ([🕑 OPTIMIZE YOUR LIFE 📈： Time Management, Productivity Hacks & Energy Budge, 2022-07](https://youtu.be/u8IRHcUWfPs?t=944))), then tried for 8-9 h in 2024 ( ([Do you look better than Silver Era lifters? (Physique Review LIVE), 2024-12](https://youtu.be/ZLheQPgEfoA?t=4687))). In 2025 he said hypertrophy training raises sleep need ( ([You know what time it is... STORY TIME, 2025-01](https://youtu.be/0O0nG2jLadU?t=509))).
- **Screens.** In 2020 blue light didn't bother him and only susceptible people needed to avoid it ( ([5 tips to sleep quick & deep, 2020-08](https://youtu.be/7eZtMIgSnOE?t=560))). In 2024 he said to ban screens ≥1.5 h before bed ( ([How to get buff GF (Dating & Relationships Q&A), 2024-11](https://youtu.be/o40xCjIzl14?t=134))).
- **Forearm frequency.** In 2020 a grip drill was every 4-6 days, never daily ( ([How to do Coan grip, 2020-01](https://youtu.be/VUNsazYt-uo?t=124))). In 2024 forearms recover fast enough for consecutive days with different curls ( ([So you think you can lift? (Program Review LIVE), 2024-11](https://youtu.be/6p2x4kDDjzs?t=2930))). Later view: more frequent.
- **Lower-body recovery lengthened.** In 2022 he trained legs every 2 days without soreness ( ([Level up your back, 2022-02](https://youtu.be/dVssxcEh1UQ?t=999))). In 2024 he needed 72 h+ and said lower body 3×/week is too much ( ([Bodybuilding is killing me (Hypertrophy Log #8), 2024-09](https://youtu.be/JW73oft8Q60?t=1110))).
- **Cold exposure de-emphasized.** In 2020 he discussed it at length as useful for sleep and circulation ( ([Cold showers benefits, 2020-06](https://youtu.be/mfweKhLM5L0?t=379))). In 2024 he said it won't revolutionise recovery, and recovery is eating, sleeping and napping ( ([You're not hardcore, you're just an idiot., 2024-05](https://youtu.be/Eta-sxecx9E?t=442); [You're not hardcore, you're just an idiot., 2024-05](https://youtu.be/Eta-sxecx9E?t=400))).

**Contradictions**

- **Full recovery needed?** In 2020: "training again before full recovery steals gains" ( ([The hypertrophy series： modifying sessions frequency to control volume/intensity, 2020-09](https://youtu.be/sfUkrygYNiU?t=315))). In 2021-2022: you can train at 20% or 90-95% recovery and still grow ( ([The Recovery Pot Explained (a complete guide to muscle recuperation), 2021-02](https://youtu.be/p-kR3RfGBHw); [Why I never deload (and why you shouldn't either), 2022-02](https://youtu.be/BJXFeQWGUuY?t=1016))). The two can be reconciled only as "not constantly".
- **Triceps recovery speed.** In 2020 his triceps recovered very fast ( ([Push/Pull Pull/Legs Legs/Push 3 days program review, 2020-05](https://youtu.be/eFhwWirR70o?t=127))). In 2023 triceps take long to recover, especially if untrained ( ([We're turning Alan Thrall into a bodybuilder!, 2023-05](https://youtu.be/d1eLAd5WvIA?t=3312))). The first is personal and the second general, so this is possibly not a real conflict.

## Strength

**Changed over time**

- **Deadlift practice**: 2020-21 he pushed the deadlift hardest with 2RMs and saw the most progress there (495x2 PR) ([Synchronizing evolving rep range with movement patterns, variations & rotations , 2020-11](https://youtu.be/mbtAKsbDz9I?t=330); [⚠️ Don't make this mistake ⚠️, 2021-09](https://youtu.be/twEeL-z4Zug?t=891)). 2024: frequent max testing had stalled him at 465-485 for a year, so he now deadlifts every ~40 days with RDLs, good mornings and hypers doing the work ([The WORST Bodybuilding Program Ever Created (my bad), 2024-04](https://youtu.be/Ft039H8jzXU?t=1822); [The WORST Bodybuilding Program Ever Created (my bad), 2024-04](https://youtu.be/Ft039H8jzXU?t=1884)). Later view = low-frequency deadlifts, no max testing.
- **Strength blocks and powerbuilding**: 2020 says most bodybuilding "is really powerbuilding", and 1-2 mesocycles of a powerlifting program to raise strength is "a good use" ([Upper Body dominant 4 Days split review, 2020-06](https://youtu.be/PYmr91aELnE?t=413); [The Bridge (by Austin Baraki & Jordan Feigenbaum ft Alan Thrall) Program review, 2020-07](https://youtu.be/YcHkXwsIOI8?t=1406)). 2022-24 rejects powerbuilding and strength blocks, and calls "build a strength base first" a lie ([Tips to Avoid a Mediocre Physique, 2022-11](https://youtu.be/JgAoGDmM4n4?t=686); [Powerbuilding Drama： The Final Answer, 2023-11](https://youtu.be/SZEjCsuclx8?t=1968); [Powerbuilding is an Abomination., 2023-10](https://youtu.be/x9GNS5HBZ_4?t=63)). Later view = no strength phases for bodybuilders.
- **Size and strength moving apart**: 2020 rejects that strength can rise while muscles shrink, saying size can't rise while strength stays flat ([＂What is the point of lifting natty past 30 if test levels crash?＂, 2020-04](https://youtu.be/TIsnQ03FegQ?t=338); [The hypertrophy series： developing the values of size and strength, 2020-10](https://youtu.be/k8k1PycHKDI?t=220)). 2022 cites Candito losing size while his total rose and says you can trade one for the other ([Strength standards are useless, 2022-04](https://youtu.be/LxGdGChvk2c?t=3139); [Strength standards are useless, 2022-04](https://youtu.be/LxGdGChvk2c?t=3076)). Later view = correlated within a person but tradeable.
- **Role of big-lift strength work**: 2020-21 "a day with zero strength work is bad", strength work is the backbone, never cut ([Kizen Strength & Aesthetics Powerbuilding program review, 2020-09](https://youtu.be/-banYSTnkq4?t=230); [The hypertrophy series： utilizing tonnage for muscle growth, 2021-01](https://youtu.be/_2M6FhWuIvs?t=314)). 2024-25: high-bar squat and bench only 3-5x/year, he "doesn't care about strength", and his heavy work moved to dips and weighted pull-ups ([You know what time it is... STORY TIME, 2025-01](https://youtu.be/0O0nG2jLadU?t=572); [3 hours of Story Time, 2025-02](https://youtu.be/-7bzbmL-x3Q?t=748); [Do you look better than Silver Era lifters? (Physique Review LIVE), 2024-12](https://youtu.be/ZLheQPgEfoA?t=4816)). Later view = strength via less risky movements, still trending up.
- **Neural window (refinement)**: "~6 months of weekly practice" (2020) ([Strength training is for SUCKERS (Natty or not.com), 2020-07](https://youtu.be/7XqE7GhDsgc?t=938)) → "a month to a year" (2021) ([The hypertrophy series： pairing neurological adaptation and muscle gains, 2021-02](https://youtu.be/AeIKc3A2FiY?t=270)).

**Contradictions**

- **OHP suitability**: "a safe lift, you can even do 1-2 rep maxes" ([Upper Lower Light/Heavy 4 days split with mirror Week program review (part. 1), 2020-12](https://youtu.be/niD0UuwTUvg?t=129)) vs "progresses too slowly and strains some lower backs" for daily maxing ([Wisconsin method aka Bulgarian light review (from a muscular hypertrophy standpo, 2020-02](https://youtu.be/RaGX9rPQr4k?t=790)) (both 2020; different contexts, so a mild conflict).
- **2RMs vs no maxing**: he recommends never maxing and calls 1RMs a waste ([5 reasons to only lift heavy weight DEBUNKED, 2021-01](https://youtu.be/CTMwuqNsY9Q?t=498)), while personally doing deadlift 2RMs and calling them hypertrophy training ([The issue with Novice Programs, 2021-03](https://youtu.be/S0qBQppUtTQ?t=1810)). It is consistent only if 2RM ≠ 1RM.
- **Bench strictness**: "Bench is the one lift you can get away with not treating as strict strength work" ([5 days Upper Lower program review (part. 1), 2020-10](https://youtu.be/TD9SB9Bt45o?t=378)) vs bench never below 4 reps, needing full focus and never supersetting ([Why I superset EVERYTHING (the giant sets principle), 2020-01](https://youtu.be/Z-D9kRwK90I?t=63)) — yet he also allows bench and row supersets ([3 days Upper 2 days Lower program review (for an advanced calisthenics guy part., 2020-11](https://youtu.be/D3mJh0ZA5nc?t=524)).

## Supplements

**Changed over time**

- **Protein powder use:** 2020 he used whey or pea for convenience ([Supplements are (mostly) useless, 2020-06](https://youtu.be/dgxdlxNZUUs?t=126)). In 2021 he cut from 3x/day to ~2 scoops/week ([TURKESTERONE / ECDYSTERONE MARKETING SCHEMES： How Supplements Companies TRICK yo, 2021-12](https://youtu.be/S_EF3ebs5Jg?t=1457)). In 2023-24 he takes 1 scoop/day or 3-4x/week ([Full Day of Eating (Lean Bulk), 2023-10](https://youtu.be/TxDUQPe3B0E?t=252); [Everything I eat to get HUGE (Full Bulking Plan), 2024-03](https://youtu.be/SV5rA-iMHRE?t=1900)), and in 2024 he says powder is "not worth the money" ([1st Natural Hypertrophy stream! ASK YOUR QUESTIONS AND I SHALL ANSWER, 2024-09](https://youtu.be/bRKQIOYo2u4?t=12049)).
- **Bee pollen:** six months a year (2022) ([Nutrition Q&A #3, 2022-03](https://youtu.be/7Sp526pPxEU?t=1005)) → every day (2024) ([1st Natural Hypertrophy stream! ASK YOUR QUESTIONS AND I SHALL ANSWER, 2024-09](https://youtu.be/bRKQIOYo2u4?t=326)).
- **Garlic dose:** 3-6 cloves/day (2020, nutrition file) ([Raw garlic for insane pumps & a stronger immune system, 2020-03](https://youtu.be/Jd2wr0Qe42I?t=374)) → 1-2 cloves every other day, starting at ½ clove (2023) ([My Favorite ＂Anabolic Herbs＂ for Bodybuilding, 2023-05](https://youtu.be/8C3R94M4yNM?t=686)). The later view is the lower dose.
- **MSM:** 1-2x/week (2020) ([Supplements are (mostly) useless, 2020-06](https://youtu.be/dgxdlxNZUUs?t=312)) → daily and nonstop (2024) ([1st Natural Hypertrophy stream! ASK YOUR QUESTIONS AND I SHALL ANSWER, 2024-09](https://youtu.be/bRKQIOYo2u4?t=1791); [Everything I eat to get HUGE (Full Bulking Plan), 2024-03](https://youtu.be/SV5rA-iMHRE?t=1962)).
- **Coffee:** 2020-21 he called it an addiction and a sleep-wrecker ([5 tips to sleep quick & deep, 2020-08](https://youtu.be/7eZtMIgSnOE?t=476); [Nutrition Q&A #2, 2021-04](https://youtu.be/XASWAdsSu0M?t=1271)). By 2024 he says to drink coffee instead of a pre-workout, and that one morning cup is a ritual, not an addiction ([Judging and Grading every Fitness Channel (Sam Sulek, Max Euceda, Lex Little), 2024-01](https://youtu.be/jDk3LytTEjA?t=3530); [TIME TO GROW BOYS (Live Q&A / Self-Improvement), 2024-09](https://youtu.be/lyj1BFZ85Dg?t=8510)). He still personally abstains.
- **His stack:** creatine/MSM/bee pollen (2022) ([Nutrition Q&A #3, 2022-03](https://youtu.be/7Sp526pPxEU?t=1005)) → creatine/MSM/protein (2024) ([Your lifting program SUCKS! (Hypertrophy Q&A / Program review), 2024-10](https://youtu.be/c7hl9u3h_s0?t=6052)). Garlic and ginger became his preferred "tonic herbs" from 2022-23 ([Nutrition Q&A #3, 2022-03](https://youtu.be/7Sp526pPxEU?t=1070)).

**Contradictions**

- **Vitamins.** 2022: vitamin supplements are crutches a balanced diet removes, and vitamin D replaces sun ([🥐 My New Diet for Natural Hypertrophy 🍖 (Vegan? Meat only?), 2022-07](https://youtu.be/gSFUgZ42R1A?t=1263); [SIGMA： Critiquing More Plates More Dates’ Testosterone Booster (feat Gorilla M, 2022-04](https://youtu.be/L_aq5x4lom8?t=2877)). 2024: multivitamins and vitamin D are among the only four worth taking ([Judging and Grading every Fitness Channel (Sam Sulek, Max Euceda, Lex Little), 2024-01](https://youtu.be/jDk3LytTEjA?t=1611)).
- **Dose.** He says to take half the label dose of any supplement ([Nutrition Q&A #1, 2020-11](https://youtu.be/vC9cKh9tFxs?t=530); [TURKESTERONE / ECDYSTERONE MARKETING SCHEMES： How Supplements Companies TRICK yo, 2021-12](https://youtu.be/S_EF3ebs5Jg?t=1519)), yet takes creatine above the label dose ([Everything I eat to get HUGE (Full Bulking Plan), 2024-03](https://youtu.be/SV5rA-iMHRE?t=1900)).
- **MSM frequency, same month (2020-06).** About a teaspoon a day ([Curing patellar tendinitis (part. 3)： Recovery hacks & supplements, 2020-06](https://youtu.be/UgafGUt-VBc?t=816)) vs once or twice a week ([Supplements are (mostly) useless, 2020-06](https://youtu.be/dgxdlxNZUUs?t=312)).
- **Whey.** In 2024 it is one of the few worthwhile supplements ([Judging and Grading every Fitness Channel (Sam Sulek, Max Euceda, Lex Little), 2024-01](https://youtu.be/jDk3LytTEjA?t=1611)) and he still uses it ([Everything I eat to get HUGE (Full Bulking Plan), 2024-03](https://youtu.be/SV5rA-iMHRE?t=1900)), but powder is also "not worth the money" ([1st Natural Hypertrophy stream! ASK YOUR QUESTIONS AND I SHALL ANSWER, 2024-09](https://youtu.be/bRKQIOYo2u4?t=12049)).

## Technique

**Changed over time**

- **Cheating**: 2020-2022 cheat reps are a legitimate tool; he did almost only cheat curls for ~10 years and biceps became his best part ([Cheat curls tutorial (theoretical aspects), 2020-08](https://youtu.be/7lwWsxNXDmo?t=377); [13 YEARS OF CHEAT CURLS： Was it worth it?, 2022-05](https://youtu.be/iL0AsMX4-hA?t=190)) → 2022 in hindsight strict curls would likely have given the same ([13 YEARS OF CHEAT CURLS： Was it worth it?, 2022-05](https://youtu.be/iL0AsMX4-hA?t=254)) → 2023 cheat reps C tier, "mostly wasteful" ([The Most IMPORTANT Methods for Muscle Growth (Hypertrophy Tier-List), 2023-11](https://youtu.be/SxqjF2oPasg?t=2582)) → 2024 cheat reps/body English = ego lifting ([New hypertrophy study just dropped (And Basically You're F＊cking Stupid), 2024-01](https://youtu.be/vVQmYGw7Kj8?t=1201)). Later view: strict.
- **Scapula on back work**: 2020-2021 retract the scapula, novices fail by not retracting on rows ([Fierce 5 novice program review (from an hypertrophy standpoint), 2020-02](https://youtu.be/OATtf3kPtdI?t=439); [Jeff Nippard's Push Pull Legs program review, 2021-01](https://youtu.be/pey1Ni6HPlY?t=400)) → 2024 protraction to stretch the back matters more; "shoulders back" is the wrong cue ([Arnold trained like an idiot?, 2024-04](https://youtu.be/-OYtq2AHGX8?t=193); [Arnold trained like an idiot?, 2024-04](https://youtu.be/-OYtq2AHGX8?t=257)). (Pull-ups keep scapular engagement.) Later view: protract on rows.
- **Rounded back on rows/hinges**: 2020 rounding as the weight descends on rows is bad form ([Tips to combat lower back pain #1, 2020-02](https://youtu.be/IqCdPJopcC4?t=187)); he "never rounds his back" ([Lower back rounding： The Good, the Bad and the Ugly, 2020-09](https://youtu.be/rIngKQqTJMs?t=375)) → 2024 rounded-back T-bar rows and deep rounded rack hinges at slow tempo are OK, earned exotic form ([Arnold trained like an idiot?, 2024-04](https://youtu.be/-OYtq2AHGX8?t=385); [This is Peak Bulk (Hypertrophy Log #6), 2024-05](https://youtu.be/l6L6HlGM4F0?t=63); [Don't be THAT GUY in 2024, 2024-01](https://youtu.be/uOAia_t5c_I?t=754)). Lumbar rule for squat/deadlift unchanged.
- **Squat stance**: 2020 slightly wider stance with knees out spares the knee ([Curing patellar tendinitis (part. 2)： Rehab & precautions, 2020-05](https://youtu.be/vHf2ZoHWHQs?t=690)) → 2021-2024 narrow/medium stance, toes forward, knees forward; wide toes-out stance injured him ([How to do squats for SIZE, 2022-09](https://youtu.be/XAcv427WvMw?t=300); [Your lifting program SUCKS! (Hypertrophy Q&A / Program review), 2024-10](https://youtu.be/c7hl9u3h_s0?t=951); [How I Built Monster Legs, 2024-12](https://youtu.be/-OjJEzZTXtQ?t=190)).
- **Top squeeze**: 2020 squeeze at the top (curls slow positive for the squeeze; Piana calf raises: squeeze matters more than stretch) ([The training principles series： slow negatives, 2020-02](https://youtu.be/NGSCZU6obAQ?t=189); [How to do Piana & Toshiki raises, 2020-01](https://youtu.be/AK6xwDBOJLE?t=61)) → 2021-2024 top squeeze gives no tension, C/D tier; bottom of calf raise is where growth is ([The form p＊lice is under arrest, 2021-07](https://youtu.be/GH8tqzGTgH8?t=3139); [The Most IMPORTANT Methods for Muscle Growth (Hypertrophy Tier-List), 2023-11](https://youtu.be/SxqjF2oPasg?t=2143); [So you think you can lift? (Program Review LIVE), 2024-11](https://youtu.be/6p2x4kDDjzs?t=7076)).
- **Tempo emphasis**: 2020 "slow negative, fast positive"; 2021 don't slow negatives on purpose, TUT overrated ([The hypertrophy series： eccentric vs concentric movements, 2020-09](https://youtu.be/L5gcFxTG_cU?t=500); [The Hypertrophy Iceberg Explained (a complete guide to muscle growth), 2021-07](https://youtu.be/8ELQ2XZgpls?t=2383)) → 2023-2024 tempo S tier, slow down near the stretch, ≥1 s eccentric, negative "where most hypertrophy occurs" ([The Most IMPORTANT Methods for Muscle Growth (Hypertrophy Tier-List), 2023-11](https://youtu.be/SxqjF2oPasg?t=2143); [Training for Aesthetics： You're doing it WRONG., 2023-05](https://youtu.be/Zqv7KVsmu78?t=505); [I am officially obese (Hypertrophy Log #7), 2024-08](https://youtu.be/sZntx8mqaH8?t=62)). Later view: more weight on controlled/slow negatives, still no counting.
- **Partials / lengthened partials**: 2020 full ROM best, novices never partial ([The training principles series： full range of motion, 2020-04](https://youtu.be/-wk3jSpm434?t=381); [How to program for novices (with an hypertrophy bias), 2020-02](https://youtu.be/QpTHtmI8nrU?t=378)) → 2021 full ROM all the time is a mistake ([The Hypertrophy Iceberg Explained (a complete guide to muscle growth), 2021-07](https://youtu.be/8ELQ2XZgpls?t=1054)) → 2023 partials A tier ([The Most IMPORTANT Methods for Muscle Growth (Hypertrophy Tier-List), 2023-11](https://youtu.be/SxqjF2oPasg?t=2268)) → 2024 lengthened partials may beat full ROM ([New hypertrophy study just dropped (And Basically You're F＊cking Stupid), 2024-01](https://youtu.be/vVQmYGw7Kj8?t=189)). Later view: full ROM default, lengthened-range emphasis.
- **Mind-muscle connection**: 2020 central (prioritising muscles in compounds) ([The training principle series： mind muscle connection, 2020-02](https://youtu.be/rAn5y7bka9w?t=125)) → 2021-2023 only useful for lagging muscles, B tier, can be an excuse for baby weights ([5 lifting conspiracy theories, 2021-04](https://youtu.be/VdBmYdUYCKM?t=819); [The Most IMPORTANT Methods for Muscle Growth (Hypertrophy Tier-List), 2023-11](https://youtu.be/SxqjF2oPasg?t=2769)).
- **Lat pulldown**: 2020 V-bar to the stomach, lean back ([Push/Pull Pull/Legs Legs/Push 3 days program review, 2020-05](https://youtu.be/eFhwWirR70o?t=1116)) → 2023-2024 don't lean way back, pull in line with the cable; leaning back is valid but he prefers vertical ([This is why you don't have a Demon Back (Advanced Tips), 2023-11](https://youtu.be/4t72r8Q0vXQ?t=1004); [Arnold trained like an idiot?, 2024-04](https://youtu.be/-OYtq2AHGX8?t=514)).
- **Wall curls**: 2021-2022 wall curls don't stop cheating ([How to do curls (strict barbell curls tutorial), 2021-02](https://youtu.be/N4-K79MZNPs?t=400); [The ULTIMATE Biceps Exercises Tier-List (Arnold-tier to Noodle-tier), 2022-10](https://youtu.be/RwEJpHTwWm0?t=1384)) → 2024 wall curls reduce cheating and allow slower negatives ([I am officially obese (Hypertrophy Log #7), 2024-08](https://youtu.be/sZntx8mqaH8?t=62)).
- **OHP minimum reps**: 2020 ≥5 reps ([Tips to combat shoulder pain, 2020-02](https://youtu.be/IahVc0kbGOU?t=314)) → 2022 never below 6, lower reps degraded his form ([Come with me if you want big shoulders (JOIN THE CHALLENGE!), 2022-10](https://youtu.be/BhOuuyriBDw?t=570)).

**Contradictions**

- **Pristine form vs heavier sloppy reps**: 2023 slight ego lifting with more weight and a better stretch "can be better" ([I'm BACK! (Hypertrophy Log #4), 2023-08](https://youtu.be/B5eAFxfON3A?t=442)) vs 2023-2024 cutting ROM to lift more and body English are ego lifting ([What everyone gets WRONG about Range of Motion, 2023-03](https://youtu.be/1apseBbt0-o?t=690); [New hypertrophy study just dropped (And Basically You're F＊cking Stupid), 2024-01](https://youtu.be/vVQmYGw7Kj8?t=1201)).
- **Elbow flare on bench**: 2020 flaring is objectively bad 100% of the time ([The training principles series： good form, 2020-02](https://youtu.be/M-a4cj1yFX8?t=188); [How to do high frequency/volume bench press without shoulder pain, 2020-02](https://youtu.be/xoLo7fptNA8)) vs 2022 flaring is how you recruit more chest ([The ULTIMATE Chest Exercises Tier-List (Gorilla-tier to A cup-tier), 2022-12](https://youtu.be/cUkWvnY8AJI?t=1503)).
- **Lengthened partials**: 2023 C tier, used only for calves ([The Most IMPORTANT Methods for Muscle Growth (Hypertrophy Tier-List), 2023-11](https://youtu.be/SxqjF2oPasg?t=2392)) vs 2024 may beat full ROM ([New hypertrophy study just dropped (And Basically You're F＊cking Stupid), 2024-01](https://youtu.be/vVQmYGw7Kj8?t=126)) (possibly an update from new data, but only 3 months apart).
- **OHP range**: prefers full ROM down to the collarbone ([AlphaDestiny Novice Program review (part. 2： FAQ), 2020-04](https://youtu.be/T_DyRlu3Y7I?t=568)) vs "he doesn't use full ROM on overhead press either" ([Response to Steve Shaw (Massive Iron) - Going to WAR Over FRONT DELT training, 2020-03](https://youtu.be/KMcJAERb9Dk?t=1754)) (both 2020).
- **Bench negative**: slow negatives as philosophy ([The hypertrophy series： eccentric vs concentric movements, 2020-09](https://youtu.be/L5gcFxTG_cU?t=500)) vs on bench he lowers "fairly fast but controlled" since slow never helps his positive ([The training principles series： slow negatives, 2020-02](https://youtu.be/NGSCZU6obAQ?t=127)); cheat curls not deliberately slowed ([Cheat curls： EZ bar vs Dumbbells, 2020-07](https://youtu.be/uND20Zam2jI?t=697)).
- **Partials' purpose**: high reps, not heavy weight ([Synchronizing evolving rep range with movement patterns, variations & rotations , 2020-11](https://youtu.be/mbtAKsbDz9I?t=400)) vs a good partial lets more reps *with more weight* ([What everyone gets WRONG about Range of Motion, 2023-03](https://youtu.be/1apseBbt0-o?t=1887)).
- **Technique value**: S tier ([The Most IMPORTANT Methods for Muscle Growth (Hypertrophy Tier-List), 2023-11](https://youtu.be/SxqjF2oPasg?t=2644)) vs "technique is the enemy of the bodybuilder" ([The Streetlifting MUTANT w/ Steel Cable Tendons (Artem Shirokov), 2023-12](https://youtu.be/M2yqxp4IHXg?t=1256)) (reconcilable: master enough, no more).
- **Bodybuilder vs powerlifter form**: "only form" exists ([No such thing as a dangerous lift (the good morning example), 2021-04](https://youtu.be/sFMQj4Lflk0?t=64)) vs optimal strength and bodybuilding form sit at opposite ends ([You're not hardcore, you're just an idiot., 2024-05](https://youtu.be/Eta-sxecx9E?t=1060)).

## Volume

**Changed over time**

- **Overall volume, from maximalist to minimal-effective.** 2020: more work always gives better results, sit at the brink of overtraining, and naturals can't build a big body in an hour a day ([The hypertrophy series： maximum recoverable volume, 2020-04](https://youtu.be/tZ9CSu2DMIE?t=61); [The hypertrophy series： maximum recoverable volume, 2020-04](https://youtu.be/tZ9CSu2DMIE?t=248); [ANIME WORKOUTS - Can you look like Baki Hanma in real life?, 2020-10](https://youtu.be/dfnn-YdXerg?t=855)). From 2021: do as little as possible for as much as possible ([The hypertrophy series： the optimal number of sets for muscle growth, 2021-02](https://youtu.be/QL9Dh9CGOBQ?t=114); [Viking's the Bare Bones Series Program review, 2021-03](https://youtu.be/8mGHG5C-EPE?t=1107)). 2024: low on the volume spectrum, "closer to HIT than to 18-20 sets", and his earliest programs had far too many sets ([BACK 2 THE GYM STREAM (Program reviews & Answering training questions), 2024-09](https://youtu.be/okm6bZHKHI4?t=5998); [1st Natural Hypertrophy stream! ASK YOUR QUESTIONS AND I SHALL ANSWER, 2024-09](https://youtu.be/bRKQIOYo2u4?t=389)). 2025: volume serves progression only ([New Hypertrophy Gimmick™ just dropped 🤡, 2025-03](https://youtu.be/ACFKXT44BzM?t=751)). The later view is the minimal-effective one.
- **Sets per exercise.** 2020: accessories almost always 4 sets, 2 not enough ([My sets/frequency for Natural Hypertrophy, 2020-01](https://youtu.be/m_IGaiqrCvA?t=319)). 2023: rule of three (2-4) ([The Monster Natty that trains EVERY DAY (Geoffrey Verity Schofield), 2023-04](https://youtu.be/aJ1e41y8Na4?t=379)). 2024-2025: 3 for novice/intermediate, 2 for advanced, 2 per taxing lift ([So you think you can lift? (Program Review LIVE), 2024-11](https://youtu.be/6p2x4kDDjzs?t=2081); [New Hypertrophy Gimmick™ just dropped 🤡, 2025-03](https://youtu.be/ACFKXT44BzM?t=751)). Later = fewer.
- **His own training.** 2020: 2-3 h sessions, 6 days/wk, responds to high volume ([How I split up my week for Natural Hypertrophy, 2020-01](https://youtu.be/cHYOYTgiRlM?t=187); [Recomp guide (part. 3)： performance & body fat loss/distribution, 2020-06](https://youtu.be/UieXEWMNnfI?t=380)). 2023: prefers fewer quality sets made possible by high frequency ([Leg Day + Bulk Update (Hypertrophy Log #2), 2023-07](https://youtu.be/6KA80BQ9W3k?t=1006)). 2024: chest 6/wk, arms 9 each, shoulders 9-12, legs 6+6 ([BACK 2 THE GYM STREAM (Program reviews & Answering training questions), 2024-09](https://youtu.be/okm6bZHKHI4?t=9295); [So you think you can lift? (Program Review LIVE), 2024-11](https://youtu.be/6p2x4kDDjzs?t=1680)). In 2020 he attributed his legs to hundreds of thousands of pounds of volume squats ([Wisconsin method aka Bulgarian light review (from a muscular hypertrophy standpo, 2020-02](https://youtu.be/RaGX9rPQr4k?t=499)).
- **Nucleus overload.** 2020-2022: an advocated accessory method for nearly every body part he wanted to grow ([Nucleus overload guide (part. 3)： my experience & sports applications, 2020-06](https://youtu.be/2edX06SQDnU); [Greek Aesthetics Bodybuilding Program (Apollonian Physique Workout), 2022-05](https://youtu.be/SPicD3F686s?t=378)). 2023: D tier, 1-2% of results ([The Most IMPORTANT Methods for Muscle Growth (Hypertrophy Tier-List), 2023-11](https://youtu.be/SxqjF2oPasg?t=2959)).
- **Back-off/backup sets.** 2020: "a must for hypertrophy… free tonnage" ([The hypertrophy series： utilizing back-off sets to accumulate quality tonnage, 2020-10](https://youtu.be/Rz4uzjM068M?t=942)). 2023: B tier, better as a variation ([The Most IMPORTANT Methods for Muscle Growth (Hypertrophy Tier-List), 2023-11](https://youtu.be/SxqjF2oPasg?t=1761)). 2024: he skips them on dips and on non-priority squats ([Your lifting program SUCKS! (Hypertrophy Q&A / Program review), 2024-10](https://youtu.be/c7hl9u3h_s0?t=10491); [Your lifting program SUCKS! (Hypertrophy Q&A / Program review), 2024-10](https://youtu.be/c7hl9u3h_s0?t=6752)).
- **Finishers.** 2021: fine, they build work capacity ([The Hypertrophy Iceberg Explained (a complete guide to muscle growth), 2021-07](https://youtu.be/8ELQ2XZgpls?t=1891)). 2023: D tier, junk volume or active recovery at best ([The Most IMPORTANT Methods for Muscle Growth (Hypertrophy Tier-List), 2023-11](https://youtu.be/SxqjF2oPasg?t=1889)).
- **Leg volume.** 2020: at least 11-12 heavy squats per squat day, plus giant-set finishers ([My sets/frequency for Natural Hypertrophy, 2020-01](https://youtu.be/m_IGaiqrCvA?t=191); [How I program my Squat days for Natural Hypertrophy, 2020-02](https://youtu.be/j5PP3gx7DC4?t=377)). 2022-2024: legs respond to minimalism; 3 sets each of a quad and a hinge movement; 6+6 weekly sets ([Hypertrophy Q&A #9, 2022-01](https://youtu.be/9y2s6kyFkPc?t=189); [Hypertrophy Q&A #9, 2022-01](https://youtu.be/9y2s6kyFkPc?t=126); [How I Built Monster Legs, 2024-12](https://youtu.be/-OjJEzZTXtQ?t=1071)).
- **High reps.** 2020: high ranges fine for isolation, pump work up to 50, face pulls 15-20 "never enough" ([Upper Body dominant 4 Days split review, 2020-06](https://youtu.be/PYmr91aELnE?t=289); [Upper Body dominant 4 Days split review, 2020-06](https://youtu.be/PYmr91aELnE?t=974); [Upper Body focused 5 days PPL + sprints program review, 2020-09](https://youtu.be/aaQr-Av0x9Y?t=580)). 2021-2023: stay at 2-12 with few sets near 15, above 15 risks junk, never below 6 on accessories ([The hypertrophy series： bypassing muscular endurance thresholds, 2021-01](https://youtu.be/fC5KHhv4_bI?t=193); [Come with me if you want big shoulders (JOIN THE CHALLENGE!), 2022-10](https://youtu.be/BhOuuyriBDw?t=632); [Come with me if you want massive arms (Step by Step MASSterplan), 2023-01](https://youtu.be/HXoY7xzHlWU?t=1071)).
- **Junk-volume framing.** 2021: the concept is "overblown" and junk is only bad if it replaces hard sets ([The Hypertrophy Iceberg Explained (a complete guide to muscle growth), 2021-07](https://youtu.be/8ELQ2XZgpls?t=3452)). 2022-2024: he applies the label widely and calls for the "bare effective minimum" ([Good chest day vs Bad chest day, 2022-05](https://youtu.be/k9_dDbGLFZQ?t=248); [This Calisthenics Freak Makes Bodybuilders Look Small (Baki_HD), 2024-06](https://youtu.be/2LoP6-KdEx4?t=504)).
- **Session-length philosophy.** 2020: advanced lifters must lengthen sessions ([Hypertrophy Q&A #3, 2020-11](https://youtu.be/6sFaB3rAY1A?t=2823)). 2021: as short as possible, 1h15 target ([The hypertrophy series： determining the optimal workout length, 2021-01](https://youtu.be/UprNxHue9d0); [Viking's the Bare Bones Series Program review, 2021-03](https://youtu.be/8mGHG5C-EPE?t=1107)). 2024: don't train to a clock, 45-60 min of hard sets exhausts most ([Don't be THAT GUY in 2024, 2024-01](https://youtu.be/uOAia_t5c_I?t=1067)).

**Contradictions**

- **Maximalist vs near-HIT, both in 2024.** He calls maximalist whole-body isolation the best, with the last 20% mattering for advanced lifters ([1st Natural Hypertrophy stream! ASK YOUR QUESTIONS AND I SHALL ANSWER, 2024-09](https://youtu.be/bRKQIOYo2u4?t=1280)), yet also places himself closer to HIT and says most could cut 20-30% ([BACK 2 THE GYM STREAM (Program reviews & Answering training questions), 2024-09](https://youtu.be/okm6bZHKHI4?t=5998); [Your lifting program SUCKS! (Hypertrophy Q&A / Program review), 2024-10](https://youtu.be/c7hl9u3h_s0?t=7961)).
- **20 weekly sets.** 2022: almost no one needs 16-20 and 20/wk is impractical ([How often should you train for 𝐁𝐎𝐃𝐘𝐁𝐔𝐈𝐋𝐃𝐈𝐍𝐆 , 2022-07](https://youtu.be/iDua_rNsBO8?t=1069); [How often should you train for 𝐁𝐎𝐃𝐘𝐁𝐔𝐈𝐋𝐃𝐈𝐍𝐆 , 2022-07](https://youtu.be/iDua_rNsBO8?t=1132)). 2023: back caps reach 20-28 and he runs 20 back and 18 shoulder sets ([Come with me if you want a BIG BACK (4 steps MASSterplan), 2023-09](https://youtu.be/7uBT8vp0lNw?t=1576); [The ULTIMATE PPL Program (Doom Slayer Physique), 2023-11](https://youtu.be/DA7QvIAyptw?t=1704)). Partly explained by the back's tolerance.
- **Isolation vs compound share.** 2023: about 2:1 isolation:compound per muscle ([Why spamming lateral raises won't work, 2023-12](https://youtu.be/yRRXCYcgzJs?t=510)). 2024: compounds should be the bulk of a program ([Why you shouldn't listen to Genetic Freaks (The Joel Williams Example), 2024-02](https://youtu.be/GyK1Y6WTR-g?t=887)).
- **Deadlift sets (2020-2022).** 1x5 is "good for strength not hypertrophy, prefer 3x3" ([4 days Upper Lower split Program review, 2020-04](https://youtu.be/fSOiGuUPqBc?t=124)), vs 1x5 is "great" and enough ([Icecream Fitness Program review, 2020-06](https://youtu.be/5Wz0xTfWOOs?t=940); [Icecream Fitness FAQ review, 2020-06](https://youtu.be/MCUpClPnPkQ?t=626)). 2021: 3x5 is too much ([The Smartest Push Pull Legs Routine by Jeff Nippard review, 2021-06](https://youtu.be/Mq2TaHm_ySI?t=823)), vs 2022: deadlifts only need 3x5 ([Can you look like Zodd from Berserk in real life? (ANIME WORKOUTS), 2022-10](https://youtu.be/CSwbuwl33eA?t=749)).
- **Supersetting squats/deadlifts (2020).** He will never superset them ([5 days Upper Lower (2 Uppers 2 Lowers + 1 Arm day) program review, 2020-10](https://youtu.be/dHXPhjaWBWk?t=1068)), yet he giant-sets even lower-body lifts ([FREE 4 days Body Parts split for Intermediates, 2020-06](https://youtu.be/o3RTXWAia4A?t=760)). 2022 refines this: pair squats only with unrelated small muscles ([Going to WAR over Giant Sets (Response to Bald Omni Man), 2022-09](https://youtu.be/nqzVqvMvQ1s?t=376)).
- **Calves/abs.** "You can never train abs or calves too much" ([BLOW UP your ARMS with these 3 GIANT sets (Biceps/Triceps/Forearms), 2022-09](https://youtu.be/QNxCVZro9jc?t=375)), vs 6 sit-up sets is too much and two ab isolations are redundant ([BACK 2 THE GYM STREAM (Program reviews & Answering training questions), 2024-09](https://youtu.be/okm6bZHKHI4?t=11459); [So you think you can lift? (Program Review LIVE), 2024-11](https://youtu.be/6p2x4kDDjzs?t=4861)).
- **Can extra sets hurt?** 2020/2022: one or two extra sets won't stop progress ([The hypertrophy series： maximum recoverable volume, 2020-04](https://youtu.be/tZ9CSu2DMIE?t=61); [Mike Mentzer： Mustachioed fraud or Bodybuilding genius? (🆃🅷🅴 🅷🅸, 2022-08](https://youtu.be/lmhW2W2UQto?t=754)), vs 2021: too much volume can stop a muscle growing (glued-chair analogy) ([Hypertrophy Q&A #7, 2021-05](https://youtu.be/D1_tXh-Kp9Y?t=696)).

# Appendix B. Glossary

NH's own vocabulary and the training jargon used in this book, defined as he uses it, with pointers to the principles where each term does its work.

- **1/2/3/4-plate standard** — The idea that a trained man should bench 1 plate, squat 2 and so on; NH says it roughly fits novices because the loads are low, but leverages make fixed numbers meaningless after that. See STR-59, STR-57.
- **85% rule** — His step-loading rule: build reps and sets at a weight until it feels like about 70% effort, then add weight to get back to about 85%, trim sets or reps, and rebuild. It deliberately does not maximise strength, so volume can accumulate. See PRG-48, STR-29.
- **543 (elevator) scheme** — A ladder for heavy deadlifts and overhead press: keep the weight, climb sets and reps up the ladder, then add weight and restart at the bottom. See PRG-43.
- **Ab anxiety** — Clinging to a skinny six-pack and refusing to gain weight; a form of "small guy syndrome" that keeps lifters small. See BLK-87.
- **Absolute intensity** — What you can move fresh and warmed up. Contrast relative intensity, which climbs through each set and session as fatigue builds. See INT-09, INT-10, VOL-04.
- **Accidental physique** — The look you get from strength-only or compound-only training without aesthetic intent: big trunk and quads, small arms. See AES-02, AES-30.
- **Adherence** — Sticking with a program. He puts it at the top of the muscle-building pyramid: a lift or program you enjoy beats a "better" one you skip. See MND-14, BEG-73, PRG-117.
- **AMRAP** — "As many reps as possible." He keeps it for finishers and unweighted calisthenics, never for loaded top sets or deadlifts. See INT-59, INJ-76.
- **Anabolic bank** — His image for how naturals grow: long, stable exposure to their own hormones over years, as opposed to the flat, permanently high levels of an injector. See NAT-17, GEN-57.
- **Anabolic window** — The supposed post-workout deadline for protein; he calls it a protein-powder marketing tactic. See NUT-36, IND-11.
- **Apollonian vs Herculean** — Two branches of the Greek ideal: Apollonian is wide shoulders and lats, small waist, smaller legs, low fat; Herculean (Farnese) is thicker waist, big limbs, legs and core. He prefers the Herculean. See AES-20.
- **Arm day** — A low-CNS day of a few upper compounds then arm isolation; earned once legs are trained twice a week, optional, and able to double as active recovery. See FRQ-66, FRQ-67, ARM-37.
- **Artificial failure** — A set ended by cardio, burn, pump, occlusion or a structural breakdown rather than by the target muscle; it feels hard but builds little. See INT-25, TEC-16.
- **Autoregulation** — Adjusting the day's work to how you are recovering. It needs rotation options built into the program and regulation skill first, so it suits advanced lifters. See FAT-16, PRG-116.
- **Back-off sets** — Sets after the opening strength work, tied to its weight and still pushed near failure; usually 2-3 of the same pattern with a modest drop. See INT-50, VOL-51, PRG-84.
- **Bear mode** — His term for the thick, Herculean look: big limbs, waist, legs, upper back and traps. See AES-20, AES-39.
- **Berserker physique** — His personal ideal: massive arms, forearms and legs slightly out of proportion with the trunk, a strong core, developed upper back and smaller shoulders. See AES-21.
- **Big ten** — The bare-minimum list of lifts that together cover every body part and the six size patterns. See EXS-09.
- **Bigorexia** — Muscle dysmorphia, the "I am too small" feeling; he says every lifter meets it, himself included. See MND-87, MND-88, JRN-72.
- **Blackpill** — Demoralised fatalism about genetics or natural potential; he calls it an excuse for passivity and a self-fulfilling prophecy. See MND-76, NAT-73, PHI-113.
- **Body English** — Using torso movement to finish a rep. Acceptable in small doses on heavy back rows, not on isolation work. See TEC-67, TEC-64.
- **Bracing** — A normal nose breath and tightening the abs as if about to be punched, holding the spine position through the rep; it matters mainly on heavy squats and deadlifts. See TEC-30.
- **Bridge program** — A transition program between low-volume novice training and high-volume intermediate training, because "an advanced program must be earned". See VOL-39, BEG-64.
- **Bro split** — One muscle per day, once a week. He calls it the worst template for naturals: too little frequency, too much per-session volume. See FRQ-37, NAT-28.
- **Bulk-cut purgatory** — Yo-yoing the same 10-20 lb up and down forever with no real progress. See BLK-78, BLK-79.
- **Bulking hypnosis** — "Size goggles" that hide fat gain on a bulk; the cut-side version is "lean goggles". Checking the mirror as often as the scale counters it. See BLK-35.
- **Cheerleader effect** — One outstanding muscle makes the weaker ones around it look better. See AES-27.
- **CNS fatigue** — Nervous-system fatigue; he says most people can't reach real CNS burnout, and strength loss blamed on it is usually diet, sleep or stress. See FAT-27, FAT-28, FAT-29.
- **Compounds and isolation ("shotgun and sniper")** — Compounds supply most of the tonnage, isolation covers what they miss; neither works alone. See EXS-01, EXS-02, EXS-08.
- **Crabs in the bucket** — People who ridicule and pull you down because your progress removes their excuses. See MND-77, PHI-50.
- **Danger rep** — The last grinding rep on a heavy squat, deadlift or variation, which he leaves in the tank. See INT-33, INT-28.
- **Deload** — A planned week of reduced training. For bodybuilders he calls scheduled deloads unnecessary, an emergency response to a programming mistake. See FAT-01, FAT-03, FAT-04.
- **Dirty bulk** — Gaining with junk food and a big surplus; he says it adds mostly fat and leverage, and his own was "wasted years". See BLK-41, JRN-14.
- **Educated barbarian** — His ideal of the lifter who develops body and mind together and arrives at the gym knowing exactly what to do. See MND-18, PHI-01.
- **Ego lifting** — Using more weight than the exercise can turn into a justified stimulus, including cutting range to lift more; he notes the label is often thrown as an insult. See TEC-19, MND-68.
- **Evolving rep ranges** — His core progression method: a fixed rep range per lift, start near the bottom, add reps, add weight when the first set hits the ceiling, stay in the range. See PRG-20, PRG-21, INT-46.
- **Evolving sets** — Progressing the number of sets inside a narrow span (usually 2-4): add a set when the top set tops the range, then add weight and drop a set. See PRG-26, VOL-52.
- **Fake natty** — Someone who uses PEDs while claiming to be natural; he says their real crime is killing trust that naturals can grow. See NAT-74, IND-38.
- **Failure** — The point where no further clean rep is possible; the set ends as soon as body English is needed. Only failure where the target muscle is the limit counts. See INT-26, INT-25, INT-27.
- **FFMI** — Fat-free mass index; he calls it worthless for judging natural status. See NAT-58.
- **Fishing-rod deadlift** — Knees locking early with a rounded back, so the back finishes the lift and the lifter struggles past the knees. See TEC-99, JRN-60.
- **Frame** — Clavicle width, waist, hips and joint size; it sets potential width and how muscle looks, and can't be trained. See AES-62, GEN-36, GEN-37.
- **Frequency** — How often a muscle or pattern is trained; the pillar of the trinity he says naturals ignore most. See FRQ-01, FRQ-04, NAT-29.
- **Fridge physique** — A thick trunk and back with no width or V-taper, typically from deadlift-only back training. See BAK-04, AES-02.
- **Frog physique** — Big legs on a small upper body, from PR-driven, squat-heavy or powerlifting training. See AES-55, STR-64.
- **Gentleman split** — His favourite template: an upper/lower skeleton whose days are built around synergistic muscle groups and a main compound, with flexible boundaries. See FRQ-38, FRQ-43.
- **Giant set** — Four or more exercises back to back; 4-5 is the sweet spot, ordered from most to least intense, and they double as a bodybuilder's conditioning. See RST-14, RST-15, CAR-21.
- **GOMAD** — "A gallon of milk a day"; he calls it idiotic, an uncontrolled surplus of milk fat and protein. See NUT-87, BLK-43.
- **Good-morning squat** — The cardinal squat fault: hips rise first, the squat turns into a good morning and the lower back takes the load instead of the quads. See TEC-109, TEC-33.
- **GPP** — General physical preparedness. For a bodybuilder, mostly supersets and giant sets of non-interfering moves plus carries and similar low-cost work. See CAR-21, CAR-27.
- **Grease the groove** — Very frequent submaximal practice of one movement; he allows it for pull-ups as an exception but blames highly repetitive Big-3 versions for novice injuries. See FRQ-26, INJ-53.
- **Gym look** — Looking like you lift in everyday clothes, relaxed. He says a relatively lean 200 lb already reads as trained, and it takes years before people notice. See AES-60, AES-66, AES-79.
- **Gymcel** — Someone who isolates in the gym believing a better body fixes everything; NH describes a "gymcel phase" of his own. See MND-96, JRN-70.
- **Hard set** — A set with a challenging load that ends at muscular failure and is repeatable within 2-3 days; he wants as much tonnage as possible to come from hard sets. See INT-40, INT-41, INT-32.
- **Hard vs soft variation** — A soft variation keeps the pattern and changes implement, grip, pause or range (near-full carryover); a hard variation is a different pattern and a new skill, so cap it. See EXS-15, EXS-17.
- **Hardgainer** — The supposed person who can't gain; he says there are no true hardgainers, only people who don't eat or train enough. See GEN-03, NUT-85, BLK-52.
- **HIT** — High-intensity training, one set to failure with long gaps (Mentzer); he says it is right about intensity but far too little volume for naturals. See INT-62, VOL-12.
- **Holy trinity of fake-natty nonsense** — His name for three ideas he says come from enhanced lifters: volume without an intensity window, avoiding compounds, and not understanding frequency. See NAT-25.
- **Intermediate hell** — The stage after novice gains where precise programming is needed and many lifters stall for years; "intermediate syndrome" is crashing by jumping straight to high volume. See JRN-26, VOL-39, MND-73.
- **Junk volume** — Work outside a relevant intensity window: unchallenging loads, pump chasing and sets ended by cardio rather than the muscle. It hurts most when it replaces hard sets. See VOL-07, VOL-08, VOL-09.
- **Lengthened partials** — Partial reps in the stretched part of the range. He says they may work and in 2024 likely beat full range, but finds them hard to standardise and prefers rest-pause. See INT-58, TEC-52.
- **Liquid tonnage** — His term for PEDs: each injection works like weeks of training. See NAT-16.
- **Maingaining** — He calls it a rebranded lean bulk and prefers "lean bulk" or "recomp". See BLK-88.
- **Mechanical failure** — The set ends because your structure (thoracic extension, setup, technique) gives out before the muscle, so tonnage stops reaching the target. See TEC-15, TEC-16, INJ-07.
- **Microloading** — Adding very small increments (microplates) to extend linear progression, especially on small muscles and presses; it also stalls eventually. See PRG-58, PRG-59.
- **Milo paradox** — Load-only progression is "designed to fail" because the ability to add weight outpaces recovery. See PRG-12.
- **Mind-muscle connection** — Prioritising the target muscle within a lift so stronger muscles don't take the work; useful for muscles that won't grow, no excuse for baby weights. See TEC-68, TEC-69, TEC-70.
- **Mirror days** — A/B days with the same emphasis but different lifts, rep ranges or order, to reduce boredom and overuse. See FRQ-75, FRQ-56.
- **MRV (maximum recoverable volume)** — The most work you can recover and grow from; individual, found by experiment and rising with training age. He aims between medium volume and MRV. See VOL-16, SLP-30.
- **Muscle memory** — Lost muscle comes back faster than it was first built; real, but not magic. See SCI-48, NAT-02.
- **Natty-or-not** — Content judging whether people are natural; he says it mostly hurts viewers by lowering standards and pushing beginners toward PEDs. See NAT-60, IND-48.
- **Natural ("natty")** — Never having taken PEDs, including TRT; take them once and you can never be natural again. See NAT-51, NAT-46.
- **Natural limit** — The claimed point where a natural stops growing. He calls it "a cultural limit, not a biological one": progress slows but continues if weight, volume and intensity keep rising. See GEN-11, GEN-12, GEN-13.
- **Noble natty** — A natural who takes pride in building a big, strong body naturally, not merely in being natural. See NAT-71.
- **Noob gains** — Fast early gains; he treats them as a quantity of development (about half your potential), not a time window that closes. See BEG-04, GEN-17, GEN-60.
- **Novice** — A lifter still on session-to-session linear progression; the stage ends when that stops, or when you want to and can write your own program, not at a strength standard. See PRG-93, BEG-06, BEG-07.
- **Novice syndrome** — Overdoing it as a beginner, the main reason novices crash; burnout is over-stimulation, not lack of potential. See BEG-71, BEG-16.
- **Nucleus overload (NO)** — Frequent, high-volume, very light work kept easy enough to repeat, complementing strength work for a muscle; the one exception to intensity windows. Later rated minor. See VOL-55, FAT-52, SCI-35.
- **Otter mode** — The lean, athletic, not-too-big look (Fight Club Brad Pitt) most women pick; staying there means never getting really strong or fully big. See AES-73, STR-17, GEN-37.
- **Overtraining** — Real but relative to the program; he says it is mostly coming back under-rested, and most "overtrained" lifters answered regression with more volume. See FAT-58, FAT-59, FAT-60.
- **Pain valley** — The window between inactive moderate pain and acute pain where he trains an irritated area to widen the pain-free range. See INJ-35.
- **Power coper / strength coper** — A lifter who hides poor muscle gains behind strength numbers or claims "the best way to get big is to get strong". See MND-64, STR-66.
- **Powerbuilding** — Heavy big-three work plus lazy isolation; he calls it a marketing term that delivers neither size nor strength. See STR-63, IND-58.
- **Progressive overload** — Something must go up for the muscles to go up: load, reps, sets, frequency, rest, variation or range. Non-negotiable. See PRG-01, PRG-11.
- **Pull-push-legs** — His order for a PPL split, so pull day's hinges and rows don't fatigue the legs right before squats. See FRQ-40, FRQ-41.
- **Pump** — The swollen feeling from fast, light reps; a by-product, not a growth signal. See INT-54, SCI-28.
- **Recomp** — Training hard at roughly maintenance so the body trades fat for muscle; slow but real, needs fat to trade, and needs at least a year. See BLK-54, BLK-55, BLK-57.
- **Recovery pot** — His model of recovery as a tub whose size is your MRV: take only part of it each session, keep it relatively full, never empty. See SLP-30, FRQ-07, SLP-31.
- **Red zone** — The disadvantaged part of a rep, usually where the negative turns into the positive; it stimulates most and is where injuries happen. Enter it with care, don't avoid it. See TEC-22, INJ-04.
- **Relevant intensity window** — The load range where volume actually counts (roughly 60-95% of 1RM); tonnage outside it is junk. See VOL-02, INT-15.
- **Rest-pause** — His preferred intensity technique: at failure, rest briefly, then add reps that must be the hardest of the set. See INT-56, INT-55.
- **RIR (reps in reserve)** — Reps left in the tank at the end of a set. He uses it on heavy, risky, low-rep work and says you must learn real failure first. See INT-34, INT-35, INT-36.
- **Rotation** — Alternating close variations in one slot (week A / week B) to fight overuse and accommodation; never because a lift stalled. See EXS-17, EXS-21, FRQ-76.
- **RPE** — Rating of perceived exertion; with percentages and RIR, an "A-tier" tool he doesn't use himself. See INT-37, INT-36.
- **Sandbagging** — Giving less than full effort without a reason. Chosen sandbagging (warm-ups, planned RIR) is fine; sandbagging forced by a fixed scheme wastes quality tonnage. See INT-44, INT-45, INT-38.
- **Schrödinger's genetics** — Before working you can't know your potential; those who stick with it get called gifted, those who quit get called low-T. See GEN-06, NAT-61.
- **Selective failure** — Taking isolation, presses, rows and other low-risk lifts to failure, while keeping 1-2 reps in reserve on squats, deadlifts and good mornings. See INT-28, INT-39.
- **SFR (stimulus-to-fatigue ratio)** — How much growth stimulus a lift gives for the fatigue it costs. He calls it overrated as an excuse to avoid compounds, but relevant where fatigue lands on tendons and stabilisers. See FAT-22, FAT-24.
- **Shelf muscles** — Delts, traps and upper chest, the muscles that give the "bodybuilder look". See AES-37.
- **Skinny-fat** — Low muscle with some fat; he calls it metabolic distress, not a body type, and says to recomp at maintenance rather than cut. See BLK-05.
- **Skinny pack** — Abs that only show because the person is skinny, as opposed to trained abs that stay visible at higher body fat. See ABS-02.
- **Specificity tree** — His early way of organising lifts: movement-pattern branches topped by a king lift fed by lower lifts. Later rated C tier for bodybuilding. See EXS-39.
- **Spider physique** — A big torso on spaghetti arms, from programs that neglect arm isolation. See AES-30, ARM-39.
- **Static (fixed) schemes** — Fixed sets and reps such as 5x5 or 4x10; they force sandbagging and can only progress by adding weight. Fine for novices and as deliberate tools. See PRG-51, PRG-52, PRG-53.
- **Step loading** — Adding stimulus as reps first, then sets, then frequency, then weight, always in small steps. See PRG-14, PRG-48.
- **Strength restoration** — Tiny band or light exercises for problem tendons, supersetted between sets of main lifts at almost no recovery cost. See INJ-63.
- **Strength work** — The 1-3 heavy opening sets of a session: the "lighthouse" that drives progression while being a minority of the tonnage. Never supersetted. See PRG-83, STR-21, VOL-41.
- **Superset** — Exercises back to back with no planned rest, then rest after the round. He supersets accessory and isolation work for different or antagonist muscles. See RST-13, RST-09, RST-10.
- **Technical rating** — How much practice a lift takes to master and keep; high-rated lifts are "jealous" and decay without constant practice. See TEC-74, TEC-75.
- **Tonnage** — Reps x weight accumulated over time; "tonnage is king" as long as it sits in a relevant intensity window. See VOL-02, PRG-02, VOL-06.
- **Tonnage sacrifice** — Deliberately holding strength work steady while pushing volume or a secondary lift; not a plateau. See PRG-80.
- **Top set** — The first and heaviest working set of a lift; only it needs to reach the top of the range before you add weight. See PRG-21, PRG-47.
- **Trinity (volume, intensity, frequency)** — The three variables he treats as one system and the main drivers of hypertrophy; push one while ignoring the others and the system breaks. See VOL-01, SCI-25, FAT-15.
- **TRT** — Testosterone replacement therapy. He says any exogenous hormone revokes natural status, real TRT is rare, and clinics use it as a gateway. See NAT-46, NAT-47, NAT-48.
- **V-taper** — Width from shoulders, lats and serratus over a small waist; without lats you get a T-taper. See AES-36, BAK-21.
- **Weighted stretch** — Loading a muscle in its lengthened position; he calls it underused, and the way traps and forearms grow from heavy holds. See TEC-89, BAK-35, FOR-04.
- **Widowmaker** — A high-effort squat set he treats, like burnouts, as an occasional tool rather than regular programming; also the last phase of his knee rehab ladder. See INT-60, INJ-81.
- **Work capacity** — The ability to do and recover from the volume that drives growth; built and lost gradually. Novices lack it more than they lack recovery. See VOL-38, BEG-15, CAR-02.
